# ProbOS — Architectural Decisions

Append-only log of architectural decisions made during ProbOS development. Each AD documents the reasoning behind a design choice.

See [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md) for project status. See [docs/development/roadmap.md](docs/development/roadmap.md) for future plans.

**Archives:** [Era I — Genesis](decisions-era-1-genesis.md) | [Era II — Emergence](decisions-era-2-emergence.md) | [Era III — Product](decisions-era-3-product.md) | [Era IV — Evolution](decisions-era-4-evolution.md)

## Era V — Civilization (Phases 31-36)

### AD-1017: MCP server authentication — static tokens + OAuth authorization-code (#958, epic #955)

**Context.** AD-1015 shipped the MCP server registration store with `auth_kind` (none|static|oauth) + `credential_ref` as **inert** strings, and AD-1016 added the keychain credential backend; this AD makes auth **live** — resolve a server's stored credential and inject it at register time, with **secrets only in the credential vault by ref, never in the store row, never in any API response, never logged.** **Decision.** Architect→Builder. New `integrations/mcp_bridge/mcp_oauth.py` `McpOAuthProvider` modeled on the AD-720c `CloudPickerProvider` (reuses `OAuthTokenBundle` by **import only** — cloud-picker code untouched), parameterized by the record's non-secret `oauth_json` (client_id/authorize_url/token_url/scopes/redirect_uri) + the vault-stored `client_secret`: `start_authorization(*,state)→url`, `async handle_callback(*,code)→OAuthTokenBundle` (httpx POST `grant_type=authorization_code`), `async refresh(*,refresh_token)→OAuthTokenBundle` (`grant_type=refresh_token`); a self-contained `McpOAuthError` (no coupling to the cloud-picker error taxonomy); **token values are never logged** (failures log only status code / exception type, never the response body). `store.py` `McpServerRecord` gains four **non-secret** fields — `auth_header_name`("Authorization")/`auth_scheme`("Bearer")/`auth_env_var`("")/`oauth_json`("") — added to the schema, `to_public_dict`, `_row_to_record`/`create`/`update`/`_record_to_params` round-trip, and a migration-safe `_migrate_ad1017()` (`ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` with defaults, `sqlite3.OperationalError` swallowed when already present); the four columns are appended **after** `created_at`/`updated_at` in the `CREATE TABLE` so a fresh DB and an `ALTER`-migrated AD-1015 DB share identical positional column order (the positional `_row_to_record` indices stay valid). `validate_record`'s secret-key denylist is unchanged — it still refuses credential-bearing header/env *values*. `routers/mcp_servers.py` adds `_resolve_auth_headers`/`_resolve_auth_env` (+ a shared `_resolve_secret_value` vault read; `none`/vault-miss → `{}` + warning, honest-degrade) merged into a runtime-aware `_register` (http `headers={**record.headers, **auth}`, stdio `env={**record.env, auth_env_var:value}`) — `auth_kind=="none"` resolves to `{}` so register is **byte-identical to AD-1015**. New endpoints (all gated on `management_enabled`, 404 when off): `POST/DELETE /{id}/credential` (static — store/delete the token in the vault by ref `mcp:{id}`, persist non-secret header/scheme/env-var, re-register; 503 when no vault); `POST /{id}/auth/start` (persist `oauth_json` + vault the `client_secret` under `mcp:{id}:oauth_secret`, mint CSRF state via a lazy per-runtime `_get_state_store` mirroring `cloud_pickers.py:59` + `_clear_state_stores()` test hook, return `{auth_url,state}`); `GET /{id}/auth/callback?code=&state=` (consume state → 403 on invalid, exchange, store the bundle under `mcp:{id}:oauth`, flip `auth_kind="oauth"`, return the **same popup-close HTML** as the cloud-picker callback); `POST /{id}/auth/refresh` (reactive — read bundle, `provider.refresh`, re-store, re-register; 400 when no refresh_token). **Scope (named, not built):** device-code → AD-1017a; HXI → AD-1018; per-agent grants → AD-1019. **No secret ever reaches the store row / a response body / logs.** **Tests.** `test_ad1017_mcp_auth.py` (38, BF-287 real `McpServerStore` + real `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` on tmp_path + real `MCPBridge` + real `TestClient`; only the external httpx token exchange is `MockTransport`-mocked): static store/resolve/inject/custom-header/bare-scheme/delete-purges-vault/503-no-vault/404; **token never in row/response (asserted), never in logs (caplog asserted)**; OAuth start→callback→resolve-Bearer/invalid-state-403/exchange-502/refresh-restores/no-refresh-400/token-never-in-response; `auth_kind=="none"` byte-identical; gate-off ⇒ all 404; provider unit tests (authcode/refresh/non-200/no-access-token/transport-error); store migration reads a pre-AD-1017 row with column defaults + fresh-DB round-trip of the four fields. New 38 green; parity `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597 or ad1015 or credential or cloud_picker"` **384 passed** (346 **unchanged** + 38). Default `auth_kind="none"` ⇒ byte-identical.

### AD-1016: Credential backend abstraction — OS keychain backend (#957, epic #955)

**Context.** The credential layer (AD-706f) had a single backend: `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` (Fernet over a JSON sidecar, KEK derived from `auth.crew_scope_token`). The MCP management UX epic (#955) needs secrets to optionally live in the **OS keychain** (Windows DPAPI / macOS Keychain / Linux libsecret) instead of an app-managed encrypted file — operator-selectable. Consumers (`cloud_pickers.read`, `actions.materialize_to_temp`) already depend only on the `CredentialVault` Protocol, so a second backend is a drop-in. AD-1015's `McpServerStore.credential_ref`/`auth_kind` resolve against this layer (AD-1017 wires them). **Decision.** Architect→Builder. New `security/keyring_backend.py` `KeyringCredentialBackend` implements the `CredentialVault` Protocol **exactly** (5 async, keyword-only methods; `inspect.signature`-equal to `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` — verified structurally substitutable). Secret *values* live only in the OS keychain via the AD-754 `CredentialEncryptor` (`keyring`); the OS keychain is a `service+username→value` KV store with **no list and no metadata**, so the backend keeps a **non-secret metadata sidecar** (JSON `{"refs": {ref: {scope, created_at, last_read_at, read_count}}}` — **values NEVER in the sidecar**) with the file-vault's atomic tmp+rename write + `threading.RLock`. `keyring` is synchronous → every keyring call is wrapped in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)`; `store` writes the keyring **first** (so a failed write leaves no orphan metadata) and raises a clear `RuntimeError` on keyring failure; `read`/`delete`/`list_refs` honest-degrade (None/[]) on `NoKeyringError`/any keyring error and never crash the runtime. **Crew-token gating (RESOLVED):** the keychain is already encrypted at rest by the OS and the sidecar holds no secrets, so the keychain backend requires `enabled=True` but **not** `crew_scope_token` (the file vault still requires the token for its KEK). `config.py` `CredentialVaultConfig`: `backend` description → `"file" (default) | "keychain"` + a `@field_validator("backend")` rejecting other values, plus `keyring_index_path="data/credential_keyring_index.json"` and `keyring_service_name="probos.credentials"`. `finalize.py` (AD-706f block) switches on `vault_cfg.backend`: `"file"`/unset → today's `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` path **unchanged** (needs `enabled`+token); `"keychain"` → `KeyringCredentialBackend(service_name, index_path)` when `enabled` (token optional); both honest-degrade to None. **Scope discipline:** no MCP auth/OAuth wiring (AD-1017), no HXI (AD-1018), no per-agent grants (AD-1019); the Protocol surface, `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` behavior/wire format, `credential_encryption.py`, `cloud_pickers.py`, and `actions.py` are untouched. Default `backend="file"` ⇒ the keychain branch is skipped, file-vault construction + warning run exactly as before ⇒ **byte-identical**. **No secret value can reach the sidecar** (values flow only to the keychain; the sidecar stores scope/timestamps/count only). **Tests.** `test_ad1016_keyring_backend.py` (22, BF-287 — real dict-backed fake of `keyring.set/get/delete_password`, sidecar on `tmp_path`, NOT MagicMock): Protocol-signature parity vs `EncryptedFileCredentialVault` (5 methods, `inspect.signature`-equal + `iscoroutinefunction`), store→read, wrong-agent/expired/unknown scope→None, delete removes value **and** sidecar entry, list_refs metadata-only, read bumps read_count+last_read_at, **secret never in the on-disk index JSON** (`test_secret_value_never_in_sidecar`), materialize_to_temp writes the value (0600 best-effort), honest-degrade (keyring `get` raises → read None, list_refs still works), store raises a clear `RuntimeError` + no orphan metadata when keyring `set` raises, config `backend` default `file`/accepts `keychain`/rejects `bogus`/keyring defaults. Gate `-k "credential or vault or 706f or 754 or config"` **645 passed** (623 prior **unchanged** + 22). Tree left uncommitted (Builder hand-off).



**Context.** MCP servers were **static config + read-only** (`config.mcp.servers` registered once at boot via AD-449/AD-1014). The MCP management UX epic (#955) needs a **persisted, runtime-mutable registration store** + an HTTP CRUD surface so an operator can add/edit/remove/enable/disable servers without an edit-config-and-restart cycle. This AD is that foundation; the rest of the epic (credentials AD-1016, OAuth AD-1017, HXI AD-1018, per-agent grants AD-1019) builds on it. **Decision.** Architect→Builder workflow. New `integrations/mcp_bridge/store.py` `McpServerStore` mirrors `IntentGrantStore` exactly (`ConnectionFactory` + WAL/`busy_timeout`/`synchronous` PRAGMAs + in-memory `_cache` for sync reads + `db_path=""` cache-only for tests), with a frozen `McpServerRecord` + `to_public_dict()` (the **single serialization seam — never emits a secret**) and async `create`/`get`/`list`/`update`/`delete`/`set_enabled` + `list_sync`; `name` is the UNIQUE axis (dup → `ValueError`). A pure `validate_record(record, *, command_allowlist)` is the first gate: `http⇒url`, `stdio⇒command ∈ allowlist`, kebab-case `name`, and a **structural secret-key denylist** — a *non-empty* value on a known credential-bearing header key (`authorization`, `x-api-key`, `cookie`, …) or env key (`endswith {_token,_key,_secret,_password,_apikey,_api_key}` / exact `{token,secret,password,apikey,api_key}`) is refused with `secret_value_not_allowed` pointing the operator at `auth_kind`+`credential_ref` (AD-1016 resolves credentials at registration); empty values and all non-secret pairs pass through. New `routers/mcp_servers.py` (prefix `/api/mcp/servers`) is included **unconditionally** but gated per-endpoint on a new `MCPConfig.management_enabled=False` (404 `feature_disabled` when off → existing paths byte-identical): `GET ""`/`POST ""`(201, 400 on validation, 409 on dup name)/`GET {id}`/`PUT {id}` (re-register on a connection-affecting change)/`DELETE {id}` (best-effort unregister + delete; AD-1016 credential-cleanup TODO left)/`POST {id}/enable`+`/disable` (toggle registration, keep the row)/`POST {id}/test` (transient client, `initialize()`+`list_tools()`, **closed in `finally`** — no leaked subprocess; `{ok,tool_count}` or `{ok:false,error}` at HTTP 200, honest-degrade). Single bridge-key rule `key = url if type=="http" else name`; the http register path is **sync** (`register_server`), the stdio register/unregister paths are **async**. The **only** `bridge.py` change is a new `async unregister_server(key)` (pop + `await client.close()`, mirroring `close_all`). `finalize.py` builds the store inside `if config.mcp.enabled:` when `management_enabled`, direct-assigns `runtime.mcp_server_store`, and seeds each **enabled** stored row **after** the config-server loops — config wins (the bridge returns `False` on a duplicate key, so the seed never double-registers); a fresh DB has an empty cache ⇒ no-op ⇒ byte-identical boot. `shutdown.py` teardown mirrors `intent_grant_store`. `credential_ref`/`auth_kind` are **inert stored strings** this AD. **Scope discipline:** no HXI (AD-1018), no credential storage/reads (AD-1016), no OAuth (AD-1017), no per-agent grants (AD-1019); `routers/tools.py` catalog stays config-only (AD-1018 unions store rows). The AD-1014 pack-`mcpServers`-wiring forward-references (DECISIONS body + PROGRESS L3) are re-pointed from "AD-1015" → **AD-1020** (this AD is the stronger claim on the number). Default-OFF (`management_enabled=False`) ⇒ the router 404s, no store is constructed/seeded, **byte-identical**. **No secret value is ever persisted or returned** (the `validate_record` denylist + `to_public_dict` are the guards). **Tests.** `test_ad1015_mcp_server_store.py` + `test_ad1015_mcp_servers_api.py` (56, BF-287 — real `McpServerStore` `db_path=""` + a real-DB round-trip, real `MCPBridge`, real `TestClient`, AD-1014 stdio echo fixture for live-register/test-connection): store CRUD + dup-name `ValueError`, the full `validate_record` matrix (each error code + secret-guard accept/reject incl. empty-value-allowed + non-secret pass-through), gate-off-404, create/list/get/put-re-register/delete/enable-disable, transient test-connection ok (echo, `tool_count=3`) + honest-degrade `{ok:false}` at HTTP 200, config/store dedup (config's client wins). Parity gate `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597"` **286 passed** (230 prior **unchanged** + 56 new); config regression **574 passed** (573 prior unchanged + 1 new whose name matches `config`). Default-OFF ⇒ byte-identical.

### AD-1014: stdio/subprocess MCP transport — marketplace launch parity (#954)

**Context.** ProbOS spoke MCP over HTTP only (`MCPClient` hardcoded to `httpx`, `MCPBridge.register_server(url)`). Marketplace MCP servers (the official registry, Smithery, Anthropic Directory — 15k+) are overwhelmingly **stdio**, launched as a subprocess (`uvx`/`npx`/`command`), and the MCP spec says *"clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible."* Without a stdio transport ProbOS cannot install the bulk of the ecosystem (nor the servers a Capability Pack bundles in its already-parsed `mcpServers` field, #948). Researched against the MCP spec (2025-06-18), GitHub Copilot/VS Code, Claude Code, and Hermes Agent (Nous Research) — all four converge on `type`+`command`/`args`/`env`, a trust gate before first launch ("local MCP servers run arbitrary code"), per-server timeouts, tool-name namespacing, stderr→logs, and **install-into-isolation, never host** (the subprocess is the isolation; none pip-install into their own process). **Decision.** Architect→Builder workflow. Introduce a `Transport` Protocol behind `MCPClient` so HTTP and stdio are peers: `transport.py` adds `HttpTransport` (the existing HTTP wire body lifted **byte-identically**, incl. request-direction `Mcp-Session-Id` self-management + response-header capture) and `StdioTransport` (spawn via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`, **NDJSON** framing per the stdio spec, skip-until-matching-id read so `notifications/*` aren't mistaken for the response, held stderr-drain task, `close()` = stdin-close → terminate → kill-fallback). `MCPClient.__init__(transport=None)` defaults to `HttpTransport` so `register_server` + all AD-449/AD-597 tests stay **unchanged** (`_http` kept as a back-compat property proxy). `MCPServerConfig` gains a `type` discriminator (`http` default | `stdio`) + `command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd`/`timeout_seconds` with a `model_validator` (`http`⇒`url`, `stdio`⇒`command`); `MCPConfig` gains `stdio_enabled=False` (the default-OFF gate) + `command_allowlist=[uvx,npx,python,node,docker]`. `MCPBridge.register_stdio_server` enforces guards **in order, all before any spawn**: `stdio_enabled` → duplicate → **command allowlist** (refuse + `MCP_BRIDGE_FAILED` reason=`command_not_allowed`, no subprocess) → **consent** (`consent_fn`, refuse → `consent_denied`) → spawn. Startup wires `consent_fn` to the AD-1004/1012 HookBus `PreToolUse` gate (fail-safe: refuse on ASK and DENY) and adds an **inert-by-default** stdio registration loop. **Scope discipline — mechanism only:** no pack `mcpServers` auto-launch (AD-1020), no OS sandbox (#936 Tier-2), no marketplace UI, no runtime-venv installs; `external_discovery` (transport-agnostic) untouched. Default-OFF (`stdio_enabled=False` + empty `servers`) ⇒ **byte-identical** to prior behavior. **Tests.** `test_ad1014_stdio_mcp_transport.py` (24, BF-287 real `MCPBridge` + a real in-repo NDJSON echo subprocess fixture): handshake/list/call round-trips, `close()` terminates the proc, command-not-allowlisted → no spawn, consent-deny → no spawn, bad-JSON/timeout honest-degrade, config validator, and a focused fake-httpx test locking the request-direction `Mcp-Session-Id` injection (the #1 regression risk). HTTP parity gate: existing `-k "mcp or ad449 or ad597"` **230 passed unchanged**; config regression 573 passed.

### AD-1013: skills-only Capability-Pack loader (#948)

**Context.** First write-side slice of the Capability-Pack loader, and the lowest-risk tier. The read-side is complete (AD-1003a–f: parse → scan → inventory API → Ship's Locker list → component preview). A pack declares skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers; of these, **skills are the only non-executing component** — a `SKILL.md` is markdown *instructions* the LLM reads at reasoning time, not code that runs. So the skills tier can load with zero code-execution risk while the agent/.py + hooks/MCP tiers (which execute) wait for the AD-1014 self-mod-chain loader. **Decision.** `packs/loader.py` `load_pack_skills(pack_dir, catalog, *, origin_prefix="pack")` walks a pack's declared folder-skills (a subdir with `SKILL.md`, via the AD-1003e `preview_pack` inventory) and loads each through the **existing AD-596d `CognitiveSkillCatalog.import_skill`** path — which validates the `SKILL.md`, dedup-guards by name, copies the skill into the catalog skills dir, and registers it. Reuse over reinvention: the loader is only the orchestration; the validated import path is unchanged. Each skill is tagged `origin="pack:<name>"` for provenance (identify/remove a pack's skills as a unit). Returns a frozen `PackLoadResult` (`loaded[]`, `skipped[(name, reason)]`). **Honest-degrade:** a duplicate or invalid skill is *skipped with a reason*, never raised; a standalone `.md` (no `SKILL.md` folder) is skipped (the AgentSkills.io importer needs the folder shape); agent `.py`/`.json`/`.md` are never touched by this tier. **Consent + gating live in the caller** — a caller must check `config.packs.enabled` (default OFF) and obtain operator consent (the Ship's Locker preview is the review surface) before invoking; the loader is pure mechanism (mechanism-first, mirroring AD-1004), so it adds no live behavior on its own. **Tests.** `test_ad1013_pack_skills_loader.py` (8, BF-287 real `CognitiveSkillCatalog` cache-only + real tmp_path packs): loads-declared-folder-skills, origin-tag-provenance, custom-prefix, no-manifest→None, standalone-md-skipped, duplicate-skipped-not-raised, agents-not-loaded (a `rogue.py` is never registered/executed), partial-load mixes loaded+skipped. Pack + skill-catalog regression 191 passed.

### AD-1012: lifecycle-hook bus PreDispatch wiring — the pluggable capability gate (#949, #944)

**Context.** AD-1004 (#949) shipped the `HookBus` substrate (`HookEvent`, `HookDecision`, most-restrictive-wins aggregation, honest-degrade) but deliberately left it *unwired* — firing with no handlers is a no-op. The per-agent capability gate (AD-1007/1008) meanwhile enforced inline at two origination sites (`reply_pipeline.step_4h`, `agentic_dispatch`). The held decision (Captain-confirmed 2026-06-15): wire the bus as the canonical `PreDispatch` gate with **block** semantics, **default-OFF**. **Decision.** New `hooks/handlers.py` `make_capability_gate_handler(intent_grant_store)` — a pure policy adapter returning `HookResult(DENY)` only on an explicit `resolve_sync == "restricted"` (agent-precedence Captain disable), `ALLOW` on `granted`/`no_opinion`, `None` (abstain) on a malformed context. The bus is instantiated in `startup/communication.py` **only when `config.hooks.enabled`** (default False); when on, the capability gate is registered on `HookEvent.PRE_DISPATCH` and exposed as `runtime.hook_bus` (threaded via `CommunicationResult.hook_bus`, torn down in shutdown). `reply_pipeline.step_4h` now routes through `hook_bus.fire(PRE_DISPATCH, …)` when wired, else falls back to the inline `IntentGrantStore` check — **byte-identical default behavior** (bus is None unless the flag is set). This makes the gate the shared lifecycle point where Capability-Pack hooks (#948) and a future consensus handler attach with the same most-restrictive-wins aggregation. **Scope discipline:** the conversational [MESH] origination path is wired; the agentic-loop `PreToolUse` fire and command-based pack hooks remain follow-up slices. **Tests.** `test_ad1012_hook_bus_wiring.py` (10, BF-287 real `HookBus` + real `IntentGrantStore` cache-only): handler restricted→deny / granted→allow / no_opinion→allow / `intent` alias / missing-agent→abstain / missing-intent→abstain; bus denies-restricted, allows-ungranted, allows-granted, restriction-is-agent-scoped. AD-1004 15 + AD-1012 10 = 25 green; touched-path regression (reply_pipeline / ad1005/1007/1008 / intent_grant / mesh_read / hook / config) **714 passed**. Default-OFF → no live behavior change.

### AD-1003f: Ship's Locker pack component preview (expandable) (#944, #948)

**Context.** UI capstone of the Capability-Pack read-side: AD-1003d listed installed packs in the Ship's Locker; AD-1003e added `GET /api/packs/{name}` (component preview). This wires the two so the operator can expand a pack to see what it declares — before the deferred loader exists. **Decision.** `ShipsLockerPanel` valid-pack rows become clickable (`+`/`−` toggle); expanding fetches `GET /api/packs/{name}` (`fetchPackDetail`, deps-injectable) and renders the pack's declared `skills:` / `agents:` component names inline. A stale-response guard (only adopt detail whose `name` matches the expanded row) prevents a slow fetch from painting under the wrong pack; honest-degrade leaves the "Loading components…" / "No declared components" note on failure. Invalid packs stay non-expandable. Read-only — the preview lists components, never loads or executes them. **Tests.** `ShipsLockerPanel.test.tsx` +3: expand-shows-components, collapse-on-second-click, no-components-note. UI 16 + `npm run build` clean. The Capability-Pack **read-side is now complete end-to-end** (parse → scan → inventory API → Locker list → component preview API → Locker expand); only the trust-gated loader remains on #948.

### AD-1003e: pack content preview — read-only enumeration of a pack's declared components (#944, #948)

**Context.** Fifth Capability-Pack slice. The read-side (parse → scan → API → HXI, AD-1003a–d) lists *which packs* are installed; before the deferred loader (which executes pack code, held for the operator trust gate), the operator should be able to inspect *what a pack contains*. This is the read-only inventory the loader will consume — surfaced now so a pack can be reviewed before loading. **Decision.** `packs/scanner.py` `preview_pack(pack_dir)` loads the manifest (AD-1003a) and enumerates the actual component files under its declared `skill_paths`/`agent_paths`: a subdir with a `SKILL.md` is a folder-skill, standalone `.md` are skills, agent files are `.md`/`.json`/`.py`. Returns `PackContents` (frozen: name + `PackComponent[]` for skills/agents + hooks/mcp flags). `describe_pack_contents` is the serializable form. `GET /api/packs/{name}` (resolves by *manifest* name, not folder) returns it; 404 when disabled / not-found / no-valid-manifest. **Read-only — component files are LISTED, never opened, parsed, imported, or executed**; directory traversal is guarded (a declared path that escapes the pack dir via `..` is skipped). Paths are normalized to POSIX (`as_posix()`) so the API is cross-platform. Honest-degrade: missing dir / invalid manifest → `None`; never raises. **Tests.** `test_ad1003e_pack_preview.py` (10, BF-287 real tmp_path packs): folder-skills + agent files by ext, standalone-md skills, missing-declared-dir→empty, hooks/mcp flags, no-manifest→None, invalid-manifest→None, path-traversal-blocked, frozen component, `describe_pack_contents` shape + None. `test_ad1003c_packs_api.py` +3 (detail endpoint: lists-components-by-manifest-name, 404-disabled, 404-not-found). Pack suite 48 passed; smoke clean. The Capability-Pack read-side is now complete through component-level preview; only the loader (write-side, trust-gated) remains on #948.

### AD-1003d: Ship's Locker "Installed Packs" section (#944, #948)

**Context.** Fourth Capability-Pack slice: surface the AD-1003c `GET /api/packs` inventory in the HXI — the "installed plugins" list lives in the Ship's Locker (the ship-wide capabilities catalog), alongside tools/skills/mesh/MCP. **Decision.** `ShipsLockerPanel` gains an **INSTALLED PACKS** section + a `fetchPacks` helper (bound to `GET /api/packs`) fetched independently of the catalog — a packs failure honest-degrades to the disabled note and never blocks the catalog (the locker's primary content). Renders: the disabled note when `packs.enabled=False` (the default), "No packs installed" when empty, else one row per pack (name + `vX.Y.Z` + `hooks`/`mcp` flags + description; a bad-manifest pack shows red "invalid manifest"). Read-only — viewing only; no install/load action (that's the deferred loader slice). **Tests.** `ShipsLockerPanel.test.tsx` +3: disabled-note-by-default, lists-installed-valid+invalid, packs-honest-degrade-does-not-break-catalog. UI 13 + `npm run build` clean. The Capability-Pack read-side (parse AD-1003a → scan AD-1003b → API AD-1003c → HXI AD-1003d) is now complete; the loader (behind the operator trust gate) is the remaining write-side slice on #948.

### AD-1003c: GET /api/packs — read-only installed-pack inventory endpoint (#944, #948)

**Context.** Third Capability-Pack slice: surface the AD-1003b scanner over HTTP, the cross-tool "installed plugins" list (VS Code / Copilot CLI / Claude Code). **Decision.** `PacksConfig` (config.py, default OFF, `packs_dir="data/packs"`); `routers/packs.py` `GET /api/packs` — when `packs.enabled=False` returns `{enabled:false, packs:[], counts:{0,0,0}}`; when enabled, resolves `packs_dir` against the runtime data dir (BF-628 lesson: relative paths resolve to the platform data dir, not cwd) and returns `describe_scan(...)` + `enabled:true` + `packs_dir`. Mounted in api.py. **Read-only — nothing installed, loaded, or executed** even when enabled; the loader is a later slice behind the operator trust gate. Honest-degrade: missing config / packs dir → empty. **Tests.** `test_ad1003c_packs_api.py` (5, BF-287 real `TestClient` + tmp_path packs + config-shaped runtime): disabled→empty, enabled→lists-installed (incl. a bad-manifest error entry), relative-dir-resolved-against-data-dir, missing-dir-honest-degrades, no-config→empty. Config default-OFF smoke; broad config/execution/packs regression 737 passed (confirms the `PacksConfig` add + `ExecutionConfig` untouched).

### AD-1011: ship-wide skill coverage — the civilization skill-registry view (#815)

### BF-629: conversational web_search/read_page synthesis — reason over results, don't paste links (#953)

**Context (Captain live test, 2026-06-14).** Asked Ezri the same question as GitHub Copilot (*"web search the Fable LLM, latest news"*). Copilot returned a synthesised briefing (what it is / breaking news / capabilities / sources / bottom line); Ezri returned a **raw list of links** and only synthesised after the Captain pushed back ("you gave me links but didn't reason over the articles"). Repeated across several turns — the Captain was manually driving the search→reason→summarise loop turn by turn.

**Root cause (verified).** Ezri's conversational reply uses the AD-869 Tier-2 **do-and-report** `[MESH web_search …]` affordance, not an agentic tool-use loop. `reply_pipeline.step_4h_mesh_read_parse` sends the intent to a **separate** `WebSearchAgent` and pastes its result **verbatim** via `_render_mesh_read_result`; the originating agent never reasons over it. `WebSearchAgent.instructions` say "present the results clearly" → it **lists** (title/url/snippet). The tell: the Captain's *next* turn synthesised — because by then the results were in conversation history and a normal reply pass reasoned over them. Contrast: Copilot and ProbOS's own `AgenticLoop`/`WorkItemAgenticExecutor` (AD-545/856) keep the tool result in the *same* model's context and continue reasoning — the conversational path took the fast delegate-and-paste shortcut.

**Decision.** Add a **synthesis pass** to `step_4h_mesh_read_parse`: after a `requires_reflect` read — `_MESH_READ_SYNTHESIZE_INTENTS = {web_search, read_page}`, exactly the network/LLM-bound reads — a new `_synthesize_mesh_read` helper makes ONE LLM pass through `runtime.llm_client` (mirroring the AD-934 deliberate re-roll) so the **originating** agent reasons over the result in its own voice, with the Captain's question + the rendered results as context, producing a synthesised answer (key findings + inline sources) instead of the raw list. Verbatim reads (`read_file`/`list_directory`/`stat_file`/`search_*`) skip synthesis — the raw output IS the answer. `DmMeshSynthesisConfig` (`enabled`/`tier=standard`/`max_tokens=700`) defaults **OFF in the model** (deterministic tests, safe-by-default) and **ON in `config/system.yaml`** (the running instance gets the Copilot-parity behavior — the AD-935 ship-it pattern).

**Honest-degrade (and the empty-content interaction).** A disabled flag, missing client, empty `rendered`, or an empty/raised LLM response all return the verbatim `rendered` unchanged — so a degraded LLM **never drops the Captain's results**, it falls back to the raw list. This is also the exact protection for the **BF-289/612 empty-content proxy surface** the Captain hit in the same session (a wedged keep-alive socket returns HTTP 200 empty): BF-612's socket-recycle is the primary mitigation; this fix ensures that even if the synthesis pass itself hits an empty response, the search results still reach the Captain rather than "(no reply)".

**Scope fence.** Conversational `[MESH]` path only. No change to the `WebSearchAgent`/`PageReaderAgent` themselves, the Tier-3 `[CREATE_TASK]` async path, the agentic loop, or the verbatim local-IO reads. The AD-935 OFF-in-model/ON-in-yaml default keeps every existing test deterministic (default-OFF) with zero obsolete-contract updates.

**Tests.** `test_bf629_mesh_synthesis.py` (9, BF-287 — real `DmReplyPipeline` + real `DmSanityGate` + real config-shaped runtime; fake intent-bus + LLM only at the I/O edges): web_search + read_page synthesise; prompt carries the Captain's question + rendered results + agent voice + tier; disabled→verbatim (no LLM call); read_file not synthesised; empty-LLM / no-client / raising-LLM all fall back to verbatim; a failed read never synthesises. Regression: AD-869 mesh-read + AD-870/933/934 pipeline 48 passed; AD-726 pipeline + capability 44 passed; config defaults OFF + `system.yaml` loads ON.

### AD-1009: role templates — view a role's loadout + apply it as a starting template (Agent Customizations epic #944, #952)

**Context.** The Captain's role-framework directive: *"assign a role to an agent like 'Counselor' — that role has tools and capabilities already assigned (a template) — use that as a template to start with, then enable/disable per agent which overrides the role."* The role→skills→tools engine already exists at agent birth (`ACM.commission`, AD-889); per-agent override of tools/skills/capabilities already exists (AD-894/AD-983b/AD-1007). What was missing: **visibility** of what a role grants, and an **explicit apply action** (commission only ran at birth).

**Decision (backend).**
- **`GET /api/crew/roles`** — enumerate every role from the ontology assignments, each with: `role_id` (post_id), `agent_type`, `callsign`, post `title`/`department`, required `skills` (from `RoleTemplate`), the `tools` those skills resolve to (AD-888 `resolve_tools_for_skill`, honest-degrade `[]`), and the mesh `capabilities` the role's `agent_type` serves (from live `intent_descriptors`). Read-only, derived — no new role config. The complete "what does this role include as a template" view.
- **`POST /api/crew/{agent_id}/apply-role`** (`ApplyRole{role_id?}`) — apply a role's skill+tool template to an agent via `ACM.commission`. `role_id` selects which role (resolved post→agent_type via `get_agents_for_post`); omitted → the agent's own role (refresh from template). Additive + reversible (grants are revocable) → no consensus gate (Minimal Authority). Capabilities stay governed per-agent (AD-1007); they are not stamped by a role.
- **AD-889 commission guard fix (agent-precedence on re-apply).** The tool-grant idempotency check changed from `if any(not g.is_restriction for g in existing)` to `if existing` — i.e. skip if ANY active per-agent decision exists (a grant OR a manual Captain restriction). Re-applying a role template therefore never clobbers a per-agent override: a manual *disable* survives re-apply. Byte-identical at birth (no decisions exist yet); only re-apply benefits.

**Deferred (follow-ons).** Role-level capability/tool DISABLE *authoring* (so a role can disable a capability by default, activating the grant-overrides-role-disable direction end-to-end) needs a role-defaults store + UI — not built (today a CAN-REQUEST capability's role default is "enabled/reachable," so the live action is a per-agent disable, AD-1007). The Personnel Console role-picker UI (apply-role from the Ship's Office, role template browser) is the AD-1010 UI slice.

**Tests.** `test_ad1009_roles.py` (10, BF-287 real route handlers + real `SimpleNamespace` ontology/registry + a recording ACM stub): served-intent grouping + no-registry degrade; `list_roles` view assembly (title/dept/skills/served-caps/tool-degrade) + no-ontology degrade + dept/title sort; apply-role own-role / explicit-role-id-resolution / unknown-role-404 / unknown-agent-404 / no-acm-503. `test_ad889_commission_chain.py` +1 (`test_recommission_preserves_manual_restriction` — real `ToolPermissionStore` + `SkillRegistry` + `AgentSkillService`: a manual restriction survives re-commission, scanner NOT re-granted). Regression across acm/commission/capability/tool-cert: 85 passed. Import smoke clean.

The **SERVES** rows stay read-only — a served intent's enablement is governed by the agent's role (the AD-1009 role layer), not a per-agent origination gate, so toggling it here would imply an enforcement that does not exist. `MeshIntent` carries `granted`/`source` from AD-1007; `setCapability`'s `kind` widens to `tool|skill|capability`. **Tests.** `CapabilityPanel.test.tsx` +3 (CAN-REQUEST toggleable / SERVES read-only, optimistic POST `kind=capability`, revert-on-failure); UI suite + `npm run build` clean. ### AD-1007: per-agent mesh-capability gate — disable blocks the agent, agent-precedence over role (Agent Customizations epic #944, #952)

**Context.** The Captain's steer (2026-06-14) on the held capability-enforcement design: *"If I disable a capability it should block the agent. Anything assigned directly to the agent takes precedence over the role — a per-agent disable is not overridden by the role, and a per-agent grant overrides a role disable."* That is **agent-precedence**, not most-restrictive-wins (the two differ when the role disables and the agent grants — the Captain wants ENABLED). AD-1005 shipped the `IntentGrantStore` substrate (mechanism-only, default-OFF); this wires it into enforcement.

**Decision.**
- **Three-state resolver.** `IntentGrantStore.resolve_sync(agent_id, intent) -> "granted" | "restricted" | "no_opinion"`. Unlike the binary `is_granted_sync` (default-deny), it distinguishes "no per-agent decision" (fall through to the role/ship default) from an explicit grant/restriction, so an enforcement caller honors agent-precedence in both directions. Defensive conflict handling: most-recent `issued_at` wins; an exact tie is fail-safe `"restricted"`. The `capabilities/set` endpoint revokes the opposite active decision before issuing a new one, so a pair carries at most one live decision.
- **Store wired.** `IntentGrantStore` is now instantiated at startup (`startup/communication.py`, mirroring `skill_grant_store`), surfaced on `CommunicationResult` + `runtime.intent_grant_store`, and stopped in `shutdown.py`. (Was previously class-only / never instantiated.)
- **Set endpoint.** `SetCapability.kind` widens to `^(tool|skill|capability)$`; `set_agent_capability`'s capability branch validates the id is a reachable mesh intent (404 otherwise), revokes any prior active decision, then issues a grant (enable) or restriction (disable).
- **Enforcement at TWO origination points.** (1) Conversational: `reply_pipeline.step_4h_mesh_read_parse` — after the AD-869 read-only allowlist, a `resolve_sync == "restricted"` blocks the `[MESH …]` request (strip tag + honest note, never dispatched). (2) Agentic loop: `WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run` filters restricted mesh-intent tools out of the tool set offered to the LLM. Both honest-degrade (no store → no gating) and gate only on an explicit `restricted` (grant/no_opinion fall through to the role/ship default = reachable, today).
- **Read surface.** `get_agent_capabilities` tags each mesh intent `granted`/`source` from `resolve_sync` so the AD-1008 toggle renders the right state.
- **Role-default layer deferred (AD-1009, #952).** Capabilities are not yet in `RoleTemplate`; today the role default for a CAN-REQUEST capability is "enabled (reachable)," so the meaningful action is a per-agent disable. The grant-overrides-role-disable direction activates once roles can disable a capability by default. SERVES-capability disabling (the agent is the handler) is a role/duty concern, not an origination gate — also AD-1009.

**Tests.** `test_ad1007_capability_gate.py` (15, BF-287 real `IntentGrantStore` + `DmSanityGate` + `ToolRegistry` + `IntentBus` + real route handlers): resolver three-state + most-recent-wins + tie-fail-safe + per-pair isolation; set-endpoint grant/restrict/revoke-opposite/404/503/unknown-agent; `get_agent_capabilities` state surface; `step_4h` blocks-restricted / allows-unrestricted; agentic-loop filters restricted mesh tool (monkeypatched `AgenticLoop` capturing the tool set). Regression across intent-grants/capability/agentic-dispatch/mesh-catalog/reply-pipeline: 49 passed. Field-wiring smoke clean.

### AD-1006: capability clarity — "serves" vs ship-wide "can request" + tools/capabilities explainer (Agent Customizations epic #944)

**Context.** Captain review of the AD-1000c Profile **Service** tab: every crew card showed an identical **83 capabilities**, **0 tools**, and the Ship's Counselor (Ezri) could not tell tools from capabilities ("83 capabilities but no assigned tools would explain why nothing new feels available"). Root cause: the capability axis is the mesh-intent surface, and `_mesh_intents` unions EVERY registered agent's `intent_descriptors` deduped — it is the ship-wide reachable set, identical for all agents, not the viewed agent's role. The genuinely role-specific fact (only the Counselor *serves* `counselor_wellness_report`) was invisible because the panel never distinguished "what this agent serves" from "what any agent can request."

**Decision (Phase 1 of the per-agent capability work — read-only clarity, no gating change).** `routers/agents.py get_agent_capabilities` now tags each mesh intent with `served: bool` — true when the *viewed* agent declares it (`agent.intent_descriptors`), false for the ship-wide remainder. `CapabilityPanel.tsx` splits the single `CAPABILITIES (n)` block into **CAPABILITIES — SERVES (n)** ("mesh intents only this agent fulfils") and **CAPABILITIES — CAN REQUEST (n)** ("ship-wide surface any agent can request; served by other crew or pools"). The Service-tab intro and the empty-tools state are rewritten to teach the model: **Tools** = callable functions wired into the agent's context (the Copilot sense), **Skills** = cognitive specialties from the role, **Capabilities** = mesh intents the agent can request. A backend without the `served` flag leaves every intent in CAN REQUEST — byte-identical to the pre-AD-1006 single section.

**Scope: presentation only.** No enforcement, no new gate, no dispatch change. The per-agent capability *toggle* (wiring AD-1005 `IntentGrantStore` into live dispatch) and the role-template framework (capabilities in `RoleTemplate`, an apply-role action) are the held Phase 2/3 follow-ons (AD-1007/1008) — they change runtime behavior and await Captain steer on enforcement + precedence. The role→skills→tools template already exists at commission time (AD-889 `ACM.commission()`); AD-1007 exposes + extends it.

**Tests.** `test_ad1006_capability_serves.py` (4, BF-287 real async route handler + real `SimpleNamespace` registry): served-tags-only-this-agent's-intents, served-flag-is-per-viewed-agent, agent-serving-nothing-all-can-request (+ honest-degraded empty tool/skill axes), unknown-agent-404. `CapabilityPanel.test.tsx` +2 (serves/can-request split, no-specialty empty state) and the two obsolete single-section assertions updated; `ProfileServiceTab.test.tsx` intro-copy assertion updated. Backend 17 (with AD-1000a/1001 regression) + UI 24 + `npm run build` clean.

### AD-909: universal mesh read-intents registered into the persistent tool catalog (#872)

**Context.** The three universal mesh read-intents — `web_search`, `read_page`, `http_fetch` — are wrapped as first-class Tools by `register_mesh_intent_tools` (AD-856), but that wrapper ran *only* inside the per-dispatch executor (`WorkItemAgenticExecutor.run`), into a throwaway registry view. The persistent `tool_registry` was seeded at startup *only* from `ontology.get_tool_capabilities()` (ship_computer, ward_room, dreaming_engine, …). Net: the three reads were absent from `GET /api/tools` — the catalog the AD-899 `ToolCertifications` console and the AD-885 unified capability lens read — until an agent first used one. The Captain could not *see* web-search/page-read/http-fetch in the catalog, nor turn one off for a specific agent, even though the AD-423/894 `ToolAccessGrant` (`is_restriction`) model fully supports a per-agent off-switch.

**Decision.** Add `_wire_mesh_intent_tools(runtime)` to `startup/finalize.py`, called from `finalize_startup` right after the AD-706 browser-tool wiring (the analogous “register a Tool into the persistent registry at startup” pattern, where both `runtime.tool_registry` and `runtime.intent_bus` are live). It seeds the three reads into the persistent registry tagged `provider="mesh"` and READ-for-all (empty `default_permissions` → the registry’s Layer-3 ship-wide default grants READ to every rank). `register_mesh_intent_tools` gained a `provider: str = "AD-856"` parameter (also now tagging the registration with `[tool_id, provider]`); the per-dispatch caller keeps the default, the startup path passes `"mesh"`. Registration stays idempotent — whichever path runs first registers, the other skips; in production `finalize_startup` runs before any agentic dispatch, so the `"mesh"` tag wins.

**Off-switch already correct (verification, not a fix).** Acceptance #2 asked to confirm a restriction on a READ-for-all tool actually denies. `resolve_permission` Layer-4 already restricts down: for a tool with empty `default_permissions` the base resolves to READ, and a Captain `is_restriction` grant with permission `none` lowers it to NONE for that agent only — other agents keep the default READ, and the restriction is scoped to the one tool. No model change; the catalog registration is purely additive; no new consensus gate (Minimal Authority — a restriction is a reversible, audit-retained `ToolAccessGrant`). The UI “Restrict” verb (issue an `is_restriction` from the certification tab) is deferred to AD-910.

**Honest-degrade.** `_wire_mesh_intent_tools` returns `[]` and logs a warning when `tool_registry` or `intent_bus` is unavailable; the lazy dispatch-path registration remains the fallback. The `finalize_startup` call site is wrapped in the same try/except-log pattern as the adjacent wirings.

**Tests.** `test_ad909_mesh_intent_catalog.py` (11, BF-287 — real `ToolRegistry` + real `ToolPermissionStore` + real `IntentBus`/`SignalManager`, no MagicMock at the substrate boundary): catalog presence with `provider="mesh"` tag, default-provider preserves the dispatch tag, `list_tools` membership, idempotent re-register, first-registration-wins-provider, READ-for-all default, restriction-denies-one-agent-others-unaffected + restriction-scoped-to-one-tool, and the startup helper (seeds + both honest-degrade paths). Regression across registry/dispatch/permission/AD-706/finalize areas: 577 passed, 1 skipped. Import smoke clean.

### AD-1003a: Capability-Pack manifest parser/validator — cross-tool agent-plugin format (#944, #948)

**Context.** First (safe, additive) slice of Capability Packs (AD-1003 #948): ProbOS adopts the cross-tool agent-plugin `plugin.json` format shared by VS Code / Copilot CLI / Claude Code, so it can consume existing IDE plugins and emit portable packs. The full loader (consuming a pack into the live registries, with the operator trust/consensus gate) needs the hook-bus *wiring* first — so this slice is the **read-only parse + validate** layer only, with zero install/execution.

**Decision.** `src/probos/packs/manifest.py`: `PackManifest` (Pydantic v2 model of the cross-tool schema — name/description/version/author + component paths `skills`/`agents`/`hooks`/`mcpServers`), enforcing the same **kebab-case `name`** rule the IDEs use (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`, ≤ 64; the IDEs *silently* fail invalid names — ProbOS raises loudly at parse time). `find_manifest` checks VS Code's auto-detection order (`.plugin/plugin.json` → `plugin.json` → `.github/plugin/plugin.json` → `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`). `load_manifest` (find+read+validate), `parse_manifest` (dict→model), `describe_pack` (read-only install-preview summary). `extra="allow"` preserves ProbOS-native additive keys (mesh-intent grants, standing-order overlays) so a ProbOS pack stays a valid base plugin in the IDEs.

**Scope: parse + validate ONLY.** Nothing is installed, executed, registered, or wired — no hook runs, no MCP server starts, no skill/agent loads. Purely additive; the safe substrate the later install slice builds on.

**Tests.** `test_ad1003a_pack_manifest.py` (21, BF-287 real files on tmp_path + real Pydantic): minimal/full/inline-objects/extra-preserved manifests, the kebab-case rule (6 invalid + valid + too-long + bad-description + non-dict), `find_manifest` detection order + Claude format + absent, `load_manifest` happy/missing/malformed-JSON, `describe_pack`. Import/AST smoke clean.

### AD-1005: IntentGrantStore — per-agent mesh-intent grant substrate (#944, gating mechanism)

**Context.** The authorization substrate for the settled per-agent write-intent gating design (the AD-1004 discussion): a crew agent that *originates* a consensus-gated WRITE intent (e.g. `run_python`) must be granted that intent — per-agent authorization checked at origination, layered with (never replacing) the per-call consensus gate. Tools have `ToolPermissionStore`, skills have `SkillGrantStore`; intents had no equivalent.

**Decision.** `cognitive/intent_grants.py` `IntentGrantStore` — a near-exact mirror of `SkillGrantStore` (SQLite + WAL + in-memory sync cache + lazy expiry + soft-revoke for audit), keyed by `intent_name`. API: `start`/`stop`, `issue_grant`, `revoke_grant`, `get_active_grants_sync(agent_id, intent_name?)`, `list_grants`, and `is_granted_sync(agent_id, intent_name)` (the read a future `PreDispatch` hook consumes — most-restrictive: a restriction wins over a grant, mirroring the AD-983b skill overlay).

**Mechanism only — default OFF.** NOT wired into any enforcement path (mirrors the AD-1004 hook-bus discipline: build the substrate, wire it in a later slice). An empty store changes nothing — no agent is gated; today's write paths are unchanged (Captain/decomposer → global `execution.enabled` + consensus; agentic-loop tool calls → `ToolPermissionStore`; the `[MESH …]` affordance is read-only). The next slice registers a `PreDispatch` hook that calls `is_granted_sync` + threads the originating agent id.

### AD-1004: lifecycle-hook bus — substrate for the per-agent capability gate + Capability Packs (#944, prereq for #948)

**Context.** Two threads converge on a missing primitive. (1) The per-agent write-intent gating design (settled this session): per-agent **authorization** at *origination* (default-OFF grant), layered with — not replacing — the **consensus** per-call safety gate; the two are orthogonal (exactly VS Code's per-agent tool *enablement* + per-call *approval*). The natural enforcement point is a `PreDispatch` hook with `allow`/`ask`/`deny`. (2) Capability Packs (AD-1003) attach lifecycle hooks (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, …) — VS Code/Claude semantics. ProbOS had triggers (WatchManager / NightOrders / ScheduledTask / consensus gates) but **no unified lifecycle-hook bus** with named events + the deny-overrides-ask precedence. This AD builds that bus.

**Decision.** `src/probos/hooks/bus.py` `HookBus`: named `HookEvent`s (the cross-tool set — `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `SubagentStart`/`Stop`, `Stop` — plus ProbOS's mesh-dispatch points `PreDispatch`/`PostDispatch`). `register(event, handler, *, handler_id)` (sync or async callables), `unregister`, `handler_count`, `async fire(event, context) -> AggregateDecision`. **Gate events** (`PreToolUse`/`PreDispatch`) aggregate verdicts **most-restrictive-wins** (`deny` > `ask` > `allow`, the VS Code precedence); observational events run handlers for side effects and ignore return values. A handler returning `None` abstains. **Tier-2 honest-degrade:** a raising handler is logged and contributes *no* verdict — the bus never bricks the loop, and the independent consensus gate still applies (the bus is neutral plumbing; policy lives in handlers). `HooksConfig(enabled=False)` wired into `SystemConfig` (default OFF).

**Scope discipline — mechanism only.** The bus is **not yet wired into the live dispatch path** (the AD-979b/c mechanism-first / conservative-wiring precedent): firing with no handlers is a no-op, so the bus is inert until the follow-up slice registers the grant + consensus handlers and fires `PreDispatch` from the `IntentBus` / `PreToolUse` from the agentic loop. Command-based (shell) hooks for portable packs are also deferred (this slice is in-process callable handlers). No live behavior change.

**Tests.** `test_ad1004_hook_bus.py` (15): config default-OFF, register/unregister/count, name-derived id, empty-bus-allows, single allow, deny>ask>allow, ask>allow, None-abstain, observational-ignores-deny, async handler, mixed sync/async, raising-handler-skipped (others decide) + only-raiser-defaults-allow, context-passthrough + order-preserved. Config regression (config/hook_bus) **580 passed**; import + AST smoke clean (`hooks.enabled=False`).

### BF-628: workspace root must rebase onto the platform data dir (not the process cwd); execution enabled

**Context.** Enabling code execution surfaced that `WorkspaceManager(Path(root))` resolved the relative default `data/execution/workspaces` against the **process cwd**, not the platform data dir — the exact split-brain `_platform_data_dir()` exists to prevent (its own docstring: "Prevents split-brain where runtime.py defaults to repo-relative `data/` while `__main__.py` uses AppData/XDG"). The running instance keeps all data under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/ProbOS/data`, so the per-agent folders + the Work-tab API would have disagreed (or landed in the repo dir) depending on cwd. Also caught a near-miss: `data/workspaces` (the Captain's first guess) is **already used by the TaskSession subsystem** (AD-815a, `runtime.py:498` per-thread cowork folders) — so code-execution workspaces correctly stay under `data/execution/workspaces`, separate from TaskSessions.

**Decision.** `WorkspaceManager.__init__` now resolves the root via `_resolve_workspace_root`: absolute paths pass through (tests, operator overrides); a **relative** path is rooted under `_platform_data_dir()` with a leading `data/` stripped — mirroring `_resolve_attachments_dir` (AD-720). The platform-dir logic is **inlined** in `execution/workspace.py` (not imported from `probos.runtime`) because importing runtime pulls optional deps (`keyring`) and fails to import without them — a leaf utility must not depend on the heavy runtime module. Net resolved root on Windows: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\ProbOS\data\execution\workspaces\<agent>\`. **Also enabled execution** in `config/system.yaml`: `execution.enabled: true`, `allow_package_install: true`, `persistent_workspaces: true`, `workspace_root: data/execution/workspaces` (per the Captain's go-ahead). Restart required for the runtime to register the `code_runner` template + spawn its pool (both gated on `execution.enabled`, BF-627).

**Tests.** `test_ad997_workspace.py` +2 (`test_relative_root_rebases_onto_platform_data_dir` via `PROBOS_DATA_DIR` override; `test_absolute_root_used_as_is`) — 21 total. Verified live: `WorkspaceManager("data/execution/workspaces").resolve("ezri")` → `C:\Users\seang\AppData\Local\ProbOS\data\execution\workspaces\ezri`. Config loads with `enabled=True`/`allow_package_install=True`. Regression (workspace/code_runner/isolation/section_registry/agent_fleet/config) green.

### AD-997 + AD-998 + AD-999: per-agent working folders for code execution — configurable root, profile-card Work-tab view (#936 epic)

**Context.** After AD-992-996 shipped Tier-1 execution as *ephemeral per-task scratch* (a fresh dir reaped after each run), the Captain asked four follow-ups: should crew share one working dir or each get their own; how is the root set; it should be configurable from the HXI; and the folder should be viewable from the profile card's Work tab. Viewing implies **persistence** (an ephemeral dir is empty between runs), and per-crew-member folders imply keying by the *owning* agent. Architecture constraint surfaced during design: `IntentMessage` has **no requester field** (only `target_agent_id` / `thread_id`), and `CodeRunnerAgent` is a single core tool agent — so "per-crew folder" must be carried as an explicit owner in `params`, defaulting to the executor's own key (forward-compatible with future crew-delegation tagging).

**Decision (per-agent persistent, recommended model).** **AD-997 (backend)** — `execution/workspace.py` `WorkspaceManager`: single source of truth for "where does agent *X* work". Keyed by an owner string; `sanitize` (→ `[a-z0-9_-]`, traversal-safe, `"shared"` fallback), `key_for_agent` (callsign → type → id), `resolve(owner, create=)`, `venv_dir`, `list_files` (deterministic, bounded, treats `.venv`/`__pycache__`/`.git` as one opaque entry — never recurses the venv's thousands of files), `total_bytes`; Tier-2 honest-degrade (never raises). `ExecutionConfig` gains `persistent_workspaces: bool = True` + `workspace_root: str = "data/execution/workspaces"`. `CodeRunnerAgent` resolves owner = `params["workspace_owner"]` (a delegating crew agent's key) else its own key; persistent → the owner's stable folder under the root (work products + venv survive + are visible), passed as `workdir` (the sandbox does not reap an explicit workdir); the venv is **reused** across runs (`<ws>/.venv`, idempotent pip — no re-download every run). `persistent_workspaces=False` keeps the original ephemeral-reaped behavior. Result data carries `workspace`/`owner`/`persistent`. **AD-998 (API)** — `GET /api/agent/{id}/workspace` resolves the folder by the SAME `key_for_agent`, returning `{enabled, persistent, root, path, owner, exists, files[], total_bytes}`; honest-degrades to `enabled:false` / `persistent:false` / empty list. Read-only. **AD-999 (HXI)** — a Core "Code Execution" section in `settings/section_registry.py` (`execution.enabled` / `workspace_root` / `persistent_workspaces` / `allow_package_install` / `timeout_seconds` / `max_memory_mb` — the configurable root the Captain asked for) + `ui/.../profile/WorkspaceFolder.tsx` (read-only, deps-injectable, HXI stroke-no-emoji) mounted in `ProfileWorkTab`, showing the path + file list (or "disabled" / "ephemeral" / "no files yet").

**Default-OFF preserved.** Execution stays off until the operator flips `execution.enabled` (now possible from HXI Settings); nothing enabled in `config/system.yaml`. The per-agent folder is *organizational attribution* + confinement-by-convention, not a kernel boundary (Tier 1 caveat unchanged).

**Tests.** `test_ad997_workspace.py` (19: sanitize/keying/traversal-guard, list_files entries + venv-opacity + bound, persistent persists + owner routing + two-owner isolation + venv reuse, ephemeral reaps) + `test_ad998_workspace_api.py` (6: lists files, empty, disabled, ephemeral, callsign-keyed, 404) + `test_ad741_section_registry.py` (5, field ids resolve) + `WorkspaceFolder.test.tsx` (9, deps-injected, no-emoji guard). UI: 188 profile tests + build clean. Backend regression (workspace/code_runner/isolation/section_registry/ad983b/runtime/agent_fleet/config) green.

### BF-627: code execution must not be advertised to the planner when disabled; run_python is not a read-only affordance

**Context.** While answering the Captain's "how do the agents know they can run Python?" question, two defects surfaced in the AD-994 code shipped earlier today (1fbedde9). (1) `runtime.py` registered the `code_runner` template **unconditionally**, but `_collect_intent_descriptors()` walks `spawner._templates` to build the decomposer's planning prompt — so the planner advertised `run_python`/`install_package` even when `execution.enabled=False`, i.e. it would route a task to a capability with **no pool to serve it** (violates AD-592: never offer what the ship cannot back; the `agent_fleet` pool is correctly gated, but the template registration was not). (2) `run_python` carried a `usage_hint`, which surfaces a capability in the AD-983a `_conversational_capability_block` — the read-only "[MESH …] — these reads change nothing" do-and-report affordance. `run_python` is a **consensus WRITE**, so it must not appear there.

**Decision.** (1) Gate `register_template("code_runner", …)` on `config.execution.enabled` (mirrors the `agent_fleet` pool gate) — when disabled, the planner never sees the intent; when enabled, both template and pool appear together. (2) Remove the `usage_hint` from the `run_python` descriptor (keep `requires_consensus=True`); the planner still learns it from `description` and routes it through the plan → consensus path, just not via the read-only affordance block.

**Tests.** AD-993/994 unchanged (25 passed / 1 skipped — agents construct directly, unaffected by registration gating). Regression blast (code_runner/isolation/runtime/decomposer/agent_fleet/fleet_organization/collect_intent/capability/ad983a) **825 passed / 7 skipped** (BF-326 MagicMock-dir noise only). Disabled (default) → `run_python` invisible to planner + affordance block; enabled → planner sees it as a consensus intent, never as a free read.

### AD-992 + AD-993 + AD-994 (+ AD-995/996 stubs): governed code execution — tiered isolation for safe Python (Copilot/Claude Code parity) (#936 epic ← #937/#938/#939/#940)

**Context.** The Captain asked for the capability GitHub Copilot and Claude Code have — **create and run Python scripts, installing libraries as needed to perform tasks** — and named the isolation reference points (Copilot's working folder, Cowork's containers, Microsoft MXC). ProbOS had **no general-purpose Python execution path**: it treats capability evolution as a *design* problem (`self_mod` designs persistent agents through `agent_designer` → `CodeValidator` static analysis → `SandboxRunner` importlib test → Beta(1,3) probationary trust → register), not a *runtime-execution* problem. `CodeValidator.forbidden_patterns` deliberately bans `subprocess`/`eval`/`exec`/`compile`/`__import__`/`os.system` for designed-agent code; `ShellCommandAgent` runs **shell**, not Python, and validates `argv[0]` on PATH. So **ephemeral one-off computation had no home** — an agent either abstained or over-built a persistent agent. (Adjacent finding: `cognitive/sandbox.py SandboxRunner` loads designed-agent code **in-process** via `importlib` — a test harness, not a security sandbox; the AD-993 substrate is what hardens that later, tracked separately.)

**Decision — *governed ephemeral execution*, not an ungoverned scratchpad.** Copilot/Claude Code give the right *ergonomics* (working folder + real interpreter) but the wrong *governance* for an agent-native OS where the code author may be an autonomous agent. ProbOS adds four controls: **consensus-gated** (quorum-authorized like `run_command`), **episodically logged** (the run is evidence in the learning loop), **default-OFF** (highest-risk capability is inert until opt-in), and **tier-isolated** (sandbox strength is a config dial behind one backend protocol). **Tiered model:** Tier 1 = subprocess/working-folder (process isolation + confinement-by-convention, NOT kernel containment); Tier 2 = OS-native kernel-enforced (bubblewrap/Seatbelt/AppContainer/MXC); Tier 3 = container/microVM (full isolation + reproducibility + multi-tenant). All tiers implement one `IsolationBackend` protocol; `config.execution.default_tier` selects the backend; **escalation can skip Tier 2 → Tier 3 directly** (independent backends, not a ladder).

**Built today (Tier 1).** **AD-993** — `src/probos/execution/isolation.py`: `IsolationTier(IntEnum)`, `ExecutionRequest`/`ExecutionResult` dataclasses, `IsolationBackend(Protocol)` (`tier`, `available()`, `async run()`), and `SubprocessSandbox` — ephemeral per-task scratch folder (uuid, reaped in `finally`), `subprocess.Popen` in `run_in_executor` (mirrors `ShellCommandAgent`; Windows `SelectorEventLoop` can't host `create_subprocess_exec`), **arg-list never `shell=True`** (no injection), code path `[python,"-I","-B",script]`, scrubbed env + blackhole-proxy when `allow_network=False` (soft deterrent — true network cut is a Tier-2 guarantee), POSIX `preexec_fn` RLIMIT_AS/CPU/FSIZE + process-group kill / Windows `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP`, output capped, **honest-degrade (never raises)**. Module docstring states in-band that Tier 1 is *process isolation + bounds + confinement-by-convention governed by consensus, NOT kernel containment*. **AD-994** — `agents/code_runner.py` `CodeRunnerAgent` (core tier), two **consensus-gated** intents: `run_python(code, packages?, timeout?)` (script in isolated folder; with `packages`, a throwaway per-task venv is created + libs installed first, then the script runs in it; scratch reaped after) and `install_package(packages)` (availability probe into a throwaway venv). `ExecutionConfig` (config.py, **default OFF**: `enabled=False`, `default_tier=1`, `allow_package_install=False`, scratch/timeout/output/memory/pip caps) wired into `SystemConfig`. Wiring: `runtime.register_template` + **gated pool** in `agent_fleet` (spawned only when `execution.enabled`, with `runtime` kwarg) + `fleet_organization` core membership; **NOT** in `_MESH_READ_INTENT_POOLS` (consensus/WRITE, not read). Defense in depth: pool-not-spawned-unless-enabled + agent refuses at `decide()` + separate install gate + `_clean_packages` drops `-`-prefixed tokens (no pip-flag injection) + timeout clamp ≤300s. **Not enabled in `config/system.yaml`** — left inert for the operator to flip after review.

**Stubbed (design only).** **AD-995** — Tier-2 OS-native sandbox, *waiting for MXC to mature*: MXC is MIT, cross-platform Rust binaries + TS SDK (no Python SDK), **0.7.0-alpha**, README says *"no MXC profiles should be treated as security boundaries currently."* Disposition: track as a forward-marker backend, absorb the pluggable-backend *pattern* (AD-993 already does), **never link the SDK** (shell to the binary BYO-style if ever used). **AD-996** — Tier-3 container/microVM, deferred. **Answers "once we have Tier 2 do we need Tier 3?":** for the stated goal on the single-operator/own-machine default, **Tier 2 suffices**; Tier 3 only earns its place under a stronger threat model (hostile/untrusted code, **multi-tenant**) or reproducible/persistent environments — both **hosted/commercial** concerns. So Tier 3 is desirable-not-required for the OSS goal, and buildable directly after Tier 1 (skipping Tier 2) if a hosted use case lands first.

**Tests.** `test_ad993_isolation.py` (16: protocol conformance, stdout/argv/exit/stderr, timeout-kills, output-capped, bad-exe + no-input degrade, internal-scratch reaped, explicit-workdir preserved, POSIX memory-limit skipif-win32) + `test_ad994_code_runner.py` (14, BF-287 real `ExecutionConfig` boundary: disabled-gate both intents, no-runtime degrade, run_python happy/nonzero/empty/timeout, packages-blocked-when-install-off, install no-packages, **real offline venv+pip honest-degrade**, `_clean_packages` flag-strip, timeout clamp, venv path). New tests **30 passed / 1 skipped**. Regression blast (code_runner/isolation/agent_fleet/fleet_organization/shell_command/self_mod/capability/decomposer/prompt_builder) **601 passed / 8 skipped**.
