### AD-989 + AD-990 + AD-991: ripgrep-absorption wave — lexical content grep for the mesh (#933, #934, #935)

**Context.** The Captain observed that Claude Code (and Cursor/Aider) navigate a codebase with **lexical project search (ripgrep)** rather than vector/RAG retrieval, and asked what ProbOS could absorb. Code is an *exact-token* domain — grep beats embeddings for it (exact, always-fresh, self-explaining: the match `path:line:text` *is* the evidence, which directly serves the AD-988 retrieval-transparency thread). ProbOS had been drifting lexical already (AD-979c hybrid FTS5, BF-625 BM25 ranking) but had **no content-grep capability in the mesh at all**: `FileSearchAgent` did filename-glob only (raw `rglob`, descending `.venv`/`node_modules`); `CodebaseIndex` does AST + word-scoring (ranked files, not line matches); `dm_targeted_lookup` even *detects* "grep the codebase" but routed it to the word-scorer because no grep existed. **License/disposition (surfaced per standing rule):** ripgrep is dual MIT/Unlicense — pattern-absorbed, never vendored (it is Rust). Zero new hard deps (`pathspec`/`re2` not installed → pure Python; `re2` a forward marker); `rg` is an *optional* operator binary resolved like Piper/Rhubarb under gitignored `/tools/`.

**Decision (three ADs, leaf→headline; all read-only, no consensus).** **AD-991 (#935, security leaf)** — `substrate/safe_regex.py`: `safe_compile(pattern, *, flags, max_len=1000)` rejects over-length patterns + known catastrophic-backtracking signatures (nested quantifiers on a group, `(a+)+` / `(a*)*` / `{n,}` forms) before compiling, re-raising invalid `re.error` as `UnsafePatternError`. Absorbs ripgrep's linear-time *guarantee intent* as a boundary guard (Python `re` is a backtracking engine → an agent/Captain-supplied pattern is a latent ReDoS/DoS vector); documented as defense-in-depth, not a proof. **AD-990 (#934, traversal leaf)** — `substrate/file_walk.py`: `IgnoreSpec` (faithful common-subset gitignore: comments, `!` negation, trailing-`/` dir-only, leading-`/` anchor, `*`/`?`/`**` via `fnmatch.translate`, last-match-wins), `DEFAULT_IGNORE_DIRS` backstop, `is_binary` NUL-sniff, and `iter_files(root, …)` (os.walk with in-place dir pruning, hidden/binary skip, `max_files` bound, deterministic, Tier-2). `FileSearchAgent` gains `include_ignored: bool=False` and walks ignore-aware by default (fixes the `.venv` bug — a strictly-better behavior change; the raw `rglob` is the escape hatch). **AD-989 (#933, headline)** — `agents/code_search.py` `CodeSearchAgent`: core-tier read-only `search_content` intent returning `{path, line, text}`. Engine selection mirrors the AD-738 BYO-binary pattern — **prefer `rg`** (`shutil.which` / `tools/rg`, run via `create_subprocess_exec`, no shell → no injection, bounded by timeout + `--max-count`); **fall back to a bounded pure-Python scan** over the AD-990 walk with every pattern through the AD-991 guard (per-line cap, `max_results`). Wired into the pool topology (`runtime` register_template + `agent_fleet` builtin pool + `fleet_organization` membership) and the `_MESH_READ_INTENT_POOLS` allowlist (so the `[MESH search_content]` AD-983a affordance surfaces crew-wide).

**Tests.** `test_ad991_safe_regex.py` (16), `test_ad990_file_walk.py` (13, BF-287 real tmp tree + FileSearchAgent), `test_ad989_code_search.py` (13, BF-287 real tree + agent; Python engine forced deterministic via `which→None`). The AD-869 allowlist test updated (obsolete-contract: `search_content` is the 7th read-only intent). Wiring blast (fleet/reply_pipeline/mesh_read/ad983a/ad870/ad869) **97 passed**; descriptor-consuming blast (capability/decomposer/prompt_builder/ad983/ad152) **474 passed / 6 skipped**; import + AST smoke clean. PUSHED. Commercial research note: `lexical-first-retrieval-2026-06-13.md` (the "route retrieval by domain — grep for code, semantics for autobiographical recall, hybrid RRF as the bridge" stance). Forward markers: `re2`/`pathspec` for true linear-time + full gitignore; a `[MESH search_content]` Architect/Builder wiring.

### AD-986a + AD-987: group-memory enrichment — speaker attribution + reflection fidelity + visual↔conversational binding (#929, #931; the AD-986 dual-layer conversational-memory epic)

**Context.** The Counselor's live recall feedback (2026-06-13, post-AD-986b validation) surfaced two code-grounded gaps, both at the AD-933a group-episode write (`thread_fanout.py`). (1) **Attribution + fidelity (AD-986a / #929):** the round-0 Captain trigger was stored unlabeled (`"[group chat] <text>"`) and the agent's own reply was capped at 240 chars — so "who said what" was weak on recall and a substantive multi-paragraph contribution's payload was never indexed. The `AnchorFrame.trigger_agent` SOCIAL slot existed (`types.py:391`) but was never set. (2) **The binding problem (AD-987 / #931):** the conversation episode and the frame the agent *saw* are two disconnected streams — the `Episode` has no visual field; the frame lives in a TTL-reaped `VisionWorkingMemory` ring — so recall yields "what was said" and "what I saw" separately ("takes a little more reconstruction"). Both verified against the live code before building.

**Decision (default-OFF; byte-identical until enabled).** **AD-986a** — `MemoryConfig.group_episode_enrichment_enabled` (False) + `group_reflection_max_chars` (600). `_fan_one_round` gains a `trigger_speaker` param (round 0 = `"Captain"`; cascade rounds = `""`, their triggers already carry per-line `callsign:` labels). When enrichment is on: prefix the round-0 trigger (`"[group chat] Captain: …"`), set `AnchorFrame.trigger_agent`, and index up to `group_reflection_max_chars` of the agent's own reply. **AD-987** — `MemoryConfig.episode_visual_binding_enabled` (False); two new `AnchorFrame` EVIDENTIAL fields `visual_attachment_ref` + `visual_description` (serialize automatically via the `asdict`→`AnchorFrame(**…)` path, `episodic.py:2934`/`:767`, backward-compatible). When binding is on, the group-episode write reads the replying agent's current `get_or_create_working_memory(agent_id).latest()` and binds the frame's content-addressable `attachment_ref` + description into the episode's anchors (Tier-2 — a binding failure never blocks the write; the ref survives the ring's TTL reap because `AttachmentStore` is durable). `_prepare_document` appends `[saw: …]` when a visual description is present, so "what was I seeing when X" becomes recall-searchable — tying the two streams at the embedding level (the integrated recall the Counselor asked for). Both ADs edit the SAME write site and the SAME frozen `AnchorFrame` (all fields passed in the constructor), so they ship together. The eviction-weighted-retention half of #929 is **deferred** (it touches the retention substrate — design-gated, watch-then-calibrate).

**Tests.** `test_ad986a_987_group_memory_enrichment.py` (11, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore` + real `IntentBus` + real `VisionWorkingMemory` rings + a hand-written recording `store` stub — no MagicMock): config defaults-off; the **disabled→byte-identical** guard (unprefixed input, `[:240]` reflection, empty `trigger_agent`/`visual_*`); enrichment labels the Captain + sets `trigger_agent`; the raised cap indexes the payload past char 240; visual binding captures the ring's current frame; honest-degrade on an empty ring; binding-off ignores a present frame; `_prepare_document` indexes/omits `[saw: …]`; and the `AnchorFrame` asdict round-trip + pre-AD-987 back-compat hydrate. Fan-out regression (AD-914/915/935/977 + the new file) **65 passed**; episodic/anchor regression (AD-584d/605/598/567a/567c + new) **108 passed** (pre-existing importlib_metadata noise only). **Operational:** enabled both flags in `config/system.yaml`. PUSHED. Forward markers: AD-988 (#932, retrieval-reason transparency — the same compute-then-discard seam as AD-979a/BF-625); the deferred eviction-retention half of #929.

### BF-626: avatar-telemetry WebSocket close crashed on a boot-window peer-disconnect race ('transfer_data_task')

**Context.** The Captain saw repeated `ERROR: Exception in ASGI application` in the ProbOS log, with `AttributeError: 'WebSocketProtocol' object has no attribute 'transfer_data_task'` raised from `agents.py:1668` — `await websocket.close(code=1008, reason="no_crew_agents")` inside `fleet_avatar_telemetry_stream`. The fleet/per-agent telemetry handlers `accept()` then `close()` on a gate; the `no_crew_agents` gate fires during the **boot window** (the HXI opens the telemetry socket before crew agents finish registering, then reconnects). When the peer has already vanished, the `websockets` legacy protocol's `close()` awaits a `transfer_data_task` that was never created → unhandled ASGI exception in the log. Functionally harmless (the connection is going away), but noisy and alarming. Both telemetry handlers had the same pattern across 10 close sites (feature gates, runtime-unavailable, max-connections, no-crew).

**Decision.** Add a module-level `_safe_ws_close(websocket, *, code, reason)` helper in `routers/agents.py` that wraps `websocket.close()` in `try/except Exception`, logging at **debug** (Tier-2 honest-degrade) — a failed close has no functional impact because the socket is being torn down regardless. Route **all 10** close calls in both `agent_avatar_telemetry_stream` and `fleet_avatar_telemetry_stream` through it. No behavior change on the happy path (the close still carries the same code/reason); the only difference is that a close-time race is logged-and-ignored instead of surfacing as `Exception in ASGI application`. Scope kept tight: the one other raw close (`auth.py:90` `verify_ws_token`) is **pre-accept** (uvicorn rejects with HTTP 403, not the `transfer_data_task` path) and behind the default-off `auth.crew_scope_token`, so it is left as-is (noted, lower-risk sibling).

**Tests.** New `test_bf626_ws_safe_close.py` (4): the headline reproduction — a fake WebSocket whose `close()` raises the exact `transfer_data_task` `AttributeError` must be swallowed by `_safe_ws_close` (not re-raised) while still recording the intended `(code, reason)`; a `RuntimeError` close (already-closed socket) likewise swallowed; the happy path forwards `(code, reason)`; and a source guard asserting neither handler calls `websocket.close(` directly (all closes go through `_safe_ws_close`). The 7 existing AD-722b-4 fleet-telemetry tests pass unchanged (11 together). PUSHED.

### BF-625: transcript-grounded recall picked the wrong room — a long catch-all 1:1 outranked the named group chat (the AD-986 dual-layer conversational-memory epic)

**Context.** The Captain enabled AD-986b and live-tested it: in a 1:1 he asked the Counselor *"Do you remember the group chat with Yeo? What visual issue did he have?"* and she honestly reported no memory. Read-only forensics against the live `chat_threads.db` (copied to a temp dir; the running instance untouched) found the sovereign gate was fine — `threads_for_participant` returned all 8 of Ezri's rooms — but `consult_transcript` selected the **wrong room**: her 114-message default 1:1 thread (*"Hello Ezri"*, where Yeo/visual topics are mentioned in passing across many sessions) scored **386** while the actual *"Ezri, Yeo"* group room scored only **74**. Cause: the v1 scorer summed raw query-token overlap across *every* message, so a long room won on sheer volume of common words (*the/you/have/with/what*) — and even contained the rare content tokens at least once. A restart alone would have injected the wrong transcript.

**Decision.** Replace the raw-sum scorer in `consult_transcript` with a small, standard IR ranking: **IDF-weighted BM25 body relevance + a strongly-weighted title field.** (1) **IDF** (BM25-smoothed, computed over the candidate room set) makes ubiquitous words self-neutralise without a hand-picked stop-list — a token in every room scores ≈0; a rare one dominates. (2) **BM25** body scoring (`k1=1.5`, `b=0.75`) adds term-frequency saturation + length normalisation, so a long catch-all cannot win on volume. (3) A **title field** (`_TITLE_FIELD_WEIGHT=12.0` × IDF of query∩title tokens): for a group room the title *is* the participant callsign list (AD-942), so a query that names a participant/topic (*"the chat with Yeo"*) matches the room's identity — the strongest "which conversation" signal. The excerpt is then centred on the **content tokens** that won the room (not stopwords), with a fallback to all query tokens on a title-only match. Verified end-to-end against the live data (via the production `consult_transcript`): the Yeo query now returns an *"Ezri, Yeo"* room with Yeo saying *"I don't have the visual feed… the frame is stale"*; *"divergence event with Scout"* returns the Divergence room; both previously lost to the catch-all.

**Tests.** New `test_bf625_transcript_ranking.py` (5, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore`): the headline regression (a 61-message catch-all must not outrank a 4-message named group room — asserts the excerpt is `Room: Ezri, Yeo`); a guard that the catch-all genuinely has higher *raw* overlap (so the old scorer would have failed) yet the new ranking still picks the group room; title-names-participant breaks a body tie; IDF neutralises ubiquitous words (a rare content token carries its room over a 20-message common-word room); no-content-match → `None`. The 14 AD-986b + 21 AD-986d tests pass unchanged; transcript/AD-986/grounding blast **110 passed**. PUSHED.

### AD-986d: transcript lifecycle — retention purge + tombstones + recording-purged indication (#930; the AD-986 dual-layer conversational-memory epic)

**Context.** AD-986b gave a crew agent the ability to consult the canonical chat transcript (the recording) for rooms it took part in. But the recording is currently immortal — `ChatThreadStore` has only `archived` (a soft hide) and a manual `delete_thread`; nothing purges stale transcripts on a schedule, so the recording would persist forever. The Captain flagged the gap: recordings should not persist indefinitely, and — the subtle part — an agent could still hold a *subjective* memory of a group chat whose recording has since been purged, so it must be *told* the recording is gone rather than silently treating its lossy recollection as the complete, verifiable picture. There is a real tension here (the recording is ground truth and the contagion firewall for the AD-979 frontier), so retention is opt-in and conservative by construction.

**Decision (four parts; mechanism + conservative wiring, default-off).** (1) **Config** — `MemoryConfig.transcript_retention_days` (default **0 = never purge**, opt-in) + `transcript_reaper_interval_seconds` (default 3600). (2) **Tombstone substrate** — new `chat_thread_tombstones` table (id, title, participants JSON, last_active_at, purged_at) + `ChatThreadTombstone` dataclass + `_row_to_tombstone`. Store methods: `purge_thread(id)` (tombstone-FIRST, then hard-delete messages + thread row — a crash mid-purge never deletes without a trace), `purge_threads_older_than(cutoff_ts, *, exclude_pinned=True)` (the reaper workhorse; **pinned exempt**, archived eligible), `tombstones_for_participant(agent_ids, limit)` (sovereign-scoped, mirrors AD-986b's `threads_for_participant`). **Manual `delete_thread` deliberately does NOT tombstone** — a Captain removal is intentional, not a retention purge. (3) **Purge indication** (`cognitive/transcript_grounding.py`) — `purged_room_notice(store, agent_ids, query)` is the complement of `consult_transcript`: when no live recording matches but a *purged* room the agent took part in lexically matches the query (by title — the bodies are gone by definition), it returns an honest notice ("the recording of \"<room>\" was purged on <date> (UTC) … you may still hold your own memory of it, but the recording can no longer be consulted"); `render_purge_indication` labels it `=== RECORDING PURGED (retention) ===`, distinct from both subjective memory and a live transcript. Wired into `_recall_relevant_memories` (as the `else` branch when `consult_transcript` returns nothing → `observation["_transcript_purged"]`) + `_build_user_message`. (4) **`TranscriptReaper`** (`threads/transcript_reaper.py`) — the AD-733-1/AD-706b reaper shape (`start()`/`stop()`/`sweep_once()`, idempotent, Tier-2 honest-degrade); `start()` is a **no-op when retention ≤ 0** so the loop never runs by default; the synchronous store purge runs in the default executor so the event loop is not blocked. Started from `startup/finalize.py._start_transcript_reaper` (gated on `transcript_retention_days > 0`), stopped in `startup/shutdown.py`.

**Conservative by construction.** Default 0 → the reaper is never started, no thread is ever purged, the transcript store + recall prompts are byte-identical to AD-986b. Sovereign scope is preserved end-to-end — a purge notice is only ever surfaced to a participant of the purged room (the headline leak guard, mirroring AD-986b). The recording stays the ground-truth/contagion-firewall layer; retention is the Captain's explicit opt-in with pinned rooms always exempt.

**Tests.** `test_ad986d_transcript_retention.py` (21, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path` with an injected clock — no MagicMock): config default-off; `purge_thread` deletes + tombstones (and the tombstone carries title/participants/timestamps); `delete_thread` leaves NO tombstone; `purge_threads_older_than` purges stale-not-fresh, **exempts pinned**, includes archived, empty when none stale; `tombstones_for_participant` sovereign scope + empty-ids; `purged_room_notice` matches by title, **sovereign-scope leak guard** (a non-participant NEVER gets the notice even on a perfect query), no-match/empty/live-room → `None`; `render_purge_indication` block; and the `TranscriptReaper` — `sweep_once` purges stale + tombstones, disabled when retention 0, `start()` no-op when 0, start/stop lifecycle idempotent, and honest-degrade on a raising store (returns 0, never raises). Regression blast over transcript/thread/reaper/retention/tombstone/fan-out **430 passed**; cognitive_agent `_build_user_message`/recall + the AD-986b sibling **21 passed** (the BF-326 MagicMock-dir warning attributed to a reaper test under `-n auto` is an xdist teardown-attribution artifact — the file is clean in isolation with zero stray dirs, confirmed). PUSHED. Forward markers unchanged: AD-986a (subjective-layer hardening), AD-986c (conscious `[MESH recall_transcript]` affordance), AD-981b (FoK-band-gated consult — the research's ideal trigger, so the recording is consulted only when subjective recall is weak).

### BF-624: shared-meeting vision refreshes a STALE ring (not just an empty one) — the "Yeo saw a 22h-old shirt, Ezri saw live" report (#882)

**Context.** The Captain ran a live group chat (to seed a recallable memory) and the crew surfaced a vision asymmetry: the Counselor (vision-capable observer) described the LIVE frame (plaid shirt) while the Yeoman (NOT vision-capable) described a 22-hour-old frame (black shirt, teapot) for the *entire* conversation. The crew diagnosed it precisely — "the camera channel routes to Ezri's context, not mine; consistent absence, a routing miss." Root cause: `_render_agent_scene_block` (thread_fanout.py) shared the consumer's latest observation into a participant's ring ONLY when that ring was **empty** (the BF-617/BF-620 fallback, `if not _wm.entries()`). The Yeoman's ring was NOT empty — it held a stale disk-hydrated frame (AD-742f) — so the fallback never fired and he never refreshed, while `force_describe_current_frame` only writes to vision-capable **observers'** rings (the Counselor's), never his.

**Decision.** Generalize the fallback from *empty-ring* to *stale-ring*: share the consumer's `latest_shared_observation()` into the agent's ring whenever it is **fresher** than the ring's own latest (`_own is None or _shared.timestamp > _own.timestamp`). This covers both the empty case (BF-617/BF-620) and the stale case (BF-624). Byte-identical for an up-to-date observer — the shared obs is not newer than its own latest, so nothing is appended; and an agent whose own ring is somehow fresher keeps it (never replace a newer frame with an older shared one). Still meeting-scoped (this render path only), still no `register_observer` (no ambient cost). `VisionObservation` is a frozen dataclass with a `.timestamp`, so the comparison is a pure read.

**Tests.** `test_bf624_stale_meeting_vision_refresh.py` (6, BF-287 real `VisionConsumer` + real `VisionWorkingMemory` rings, the canonical BF-620 fixture): the headline stale-ring refresh (22h-old black shirt → live plaid shirt); empty-ring still refreshed (BF-617/BF-620 preserved); an up-to-date observer ring is NOT downgraded/duplicated (byte-identical, no append); an agent with a fresher own frame keeps it; no-shared-obs leaves the BF-294 sentinel; perception-disabled → `""`. BF-617 + BF-620 + AD-978 vision regression green together (30 passed).

**Operational config (this session, not new code).** Set `temporal.captain_timezone: America/Denver` in `config/system.yaml` — the AD-984d feature shipped correctly but the config value was empty (`""`), so the crew only saw UTC and honestly degraded to "we're estimating" (the Captain's "added a feature… why it wasn't getting picked up"). Also enabled `memory.transcript_grounded_recall_enabled: true` so the Captain's upcoming 1:1 recall test exercises AD-986b. Both require a restart to take effect.

### AD-986b: transcript-grounded recall — consult the canonical record (the recording) (#928; the AD-986 dual-layer conversational-memory epic)

**Context.** A live recall-calibration session (AD-981a FoK logging on) had the Counselor honestly report she could not recall a *group chat* she had in fact participated in and contributed substantively to. An offline read-only query of the live episodic store resolved the cause and ruled out the obvious hypotheses: group chats **do** create memories (30 `group_chat_fanout` episodes, AD-933a; 28/30 carrying the AD-977 reflection), and attribution is **correct** (episodes sharded to the replier; the owner-id matches the agent's 1:1 owner-id). The real cause is that the agent's *substantive contribution* survived only as the **trigger text of the next speaker's episode** (owned by that speaker) plus that speaker's dream-reflection — her own recallable shard held only greetings, the substance lost to **reflection truncation** (240-char cap) compounded by **recency-weighted eviction** (she dropped 393→372 episodes during the session). The honesty stack worked perfectly (AD-592/AD-567/AD-541b). This is not an honesty bug and not a wrong-shard bug: the sovereign shard is a *subjective, lossy* recollection **by design**, and the missing piece is an **objective record layer** — the canonical transcript an agent can consult to ground a recollection (the Captain's framing: "if it was recorded they can review it to validate they have the complete picture").

**Prior art (architecture only; full absorption analysis in the commercial research doc).** Transactive memory (Wegner 1985): group memory = per-individual stores + metamemory of who-knows-what + retrieval against **external recordings**. Distributed cognition (Hutchins 1995, *Cognition in the Wild* — the ship-navigation example): cognition spans **internal** (minds) + **external** (artifacts/record) representations. Collaborative-memory / memory-contagion literature: the objective record is the contagion firewall — which de-risks the AD-979d/e frontier (ground against the recording, never silently against a peer's reconstruction). ProbOS already ships both stores (sovereign shards + `ChatThreadStore` transcript); the gap was the coupling. No major agent-memory system (Generative Agents, A-MEM, Mem0, MemGPT, debate frameworks) pairs per-participant *subjective* shards with a consultable *objective* transcript — white space.

**Decision.** New **`ChatThreadStore.threads_for_participant(agent_ids, *, limit=8)`** — non-archived rooms where any of the agent's own ids is a participant, recent-first (sovereign scope: an agent may only consult rooms it took part in). New pure module **`cognitive/transcript_grounding.py`**: `consult_transcript(store, agent_ids, query, *, max_threads, max_chars)` finds the agent's participated rooms, scores them by deterministic AD-979c lexical token overlap (`fts_or_query` — no embedding on the recall hot path), and returns a bounded excerpt of the best-matching room centred on the matching lines (±1 neighbour), or `None` when nothing meaningfully matches (sparse injection); `render_transcript_grounding(excerpt)` renders it under a **`=== CANONICAL TRANSCRIPT (the recording) ===`** header that explicitly tells the agent this is the recording, NOT its memory — so it grounds/quotes rather than conflates. Wired into `CognitiveAgent._recall_relevant_memories` (builds `observation["_transcript_grounding"]` for `direct_message`, Tier-2, after the sovereign recall) + `_build_user_message` (renders the labeled block right after the subjective `recent_memories` section). New `MemoryConfig.transcript_grounded_recall_enabled: bool = False` (+ `transcript_grounding_max_threads=8`, `transcript_grounding_max_chars=1200`) — default off → byte-identical recall (no transcript injected).

**Sovereign scope is load-bearing.** An agent must NEVER receive a transcript for a room it was not in; `threads_for_participant` filters on `agent_id ∈ participants` and `consult_transcript` re-checks the intersection per room. The headline test asserts a perfectly query-matching room the agent is NOT a participant in returns `None`.

**Tests.** `test_ad986b_transcript_grounding.py` (14, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore` on tmp_path): config defaults off; `threads_for_participant` owned-only + empty-ids + limit; `consult_transcript` returns the excerpt for an owned matching room (callsign-labeled); the **sovereign-scope leak guard** (unowned matching room → `None`); no-lexical-match → `None`; empty query/ids → `None`; best-room selection; `max_chars` bound; multi-id robustness; the render label + `_speaker` + `_tokens` pure helpers. Regression blast over threads/recall/cognitive_agent/config/episodic **1633 passed / 1 skipped** (pre-existing importlib_metadata noise only). PUSHED. Next: AD-986a (subjective-layer hardening — reflection fidelity + importance-weighted eviction); forward marker AD-986c (promote grounding to a conscious AD-983a `[MESH recall_transcript]` affordance).

### AD-985 + BF-623: hands-free voice wave — group-meeting open-mic + 1:1 conversation-mode gate fix (#925, #924)

**Context.** The Captain live-tested "Conversation mode" and hit two faults. (1) **BF-623**: selecting Conversation mode in a 1:1 DM still required a manual mic press each turn — the `ConversationController` (AD-747) silently disarmed because its arm effect was gated on the global Ship's-Computer `voiceEnabled` flag (default OFF, AD-945), the same mis-gating class as BF-614/AD-949. (2) **AD-985**: in a *group meeting* there was no continuous-listen path at all — the controller is a 1:1 duplex that POSTs to `/api/agent/{id}/chat`, while meetings use composer push-to-talk (AD-922/973), so a call could never be truly hands-free.

**Decision — BF-623 (the gate).** Conversation mode is **itself** the voice opt-in: the 1:1 arm effect now depends ONLY on the mic-mode selection (`micMode === 'conversation'`), not on any voice-output flag. The open mic is an *input* affordance; whether a reply is *spoken* stays a per-reply decision in `onAgentReply` (which reads the live `hxi_chat_tts_{agentId}` pref), so the Captain can talk to an agent and read text replies with no voice output enabled. (This is the reading both the existing BF-290 "TTS-disabled conversation" test and the issue's disarm-trigger — "when conversation mode is deselected" — already encode.)

**Decision — AD-985 (the feature).** Generalize the singleton `ConversationController` with two optional `ArmOptions` hooks rather than forking it: (1) **`submitTranscript(text, history)`** — when provided, a completed utterance is handed to this callback INSTEAD of the built-in 1:1 chat POST; the meeting path routes it through the live `sendText` (the AD-914 group fan-out), and since `useMeetingVoice` speaks the crew's replies the controller does NOT enter `agent_speaking` — it goes straight to `silence_pending` (mic stays live, echo-gated) for the Captain's next turn. (2) **`canListen()`** — the AD-922 **meeting-wide echo gate**: a transcript is dropped while `speakingAgentId != null` (ANY crew member mid-TTS, not BF-300's host-filtered ref which misses non-host speakers — the load-bearing AD-922 lesson), so the mic never transcribes the crew's own speech; a dropped echo refreshes the silence timer (room activity keeps the session alive through a long crew turn). Extracted `_enterSilencePending()` (shared by `markAgentReplyComplete` and the group path) + `_refreshSilenceTimer()`. The 30s-silence release (AD-747) still fires on true silence.

**Wiring (ProfileChatTab).** The arm effect is **relocated** below `sendText` so it can read `meetingActive` / `callAudioEnabled` / `sendText` / `speakingAgentId` (all defined later in the component); the single-armed-controller invariant is unchanged. It branches: `micMode !== 'conversation'` → disarm; `meetingActive` → arm the meeting open-mic (gated on the AD-949 call-scoped `callAudioEnabled`, default ON) with `canListen: () => speakingAgentIdRef.current == null` + `submitTranscript: (t) => void sendTextRef.current(t)` and NO `onAgentReply` (useMeetingVoice speaks); else → the 1:1 path (BF-623, mode-only gate). Two refs (`speakingAgentIdRef`, `sendTextRef`) keep the callbacks current without re-arming on every render. The old `voiceEnabled`-gated effect is removed.

**Tests.** New `conversationController.group.test.ts` (6, mocked module boundary): submit routes to `submitTranscript` not the 1:1 fetch; post-submit state is `silence_pending`; the echo gate drops a transcript while speaking (no submit) and admits it once silent; an echo drop refreshes the release timer; 30s of true silence still releases; clean disarm. New `ProfileChatTab.voicewave.test.tsx` (11, `?raw` source assertions, the groupsend/threadTranscript convention): the 1:1 path no longer couples to `globalVoiceEnabled` or `ttsEnabled`; the meeting branch gates on `callAudioEnabled`, uses the `speakingAgentId` echo gate, routes through `sendText`, and depends on the right flags; HXI no-emoji. Two obsolete-contract tests updated: `ProfileChatTab.conversationWiring` (a `voiceEnabled` flip no longer disarms — BF-623 decoupling) and `ProfileChatTab.bf290` (TTS-disabled conversation now arms, per reading B). Full UI **1480 passed / 1 skipped** (241 files), `npm run build` clean. PUSHED.

### AD-981a: recall-confidence on the live sovereign path — Feeling-of-Knowing logging for `recall_for_agent` (the earmarked AD-981 recall live-wiring)

**Context.** AD-979a built the recall-confidence Feeling-of-Knowing signal (`RecallConfidence` band strong/weak/none) and AD-979c the hybrid lexical axis — but both landed on `recall()` / `recall_with_confidence`, while the crew's actual sovereign recall goes through `recall_for_agent` (agent-scoped, AD-397). So the live tracing during the AD-979 wave found those mechanisms were **mechanism-only**: the "invisible miss" (a relevant-ish memory just under the bar) the crew flagged was still invisible on the very path that matters. AD-981 was earmarked for this live-wiring; AD-981a is its first, conservative slice — observability, no behavior change.

**Decision (mirrors the AD-979a `recall`→`recall_with_confidence` shim exactly).** New **`EpisodicMemory.recall_for_agent_with_confidence(agent_id, query, k)`** is the single source of truth for the sovereign path; **`recall_for_agent` is now a thin byte-identical shim** over it (returns just the episodes), so every existing caller is unchanged. The new method surfaces an **agent-scoped** band: it tallies the best similarity and candidate count over the agent's **own** episodes (the sovereign-shard subset), *before* the BF-027 relaxed return threshold (Koriat accessibility), and classifies them against the **general** `relevance_threshold` / `weak_floor` (not the relaxed agent-return threshold) so the band is directly comparable to the global AD-979a signal. This is the right axis for the sovereign path — "how accessible is *this agent's* memory for this query" — distinct from `recall_with_confidence`'s global accessibility. A new default-off **`MemoryConfig.recall_fok_logging_enabled`** (threaded through `__main__.py` → `EpisodicMemory.__init__` → `self._recall_fok_logging`) emits the band as a structured `INFO` line per sovereign recall (agent, band, best_sim, owned-candidate count, returned count, truncated query), turning a live multi-agent session into a recall-calibration tool. The band is logged even on an empty recall (an honest "I have nothing" is exactly what calibration wants).

**Conservative by construction.** Default off → zero extra log noise and byte-identical recalled episodes (the FoK tally is read-only — the returned set is governed by the unchanged threshold/shard `continue` guards + k-cap). The agent-scoped band is logged, **not** yet used to drive control (the AD-979b expand loop on the sovereign path is a deliberate follow-up — AD-981b — once the logged bands give calibration data, the AD-956 watch-then-calibrate discipline). Hybrid fusion on the sovereign path is likewise deferred.

**Tests.** `test_ad981a_recall_fok_logging.py` (10, BF-287 real `EpisodicMemory` on `tmp_path` + real ONNX embeddings, no MagicMock): config default off; fast-absence on empty store; strong self-query returns the episode + strong band; band consistent with the pure classifier; **agent-scoped not global** (a counselor-owned strong match yields a non-strong band for the yeoman, strong for the counselor); the `recall_for_agent` shim returns the same episode ids as the core method; the FoK flag does not change the recalled set; flag-off emits no FoK log; flag-on emits the band line; the band is logged even on empty recall. Episodic/recall regression blast (`ad979`/`ad567`/`ad873`/`ad541`/`ad397`/`bf027`/`recall`/`episodic`) **737 passed / 1 skipped** (pre-existing AsyncMock dream-provenance warnings only). PUSHED.

### AD-983d: deferred-tool model — manifest + lazy `find_intents` retrieval (#917; completes the AD-983 epic)

**Context.** The scale piece of the AD-983 Copilot-parity epic (#913). `PromptBuilder.build_system_prompt` renders **every** registered `IntentDescriptor` into the decomposer prompt (full param tables), and the AD-983a affordance block renders every reachable hint. At ~30 intents that is fine; at hundreds it (a) blows the context budget and (b) **degrades selection** — a long flat near-duplicate list makes the model worse at picking. This is exactly the failure the GitHub Copilot **deferred-tool** mechanism exists to prevent: a small always-loaded set carries full schemas; the large remainder is present only as a cheap **manifest** (names), and a **search** returns full detail for the matching few on demand.

**Decision (three parts; mechanism + conservative wiring, default-off — the AD-979b/c precedent).** (1) **`CapabilityRetriever`** (`cognitive/capability_retriever.py`) — `tool_search` for ProbOS. Built once from the full catalog; queried with a per-call `scope` (the agent's granted ∩ live set — AD-983a/b). `manifest(scope=None)` → sorted `[(name, one_line_description)]` (cheap, never param tables). `find_intents(concept, *, scope=None, k=8, dense_ranking=None)` → up to `k` full `IntentDescriptor`s ranked by the AD-979c **`reciprocal_rank_fusion`** over two **lexical** axes — a name-token axis and a full-text axis (description + `usage_hint` + param text) — reusing the AD-979c **`fts_or_query`** tokenizer. **Deterministic** for a given `(scope, concept, catalog)` (the PromptBuilder's sorted-stable contract, preserved). **Vocabulary-mismatch safe** (AD-979c hybrid principle): matching over the full descriptor surface surfaces a capability whose *name* shares no token with the query when its *description* does. `dense_ranking` (a future semantic axis) is fused through the *same* RRF call — the forward extension point; the default path is deterministic lexical only. (2) **`CognitiveConfig.deferred_capability_threshold: int = 0`** — when the decomposer's catalog **exceeds** this many descriptors, the domain tier renders as a manifest; **0 disables** (full render always), so the default is byte-identical to today. (3) **`PromptBuilder.build_system_prompt(..., *, manifest_mode=False)`** + **`_build_intent_table(..., *, manifest_mode=False)`** — in manifest mode the always-needed **core/utility** tiers keep their full param tables (**tiering**), while the unbounded **domain** tier becomes a compact `## Additional capabilities (manifest …)` name + one-line list. `manifest_mode=False` is byte-identical to the pre-AD-983d output.

**Wiring.** `IntentDecomposer.__init__` gains `deferred_capability_threshold: int = 0` + a `_use_manifest()` gate (`threshold > 0 AND catalog > threshold`); `decompose()` passes `manifest_mode=self._use_manifest()` to `build_system_prompt`. `runtime.py` threads `cog_cfg.deferred_capability_threshold` into the decomposer. Default off → the live decomposer prompt is unchanged at today's catalog size.

**Skill bodies.** Lazy skill-body loading already exists (AD-596: `CognitiveSkillEntry` manifest + on-relevance `SKILL.md` read), so this AD does not add a separate skill retriever — that remains the established model (forward marker if a unified skill+tool retriever is ever wanted).

**Tests.** `test_ad983d_deferred_capability.py` (21, BF-287 real `IntentDescriptor`s + real `CapabilityRetriever`/`PromptBuilder`/`AgentRegistry`, no MagicMock): manifest scopes 8-of-200 → 8; `find_intents("search the web")` → `web_search` with full params + `usage_hint`; determinism (repeat → identical order); vocabulary-mismatch via description; empty/no-match → `[]`; scope excludes ungranted; `k` cap; `dense_ranking` fused + scoped; build from a real registry; **byte-identical** default vs `manifest_mode=False`; manifest mode defers domain params + keeps core + lists the deferred capability; prompt-growth boundedness (manifest render shorter than full for a 120-intent catalog); the `_use_manifest` gate (0 = off, strictly-greater trigger); config default 0; pure-helper tokenizer/one-line. Regression blast over `prompt_builder`/`decomposer`/`ad152`(byte-identical)/`capability`/`ad317`/`ad514`/`ad983a` **455 passed / 6 skipped** (known BF-326 MagicMock-dir + importlib_metadata noise only). **This completes the AD-983 epic (a→b→c→d).** PUSHED.

The "each agent independently enables different tools/skills" half of the AD-983 epic (#913) needed a reusable UI that exposes the *full* tool + skill set per agent — the generalization of the vision toggle from one flag to the whole capability surface.

### AD-983b: per-agent capability enablement — per-agent skill grants + unified /capabilities API (#915)

**Context.** The "each crew agent independently enables different tools and skills" piece of the AD-983 epic (#913). Tools already had per-agent enablement (`ToolPermissionStore`, AD-423b — grant/revoke/restrict, enforced at the agentic loop). Cognitive skills did NOT: `CognitiveSkillCatalog` gated only by `department` + `min_rank`, so a skill could not be enabled on one agent and withheld from its department peers. And there was no unified read/write surface for an agent's capabilities.

**Decision (three parts).** (1) **`SkillGrantStore`** (`cognitive/skill_grants.py`) — the skill counterpart to `ToolPermissionStore`, mirroring it exactly (SQLite + WAL + in-memory cache, `issue_grant`/`revoke_grant`/`get_active_grants_sync`/`list_grants`, soft-revoke for audit, lazy expiry) minus the permission level (a cognitive skill is binary). `SkillAccessGrant` dataclass. (2) **Catalog overlay** — `CognitiveSkillCatalog.set_grant_store()` (injected at startup, mirroring `tool_registry.set_permission_store`) + `effective_entries_for_agent(agent_id, *, department, min_rank)` = the dept/rank defaults PLUS explicitly-granted skills (even outside the agent's dept/rank) MINUS explicitly-restricted skills. Back-compat: with no grant store wired it is byte-identical to `list_entries(department, min_rank)`. The onboarding intent-subscription path (`agent_onboarding.py`) now resolves an agent's skill intents through `effective_entries_for_agent`, so per-agent grants drive what the agent can actually reach. (3) **Unified API** (`routers/agents.py`) — `GET /api/agent/{id}/capabilities` → `{tools: [...], skills: [...]}` each with `granted` + `source` (`grant`/`restriction`/`role_default` for tools; `grant`/`restriction`/`dept_default` for skills); `POST /api/agent/{id}/capabilities/set` `{kind: tool|skill, id, enabled, reason}` (`enabled=False` issues a restriction that overrides a default), audit-logged via the new `CAPABILITY_ACCESS_RESOLVED` event — the generalization of the AD-982 vision `set` endpoint. New `SetCapability` Pydantic model (`kind` pattern-validated).

**Wiring.** `SkillGrantStore` created in `startup/communication.py` (`data/skill_grants.db`), injected into the catalog, threaded through `CommunicationResult` → `runtime.skill_grant_store`, stopped in `startup/shutdown.py`.

**Independence proven.** A skill granted to agent A is in A's effective set and NOT in a same-department peer B's; a restriction removes a default the agent would otherwise hold. Tests: `test_ad983b_capability_enablement.py` (16, BF-287 real `SkillGrantStore` + real `CognitiveSkillCatalog` with on-disk `SKILL.md`): store issue/restrict/revoke/persist-across-restart; the headline grant-one-agent-not-its-peer; restriction-removes-default; no-store back-compat; and the API (GET shape + source tags, POST grant→restrict, 404 unknown agent/skill, 422 invalid kind). The 5 BF-326 MagicMock-dir warnings are the known config-boundary noise (auto-cleaned), consistent with the AD-982a API tests. Regression blast over skill-catalog/onboarding/acm/tool-permission/agents green. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed. Next: AD-983c (#916) the Capability panel UI.

### AD-983a: capability affordance layer — the tool carries its own manual (#914; supersedes AD-957/#893)

**Context.** The headline of the AD-983 Copilot-harness-parity epic (#913). A capability's *affordance* — "how to invoke a tool you hold" — was authored into ONE agent's behavior rules: the `[MESH ...]` do-and-report teaching lived in `YeomanAgent` (BF-599 capability block + AD-870 task-protocol tiers). Every other crew agent held the same capabilities through the mesh and had no idea how to reach them (the web-search incident — Ezri couldn't look things up). That is a category error: the affordance should travel WITH the capability and surface to whoever can reach it (the Copilot tool-schema model), not be written into a behavior rule. The right pattern already existed — `_conversational_notebook_protocol` (AD-912) is generalized to all crew AND substrate-gated — it just had not been applied to tools.

**Decision (three moves, one sub-AD).** (1) **`IntentDescriptor.usage_hint: str = ""`** — an optional AGENT-FACING invocation manual declared once on the capability (`description` serves the decomposer/planning; `usage_hint` serves the agent at reply time). Declared on the five AD-869 `[MESH]`-backed read intents: `list_directory`, `read_file`, `search_files` (on their core agents), `web_search`, `read_page` (on the web agents). (2) **`CognitiveAgent.capability_affordances()`** — a derived `{intent: usage_hint}` map built from the LIVE registry: walk `registry.all()`, read each agent's declared `intent_descriptors`, collect the ones with a `usage_hint`, dedupe by intent name. **Substrate-gated by construction** — only agents actually serving contribute, so a capability whose pool is down is absent (the BF-599 honest-degrade generalized off Yeo's `_available_mesh_read_intents`). (3) The base **`_conversational_capability_block`** (previously returned `""`) now renders those hints (deterministically sorted) into EVERY crew agent's conversational prompt, so any agent — not just Yeo — is told it can fetch a web search / read a page / list a directory / read a file this turn. **Folds in AD-957 (#893)**: generalizes "web search for everyone" to "every reachable capability, for everyone."

**Yeo retirement.** Removed Yeo's `_conversational_capability_block` override and the `_available_mesh_read_intents` helper (the base now provides live-capability grounding to all crew). Yeo's `_conversational_task_protocol` keeps only its genuinely role-specific delegation JUDGMENT — the Tier-3 `[CREATE_TASK]` write-it-down threshold (gated on a work-item store) + the rule-of-thumb; its quick-lookup tier now points at the ship-capability tags the base renders above, rather than re-enumerating the `[MESH ...]` forms. Net: the affordance is universal; only the delegation judgment stays Yeo's.

**Gates.** New `tests/test_ad983a_capability_affordances.py` (18, BF-287 real `AgentRegistry` + real `IntentDescriptor`: affordance collection/dedup/substrate-gating/no-runtime; base block render/order/empty/gap-safe; a non-Yeo CounselorAgent gets the web affordance with no override — the headline; the five real read descriptors ship hints). `test_ad870_*` rewritten (task protocol now teaches `[CREATE_TASK]` only; `[MESH]` moved to the base affordance). `test_bf599_*` rewritten (descriptor-driven, generalized — Yeo gets the web affordance from a live web agent via the base hook). AD-845/AD-869 Yeo tests green. Backend regression blast over yeoman/cognitive_agent/dm/decomposer/web_agent/capability green. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed. Next in the epic: AD-983b (#915) per-agent skill grants + unified `/capabilities` API.

### AD-984 + BF-622: meeting voice/chat experience wave — hide-chat toggle, interruptible scroll, Captain-local time, scaffolding-echo guard (#882, #918-#923)

**Context.** A live group-meeting test produced a design conversation (Captain + Ezri + Yeo) with one organizing insight: a meeting is **one conversation**, and voice is the Captain's chosen *interface* to it — so the text chat should be able to recede when voice is the interface. The voice-first loop is already in place (AD-921/922/923/949 + BF-621); the gap is the presentation layer. This wave ships the build-ready slice of the AD-984 epic plus a robustness bug. AD-984b (condensed-sidebar presentation + WCAG 2.1 AA) stays design-deferred.

**AD-984a — hide-chat toggle in meeting mode (frontend).** New session-scoped store flag `meetingChatVisible` (default **true** = byte-identical) + `setMeetingChatVisible`, mirroring the AD-949 `callAudioEnabled` slice (no localStorage). `GroupChatHeader` renders a `data-testid="chat-visibility-toggle"` speech-bubble stroke-SVG button **only while `meetingActive`** (amber shown / dim+slash hidden, `aria-pressed`, no emoji / no `Glyphs.tsx` export). `ProfileChatTab` gates the transcript message-list on `showTranscript = !(meetingActive && !meetingChatVisible)` — `MeetingView` (avatars) + composer stay; only the transcript collapses. Persistence and the BF-621 voice reveal are unaffected (replies still land + are spoken; re-showing reveals the full transcript).

**AD-984c — interruptible auto-scroll (frontend).** New pure helper `chat/scrollAnchor.ts` `isPinnedToBottom(el, threshold=80)` (a non-overflowing or at-bottom container is pinned). `ProfileChatTab` tracks a `pinnedToBottomRef` via an `onScroll` handler on the message-list container, and the auto-scroll effect moves the view ONLY when pinned — so a new message never yanks the Captain down while they are reading an earlier turn. Starts pinned (fresh view); returning to the bottom re-engages.

**AD-984d — Captain-local timezone in crew context (backend).** New `TemporalConfig.captain_timezone: str = ""` (IANA name). When set, `_build_temporal_context` adds a "Captain's local time: …" line (converted via `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo`) alongside the UTC line — a FACT provided to the crew, removing the confabulation source (the crew inferred "3am" from UTC when it was 9pm Mountain). Unset = unchanged (UTC only; the crew must not assert a local time). A bad/unknown zone name honest-degrades to no extra line. **`tzdata` added to dependencies** — Windows has no system IANA database, so `zoneinfo` needs it (a silent honest-degrade would have hidden the feature on the Captain's OS).

**BF-622 — scaffolding-echo guard (backend).** The AD-978/AD-733a `--- Current Visual Context --- … --- End Visual Context ---` block is prepended to the LLM INPUT so an agent can describe what it sees; it leaked into the chat once when a degraded LLM proxy echoed its own input prompt back as the completion. New pure `strip_visual_context_block(text)` in `working_memory.py` (regex on the exact delimiters `render_for_prompt` emits — single source of truth) removes the span before persist. Applied at both reply chokepoints (`thread_fanout._send_one` group path, `routers/agents.py` 1:1 path), guarded on the `"Current Visual Context"` substring so normal replies are untouched; a reply that was ONLY echoed scaffolding degrades to the non-reply sentinel.

**Gates.** New tests: `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` +3 (AD-984a hidden-when-no-meeting / shown+`aria-pressed` / click hides), `chat/__tests__/scrollAnchor.test.ts` (7, AD-984c pure helper), `test_ad984d_captain_timezone.py` (6, BF-287 real `SystemConfig` + real `_build_temporal_context`), `test_bf622_strip_visual_context.py` (8, incl. the round-trip that the strip matches the real `render_for_prompt` delimiters). Full UI **1453 passed / 1 skipped** (+10 over the 1438 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean; backend blast over perception/temporal/thread_fanout/vision/cognitive/dm/agents **1266 passed / 0 failed** (pre-existing BF-326 MagicMock-dir warnings only). COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed. AD-984b deferred (design).

### BF-617 + BF-618 + BF-619: live group-meeting test fixes — shared vision, paced text, end-of-turn hand-offs (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain's first live group-meeting test of the AD-976/978 wave surfaced three bugs that the mocked unit tests missed (the recurring AD-933a integration-gap lesson — scripted handlers don't exercise real perception/voice/cascade wiring): (1) "Yeo can't see me but Ezri can"; (2) all reply text appeared at once instead of landing as each agent spoke; (3) Ezri ended a turn with "Yeo, anything on your end?" and Yeo never answered.

**BF-617 — shared meeting vision.** Root cause: perception frames fan out only to REGISTERED observers (crew with `vision_capable=True` — only `counselor`/`architect`), so the yeoman's working-memory ring was empty and AD-978 rendered the BF-294 "camera not active" sentinel even with a live feed. A shared-camera meeting has ONE feed that everyone present should see. `VisionConsumer` now records the latest observation it produces (`_last_observation` + `latest_shared_observation()`), and `_render_agent_scene_block` falls back to it when an agent's own ring is empty — sharing the frame into that agent's ring on the render path. Meeting-scoped: it does NOT `register_observer` the agent, so there is no ambient-perception enrollment, no added per-frame fan-out cost, and no proactive-emit behavior change. An observer with its own ring still renders that; with no frame described yet, the honest sentinel still shows.

### BF-620: shared meeting vision survives restart (follow-up to BF-617, #882)

**Context.** The Captain's RE-TEST after BF-617 shipped STILL showed "Yeo can't see but Ezri can." BF-617's mechanism (the `_render_agent_scene_block` fallback to `latest_shared_observation()`) is correct in isolation (its tests pass) but failed live — the recurring integration-gap lesson again: the fallback's *source* was wrong post-restart.

**Root cause.** `VisionConsumer._last_observation` is in-RAM and starts `None` after a restart, but a vision-capable observer's ring **hydrates from disk** (AD-742f persistence) on first access. So right after the Captain's pre-test restart, Ezri (observer) renders a hydrated scene while the yeoman's fallback reads `_last_observation == None` → the BF-294 "camera not active" sentinel → "I can't see." The Captain restarts before every test, so it reproduced every time. BF-617's own tests use a `_FakeConsumer` returning a fixed obs, so they never exercised the in-RAM-vs-hydrated split.

**Fix.** `latest_shared_observation()` now, when `_last_observation` is unset, falls back to the most-recent observation any REGISTERED OBSERVER currently holds (scanning their real rings, hydrated or live) — so a non-observer borrows the live shared feed regardless of restart. Strictly additive: when a fresh in-RAM describe exists it is returned directly (zero change to the warm path). Tier-2 per-ring scan (a failed ring read is skipped).

**Gates.** `test_bf620_shared_meeting_vision_restart.py` (5, BF-287 real `VisionConsumer` + real `VisionWorkingMemory` rings: last-obs-wins-when-set; observer-ring fallback after restart; none-anywhere → None; most-recent-across-observers; non-observer borrows feed end-to-end through `_render_agent_scene_block`). BF-617 (6) + AD-978 (13) + AD-733a (26) regression green (50 total). COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

**BF-618 — paced meeting text reveal.** Root cause: the original AD-976 coupled the text reveal to TTS `speakingAgentId` events; when speech fired fast or didn't pace (cold Piper / muted / autoplay-blocked), the staged reveals burst to all-at-once. Replaced with the SAME timer-paced progressive reveal text chat uses (`revealRepliesProgressively`, built-in inter-reply spacing — cannot burst), in both meeting and text-chat paths. Voice (`speakMeetingReplies`) is now kicked off BEFORE the awaited reveal so it runs concurrently rather than after. The fragile staging apparatus (per-agent staging map, reveal-on-speaking effect, ref bridge) is removed. Exact word-level karaoke sync remains forward marker AD-976a (needs Piper streaming timing metadata).

### BF-621: meeting text reveal follows speech — "hear, then see" + "is speaking" label (#882)

**Context.** The Captain's re-test of BF-618: text was "more delayed now, but still not what I expected" — it said "{callsign} is typing" *while the agent was speaking*, and the timer-paced reveal drifted from the voice. The Captain's decision: in a live meeting with voice, label it "{callsign} is **speaking**…", and reveal each reply's text **after** that agent finishes speaking (hear the response, then see it land in the chat).

**Root cause of the drift.** BF-618 ran two independent clocks concurrently: `speakMeetingReplies` (voice) and a timer-paced `revealRepliesProgressively` (text). With voice audible they are uncorrelated, so text and speech diverge and the "typing" label is simply wrong while the agent talks.

**Decision.** When a meeting is live AND call audio is ON, drive the reveal off the AD-921 voice sequencer's per-utterance completion — the sequencer is the single clock (it already awaits each utterance one at a time), so text strictly follows speech and cannot drift or burst (the BF-618 burst was a *separate* timer racing the voice, not the voice itself). Mechanism: `MeetingVoiceDeps` gains `onUtteranceStart(reply)` (fired before each utterance, with the full reply for the callsign) and `onUtteranceEnd(reply)` (fired after the utterance completes AND after `onSpeakingChange(null)`); `speakRepliesSequentially` calls them around `_speakAndWait`. `useMeetingVoice.speakReplies(replies, hooks?)` forwards them gen-guarded (a superseded batch never labels/reveals stale text). `ProfileChatTab.sendText` branches: meeting+audio → `onUtteranceStart` sets `typingAgent` `{verb:'speaking'}`, `onUtteranceEnd` clears it and appends that reply (hear → label clears → text lands); audio OFF/muted or text chat → the AD-960 timer-paced reveal is unchanged. `TypingIndicator` + the `typingAgent` slice gain the `'speaking'` verb. A reply skipped by `shouldContinue` is neither spoken nor revealed (correct — stale). Honest-degrade: if audio is on but TTS fails, `onUtteranceEnd` fires on the BF-615 length-proportional safety timeout, so text still lands (never lost). Word-level karaoke sync stays AD-976a.

**Gates.** `meetingVoice.test.ts` +3 (start-before-speak; end-after-`speaking:null` timeline; superseded batch reveals nothing), `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` rewritten to the BF-621 branch (voice-driven vs timer; speaking-label→clear→append order; muted-meeting + text-chat fall back to timer), `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` +1 (`'speaking'` verb). Full UI **1443 passed / 1 skipped** (+5 over the 1438 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. Frontend only — no backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

**BF-619 — end-of-turn hand-off detection.** Root cause: AD-951's `extract_directed_callsign` matches a LEADING vocative only, but a natural hand-off comes at the END of a turn ("... Yeo, anything on your end?"), so the cascade's addressed-set was empty, no AD-961 extension fired, and the addressed peer never spoke. New `extract_handoff_callsign` also detects a final-sentence leading vocative and a trailing comma-vocative ("what do you think, Yeo?"), while keeping the BF #467 discipline (a message ABOUT a peer — "I agree with Yeo." — is not a hand-off; the comma/colon is the discriminator). The group cascade now uses it for addressed-detection, so an end-of-turn hand-off hard-includes the peer and (past the round cap) earns the AD-961 address-extension. Traced against the live transcript: Ezri's final-sentence "Yeo, ..." now resolves to `yeo`, extends one round, and Yeo answers.

**Gates.** `test_bf619_handoff_callsign.py` (leading parity + the end-of-turn case + the referential-mention negatives) + `test_bf617_shared_meeting_vision.py` (observer renders own ring; non-observer falls back to the shared feed + ring populated; no-frame sentinel; disabled/no-consumer degrade) + rewritten `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` (voice-before-reveal ordering; always-progressive, no instant-dump branch). Backend blast across fanout/group/perception/AD-951/961/crew_profile green; full UI **1429 passed / 1 skipped**, build clean.

### AD-976: Meeting-mode text follows the voice — reveal each reply as its agent speaks (Natural Conversation epic, #899)

**Context.** In a live (audio-on) meeting the AD-921 voice sequencer speaks the crew's replies one at a time, but the text path dumped ALL replies into the transcript instantly (`for (const r of replies) appendReply(r)`). The Captain read the whole room's answers before the voices had said them — "shouldn't see the text until you've said the words."

**Decision (frontend only).** Reveal a reply's text as its agent STARTS speaking, off the existing `useMeetingVoice` `speakingAgentId` seam (AD-923) — leaving the working voice hook untouched (lowest risk). `ProfileChatTab` now: (1) reads `callAudioEnabled` reactively; (2) in the send handler, branches `meetingActive && callAudioEnabled` → STAGE the round's replies in `pendingMeetingRepliesRef` (a `Map<agent_id, reply>`) and clear `revealedSpeakingRef`, instead of dumping them; (3) an effect on `speakingAgentId` reveals each staged reply exactly once as its agent begins to speak (a `revealedSpeakingRef` set guards against re-entry). The handler-scope `appendReply` closure is bridged to the render-scope effect via `appendMeetingReplyRef` (the file's stale-closure ref discipline). A MUTED meeting (no voice to pace the reveal) and TEXT chat both fall back to the existing AD-960 progressive reveal, so text never silently fails to appear. `speakMeetingReplies` is unchanged — it drives `speakingAgentId`, which now drives the reveal.

**Gates.** `ProfileChatTab.ad976.test.tsx` (8, the faithful-mirror convention used for this heavy component: the reveal-mode decision — audio-on→speech-synced, muted/text→progressive; staging keyed by agent_id dropping blank ids; speech-synced reveal in speaking order, exactly-once on re-entry, no-op for an unstaged speaker). Full UI suite **1434 passed / 1 skipped** (+8), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. Forward marker AD-976a: sentence-level karaoke sync (needs Piper streaming timing metadata).

### AD-980c: Dream interpretation — an agent interprets its own dream (Agent self-interpretation epic, #912)

**Context.** The novel loop Ezri's question pointed at: sleep -> dream -> wake -> interpret -> revise-self. AD-980b gives a dream a dreamer (per-agent reflection episodes); AD-980a is the interpretation engine. AD-980c closes the loop: an agent interprets ITS OWN dream and stores the interpretation as an agent-owned episode that feeds its self-model. No published agent system has a sovereign agent interpret its own distinct consolidation artifact as a dream.

**Decision.** New `CognitiveAgent.interpret_own_dream(*, k=5)`: gathers the agent's recent `MemorySource.REFLECTION` episodes (the AD-980b-attributed dreams) via `recent_for_agent` (scanning a wider window so non-dream episodes don't crowd the dreams out), then runs the shared interpretation engine over them with a dream-specific focus ("what these dream reflections reveal about how you work and what matters to you"). The AD-980a `interpret_recall` body was refactored into a shared `_run_interpretation(episodes, focus, store)` engine (no gate) that both public entrypoints call after their own flag gate — `interpret_recall` gates on `recall_interpretation_enabled`, `interpret_own_dream` on `dream_interpretation_enabled`. Honesty-bound (AD-592): the dreams are real consolidated material; with none, nothing to interpret (`None`); the stored interpretation is the same agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION episode as AD-980a. Opt-in (default **False**, an extra LLM pass per agent per dream); not auto-invoked in the dream cycle — an explicit call (the Captain enables the flag + the loop is driven on wake/idle), keeping the behavior observable.

**Gates.** `test_ad980c_dream_interpretation.py` (7: disabled→None, no-dreams→None, empty-window→None, interprets only the REFLECTION episodes in the window and stores an agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION, dream-specific focus in the prompt, no-LLM→None, k bounds the dreams) + AD-980a (9) + AD-980b (5) green together (21) — the `_run_interpretation` refactor kept AD-980a byte-identical. **The full sleep->dream->wake->interpret loop (AD-980a+b+c) is built and tested.**

### AD-980b: Per-agent dream attribution — give a dream a dreamer (Agent self-interpretation epic, #911)

**Context.** The subjectivity gap behind Ezri's dream question: dream-consolidation reflections (AD-599 `_step_15_reflection_promotion`) were stored with `agent_ids=[]` — ownerless. Dream consolidation is a system-wide pass, so there was no "Ezri's dream"; an agent could not recall *its* dream because it did not have one. A dream needs a dreamer before it can be interpreted (AD-980c). Crucially, each reflection candidate ALREADY computes its `involved_agents` (the agents whose episodes it was consolidated from — e.g. a convergence report's agents, or a cluster's participating agents) and records them in `dag_summary["involved_agents"]` — but then threw that away at storage by hardcoding `agent_ids=[]`.

**Decision.** When `DreamingConfig.per_agent_dream_attribution_enabled` is set, the reflection episode is stored with `agent_ids=list(involved_agents)` instead of `[]`, so `recall_for_agent` (which filters on `agent_ids`) returns it for each dreamer — one episode, multi-owner, recallable by each participant. A reflection with NO involved agents (an emergence/notebook snapshot — genuinely system-level) stays ownerless even when the flag is on (not every reflection has a dreamer). Default **OFF** → `agent_ids=[]` (byte-identical to AD-599); the Captain enables it to turn on the dream-interpretation loop. This is the prerequisite for AD-980c.

**Gates.** `test_ad980b_dream_attribution.py` (5: flag-off keeps reflections ownerless + provenance in dag_summary; flag-on attributes a convergence reflection to its agents and a cluster reflection to its participating agents; an agentless emergence snapshot stays ownerless even when on; default is off) + the AD-599 suite (18) green — the default-off gate keeps every AD-599 `agent_ids == []` assertion intact.

### AD-980a: Reflective recall interpretation — the meaning-making rung above metamemory (Agent self-interpretation epic, #910)

**Context.** Ezri (Counselor) asked whether crew agents can interpret their dreams; the question generalizes to memories and Oracle recall. AD-979 made recall *honest* (the Feeling-of-Knowing signal — do I know this, how sure?); AD-980a adds the rung above it: *meaning* (what do I make of it?). Recalled episodes were injected into context and reasoned over implicitly — there was no first-class act where an agent stands back and interprets its own memories. The mechanism already existed and was pointed elsewhere: `propose_appearance` (AD-721d) does instructions-first LLM reflection over the agent's own state for self-image. AD-980a points that same shape at recalled memories. Prior art: Generative Agents (Park 2023) synthesizes reflections from memory clusters — ProbOS had absorbed Park's retrieval *scoring* (AD-873) but not the reflection *synthesis*; this adds it, plus the honesty bound prior art lacks.

**Decision.** New `CognitiveAgent.interpret_recall(episodes, *, focus="", store=True) -> str | None`: an instructions-first LLM pass that returns a brief first-person interpretation of the agent's OWN recalled episodes, and (via `_store_interpretation_episode`) optionally persists it as an **agent-owned** reflection episode (`agent_ids=[sovereign]`, `MemorySource.REFLECTION`, `[interpretation]`-prefixed reflection, `importance=6`, the interpretation carried as the outcome `response` so the AD selective-encoding gate retains it). Honesty bound (AD-592): the system prompt instructs the agent to ground every statement in the memories shown and to say plainly when they do not support a conclusion; with **no episodes there is nothing to interpret, so it returns `None`** (honest by construction, never invents). The instruction text is gap-regex-safe (does not trip `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`). Opt-in `CommunicationsConfig.recall_interpretation_enabled` (default **False** — it is a real extra LLM pass, unlike the pure-prompt-text knobs), and the method is not yet wired into the live path (AD-980c will drive it over a per-agent dream). Tier-2: any LLM failure returns `None`.

**Gates.** `test_ad980a_recall_interpretation.py` (9: disabled→None, no-episodes→None honest no-op, enabled produces interpretation with recalled material in the prompt, LLM-failure→None, stored as agent-owned `[interpretation]` REFLECTION with the text in both reflection and outcome response, `store=False` persists nothing, focus reaches the prompt, system+user prompts gap-regex-safe, reflection-only episodes usable). Real `CommunicationsConfig` + recording episodic + scripted fake LLM (no MagicMock).

### AD-977: Group-thread episodic continuity — index the agent's own reply so it can recall group conversations (Natural Conversation epic, #900)

**Context.** Both crew agents flagged (honestly, no confabulation) that recall of GROUP conversations was patchy. Investigation: AD-933a writes a group episode per reply, but the embedded document (`EpisodicMemory._prepare_document`) and the FTS5 sidecar index `user_input` + `reflection` — NOT `outcomes[].response`. The AD-933a group episode set `user_input = "[group chat] <trigger>"` (the Captain's prompt) and **no `reflection`**, so the agent's OWN reply lived only in `outcomes[]` and was never embedded or FTS-indexed. Net: a group episode was findable by the Captain's trigger text but never by the agent's contribution — the group-vs-1:1 gap. (The 1:1 `_store_action_episode` already indexes the response via `reflection="<callsign> handled <intent>: <response>"`.)

**Decision.** Mirror the 1:1 pattern: the AD-933a group episode now sets `reflection="<callsign> said in group chat: <reply[:240]>"`. Because `_prepare_document` and the FTS5 dual-write both index `reflection`, the agent's own room contribution becomes recallable by its own words (dense AND — with AD-979c — keyword). Additive: `user_input` (the trigger) and `outcomes[].response` (the full reply, untruncated to 500) are unchanged, so existing AD-933a anchoring/labeling is byte-identical apart from the added reflection. Tier-2 honest-degrade on the store call is unchanged.

**Gates.** `test_ad977_group_recall.py` (3: reflection carries the agent's reply + names the speaker; reflection is distinct indexable content from the trigger; `outcomes[].response` preserved) + the AD-933a suite (7) green together. Composes with AD-979a/b/c (a group episode that still recalls weakly now also benefits from the hybrid keyword axis and the confidence signal).

### AD-979c + AD-979b: Hybrid dense+sparse retrieval (RRF) + metacognitive control loop (Oracle recall epic, #905, #904)

**Context.** Two follow-ons to AD-979a, both on the recall path. **AD-979c** targets the *vocabulary-mismatch gap*: recall was purely cosine over embeddings, so a memory encoded under different words than the query scored below `relevance_threshold` and was dropped even when relevant. **AD-979b** targets what to *do* about a weak recall: a human, on a Feeling-of-Knowing, keeps searching differently (Nelson & Narens 1990 — the monitor signal drives a control action), where recall previously had no recourse but to report uncertainty.

**AD-979c — hybrid dense+sparse retrieval.** Two pure helpers: `fts_or_query(query)` turns a natural query into an FTS5 OR-of-quoted-keywords MATCH string (so the sparse axis surfaces a memory by ANY shared keyword), and `reciprocal_rank_fusion(rankings, *, k=60)` fuses ranked id lists by `sum 1/(k+rank)` — rank-based, so a cosine ranking and an FTS ranking fuse without score-scale calibration, and a SINGLE ranking is returned in its original order (the byte-identical-when-sparse-empty guarantee). `recall_with_confidence` gains a gated tail: when `hybrid_recall_enabled` and the FTS5 sidecar is present, `_fuse_dense_sparse` unions the dense episode ranking with `keyword_search` (the existing AD-567b FTS axis) via RRF, hydrating sparse-only ids through `get_by_ids`. The Feeling-of-Knowing signal is intentionally left as the DENSE distribution (hybrid changes *which* episodes return, not how confident the cosine recall was). New `MemoryConfig.hybrid_recall_enabled` (default **False** → byte-identical) + `hybrid_rrf_k` (60). Prior art absorbed as patterns (permissive, no vendoring): Mem0's parallel semantic+BM25 fusion, RRF (Cormack 2009).

**AD-979b — metacognitive control loop.** Pure `decide_recall_control(band)` maps the AD-979a monitor band to an action: `strong→accept`, `weak→expand`, `none→abstain` — so only the *invisible miss* triggers work (zero cost on the happy path and on genuine absence). Pure `recall_expansion_variants(query, *, max_n)` produces bounded, deduped re-query variants, highest-value first: a content-word "soup" (query stripped of scaffolding to its content tokens — often embeds closer to a terse stored episode) then the AD-584 question→declarative reformulation. `recall_with_control(query, k, *, max_expansions=1)` runs the monitor (`recall_with_confidence`), and on a `weak` band issues at most `max_expansions` re-queries, adopting a variant only when it is strictly more accessible (higher best similarity) and stopping early at `strong`. Returns `(episodes, confidence, actions)` where `actions` is the audit trail (e.g. `["expand", "requery:weak", "requery:strong"]`) so the agent can report honestly (AD-592): a still-weak/none final band means "I looked, expanded, and remain uncertain," never a fabrication. The mechanism is built + tested but NOT yet wired into the live conversational recall path (a follow-up activation AD, mirroring how `recall_with_confidence` is available but the live path still calls `recall_for_agent`) — the conservative boundary keeps a behavior change observable.

**Gates.** `test_ad979c_hybrid_retrieval.py` (16: pure `fts_or_query` + `reciprocal_rank_fusion` incl. single-ranking identity, plus real-store fusion surfacing a keyword-matched episode the cosine axis missed, flag-off byte-identical) + `test_ad979b_control_loop.py` (15: the pure policy + expansion generator + real-store loop — strong accepts with no expansion, empty store abstains, weak triggers bounded re-query, three-tuple shape). The three AD-979 suites together: **44 passed**. AD-979a's episodic blast (804 passed) already covered the shared recall path; AD-979c adds only a default-off branch and AD-979b only new methods.

### AD-979a: Recall-confidence Feeling-of-Knowing signal — make the invisible miss visible (Oracle recall epic, #903)

**Context.** `EpisodicMemory.recall()` computed `similarity = 1.0 - distance` for every candidate and then *discarded* it (a silent `continue` below `relevance_threshold`), returning only `list[Episode]`. So a caller could not distinguish "I have NOTHING on this" (fast-absence) from "the best match was 0.65, just under the bar" (the *invisible miss*) — the crew (Yeo/Ezri) flagged exactly this as a confidence-calibration gap at a session wrap-up. Cognitive-science framing: a Feeling-of-Knowing (Hart 1965) is *computed from the accessibility* of partial retrieved information (Koriat's accessibility hypothesis, 1993) — which is precisely the similarity distribution `recall()` already had and threw away.

**Decision.** Surface the signal `recall()` already computes. A new frozen `RecallConfidence` dataclass (`band`, `best_similarity`, `candidate_count`, `query`) and a pure `classify_recall_confidence(best_similarity, candidate_count, *, relevance_threshold, weak_floor)` classifier: `candidate_count <= 0` → `none` (fast-absence); `best >= relevance_threshold` → `strong` (== what `recall()` returns); `best >= weak_floor` → `weak` (the invisible miss); else `none` (slow-gap — candidates present but too distant). The band is **accessibility-derived, never self-reported** (the literature's anti-inflation invariant, same discipline as AD-955 outcome-derived trust). New `recall_with_confidence(query, k) -> tuple[list[Episode], RecallConfidence]` is now the single source of truth for the query+filter+rerank path; **`recall()` is a thin byte-identical shim** over it (returns just the episodes), so every existing caller is unchanged. The `candidate_count` split makes the fast-absence vs slow-gap distinction explicit — the slow-gap is the AD-979c hybrid-retrieval (vocabulary-mismatch) case, and a `weak` signal is what AD-979b's metacognitive control loop will act on. New `MemoryConfig.recall_confidence_weak_floor` (default 0.45, above the AD-655 contrastive 0.4 floor), wired through `__main__.py`.

**Gates.** `test_ad979a_recall_confidence.py` (13: the pure classifier across all bands + the fast-absence/slow-gap boundary, plus real-`EpisodicMemory`-on-tmp_path integration proving the signal is consistent with the classifier at the store's own thresholds, `recall()` is a byte-identical shim, empty store = fast-absence, populated store + unrelated query = slow-gap not fast-absence). Episodic/recall regression blast: **804 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**.

### AD-978: Camera scene-context injected into the group fan-out — the crew can SEE in a group chat (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain reported that the camera feed was invisible to the crew in a group chat, even though the camera→perception→describe pipeline works (the 1:1 chat preview shows live scene descriptions). Root cause (verified): the AD-733a scene-context injection lives ONLY in the 1:1 DM path (`routers/agents.py` prepends `get_or_create_working_memory(agent_id).render_for_prompt()` to the message). The group fan-out (`routers/thread_fanout.py` `_send_one`) never pulled each agent's `VisionWorkingMemory`, so the visual block never reached the dispatched agents' prompts. (AD-916 `vision_messages` is a separate concern — image *attachments* on a message, not the ambient camera.)

**Decision.** Mirror the 1:1 injection into the group fan-out, respecting the multi-agent shape: (1) a new `_maybe_force_describe_frame(runtime)` runs ONCE per round in `_fan_one_round`, before the parallel `asyncio.gather` — the shared camera frame is described once (and `force_describe_current_frame` writes the same observation to every observer's WM), so N speakers don't trigger N redundant describes of the same frame; (2) a new `_render_agent_scene_block(runtime, agent_id)` renders THIS agent's own ring (each agent owns a `VisionWorkingMemory` keyed by `agent_id`) and notes per-agent DM engagement (AD-733c-5, so a group turn doesn't transition the whole mesh), and `_send_one` prepends the block to `params["text"]` (what the LLM receives) while leaving `trigger_body` clean for the episode/pipeline (the stored episode records the Captain's actual message, not the ephemeral scene). Both are gated on `perception.enabled` (Pydantic default **False** → byte-identical when the subsystem is off, exactly the 1:1 gate). BF-294 confabulation guard is preserved: an empty ring renders the non-empty "Camera not active … Do NOT describe what you cannot see" sentinel, never a silent omission, so an agent can't invent a scene. Tier-2 honest-degrade throughout (any failure logs at debug and the round proceeds text-only).

**Gates.** `test_ad978_group_perception.py` (13: the two helpers in isolation — disabled/enabled/empty-ring-sentinel/per-agent/degrade/per-agent-engagement — plus end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` proving the scene block reaches each dispatched agent's `params["text"]`, force-describe fires once per round not per agent, and byte-identical text when perception is off). Regression blast over fan-out / group-chat / perception / AD-733 vision-context: **410 passed, 0 failed**.

### AD-975 + AD-963a: Turn-taking self-knowledge + broadcast terminator (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain ran a live 3-person room (Captain + Ezri + Yeo) and reviewed the transcript. It validated the recent fixes (AD-967 roster grounding, AD-935/950/951/955 self-regulating turn-taking — the crew read the floor, hand off by name, and don't address absent peers). It also surfaced two refinements, both built here. The transcript was captured as the **first AD-956 calibration data point** on #892 (the threshold work stays deferred — N=3 has not yet exposed the collision seam, only a correct prediction of it).

**AD-975 — crew turn-taking self-knowledge.** In the test the crew reasoned accurately about reading the floor but assumed possible **simultaneity** ("two of us could respond before either sees the other's reply"). In reality `group_chat_fanout` is sequential + synchronous: one speaker per turn, each later speaker receives every prior reply in full before its own turn, so two crew never answer the same point at once. **Decision (instructions-first, DP#6):** extend the AD-935/967 `_conversational_group_chat_protocol` hook with a "How turn-taking works here" paragraph teaching the real mechanism — turns are sequential (you see completed replies, never simultaneous), collisions are structurally impossible so build with confidence on prior turns, there is no live "typing" cue from a peer (a turn arrives when they finish), and addressing a colleague by name invites them to take the next turn (the AD-951 hand-off).
