Gated on `is_group_chat` (1:1 unaffected); composes with the AD-967 roster + AD-935 decline guidance; gap-regex-safe. Tests: `test_ad975_turn_taking_self_knowledge.py` (7, pure hook assertions).

**AD-963a — broadcast turn-mode terminator.** The AD-935 cascade stops at `max_agent_rounds` or the convergence gate — correct for a DISCUSSION, but wrong for a BROADCAST ("what do you ALL think?") where the Captain wants EACH relevant crew member to answer once. In the test only 2 of 3 agents got turns because the round cap, not completeness, bounded a plural ask. **Decision (the ratified AD-963 recommendation, build-split part a):** a pure `classify_broadcast(text)` cue detector (conservative — only clear plural-address cues like "you all" / "everyone" / "each of you" / "whole team" match; everything ambiguous stays DISCUSSION) drives a broadcast terminator in `group_chat_fanout`: when a broadcast is detected, the cascade round-robins every crew participant **exactly once** (cumulative exclude of all prior speakers, relevance-ordered by the existing facilitator rank, each seeing prior answers), naturally bounded by the participant count — bypassing the discussion cap + the AD-961 address-extension budget. Directed addresses remain AD-951's job; the default (Discussion) classification is byte-identical to AD-935/961. New `GroupChatConfig.broadcast_terminator_enabled` (Pydantic default False; `system.yaml` enables it). The Broadcast department weight tilt (AD-963b) is deferred for a live look, as is parallel round-0 (deprioritized — agents must see each other to avoid echo; genuine independence is AD-958b's quorum, for decisions not chat). Tests: `test_ad963a_broadcast_terminator.py` (8: classifier match/miss/non-string; broadcast lets all crew speak once; discussion capped; flag-off byte-identical).

**Gates.** AD-975 + AD-963a suites + AD-935/951/955/961/967 cascade regressions green in isolation; broad backend blast green; full UI unchanged (no UI change). The trust-ledger-write core (AD-958), the AD-956 threshold, the AD-963b weight tilt, and the AD-954a dedicated window all remain correctly deferred to further live observation.

### AD-972 → AD-974: Meeting/call UX polish — faster TTS start, one mic, resizable video (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain tested the improved group-chat/call experience and reported three issues: (1) a long delay between seeing the crew's messages and hearing TTS; (2) two microphone buttons in a call (only one is wanted, the one next to Send); (3) no way to enlarge the video portraits.

**AD-972 — cut the seen-message → TTS-start delay.** The meeting voice path spoke each reply only after `await resolveProfile(agent_id)` — a cold `GET /api/agent/{id}/profile` fetch — and `speakResponse` then probed `/api/avatars/tts/status` before the Piper synth POST. So the FIRST utterance was gated on two network round-trips before synthesis even began, and every subsequent speaker paid the profile fetch as an audible gap. **Decision (frontend only):** (1) `useMeetingVoice` now prewarms when the meeting opens — it calls a new `prewarmTts()` (exported from `voice.ts`, idempotent over the cached one-time probe) and prefetches every room participant's voice profile (passed as `participantAgentIds` from `ProfileChatTab`), so by the time replies arrive (seconds later, after LLM generation) the profile cache is warm and the status probe is done. (2) `createVoiceProfileResolver` now caches the in-flight PROMISE (not just the resolved value) so the prewarm and the per-utterance resolve dedupe to one fetch. (3) `speakReplies` also kicks off all reply profile fetches up front. Net: the first agent speaks as soon as the synth returns (no profile/status round-trip first) and inter-speaker gaps are gone. The Piper synth latency itself is server-side and inherent. Tests: `useMeetingVoice.test.tsx` +2 (prewarm fires on open / not when inactive); `meetingVoice.test.ts` resolver cache contract preserved.

**AD-973 — one microphone, next to Send.** A live call showed TWO mic affordances: the composer dictation mic (the `MicIndicator` button by Send) AND a separate centered push-to-talk (`MeetingMicButton` + `useMeetingMic`, AD-922). Both captured one VAD-bounded utterance and auto-submitted via `sendText`; the composer mic also has the BF-300 echo guard and works in every context. **Decision (frontend only):** stop rendering the redundant `MeetingMicButton` (and drop its `useMeetingMic` hook + imports) so a call shows exactly one mic — the one next to Send, as the Captain asked. The `MeetingMicButton`/`useMeetingMic` files (and their standalone tests) are left in place as a tested, reusable PTT primitive. No behavior lost — voice input in a call still flows through the composer mic.

**AD-974 — drag-to-resize the video gallery.** The meeting gallery slots were a fixed 120×160 (112×132 portrait). **Decision (frontend only):** `AvatarSlot` and `CaptainSlot` take a `scale` prop that multiplies the portrait box, wrapper, and caption width; `MeetingView` holds a `galleryScale` (clamped [1,3], persisted to `localStorage` as `hxi_meeting_gallery_scale`) and renders a drag handle (`ns-resize`, amber grip) BELOW the gallery — dragging DOWN enlarges the portraits (UP shrinks), at 220px per +1.0 scale. The handle sits outside the scaled content so the screen-pixel drag math is unaffected, and the scale restores on reopen. Tests: `MeetingView.test.tsx` +4 (handle renders, drag-down enlarges + persists, clamps to [1,3], restores persisted scale).

**Gates.** Full UI suite **1426 passed / 1 skipped** (+6 over the 1420 baseline), `npm run build` clean, Playwright e2e **4/4**. No backend change.

### AD-966 → AD-971: Agent-initiated group-chat bug cluster — make agent-started rooms first-class conversations (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Context.** The Captain live-tested agent-initiated group chats (AD-924/925) and surfaced a cluster of six bugs that are all facets of one reality: agent-initiated rooms could be *created* but were never wired into the live conversation loop the Captain-driven path uses. Each is a distinct, sequentially-numbered AD; they ship together because they are one user-visible failure ("the agents can't actually hold a group conversation they start themselves").

**AD-966 — ≥2-participant floor (Bug: a room with an absent peer).** An agent emitted `[GROUP_CHAT title="…" @peer]` where no named ref resolved to a crew peer (the peer was addressed only in prose, or the callsign was unknown/hallucinated — e.g. "Vance"). `AgentGroupChatService.create_group_chat` minted a room with ONLY the creator — an incoherent 1-participant "group chat" talking to an absent peer. **Decision:** after resolving participants, if `len(final) < 2` return `GroupChatCreateResult(ok=False, error="no_participant_resolved")` instead of creating the room. The service is the right chokepoint — it guards all three callers (proactive AD-924, crew_executor AD-925 task rooms, the bus `handle_intent`); the AD-925 task-room path always passes ≥2 crew so it is unaffected; the proactive path already records a `group_chat_suppressed` action. Tests: `test_ad966_group_chat_participant_floor.py` (9, BF-287 real store); 10 obsolete-contract AD-918 tests (whose premise was a creator-only room) updated to the new ≥2 contract.

**AD-967 — present-participant room roster (Bug: agents address absent peers).** In a group chat the agents had no idea who was actually present — they addressed peers who were never invited (asking "Sentinel" a question in a room Sentinel was not in) and assumed a peer named in prose had been added; the conversation stalled waiting on an absent member. **Decision:** inject a roster of PRESENT participants into each dispatched agent's group prompt by extending the AD-935 `_conversational_group_chat_protocol` hook — "Present in this room: X, Y, and Z. … address only present members … to bring in a colleague, ask the Captain to add them" — gap-regex-safe. The roster rides a new fan-out param `room_roster`, built once in `group_chat_fanout` from `_resolve_callsigns(agent_ids)` (+ "the Captain" when joined) and threaded through `_fan_one_round` at both call sites. Honest-degrade: absent roster ⇒ byte-identical to pre-AD-967. Tests: `test_ad967_room_roster.py` (12: roster grammar, address guidance, gap-safety, backward-compat, end-to-end delivery, Captain-inclusion).

**AD-968 — the Captain auto-joins a room they post into (Bug: "Join" on chats I'm already in).** Posting a Captain message never added `captain` to the participant set, so `captainJoined` stayed false and the sidebar kept showing the Join button on a room the Captain was actively conversing in. **Decision:** in the `POST /messages` handler, on a Captain post into a GROUP (≥2 crew) OR an agent-created room, `store.add_participant(thread_id, "captain")` before fan-out. Scoped to group/agent-created rooms — the 1:1 default thread keeps its single-participant invariant that the task-promote (`assigned_to` inference) and auto-name paths rely on. Idempotent. Tests: `test_ad968_captain_autojoin.py` (5: group join, idempotent, agent-room join, 1:1 NOT joined, 1:1 stays single-participant).

**AD-969 — add-participant mints a new thread ONLY for the 1:1 home DM (Bug: "adding Vance made a new chat").** The AD-937 add-control branched on crew count: `< 2 crew` opened the NewChatModal (minting a SEPARATE thread). That convert was designed for the Captain's per-agent 1:1 default thread, but it also fired for agent-created rooms (which often have 1 crew), so adding a member to an agent room minted a brand-new chat instead of joining the existing one. **Decision (frontend):** branch on `metadata.is_default` (the Captain's 1:1 home DM) — ONLY the home DM mints via the seeded NewChatModal; EVERY other room (group OR agent-created) adds the participant in place via `addParticipant` (the Teams behavior). Tests: `GroupChatHeader.test.tsx` updated (is_default 1:1 opens the seeded picker; agent-created room adds in place).

**AD-970 — agent-initiated kickoff (Bug: an agent opens a room but the invited crew never reply).** An agent's opening message is persisted as `role="agent"`, and the AD-914 fan-out gates on `role=="captain"`, so an agent-created room sat silent until the Captain posted. **Decision:** fan an agent's opening out to the other participants — the agent-initiated analogue of a Captain turn — by reusing `group_chat_fanout` with a new `opener_id` param so the opener is excluded from round 0 (it just spoke). Triggered from the proactive create path (`_extract_and_execute_group_chats` → new `_kickoff_group_chat` helper) when the agent opened with a first message. Gated on `GroupChatConfig.agent_initiated_kickoff_enabled` (Pydantic default False; `system.yaml` enables it), bounded by the SAME AD-935 backstops (cap / convergence / `[NO_RESPONSE]` / max_agent_rounds). Lifts the deliberate AD-918 "no auto-reply on create" boundary now that the bounded cascade exists. Tests: `test_ad970_agent_kickoff.py` (5: round-0 opener exclusion, no-opener parity, gated-on fires, gated-off no-op, honest-degrade on missing store).

**AD-971 — added participants survive close + reopen (Bug: added crew vanish on reopen, list row stale).** The Captain added Lyra + Sentinel, closed the chat, reopened it — they were gone, and the CHATS list row never updated. Root cause: `ChatsPanel.handleOpen` called `setChatThread(staleListObject)` using the local `listThreads()` snapshot, which CLOBBERED the freshly-added participants in the store (the backend *had* persisted them via `addParticipant`). **Decision (frontend):** (1) new `getThread(id)` wrapper (`GET /api/threads/{id}`); `handleOpen` is now async and re-fetches the thread's CURRENT persisted state before hydrating — authoritative, and robust across a full page reload. (2) ChatsPanel rows prefer whichever thread version is fresher by `last_active_at` (the live `chatThreads` store vs the list snapshot), so a header add reflects in the sidebar row immediately. Tier-2: a failed fetch falls back to the passed thread. The history-context ask is already satisfied — `_build_session_history` feeds recent thread turns to every participant on their turn, so a newly-added member is contextualized on its next reply. Tests: `ChatsPanel.reopenPersist.test.tsx` (3: backend hydrate no-clobber, fetch-failure fallback, fresher-row merge); 3 ChatsPanel suites updated for the now-async open.

**Gates.** Python: AD-966/967/968/970 suites + AD-918/924/935/955/914/913 regressions green in isolation. UI: AD-969 GroupChatHeader (22) + AD-971 ChatsPanel suites (45) green. Full gates + commit follow.

### AD-958a: Exploration / anti-rich-get-richer term — a domain-relevant newcomer is surfaced to earn trust (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#894)

**Context.** AD-958 (#894) is the conversational trust learning loop. Its sub-part **AD-958a** is the one piece the issue says needs no live calibration and writes nothing to the trust ledger — so it is the safe, high-value first build. The prior-art survey (and my own observation of the Ezri+Yeo room) found that trust/confidence-weighted speaker selection risks **monopolisation**: a high-trust agent keeps being surfaced and a low-trust but domain-relevant agent never gets a chance to *earn* trust. The **Minimal Authority** governance axiom requires earned trust with a path for everyone.

**Decision (backend only, `chat_facilitator.py` + `config.py` + `system.yaml`).** Add a deterministic exploration bonus to the pure `ChatFacilitator.rank()`: `weight_exploration × department_relevance × (1 − trust)`. This is **optimism under uncertainty** (UCB-style), not ε-greedy randomness — the facilitator stays pure and deterministic (load-bearing for testability + reproducibility). The shape encodes the intent precisely: the bonus grows with *relevance* (gated on `department_relevance`, so an off-topic agent is never boosted) and with *un-provenness* (`1 − trust`, so a fully-trusted agent already carried by the trust term gets ~0). A domain-relevant newcomer is surfaced to earn trust; a proven agent isn't double-counted. Bounded **below** the mention weight (`weight_exploration = 0.15` live vs `weight_mention = 0.40`), so a direct address (AD-951 rule 1a) always still wins. New `GroupChatConfig.weight_exploration` (Pydantic default **0.0** = off, ranking byte-identical to pre-AD-958a; `system.yaml` sets 0.15 for the live system). It rides the existing `factors` dict (`factors["exploration"]`) for diagnostics.

**Why this is safe to build before the live observation.** It touches ONLY the facilitator ranking — it never calls `record_outcome`, so there is zero risk of poisoning the load-bearing trust ledger (the issue's chief constraint). The trust-ledger *write* core (correction/endorsement → `record_outcome(source="conversation")`) is deliberately deferred until the live Ezri+Yeo room can ground it. AD-958a only changes *who is advised/surfaced*, bounded and default-off, with all AD-915 backstops (cap, convergence, `[NO_RESPONSE]`) intact.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad958a_exploration.py` — 8 tests (pure facilitator, no fixtures): off-by-default byte-identical; surfaces the unproven domain-relevant agent over the proven one; ~0 for a high-trust agent; 0 for an irrelevant agent; never beats a direct mention (the AD-951 bound); the exact `w×dep×(1−trust)` formula is deterministic on re-run; `from_config` reads the weight; config default is 0.0. 48 passed across AD-958a + AD-915 facilitator + AD-955 room-awareness; group-chat/config blast green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-954: "Start call" reframing — the meeting toggle is a call (Teams mental model) (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#890)

**Context.** #890 asks for a first-class group/call surface: a dedicated thread-keyed window + a "Start call" step that turns the chat into a video call. AD-965 already delivered the dedicated-room *identity* (neutral group title + Chat-only surface, decoupled from the host agent's profile chrome), and AD-920/921/947/949 already shipped the live "meeting" (avatar gallery + per-agent call voice + face framing + call audio). The remaining naming gap: the control was labelled "Start/End meeting," which doesn't match the Captain's Teams mental model ("turn this chat into a call").

**Decision (frontend only, `GroupChatHeader.tsx`).** Reframe the existing meeting toggle (already a video-camera glyph, already wired to `set_meeting_active` → the AD-947 gallery + AD-949 call audio) from "Start/End meeting" to **"Start/End call"** (`aria-label` + `title`). The `data-testid="meeting-toggle"`, the persisted `metadata.meeting_active` flag, the AD-923 end-of-meeting transcript marker, and all wiring are byte-identical — this is a label change that aligns the surface with the call mental model. The underlying "meeting" terminology stays in the backend flag/marker (no migration).

**Scope note (the larger AD-954 piece remains).** A fully separate group window keyed by `thread.id` and decoupled from `activeProfileAgent` (so a group needs no host agent set at all) is a larger architectural refactor that #890 itself says to sequence last. AD-965 already achieves the first-class *visual* surface (the panel presents as a neutral room, not a host profile), so the user-visible Teams feel is delivered; the host-agent *binding* refactor is tracked as the remaining #890 sub-task (forward marker AD-954a). This AD closes the "Start call" + dedicated-identity portion.

**Tests + gates.** `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` +1 (the toggle reads "Start call" inactive / "End call" active); the AD-941 `group-chat-open.spec.ts` e2e updated to assert `aria-label="Start call"`. Full UI suite **1416 passed / 1 skipped**, `npm run build` clean, all **4 Playwright e2e passed**. No backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-965: Neutral, nameable group surface — a group is a room, not the host agent's profile (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#898)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-10).** Starting a group with Ezri + Yeo opened *Ezri's* `AgentProfilePanel` — the title bar read "Ezri (Counselor)" with her department dot, and the 6 agent-scoped tabs (Chat / Work / Memory / Profile / Health / Self-image) framed the room as one participant's profile with a second person bolted on. A group should be a neutral, nameable surface like a Microsoft Teams group chat.

**What already existed (AD-917).** The `GroupChatHeader` (rendered inside `ProfileChatTab`) already shipped the editable room title (click-to-rename → `patchThread` → `set_title(lock=True)`), the participant avatar strip, add/remove participant, the meeting toggle, and the AD-949 in-call mute. The `ChatThread.title` field + `PATCH /api/threads/{id}` endpoint already exist, and `chatDisplayName` already derives the Teams-style "callsign, callsign" name (honoring a Captain-locked custom title). So AD-965 is the **surfacing** layer, not new plumbing.

**Decision (frontend only, `AgentProfilePanel.tsx`).** Detect the group context: when `activeProfileThreadId` resolves to a thread that `isGroupChat` (≥2 crew), the panel is a ROOM. (1) **Identity** — the title bar shows the group title (`chatDisplayName`, Teams-style or the Captain's locked name) with a neutral dot, instead of the host agent's name + department framing. (2) **Tabs** — `visibleTabs` collapses to Chat-only (the work/profile/health/memory/self_image tabs are agent-scoped and meaningless for a room); `effectiveTab` falls back to `chat` in group mode. The `GroupChatHeader` inside the chat tab still owns the participant strip + rename + meeting controls (no duplication). A 1:1 (no group thread) is byte-identical — the agent identity and full tab set are unchanged.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/AgentProfilePanel.groupSurface.test.tsx` — 4 render tests (R3F/voice mocked per the AD-721d pattern): group title shows the participant-derived name (not the host agent); a Captain-locked custom title ("Bridge Sync") wins; the tab bar collapses to Chat-only on a group; a 1:1 keeps the agent identity + full tab set. Full UI suite **1415 passed / 1 skipped** (+4 over the 1411 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-962: Typing indicator during backend generation — fill the dead air before the first reply (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#896)

**Problem.** AD-960 paces the *reveal* of crew replies at human speed, but the backend group cascade (`group_chat_fanout`) takes ~10–30s of real LLM time to produce ANY reply, and the `POST /api/threads/{id}/messages` call is fully synchronous — so from the instant the Captain sends until the first reply lands there is NO on-screen signal at all. That silent window is the most "is it broken?" moment in the experience; the AD-960 pacing improvement is undercut by it.

**Decision (frontend only, additive — extends AD-952).** Reuse the AD-952 `typingAgent` store slice + `TypingIndicator` component for a generic pre-reply beat. (1) `TypingIndicator` gains an optional `verb: 'typing' | 'thinking'` (default `'typing'`) so the label reads honestly — the crew is being *asked*, no reply exists yet, so it's *thinking*, not typing. (2) The `typingAgent` slice gains an optional `verb` field (still session-scoped, no localStorage). (3) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch sets `setTypingAgent({threadId, agentId:'', callsign:'The crew', verb:'thinking'})` the instant it enters the ≥2-crew path, BEFORE the fetch — so "The crew is thinking…" shows within a frame of send. It is cleared the moment the first reply arrives (right after the AD-960 `setSending(false)`), at which point the text path's `revealRepliesProgressively` immediately re-sets a per-agent "{callsign} is typing" beat (the AD-960 reveal), and the meeting path leaves it cleared (AD-921 voice + AD-923 speaking indicator pace the crew there). The error path also clears it so it never sticks after a failed send.

**Scope.** v1 is a generic whole-crew "thinking" beat (we don't know who will respond first until the backend runs the facilitator). Naming the likely first responder via a pre-flight facilitator rank is a v2 forward marker (AD-962a), and true streaming reply delivery remains AD-935a. The indicator's render site (threadId-guarded, after the message list) is unchanged from AD-952.

**Tests + gates.** `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` +2 (default verb "typing"; "thinking" verb renders + aria-label), `useStore.typingAgent.test.ts` +1 (the verb round-trips through the slice). Full UI suite **1411 passed / 1 skipped** (+3 over the 1408 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change → no pytest. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-961: Cascade-extend-on-address — a directed peer hand-off is always answered (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#895)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-10).** AD-951 routes a directed address ("Ezri, …" / "@ezri …") to that peer as the next cascade speaker, but only WITHIN `group_chat.max_agent_rounds` (default 2). When the address landed in the LAST normal cascade round, the addressed peer never got a turn — the Captain had to manually re-prompt ("Ezri, can you respond to Yeo?"). A hand-off that goes unanswered is the opposite of natural: a human who is directly asked a question answers it.

**Decision (backend only, `thread_fanout.py` + `config.py`).** The bounded cascade in `group_chat_fanout` was a fixed `for _ in range(max_agent_rounds)`; it is now a `while` loop with a round counter that grants up to `GroupChatConfig.max_address_extensions` (new, default **1**) EXTRA rounds PAST the cap, each consumed only by a fresh **answerable** directed address, so a hand-off is always answered — bounded so a chain of mutual hand-offs (Ezri→Yeo→Ezri…) can't ping-pong forever (the absolute ceiling is `max_agent_rounds + max_address_extensions` cascade rounds). Within the normal cap the loop is byte-identical to AD-935/AD-951 (no answerability gate — the existing rounds run regardless). The extension is **only** meaningful with `agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled` on, so `max_addr_ext` is forced to 0 when that flag is off, and the default of 1 never changes a zero-config boot (the whole cascade is off there).

**The answerability gate (the subtle correctness bit a test caught).** `extract_directed_callsign` matches any leading comma/colon word, so a conversational opener like "Agreed, the variance is fine." or "Well, …" yields a phantom callsign ("agreed"/"well"). In AD-951 that is harmless (it hard-includes nobody downstream), but using the mere *presence* of an address to decide whether to EXTEND would let an opener spuriously burn an extension round. So the extension fires only when an addressed callsign resolves (via `_resolve_callsigns`, lower-cased) to a REAL participant agent_id that is NOT in the round's own speakers — a peer who can actually take the turn. Tier-2: an empty resolution map means no extension ever fires (degrades to pre-AD-961).

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad961_cascade_extend.py` — 6 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `ChatThreadStore`/`IntentBus`/registry, scripted handlers, real `GroupChatConfig`): address-in-last-round-answered-via-extension (the core fix, Scout→Ops→Scout); extension-disabled-drops-the-handoff (`max_address_extensions=0` == pre-AD-961); mutual-hand-offs-bounded-no-pingpong (every reply addresses the other → bounded at exactly `max_rounds+ext`); extension-inert-without-next-speaker-selection (forced 0 when the flag is off); no-address-in-last-round-does-not-extend (the false-opener guard — a leading "Agreed," does NOT extend); config default == 1. 37 passed across the AD-961 + AD-951 + AD-935 cascade suites; group-chat blast (fanout/thread/ad914/915/933/935/948/951/955/961/chat/config) green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-615 + BF-616 + AD-964: three group-chat test fixes — voice cutoff, [NO_RESPONSE] leak, per-height avatar centering (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

Three Captain-reported issues from a 2026-06-10 group-chat test, shipped together (all small, all in the group-chat surface). A fourth issue — the group window is bound to the host agent's profile instead of a neutral nameable surface — is filed as a design issue (AD-965, #898) rather than built.

**BF-615 — voice cutoff on long/chained replies (frontend, `ui/src/audio/meetingVoice.ts`).** The AD-921 meeting voice sequencer awaits each utterance's TTS `'end'` event, with a FIXED 20s per-utterance safety timeout for the case where TTS is unavailable and `'end'` never fires. But a long crew reply (~180 words ≈ 60–70s of speech) runs well past 20s, so the timer fired mid-utterance, the sequencer advanced to the next reply, and that reply's `speakResponse` called `speechSynthesis.cancel()` — truncating the still-speaking prior one. The LAST reply has no successor to cancel it, so it completed: exactly the Captain's "every reply cut off except the last." Fix: a new pure `computeUtteranceTimeout(text)` scales the cap with word count at a conservative slow TTS rate (`UTTERANCE_MS_PER_WORD=460`, ~130 wpm) × `UTTERANCE_HEADROOM=1.5`, floored at the old `UTTERANCE_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS=20000` (so short replies keep the 20s net). `_speakAndWait` uses `deps.utteranceTimeoutMs ?? computeUtteranceTimeout(reply.text)` — real speech still resolves early on `'end'`; the cap only fires when `'end'` genuinely never arrives, now sized to the actual reply. +4 Vitest (`meetingVoice.test.ts`): floor for short/empty, scales-above-floor for a 180-word reply, monotonic growth, option overrides.

**BF-616 — [NO_RESPONSE] leaked into the transcript (backend, `src/probos/routers/thread_fanout.py`).** The group fan-out decline check matched only a reply that was EXACTLY the marker (`reply_text.strip().upper().replace("[","").replace("]","") == "NO_RESPONSE"`). But models routinely EXPLAIN their decline in prose and then append `[NO_RESPONSE]` instead of emitting the bare marker — so "prose + marker" slipped the equality check and the marker (plus the decline-meta prose) leaked into the visible room (Ezri's "…I'll let that question breathe rather than pile on. [NO_RESPONSE]"). Fix: a module-level `_NO_RESPONSE_RE = re.compile(r"\[NO_RESPONSE\]", re.IGNORECASE)` and a substring check (`_NO_RESPONSE_RE.search(reply_text)`), matching the established `proactive.py` contract (`"[NO_RESPONSE]" in response_text`) — any decline marker anywhere suppresses the WHOLE reply (a human who decides not to respond says nothing). +2 pytest (`test_ad935_group_reactivity.py`): prose-plus-marker fully suppressed (neither marker nor prose reaches the transcript), case-insensitive marker suppressed.

**AD-964 — per-height avatar head centering (frontend, `CrewVRM.tsx` + `MeetingView.tsx`).** AD-947 framed the gallery camera at a FIXED face height (1.42m) for every avatar, so crew of different statures were cropped inconsistently (a tall avatar showed mid-chest, a short one too much headroom). Fix: `CrewVRM` gains an optional `onHeadY` callback that measures the posed scene's bounding-box crown (top-of-head, hair included; computed AFTER the A-pose + VRM0 rotation, local-Y == world-Y since each slot renders at the origin) and reports it once after load (Tier-2 — any failure skips the callback and the slot keeps default framing). `MeetingView.AvatarSlot` holds the reported `headTopY` in state; `FaceFraming` now takes a per-avatar `targetY` (crown − `_HEAD_CENTER_DROP` 0.12 = face center), positions the camera level with it and aims there, defaulting to ~1.42 until measured (prior framing preserved). MeetingView test mock camera extended with `position.set`. UI suite 1408 passed / 1 skipped (+4 BF-615), `npm run build` clean; group-chat pytest blast 576 passed. Forward marker: AD-965 (#898) neutral nameable group surface. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-960: Human-paced group-chat reveal — think-time + 60 wpm typing, and free the composer during the reveal (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Problem (Captain group-chat test, 2026-06-09).** AD-952 paced the group-reply reveal, but the cadence was a fast char-based beat (`[360,2400]ms`) tuned to "not all at once," not to "reads like a human." The Captain's spec: a crew reply should arrive at roughly human speed — a brief think-time, then a "typing" beat proportional to length at ~60 wpm. Separately, the composer was disabled for the WHOLE reveal (`disabled={sending}`), which at the old fast pace was a few seconds but at human pace would lock input for 20–40s.

**Decision (frontend only, additive — refines AD-952).** (1) `ui/src/chat/staggerReplies.ts` timing model reworked from char-based to a two-part word-based model with exported single-source constants: `computeTypingDelay(text)` now estimates composing time at `TYPING_MS_PER_WORD = 1000` (60 wpm), clamped `[TYPING_MIN_MS 800, TYPING_MAX_MS 9000]`; a new pure `computeProcessingDelay(index)` returns the think-time beat — `PROCESSING_FIRST_MS = 5000` for the first revealed reply (the crew reading the Captain's message), `PROCESSING_CASCADE_MS = 2500` for later reactions in an already-engaged exchange. `revealRepliesProgressively` shows the "{callsign} is typing" indicator for the WHOLE `processing + typing` window (no dead air), then clears it the instant the message lands, then appends — and it counts the revealed-index over NON-empty replies so an empty leading reply doesn't consume the longer first beat. (2) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch calls `setSending(false)` the moment `per_agent_replies` arrives — the composer is released so the Captain can read and reply WHILE the reveal paces in the background, instead of being locked for the full (now human-speed) reveal; the reveal is still awaited so the AD-921 meeting-voice ordering is unchanged, and the `finally` `setSending(false)` stays as an idempotent error-path safety.

**Why sequential, not parallel.** The reveal stays one-at-a-time in AD-915 facilitator order. This is temporally correct for the current relay cascade (with `max_speakers_per_turn=1`, the second agent is reacting to the first, so it MUST come after), and the Captain's own observation is that sequential is often *better* than parallel — it forces each speaker to "listen" (see the prior turn) before responding, avoiding the human group-chat failure where someone answers too fast. True parallel round-0 responses are deferred to the turn-order design issue (#897, AD-963) rather than built here.

**Tests + gates.** `staggerReplies.test.ts` reworked to the new model: word-based `computeTypingDelay` (60 wpm, clamps, overrides), `computeProcessingDelay` (first > cascade, overrides), and reveal-order asserting the new `typing → clear → append` per-reply sequence plus the first-reply-waits-longer and empty-leading-reply-doesn't-consume-first-beat invariants — 19 tests. Full UI suite **1404 passed / 1 skipped** (+7 over the 1397 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean. No backend change. The values are exported constants so the feel is trivially tunable. Forward markers: AD-961 cascade-extend-on-address (#895), AD-962 typing indicator during backend generation (#896), AD-963 group-chat turn-order policy (#897). COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-959: Lean shutdown consolidation — defer LLM-bound idle steps so shutdown never trips the AD-820 partial marker

**Problem (observed in production, 2026-06-09).** A packaged-instance shutdown stamped `shutdown_status.json` with `consolidation_result=partial, note="phase1_elapsed=39.0s"`, which AD-820 treats as not-clean → the next normal boot refuses with `UncleanShutdownDetected` (SystemExit 3) until `--force-unclean`. Root cause: the Tier-3 shutdown handler called the FULL `DreamingEngine.dream_cycle()` under the `shutdown_consolidation_timeout_s` 30s budget. `dream_cycle` is the 15-step idle-time pipeline, and at real episode volume its **LLM-bound stages** — Step 7 procedure extraction (one model call *per* success cluster), 7b evolution, 7c negative extraction, 7c-2 failure distillation, 7e observational learning, Step 11 spaced-retrieval therapy — routed through the model proxy and overran 30s. The cancelled mid-flight cycle is exactly the failure mode AD-820 was built to flag, and historically the half-written ChromaDB collection tore the HNSW index (#750). The marker even recorded a procedure (`vision_observation_collaborative_workflow`) born mid-shutdown — proof Step 7 was actively grinding when the budget blew. As episode volume grows (the active `events.db` is ~82MB) this recurs on every sleep/wake shutdown.

**Why the full cycle was never needed at shutdown.** Episodes are already persisted at creation time (BF-207); shutdown only needs the cheap learning-weight updates. Per the BF-207 design note, "partial consolidation is fine — episodes are already stored... the micro_dream handles incremental consolidation." Steps 6–15 (clustering, procedure extraction, metrics) are pure idle-time optimization that re-runs on the next dream cycle — running them inside a hard shutdown budget was unintended scope inherited from reusing `dream_cycle()` as the single consolidation entry point.

**Decision (backend only, additive).** A new `DreamingEngine.consolidate_for_shutdown() -> DreamReport` runs ONLY the in-memory, non-LLM steps the shutdown path needs — Step 0 micro-dream Hebbian replay, Step 2 weight prune, Step 3 trust consolidation — and SKIPS every LLM-bound and Chroma-writing idle step. It performs **no episodic-collection writes** (it reads `recent()` for trust, never `store()`), so it completes in well under a second and lets the subsequent `episodic_memory.stop()` close the index cleanly. Honest-degrade throughout (each step wrapped; a failure logs and the rest still run) because a clean `DreamReport` return is what lets the shutdown handler stamp a `full`/clean marker. `startup/shutdown.py` Tier-3 swaps `engine.dream_cycle()` → `engine.consolidate_for_shutdown()`; the BF-303 shield, the 30s `wait_for` (now a safety net the lean path won't hit), and the AD-820 marker logic are otherwise untouched. The deferred idle-time learning is not lost — it runs on the next normal dream cycle.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad959_shutdown_light_consolidation.py` — 10 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `HebbianRouter` / `TrustNetwork` / `DreamingConfig` + a real `_FakeEpisodicMemory` stub and a `_RecordingLLMClient`, NOT MagicMock): returns a `DreamReport`; **never calls the LLM even with success clusters**; **makes no episodic writes** (the torn-HNSW guarantee); real trust boost for a success-dominant agent; prunes below-threshold weights; micro-dream strengthens the replayed pathway; empty-memory zeros; honest-degrade when `recent()` raises; does not invoke `dream_cycle`; and a source-level wiring guard asserting `engine.consolidate_for_shutdown()` is present and `engine.dream_cycle()` is gone from the shutdown path. Two obsolete-contract shutdown-ordering tests updated to the new method name (the ordering invariant — consolidation before episodic close; close → stop_gracefully → consolidation — is preserved): `test_bf207_…::test_dream_consolidation_before_episodic_stop`, `test_bf296_…::test_phase_a_runs_before_stop_gracefully`. Blast radius (dream/shutdown/consolidat/ad820/ad828/bf207/bf303/ad825/bf296/bf602/ad959/ad551/ad567/ad568/ad572/ad574/ad428b/ad609/ad541c) green. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-955: Advisory room awareness — the facilitator as a sense organ, not a director (Natural Conversation epic, #882)

**Idea (Captain + Counselor Ezri, weighted-trust frame).** Each agent's turn carries a confidence-weighted read of what the *room* needs next, and that weight shifts with who's shown relevant expertise, who's been dominating, who's been quiet too long. The social truth: the one who's been talking a lot feels the pull to hold back; the domain expert feels the pull to speak up; and an agent that recognizes a peer has higher authority *here* can defer gracefully — not "I have nothing to add," but "Forge's signal is stronger here, I'll let that land."

**Problem this fixes — a backstop doing a director's job.** The `ChatFacilitator` (AD-915) ALREADY computes exactly this weighting every round (`SpeakerScore.factors`: mention 0.40 / recency 0.25 / department 0.25 / trust 0.10) — but it was thrown away after gating. Today an unselected agent isn't asked to defer, it's *silenced*; turn-taking in the Ezri+Yeo room isn't the agents choosing to alternate, it's `max_speakers_per_turn=1` *forcing* it. A safety cap is doing a director's job (works at 2 agents, produces "one speaks, rest mute" at 5). The fix: **determinism in PERCEPTION is fine; determinism in AGENCY is what feels robotic.** Keep the deterministic backstops (cap, convergence, max rounds), but move the *driver* into the agents' reasoning.

**Decision (instructions-first, advisory — NO dispatch change).** Surface the facilitator's per-speaker ranking to the dispatched speaker as an ADVISORY signal; the agent reasons over it. (1) Pure `chat_facilitator.build_room_signal(...)`: from the ranking + recent authorship it yields a per-agent dict — `recent_share`/`recent_window` (how much you've carried the room), `this_is_your_area` (department relevance ≥ threshold), `room_would_value` (callsign of the highest-ranked OTHER candidate = a defer/hand-off target). Returns `None` when nothing is salient. (2) `thread_fanout._fan_one_round` captures `result.scores` and, per dispatched agent, builds the signal and rides it on `IntentMessage.params["room_signal"]` (small struct, beside `is_group_chat`); a new `_resolve_callsigns` helper names the peer. Tier-2 throughout — any failure yields no signal. (3) `CognitiveAgent._conversational_room_awareness_protocol` renders it on the GROUP `direct_message` path, tying each fact to a MOVE: been carrying the conversation → lighter touch / hand off; a better-placed peer present → **defer to them by name** (an AD-951 hand-off, so deference *gives them the floor* next round) — reframed "teamwork, the mark of a confident colleague, never a shortfall" to dissolve the ego problem. The framing leads with "for your judgment, not a directive" and "most turns, simply contribute as yourself" so it self-regulates WITHOUT going quiet.

**Why advisory not gating (the naturalness bet).** A facilitator that PICKS speakers is a central scheduler for conversation — against the agent-native grain; one that PUBLISHES the room's state and lets autonomous agents decide is a sense organ feeding self-organizing agents (the Nooplex shape). And the deference Ezri described only exists if the agent has the agency to make the call — *you can't defer if you were never asked.* The hard cap stays in place: this is the lower-risk half of a two-step. **AD-956** (scale-aware enforcement: advisory below a small-N threshold, gating above) is deliberately deferred — the threshold is empirical, to be CALIBRATED after watching self-selection run *with the cap still on*, not guessed from the inside.

**Config.** `CommunicationsConfig.room_awareness_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no cost), ships ON so the Captain can observe self-selection emerge; the off-switch if the room ever reads as over-deferential.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad955_room_awareness.py` — 19 tests, BF-287 (real `CommunicationsConfig`/`ChatThreadStore`/`IntentBus`, NOT MagicMock): the pure helper (share counting, window cap, domain threshold, top-other-with-callsign selection skipping self + missing callsigns, None-when-nothing-salient); the hook (inert off-path / 1:1 / no-signal / flag-off; peer + no-peer renderings gap-safe; share numbers; the "teamwork … never a shortfall" ego-reframe regression guard; default-on; config default True); and end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` (the dispatched agent's params carry a `room_signal` naming the OTHER crew member; flag-off attaches none). Both renderings audited against the real `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` — clean. Blast-radius `-k "facilitat or fanout or thread or chat or group or cognitive_agent or config or dm or reply or pipeline or reactiv or callsign or crew_profile or ad955 or ad951 or ad950 or ad935 or ad915"` **2063 passed** (the only 4 failures are the pre-existing `TestSkillPipeline` serial-isolation flakes — same 4 seen before this work, orthogonal to a `direct_message` instruction hook), zero real regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-953: Conversational memory & callbacks — continuity without confabulation (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#889)

**Problem.** Agents replied each turn as if meeting the Captain for the first time — no "you mentioned that last time," no picking up a thread from a past exchange. A continuing presence with a shared history is one of the strongest "this is a real person" signals; an amnesiac one is an instant tell. The recalled material is already there (episodic memories + session history are injected into the reply context by AD-573/AD-723a-1), but nothing told the agent to USE it conversationally — and naively encouraging callbacks risks the opposite failure: a fabricated "as you said last week…" that never happened (the AD-592 confabulation hazard).

**Decision (backend only, instructions-first — Design Principle #6).** A new overridable hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_memory_protocol(observation)`, sibling to the AD-950 proactivity hook, returns `""` unless `intent == "direct_message"` AND `CommunicationsConfig.conversational_memory_enabled` (default **ON**, read via `getattr(..., True)` so on even when config is absent). When active it appends guidance to draw on what the agent GENUINELY recalls — the recalled memories + running conversation in its context — and weave it in naturally (pick up an earlier thread, call back to what the other person said before, let shared history shape how it addresses THIS person = recipient design), framed as the thing that makes a conversation feel continuous rather than amnesiac. The guidance carries a **hard AD-592 honesty bound stated as the top rule**: reference ONLY what is actually in the recalled material; if uncertain whether something happened, treat it as if it did not and do not bring it up; never manufacture a shared memory, a prior promise, or a callback — an invented "as you told me last week…" breaks trust far worse than no callback; when nothing genuine surfaces, speak to the present moment. The hook is invoked in the `is_conversation` instruction assembly immediately after the AD-950 proactivity hook, so it composes with (does not replace) the proactivity + group decline guidance.

**Why a cognitive_agent hook + why honest by construction.** Same surface reasoning as AD-950 (the DM/group reply path composes the CognitiveAgent `instructions` with `hardcoded_instructions=""`, so a standing order is dead here). And the instruction is grounded: the agent receives genuine recalled episodes (the `_build_user_message` sensorium renders the AD-723a-1 memory section for DM consumers), so "call back to recalled material" points at real content rather than inviting invention — the honesty bound then fences the failure mode.

**Config.** `CommunicationsConfig.conversational_memory_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no extra LLM pass, no cost), ships ON for the richness the North Star demands; the Captain's tuning knob if callbacks ever read as forced.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad953_conversational_memory.py` — 9 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `CommunicationsConfig`, the real hook bound to a `SimpleNamespace` self per the AD-950 pattern, NOT MagicMock): inert for `ward_room_notification`/`proactive_think`; 1:1 non-empty + capability-gap-safe (incl. the `lack` token); teaches callbacks ("call back"/"you mentioned" + "continuous"); recipient design ("this person"/"shared history"); honesty ("never manufacture" + "uncertain") — the anti-confabulation regression guard; applies on the group path too + gap-safe; flag-OFF == `""` for 1:1 and group; default-ON when config absent; `CommunicationsConfig().conversational_memory_enabled is True`. The rendering is audited against the real `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` (decomposer.py) — clean. Blast-radius `-k "cognitive_agent or dm or reply or pipeline or standing or group or facilitat or config or ad950 or ad953"` **1531 passed** (the only 4 failures are the pre-existing `TestSkillPipeline` serial-isolation flakes — green in isolation, unrelated to AD-953), zero real regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-952: Human response dynamics — progressive group-reply reveal + typing indicator (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#888)

**Problem.** The AD-914 group fan-out returns ALL of a round's `per_agent_replies` synchronously in one POST, and the UI rendered them in a single tight `for` loop — every crew reply materialising in the same instant. That is the single clearest "this is a bot" tell in a group chat: real people don't all answer in the same millisecond, and a wall of simultaneous text breaks the illusion the epic is chasing (a stranger couldn't tell the crew are AI).

**Decision (frontend only, additive).** Reveal the replies one at a time, each preceded by a brief "{callsign} is typing" beat whose length scales with the reply. (1) NEW pure, dependency-injected sequencer `ui/src/chat/staggerReplies.ts`: `computeTypingDelay(text)` returns a length-proportional delay clamped to `[360ms, 2400ms]` (a short "Aye." flashes by; a paragraph lingers, capped so it never stalls the room); `revealRepliesProgressively(replies, deps)` loops the replies in AD-915 facilitator order, calling `setTyping({agentId, callsign})` → `await sleep(delay)` → `setTyping(null)` → `appendReply(reply)` per reply. It builds no UI and reads no store directly (mirrors the AD-921 `speakRepliesSequentially` shape), so it is unit-testable with a fake clock; Tier-2 throughout (a throwing dep never breaks the queue; the indicator is ALWAYS cleared in `finally`, even on abort/error; `shouldContinue()` lets a thread switch stop an in-flight reveal). (2) NEW session-scoped store slice `typingAgent: {threadId, agentId, callsign} | null` + `setTypingAgent` (mirrors the AD-949 `callAudioEnabled` pattern — no localStorage). (3) NEW `ui/src/components/profile/TypingIndicator.tsx` — three amber (`#f0b060`) dots pulsing in sequence via a self-contained `@keyframes hxi-typing-blink` (the app has no global CSS file; the component carries its own motion), label "{callsign} is typing", `aria-live="polite"`, HXI #3 (no emoji) + #4 (motion = state). (4) `ProfileChatTab.sendText` group branch: the synchronous `for` loop is extracted into a shared `appendReply` closure (DRY across both paths), then — in a LIVE MEETING the AD-921 voice sequencer + AD-923 speaking indicator already pace the crew one at a time, so the text renders instantly there (byte-identical to before); in TEXT chat it runs `revealRepliesProgressively` with the real `setTypingAgent` + a real `setTimeout` sleep. The transcript renders `<TypingIndicator>` after the message list, **threadId-guarded** so a reveal only shows the beat in the thread it belongs to.

**Scope coordination.** Variable LENGTH is already taught at the instruction level by AD-950 ("Match your length to the move"); AD-952 owns the TIMING + the typing affordance, so there is no duplicate length-clause. True streaming reactivity remains the AD-935a forward marker — AD-952 paces the already-returned synchronous replies, it does not change the backend cascade.

**Tests + gates.** `staggerReplies.test.ts` (12: delay scaling/clamp/empty/overrides; reveal order, skip-empty, finally-clear, abort-before + mid-queue stop, throwing-dep resilience, empty-array), `TypingIndicator.test.tsx` (5: callsign + "is typing", aria label/live, blank-callsign fallback, no-emoji guard, pulse-motion), `useStore.typingAgent.test.ts` (4: default null, set/clear, no-localStorage). Full UI suite **1397 passed / 1 skipped** (+21 over the 1376 baseline, zero regressions), `npm run build` clean, the 4 AD-941 Playwright specs **4 passed** (the group-reply reveal is off their mocked-empty-`per_agent_replies` path — unaffected). No backend → no pytest. Forward markers: AD-952a a per-thread "natural pacing" off-switch if a power user wants instant; AD-935a real streaming once a live-refresh exists. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-951: Agent next-speaker selection — turn-allocation rule 1a for agent-to-agent hand-offs (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#887)

**Problem.** AD-950 taught agents to "hand the floor to a specific crew member ... address them directly by name (their callsign)," but nothing made that hand-off mechanically pick the next speaker. In the AD-935 reactivity cascade the next round's speakers are chosen by the AD-915 facilitator's relevance ranking (capped to 1/turn by BF-614), so when Scout says "Ops, what's your read on the variance?" the facilitator might pick Bones instead — the conversation ignores who was actually addressed. In Conversation Analysis (Sacks/Schegloff/Jefferson 1974) this is turn-allocation **rule 1a** ("current speaker selects next"): a direct address confers both the right and the obligation to speak next. The facilitator already does rule 1a for the CAPTAIN's @-mentions; AD-951 extends it to AGENT-to-AGENT hand-offs.

**Decision (backend only, routing — no new prompt text).** A new pure helper `crew_profile.extract_directed_callsign(text) -> str | None` detects a LEADING directed address — the chat-native `@yeo …` form AND, crucially, the VOCATIVE `Yeo, …` / `Yeo: …` forms (essential for AD-921 VOICE meetings, where you cannot speak an `@`). It mirrors `is_directed_mention` / BF #467 discipline: only a message *to* a peer (leading address) is a hand-off; a message *about* a peer ("I agree with @yeo") is not. In `group_chat_fanout`'s cascade loop, each prior-round reply's CLEAN text (AD-948 already stripped the `<intent>` tag) is scanned; a detected callsign other than the speaker's own is added to an `addressed` set, threaded into `_fan_one_round` → `_assemble_speaker_signals`, where a candidate whose callsign is in the set is hard-included (`mentioned=True`) exactly like a Captain @-mention. The AD-915 facilitator ALWAYS honors `mentioned` speakers (front, overriding the per-turn cap AND convergence), so the addressed peer speaks next — still bounded by `max_agent_rounds` (no infinite loop). **Honest-degrade:** a non-participant callsign matches no candidate and is silently ignored (no error, no phantom speaker); no directed address → the cascade is byte-identical to AD-935.

**Config (transitional flag, convention #14).** `GroupChatConfig.agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled: bool = False` — ships OFF (zero-config boot = AD-935 relevance-ranked), flipped `true` in `config/system.yaml` for the live system (mirroring how BF-614 enabled `agent_reactivity_enabled`). Off → the directed-address scan never runs.

**Why this composes safely.** The cascade's own-speaker exclusion (`exclude_ids = spoke_ids`) removes the round's speakers BEFORE candidates are assembled, and the addressed peer did NOT speak in the round that addressed them — so the hard-include is never cancelled by the exclude set. The scan runs on the AD-948-cleaned reply text, so the stripped `<intent>` tag can't leak a false callsign.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad951_next_speaker_selection.py` — 16 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path`, real `IntentBus(SignalManager)`, real-but-fake registry/agents with scripted `direct_message` handlers, real `GroupChatConfig`; real `_WARD_ROOM_CREW` types scout/diagnostician/counselor): the pure helper (@/vocative-comma/vocative-colon/lowercasing/end-of-string forms; bare leading word, about-mention, empty → None); `_assemble_speaker_signals` hard-include wiring (addressed → mentioned, None → no hard-include, non-participant → ignored); end-to-end through `group_chat_fanout` with a deterministic ON-vs-OFF discriminator (flag ON → vocative "Ops," pulls counselor into round 1 over the lower-order Bones; flag OFF → default pick Bones, proving the gate); non-participant hand-off ignored; no-address inert; `GroupChatConfig().agent_next_speaker_selection_enabled is False`. Blast-radius `-k "fanout or facilitat or reactiv or crew_profile or callsign or group or thread or chat or config or ad951 or ad935 or ad915 or ad914"` **1381 passed**, zero regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-950: Conversational proactivity — teach agents to ADVANCE a live conversation (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#886)

**Problem.** Sovereign agents answered and then stopped. On the live 1:1/group `direct_message` reply path the agent produced a competent answer and ended its turn — no follow-up question, no proposal, no "what about you?" — so a conversation died between Captain turns and the burden of keeping it alive fell entirely on the human. A stranger could tell instantly: humans in an engaged exchange take the conversation somewhere; a Q&A service waits to be asked. This is the CORE Turing-test lever of the epic.

**Decision (backend only, instructions-first — Design Principle #6).** The behavior lives in the CognitiveAgent INSTRUCTIONS, never in `decide()`/`act()`. (1) A new overridable hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_proactivity_protocol(observation)` returns `""` unless `intent == "direct_message"` AND `CommunicationsConfig.proactive_conversation_enabled` (default **ON**, read via `getattr(..., True)` so it's on even when config is absent). When active it appends calibrated guidance: end an ENGAGED turn with ONE forward move — a genuine follow-up question, an observation that invites a reply, or a concrete proposal/offer that gives the other party an easy opening — using recipient design (react to the SPECIFIC thing said, name it, build on it). Explicitly NOT every turn: calibrated to the Captain's engagement and the agent's own personality so it reads as conversation, not interrogation; a turn may rest when that's natural. Honest, respectful disagreement is welcomed (reflexive agreement reads as hollow); every follow-up must be grounded in what was actually said — **never invent** a question or proposal about something that did not occur (honesty preserved, AD-592). (2) When the fan-out param `params["is_group_chat"]` is set, an additional paragraph permits handing the floor to a named peer by callsign (sets up AD-951's next-speaker selection — AD-950 only PERMITS the address, it does not make the peer speak next). (3) The hook is invoked in the `is_conversation` instruction-assembly block AFTER the AD-935 group decline protocol (`_group_proto`), so it composes with — not replaces — the existing reply-only-when-substantive guidance.

**Why a cognitive_agent hook, not a standing order.** The DM/group reply path composes the CognitiveAgent `instructions` with `hardcoded_instructions=""` — a `federation.md`-style standing order is DEAD on this surface (AD-924's group standing order lives on the *proactive* path, a different surface). The only place that reliably shapes the live reply is the instruction assembly itself, so AD-950 is a hook there.

**Config flag.** `CommunicationsConfig.proactive_conversation_enabled: bool = True` — pure prompt text (no extra LLM pass, no cost, no structural change), so it ships ON for the richness the North Star demands; it is the Captain's tuning knob / off-switch if the proactivity ever reads as over-eager, not a transitional behavioral flag.

**Tests + gates.** `tests/test_ad950_conversational_proactivity.py` — 9 tests, BF-287 discipline (real `CommunicationsConfig`, the real hook bound to a `SimpleNamespace` self per the AD-934/935 pattern, NOT MagicMock): inert for `ward_room_notification`/`proactive_think`; 1:1 non-empty + capability-gap-safe + omits the group marker; teaches "forward move"/"follow-up"; calibration ("NOT on every turn" + "personality") and honesty ("never invent") clauses present (regression guards against silently becoming relentless or fabricating); group includes "hand the floor" + "callsign" + gap-safe; flag-OFF == `""` for both 1:1 and group; default-ON when config absent; `CommunicationsConfig().proactive_conversation_enabled is True`. ### AD-949: Call-scoped group/meeting voice — decouple from the Ship's-Computer `voiceEnabled` (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#885)

**Bug.** Group/meeting voice was silent even though 1:1 voice works, because the two paths gate on DIFFERENT flags. The 1:1 composer has a per-agent speaker override (`localStorage hxi_chat_tts_{agentId}`), so a 1:1 speaks regardless of any global flag. The meeting path (`useMeetingVoice.ts:50`) gated on the **global `voiceEnabled`** — the Ship's-Computer / `IntentSurface` voice that the AD-945 Engineering → Environment "voice output" toggle sets, which defaults `false`. So group/meeting voice piggybacked on the ship-computer flag and was off unless the Captain enabled the Engineering voice AND was in a meeting — exactly what BF-614 saw and triaged as "the AD-945 voice-output toggle was likely off, not a code bug." AD-949 is the structural fix.

**Decision (frontend only — a gate-flag swap + an additive in-call control).** Give the call its OWN audio gate, decoupled from `voiceEnabled`. (1) A new store flag `callAudioEnabled: boolean` (default **`true`**) + `setCallAudioEnabled` mirror the `voiceEnabled` slice MINUS the `localStorage` line — **session-scoped** (a fresh page load is audible; the Captain can mute mid-session; persisting the preference is the **AD-949a** forward marker). Default-ON is the single decoupling that fixes the bug: the hook's `meetingActive` self-gate (`useMeetingVoice.ts:49`, runs FIRST) already silences everything when no meeting is active, so `meetingActive && callAudioEnabled` means *starting a call is audible by default* WITHOUT enabling the Ship's-Computer voice. (2) `useMeetingVoice.ts:50` swaps `voiceEnabled` → `callAudioEnabled` (the one functional line; the `meetingActive` self-gate, the AD-921/922/923 `speakRepliesSequentially` sequencer, the per-agent AD-718 voice profiles, the AD-923 `speakingAgentId` seam, and the AD-922 mic echo gate are byte-for-byte intact — only the flag the gate reads changes; two JSDoc/comment lines corrected for accuracy). (3) `GroupChatHeader` (where Start/End meeting already lives, already store-wired) renders a `data-testid="call-audio-toggle"` mute/unmute button **only while `meetingActive`** — local inline speaker stroke-SVG (HXI #3 — no emoji, no `Glyphs.tsx` export so the `Glyphs.test.tsx` count is untouched), amber `#f0b060` audible / dim `#666680` muted, `aria-pressed` reflecting `callAudioEnabled`, flipping it via the store. **Name** `callAudioEnabled` (not `meetingVoiceEnabled`) reads naturally for a mute control, generalises to future 1:1 voice calls, and stays distinct from `meetingActive` (the mode flag) and `voiceEnabled` (the Ship's Computer); grep-confirmed unused. **Expected interaction (NOT a regression):** now that group voice actually plays, `speakingAgentId` becomes non-null during agent speech, so the AD-922 meeting-mic echo gate (`speaking: speakingAgentId != null`) finally engages as designed — the intended AD-922 behavior exercised for the first time. The 1:1 per-agent TTS (`hxi_chat_tts_{agentId}`), the Ship's-Computer / wake-word voice (`IntentSurface`, the AD-945 `BridgeEnvironment` toggle, the global `voiceEnabled` / `setVoiceEnabled` / `hxi_voice_enabled`), and all STT/TTS engines are byte-for-byte unchanged. The `useMeetingVoice.test.tsx` gate-flag tests migrate `voiceEnabled` → `callAudioEnabled` (verbatim rename — identical semantics, net +0); `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` gains +3 cases (hidden when no meeting / shown + `aria-pressed=true` audible by default / click mutes → `false`). Full UI suite **1376 passed / 1 skipped** (+3 over the 1373 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean; the 4 AD-941 Playwright specs **4 passed** (the meeting voice gate + group-chat header are off their seam — unaffected). No backend / REST / pytest. Forward markers: **AD-949a** persist the mute preference across sessions (localStorage, default-ON hydration), **AD-949b** also surface the control on `MeetingView`'s avatar gallery, **AD-949c** honor per-agent `hxi_chat_tts_{agentId}` overrides inside the meeting sequencer so the exact agents the Captain enabled 1:1 speak in group. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-947: Avatar camera framing — focus on faces, not feet (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#883)

**Bug.** In the meeting avatar gallery (`MeetingView` `AvatarSlot`), the crew VRM rendered showing only the **feet**. Root cause: the gallery `<Canvas camera={{ position: [0, 1.45, 0.85], fov: 28 }}>` sets the camera POSITION but no lookAt, so react-three-fiber points the camera at the default origin `[0,0,0]` (floor) — the avatar's feet. The `CrewAvatarPopout` does not have this bug because it mounts `OrbitControls target={[0, 1.42, 0]}` (face height); the non-interactive gallery slots have no controls, so nothing aimed the camera.

**Fix (frontend only, `MeetingView.tsx`).** A tiny in-Canvas `FaceFraming` helper (`useThree((s) => s.camera)` → `camera.lookAt(0, 1.42, 0)` + `updateProjectionMatrix()` once on mount, renders `null`), mounted as the first child of the gallery Canvas. Face height `1.42` matches the popout's `OrbitControls` target. `CrewAvatarPopout` and `CrewVRM` are untouched. The three MeetingView test mocks of `@react-three/fiber` gain a `useThree` stub (the mock replaces the whole module). Full UI suite **1373 passed / 1 skipped** (the 3 MeetingView files green with the new mock; net +0 tests — the R3F Canvas is mocked so the lookAt is a code-level + live-verified guard); `npm run build` clean. No backend/REST/pytest. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-948: Group-chat hygiene — strip the internal `<intent …>` self-tag from fan-out replies (Natural Conversation epic, #882/#884)

**Bug.** In a group chat, agent replies leaked the AD-722a divergence self-tag (e.g. `<intent emotion="warm">`) into the visible transcript (Captain's screenshot). The AD-722a tag is parsed + **unconditionally stripped** only on the 1:1 path (`apply_divergence_check` at `routers/agents.py:agent_chat`); the group fan-out (`routers/thread_fanout.py` `_send_one`) took the raw LLM reply and persisted/returned it **without** that strip. Internal markup reaching the human is an instant "this is AI" tell.

**Fix (backend only, `thread_fanout.py`).** `_send_one` now calls the single-source `strip_intent_self_tag` (from `avatars/divergence_detector.py`, BF-603 hardened — leading/inline/trailing, optional-quote tolerant, prose-safe) on the resolved reply text **before** the NO_RESPONSE decline check / persist / return. The strip is **unconditional** (even when divergence detection is OFF — defense-in-depth, the tag must never reach the Captain), and placed before the decline check so a decline trailing a tag is still detected. Reuse only — the regex / 1:1 call site / `apply_divergence_check` are untouched. +2 pytest (`tests/test_ad948_group_intent_tag_strip.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore`+`IntentBus`+fan-out): a quoted + unquoted tag-bearing reply is stripped in BOTH `per_agent_replies` and the persisted message rows; prose containing the word "intent" is preserved verbatim. Blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or fanout or divergence"` **607 passed**, zero regressions. No UI change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-614: Group chat — crew replied all-at-once and never to each other; an added member showed a "?" avatar

**Context.** A Captain-reported cluster of group-chat problems from an Ezri+Yeo room: (a) both agents replied to EVERY Captain message at the same time (an unnatural wall of simultaneous replies), (b) the agents never responded to EACH OTHER — only when the Captain sent, and (c) Yeo (added to the room after it was created) rendered a grey "?" avatar instead of his badge/initial.

**Root cause — (a) and (b) are ONE linked bug.** The AD-915 facilitator's `max_speakers_per_turn` defaults to `0` (= OFF, the AD-914 "all crew reply at once" behavior) and `config/system.yaml` never set it. So round 0 fanned to BOTH agents (the simultaneous wall, (a)). And the AD-935 reactivity cascade excludes a round's OWN speakers from the next round (an agent never reacts to itself) — so in a 2-agent room where BOTH spoke in round 0, round 1 had NOBODY left to react, and the cascade terminated immediately ((b)). The two symptoms share the single cause: an uncapped round 0 consumes every speaker. **(c)** is independent: the group fan-out's `_send_one` returns an empty `callsign` string when it can't resolve the added participant, and the frontend `ChatMessageRow` used `msg.callsign ?? hostCallsign` — `??` does NOT catch `''` (only null/undefined), so the badge received an empty string and `AgentAvatarBadge` rendered its `'?'` fallback initial.

**Decision.** (1) Set `group_chat.max_speakers_per_turn: 1` in `config/system.yaml` (the Pydantic default stays `0` for zero-config boot). One cap fixes BOTH (a) and (b): round 0 now picks the single most-relevant agent (an @-mentioned agent is still always included — the facilitator's hard-include is preserved), and because only one agent speaks per round the OTHER is free to react in the next round, so the cascade actually runs: Ezri → Yeo → Ezri turn-taking that references each other, bounded by `max_agent_rounds` + the convergence gate as before. (2) `ChatMessageRow` resolves the author callsign as `(msg.callsign && trim) || agents.get(authorId)?.callsign || (msg.authorId != null ? '' : hostCallsign)` — a blank reply callsign now resolves from the agents map by the real `authorId`; a genuinely unresolvable explicit author keeps the honest `'?'` (never a wrong host attribution), and a legacy/1:1 message with no author still falls back to the host. The avatar department color resolves from the same `authorAgent`.

**Not addressed here (reported, triaged):** voice ("can't hear each agent") — meeting voice gates on `meetingActive && voiceEnabled`; the voice-output toggle moved into the Engineering Bridge station (AD-945) and was most likely off (a settings state, not a code defect — verify in the station's Environment config). The "no separate meeting window" is current AD-937/938 design (add-people transitions the profile card in place). The "LLM proxy returned no response" is the BF-612/BF-289 empty-content-after-uptime surface a proxy restart clears.

**Verification.** +4 Vitest (`ChatMessageRow.test.tsx` — blank-callsign→agents-map, explicit callsign, legacy host fallback, unresolved-author→'?'); full UI suite **1373 passed / 1 skipped** (+4, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. Focused pytest `-k "group_chat or facilitat or config or fanout or thread"` **940 passed** (the `max_speakers_per_turn: 1` yaml loads cleanly; no facilitator/fanout regression). No new backend code — the facilitator already honored the cap; only the operator config value changed. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### BF-613: Meeting-view crew avatar was always the badge (the VRM was read off the never-hydrated base Agent), and the Captain had no in-meeting camera control

**Context.** In a meeting (`MeetingView`), each crew member rendered only their `AgentAvatarBadge` (the "E" glyph) instead of their VRM avatar — yet the SAME agent's VRM rendered fine in the separate `CrewAvatarPopout` window. Root cause: `AvatarSlot` read `appearance` (which carries `vrm_url`) off a **narrow cast of the store's base `Agent`** — but the base `Agent` never carries `appearance`; it is a per-agent `AgentProfileData` field hydrated on demand from `GET /api/agent/{id}/profile` (the source `AgentProfilePanel` feeds into `CrewAvatarPopout`). So `vrmUrl` was ALWAYS `undefined` in production and every slot fell to the badge. This is the BF-287 mocked-contract class: `MeetingView.test.tsx` seeded `appearance.vrm_url` **directly on the mock Agent** (`base.appearance = …`), so the test was green on a contract production never satisfies. Separately, `CaptainSlot` (AD-939) showed the Captain's camera only when it was *already* active and offered no way to start it from the meeting — the Captain asked to "turn my camera on from here to share with the meeting."

**Decision.** Two frontend-only fixes in `MeetingView.tsx`. (1) **Hydrate the crew VRM from the profile**, exactly as the popout does: `AvatarSlot` now fetches `GET /api/agent/{agentId}/profile` in a `useEffect` (cancellable, `typeof fetch` guard, `.catch` honest-degrade) and reads `vrm_url` / `expression_overrides` / `dsl.expression_resting` from the fetched `appearance` instead of the base-Agent cast; absent/failed fetch → badge (the CI/dev default with zero `.vrm` assets, and the no-backend case). Department (badge color) still comes off the store Agent. (2) **Add an in-meeting camera toggle** to `CaptainSlot`: a stroke-SVG camera button (`data-testid="captain-camera-toggle"`, `aria-pressed`, amber when on, NO emoji — HXI #3) that drives the SAME global camera the rest of the HXI uses — `startCameraStream()` when off, `stopCameraStream()` when on (both idempotent); the existing slot reflects the live stream once active.

**Verification.** The mocked tests are rewritten to the PRODUCTION contract: `MeetingView.test.tsx` no longer seeds `appearance` on the Agent — it drives a `fetch` stub keyed by agent id, and the VRM cases `await screen.findByTestId('crew-vrm-…')` (the fetch is async). +3 new `MeetingView.captain.test.tsx` cases for the toggle (present + labelled, off→`startCameraStream`, on→`stopCameraStream`). Full UI suite **1369 passed / 1 skipped** (+3 over the 1366 BF-612-era baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. **Live-verified** on the dev server (real store + components + routing): seeding a meeting fired `GET /api/agent/counselor_0/profile` (the fetch that NEVER fired before), `CrewVRM` mounted and attempted the load (`[AD-721 VRM load failed]` for the dev-only missing `.vrm` → badge, as designed), and the `captain-camera-toggle` rendered with `aria-label="Turn camera on"`. On the real backend (where the `.vrm` is the binary already shown in the popout) the identical path renders the avatar. No backend/REST/pytest change. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-946b: A bare `>` in the command palette lists every station launch (Bridge as Ship's Computer — polish, #873) — AD-946 opened the palette on a leading `>`, but `matchPaletteCommands('', …)` returned `[]`, so a bare `>` (before the Captain types a search term) rendered the CommandPalette empty-state "No matching command." instead of the full launch list — a discoverability gap: the Captain could not SEE what commands exist without already knowing a term to search. **Decision:** an empty/whitespace query now returns ALL commands — `commands.slice()`, a fresh array so a caller can never mutate the registry-derived source — so a bare `>` lists every launch (Ward Room, Chats, Crew, Personnel, Metrics, Notebooks, Records, Explorer, Work Board, System, Settings) and typing narrows it; "No matching command." now shows ONLY for a genuinely non-matching query (e.g. `>xyzzy`). This is standard fuzzy-finder semantics (an empty filter = everything) and the literal VS-Code `>`-then-nothing model (the first item is highlighted, Enter runs it). **Why it is safe (the NL guarantee holds):** the change is one line in the pure helper `matchPaletteCommands`, and BOTH call sites — `handleSubmit` (the Enter path) and the live `paletteMatches` (the render path) in `IntentSurface.tsx` — are already gated on command-mode (the leading `>`), so an empty query only ever reaches the helper once the Captain has typed `>`; a plain natural-language question (no `>`) still never calls the helper and submits byte-for-byte via `/api/chat`. The `>` trigger, the registry-as-single-source-of-truth (`buildBridgeStations`→`buildPaletteCommands`), and the presentational `CommandPalette` empty-state (unchanged — it still renders "No matching command." when handed an empty list, which now happens only on a real miss) are all untouched. Frontend only, no net test delta: the AD-946 `paletteCommands.test.ts` "empty query → `[]`" case is rewritten to "empty/whitespace query → ALL commands" + a `not.toBe(cmds)` fresh-array guard. Full UI suite **1366 passed / 1 skipped** (unchanged), `npm run build` clean. Forward marker AD-946a (voice command of stations) inherits this behavior — it consumes the same helper. COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.

### AD-940: Draggable CHATS panel (`chatsPanelPos`, GamePanel pattern) — the floating CHATS panel can now be moved by its header, so it never traps an open chat window underneath it. **Frontend only — no change to the AD-938 CHATS list/filter/open logic, no resize (forward marker AD-940a), no backend/pytest.**

**The problem (Captain-reported).** The CHATS panel was a fixed floating panel (`top:60` / `left:60` / `bottom:60`); when a chat window opened under it the Captain couldn't drag it out of the way.

**The fix.** `useStore` gains `chatsPanelPos: {x,y}` + `setChatsPanelPos` mirroring `profilePanelPos`/`setProfilePanelPos` (interface, init, action), initialised to `{x:60, y:60}` — the panel's prior on-screen origin, so enabling drag moves nothing on first render. `ChatsPanel`'s root reads the pos (`left`/`top`), and the CHATS header is a `cursor:move` drag handle (`data-testid="chats-drag-handle"`) wired with the `GamePanel.startDrag` pattern — capture the offset on mousedown, track `window` mousemove, tear the listeners down on mouseup; the New-chat / Close controls `stopPropagation` on mousedown so a click never starts a drag. The old `bottom:60` vertical pin (which would fight a free drag) becomes `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 120px)`, keeping the list bounded-scroll while the panel moves freely.

**Deviation (documented).** The build prompt said `position:'absolute'`; I kept `position:'fixed'` — it is the value of both precedents the prompt cites (`GamePanel`, `AgentProfilePanel`) and of the current code, and the mirrored drag math is viewport-coordinate (`clientX - offset`), which only positions correctly under `fixed`. `absolute` would have regressed (scroll-with-content + a coordinate-space mismatch). The init pos is the real on-screen origin `{60,60}` rather than the prompt-summary's illustrative `{24,96}`, to honor its stated "match the current on-screen position so nothing visually jumps".

**Tests & gates.** +5 Vitest (`ChatsPanel.drag.test.tsx` — the `setChatsPanelPos` action, the root rendering at a seeded pos, the header `cursor:move` + a mousedown→`window`-mousemove→mouseup sequence moving the panel, New-chat/Close NOT dragging, the HXI no-emoji guard; mocked `threadApi`, REAL store via `setState`, BF-287). Full UI suite **1328 passed / 1 skipped** (224 files; +11 over the 1317 baseline, zero regressions); `npm run build` clean. No backend → no pytest. **COMMITTED LOCAL ONLY — NOT pushed.** Forward marker: **AD-940a** (resize the CHATS panel from a corner handle, the AgentProfilePanel pattern).

### AD-939: Captain meeting slot (camera > screen > icon) — `MeetingView` now renders the Captain as the first cell of the avatar gallery, showing their live camera (preferred) or screen video when shared, else an amber stroke-SVG person icon (HXI #3). **The problem (Captain-reported).** In meeting mode the crew avatars didn't show, and the Captain themself never appeared — there was only a "You (Captain)" text chip, no video, no avatar.

**The mechanism.** Crew absence was the AD-938 hydration bug (`if (!thread) return null` short-circuited the whole gallery). Separately, `MeetingView` excludes `CAPTAIN_PARTICIPANT_ID` from the crew gallery (correct — the Captain isn't crew) but offered no Captain avatar; the live camera/screen streams (`getCameraStream()` AD-733, `getScreenStream()` AD-733-2) were already captured for the LIVE indicators but never surfaced in the meeting.

**The fix.** A new `CaptainSlot` (sibling of `AvatarSlot`) is rendered FIRST in the gallery flex row, ahead of the `crewIds.map`. It reads `useCameraStore.active` / `useScreenStore.active`, prefers the camera stream else the screen stream, and attaches the live `MediaStream` to a muted `<video autoPlay playsInline>` via a ref+effect (detach on teardown / source change); with neither active it shows an amber-tinted circle holding a stroke-SVG person glyph. The existing `captain-present` presence chip is unchanged (it is the count line; the slot is the avatar).
