**Decision B — participation-based binding (the crux), richer binding deferred (AD-927a).** A proactive turn is NOT inherently tied to a chat thread (the agent's proactive think posts to the Ward Room, not the task room), and the agent's current in-flight work-item is not cleanly available in the proactive context (noted in AD-925). The honest, minimal, faithful binding is **participation-based**: `_resolve_agent_task_room` returns the most-recently-active non-archived thread that has a `task_id` AND lists the agent as a participant (`list_threads(include_archived=False)` is already `last_active_at DESC`, so the first match wins; participants is a JSON column, filtered in Python). This builds directly on AD-925 — the auto-created task room sets the crew child-assignees (including this agent) as participants. No resolvable room → honest-degrade (suppress, strip the tag, write nothing, never crash). A richer binding off the agent's current work item is the forward marker **AD-927a**.

**Decision C — Lieutenant+ rank gate + anti-flood, all defaulted.** Three NEW `CommunicationsConfig` fields next to the AD-924 `group_chat_min_rank`: `artifact_min_rank="lieutenant"` (producing a work artifact is a normal deliverable — a lower social bar than *convening* a multi-agent room at Commander+; Ensigns cannot think proactively anyway), `artifact_max_per_turn=3`, `artifact_max_bytes=262144`. The gate is wired INLINE in `_extract_and_execute_actions` immediately after the group-chat gate, reusing the in-scope `_RANK_ORDER_DM`. The per-turn and byte caps are honest-degrade (oversize / overflow → skip that one, suppressed action, never raise). The bare opening tag of a rank-gated-out artifact is later removed by the pre-existing BF-203 hallucinated-tag cleanup — correct, the artifact path simply never ran.

**Non-goals.** No new artifact UI (the AD-797 `ArtifactDrawer` already lists + views off `activeThreadId`; a drawer mount inside a dedicated 3-pane room view is AD-929); no binary `[ARTIFACT]` upload in v1 (`text/markdown` only — binary artifacts keep the existing AttachmentStore-upload + `POST /api/artifacts` path); no richer work-item binding (AD-927a); no show-your-work status protocol (AD-928); no unified 3-pane (AD-929); no new REST route, no new `EventType`, no new `ArtifactStore`/`AttachmentStore` method; no change to `BaseAgent`, `IntentMessage`, the intent bus, or any consensus/trust path. **Tests:** `tests/test_ad927_outputs_folder.py` (+11, BF-287 — real `ArtifactStore` + real `FilesystemAttachmentStore` + real `ChatThreadStore` behind a `MagicMock(spec=ProbOSRuntime)` shell). Focused gate 30 (11 AD-927 + AD-925 + AD-924); blast-radius `-k "proactive or artifact or thread or chat or group or attachment"` 996 passed (1 pre-existing intermittent `test_browse_threads_sort_recent` timestamp flake, confirmed independent of AD-927 via stash + repeat-run). Local-only commit (the Captain reviews the epic before it goes public).

### AD-926: Inputs folder — a read-only `GET /api/threads/{thread_id}/inputs` endpoint surfacing a task room's attached files as an honest union of an additive `WorkItem.metadata["input_attachments"]` convention + AD-916 message attachments (2nd AD of the Task Workspace Rooms epic AD-925 → AD-929)

**The Input folder of the workspace room.** AD-925 makes a task fan-out auto-create one group chat with `chat_threads.task_id` set; AD-926 surfaces that room's **Input folder** — the files the crew use/process — as a read-only backend endpoint plus a thin self-contained UI list. Read-only because inputs are context, never edited in the room.

**Decision A — surface an honest union of two task-scoped sources, because a `WorkItem` has no native attachment slot.** A `WorkItem` (`workforce.py:581`) carries only a generic `metadata: dict` — there is no `attachments` / `content_hash` field (grep returns zero). So v1 returns, both scoped to a room whose `task_id` is set: (1) the **authoritative** additive convention `WorkItem.metadata["input_attachments"] = [{content_hash, mime, filename}]` (`source="task"`), and (2) the **real-today** AD-916 message attachments `msg.metadata["attachments"] = [{content_hash, mime}]` aggregated across the room's messages (`source="message"`). The two are merged and **de-duplicated by `content_hash`, task-level winning** (then message arrival order). Being honest: the work-item source is genuinely useful only once a population path exists; the message source makes the endpoint return live data the day it ships.

**Decision B — `input_attachments` is an additive convention, no schema change, population deferred (AD-926a).** The convention rides the existing free `metadata` dict (already serialized by `to_dict`), so the spec IS the migration — no `WorkItem` field, no DB change. v1 DEFINES and READS the contract; wiring a real task-creation/seed flow that WRITES it is a forward marker (**AD-926a**). The work-item source is therefore a defined-but-dormant seam until population lands — recorded honestly rather than presented as fully live.

**Decision C — honest-degrade at every seam, never raise into the response.** `get_thread` / `list_messages` are sync, `get_work_item` is async, `work_item_store` may be `None`, and `attachment_store` is a `@property` read via `getattr`. A non-task thread (`task_id` unset) returns `inputs: []`; a missing thread → 404; a `None` work-item store or a failed `get_work_item` surfaces message attachments only (Tier-2 log + continue); `size` is best-effort from `FilesystemAttachmentStore.size` (async) with `FileNotFoundError` / an absent store degrading to `size=None`. The response shape is exactly `{thread_id, task_id, inputs:[{content_hash, mime, filename, size, source}]}`.

**Decision D — reuse the existing byte endpoint; ship the UI as a self-contained drop-in.** Downloads reuse `GET /api/chat/attachments/{content_hash}` (`chat.py:985`) — no new blob store, no new content endpoint. The UI is a NEW `ui/src/components/inputs/{inputsApi.ts, InputsList.tsx}` mirroring the artifacts pane (stroke-SVG icons, no emoji per HXI #3, read-only rows, presentational — the caller passes `inputs`). Mounting it into the room / 3-pane surface is **AD-929**, not wired here, so the component stays trivially testable and AD-929 owns fetching + layout.

**Non-goals.** No write / edit / delete / upload of inputs (read-only v1); no population of `input_attachments` (AD-926a); no Output pane / artifacts (AD-927); no unified 3-pane view or mounting into the room / canvas / `GroupChatHeader` (AD-929); no new blob store or content endpoint; no change to the `AttachmentStore` Protocol, the `WorkItem` schema, or the AD-925 create path. **Tests:** `tests/test_ad926_inputs_folder.py` (+10, BF-287 — real `ChatThreadStore` + real `WorkItemStore` + real `FilesystemAttachmentStore`, direct-await `list_thread_inputs` with a `SimpleNamespace` runtime stub) + `ui/src/components/inputs/__tests__/InputsList.test.tsx` (+3, incl. a no-emoji guard). Focused gate 52; blast-radius `-k "thread or chat or attachment or workforce or input"` 746 passed; vitest 3 passed; `npm run build` clean. Local-only commit (the Captain reviews the epic before it goes public).

### AD-925: Auto-create the task-linked workspace room — `CrewTaskExecutor` opens ONE group chat for a ≥2-crew fan-out (FOUNDATION of the Task Workspace Rooms epic AD-925 → AD-929)

**The room IS the workspace.** When `CrewTaskExecutor` (AD-859) fans a parent `WorkItem` out to ≥2 distinct crew agents, AD-925 opens one task-linked group chat so the collaborators share a room while they work. A new `_maybe_open_task_room(parent_id, children)` fires at the top of `run`, immediately after the `if not children: return []` guard — the room exists BEFORE the children execute. This is the assembly-of-existing-primitives foundation the Captain ruled as Option A (extend the chat-thread + `ArtifactStore` world, NOT bridge `ConsultationWorkspace`).

**Decision A — reuse the AD-918 `create_group_chat` path, no parallel creation.** The helper calls the existing synchronous `runtime.agent_group_chat.create_group_chat(creator_id=…, title=…, participants=…, task_id=parent_id)`. Reusing it means the AD-918 per-agent cooldown + sliding-window cap + `_is_crew` participant resolution all apply unchanged — there is no second thread-creation path to keep in sync, and the storm guard is honored for free. Both `runtime.agent_group_chat` and `runtime.chat_thread_store` are public handles the executor reaches via its existing `self._runtime` (no Demeter violation).

**Decision B — the creator is the first crew child-assignee, NOT a synthetic system id.** `create_group_chat` rejects a non-crew creator (`_is_crew(creator_id)` → `error="not_crew"`) and ALWAYS auto-adds the creator as a participant. A synthetic coordinator id (e.g. `GROUP_CHAT_COORDINATOR_ID`) would therefore be both rejected AND, if accepted, would pollute the participant list. Resolution: use the first stable-sorted crew child-assignee as `creator_id` — it passes `_is_crew`, it is a participant anyway, and its `_rate_ok` budget is the natural anti-storm guard. So the final participants are exactly the crew child-assignees, and NO service change is required. A `system_created` bypass was deliberately NOT added (it would either re-introduce a non-crew participant or fork the create path — both worse than reusing a real crew creator).

**Decision C — idempotency via a new `task_id` filter on `list_threads`.** A 3-line additive `task_id` filter on `ChatThreadStore.list_threads` (mirroring the existing `project_id` clause exactly; the `task_id` column already exists since AD-791a) makes the lookup queryable. Before creating, the helper checks `list_threads(task_id=parent_id, include_archived=True, limit=1)` — if a room exists, it does nothing. A retry / re-run of the same parent finds the room and stops, so there is exactly one room per task. This is the queryable primitive AD-926/927/929 will also reuse.

**Decision D — default-OFF, doubly gated.** A new `GroupChatConfig.auto_task_room_enabled: bool = False` gates the whole helper (transitional flag, wave-10 convention #14 + the AD-918 create-storm history; the Captain flips it on after reviewing AD-925..927). The path is doubly gated: even with this flag ON, the crew pipeline that drives the executor (`agentic_dispatch.orchestrator_enabled`) itself ships OFF, so a zero-config boot creates no task rooms. The ≥2-crew gate counts DISTINCT `child.assigned_to` that resolve to crew via the shared public `is_crew_agent(agent, None)` predicate (None-guarded ontology); `< 2` distinct crew → no room. Every branch honest-degrades (Tier-2: log + return) so a disabled flag / missing collaborator / unwired substrate never breaks the fan-out.

**Non-goals.** No Input pane (AD-926); no Output/artifact tag (AD-927); no status protocol (AD-928); no UI (AD-919 already surfaces the room via `metadata.created_by_agent`); no `AgentGroupChatService` change; no `system_created` bypass; no new `EventType`; no change to `CrewOrchestrator` / `maybe_dispatch_crew` / `agentic_dispatch.orchestrator_enabled`; no `first_message` posted (that is AD-928's job). **Tests:** `tests/test_ad925_auto_task_room.py` (+8, BF-287 — real `WorkItemStore` + real `ChatThreadStore` + real `AgentGroupChatService` over the SAME store instance on both the service and the runtime stub; `_Fake*` duck stubs only). Focused gate 50 (8 AD-925 + AD-918 + AD-791 + AD-859); blast-radius `-k "crew_executor or crew_orchestrator or thread or chat or group or workforce"` 683 passed. Local-only commit (the Captain reviews the epic before it goes public).

### AD-924: Agent-facing group-chat trigger + crew awareness — direct `create_group_chat` dispatch from a proactive `[GROUP_CHAT]` tag, Commander+ rank policy in `CommunicationsConfig`, a dedicated manual (follow-up to the closed Ad-hoc Crew Collaboration epic AD-913 → AD-923)

**The emitter AD-918 deferred.** AD-918 wired the group-chat service as a bus LISTENER (`create_group_chat` subscriber) with no EMITTER — nothing parsed agent proactive output into a create, and the crew were never told the capability exists, so a crew agent literally could not open a group chat (only the Captain could, via the AD-917/919 HXI). AD-924 adds the missing three layers, mirroring exactly how the Ward Room DM capability was made usable (proactive tag extractor → standing-order instruction → crew manual).

**Decision A — dispatch is a DIRECT, synchronous `create_group_chat` call, NOT the bus.** A new `ProactiveCognitiveLoop._extract_and_execute_group_chats` (mirroring `extract_and_execute_dms`) calls `runtime.agent_group_chat.create_group_chat(creator_id=…, title=…, participants=…, first_message=…)` directly. Rationale: this matches how proactive dispatches EVERY other action (DMs → `ward_room.create_thread`, notebooks → `_records_store`, endorsements → `ward_room_router`) — direct service calls, not bus broadcasts — and `create_group_chat` is synchronous with a typed `GroupChatCreateResult` (no `IntentMessage` construction, no async round-trip). Critically it HONORS the AD-918 storm guard: `create_group_chat` runs `_rate_ok` itself, so the per-agent cooldown + 5/hour sliding-window cap apply on the direct path identically to the bus path — so there is NO new cooldown dict in `proactive.py` (DRY; the service owns the limiter). The bus `handle_intent` path is left UNTOUCHED as the forward marker for future decomposer/NL discovery.

**Decision B — the tag is `[GROUP_CHAT title="..." @cs,@cs] ... [/GROUP_CHAT]`, one module-level regex.** `title="..."` is quoted so it tolerates spaces; the participant blob is split on `[,\s]+`, each ref `lstrip('@')`, and passed raw (the service resolves each by agent_id OR callsign, dropping non-crew/unresolvable refs Tier-2). Requiring ≥1 named participant means the auto-added creator guarantees the 2+-crew floor; a title-only tag does not match and degrades cleanly (no room). The matched tag is stripped from the returned text regardless of outcome.

**Decision C — the rank POLICY lives in `CommunicationsConfig`, not `GroupChatConfig`.** A NEW `CommunicationsConfig.group_chat_min_rank: str = "commander"` sits next to `dm_min_rank`/`recreation_min_rank` (the comms rank policy), gated INLINE in `_extract_and_execute_actions` immediately after the DM block (reusing the in-scope `_RANK_ORDER_DM`), exactly mirroring the DM gate. `GroupChatConfig` keeps ONLY the AD-918 rate limits — the capability's spam budget and the comms rank policy are distinct concerns. Default `"commander"` gives Commander+ out of the box, config-overridable.

**Decision D — a dedicated `config/manuals/group-chat.md`, NOT an extension of `ward-room.md`.** The Captain ruling for this epic was explicit: the substrate is `ChatThreadStore` (AD-791), NOT the Ward Room — folding group chat into `ward-room.md` would conflate two distinct communication fabrics. `recreation.md` is the established focused-single-capability-manual precedent, and `seed_manuals` globs `*.md` so the new file is drop-in with zero wiring. The manual covers the `[GROUP_CHAT]` tag AND the AD-920→923 meeting experience (Start Meeting, avatar gallery, sequenced voice, push-to-talk). The standing order is a new `### Group Chat (Ad-Hoc Collaboration)` block in `federation.md`'s `## Communications` section (ASCII-only per the Encoding Safety rule) carrying the anti-flood guardrail ("2+ crew genuinely working a task, NOT idle proactive thinking, one room per collaboration").

**Decision E — `task_id` is omitted in v1 (forward marker).** The proactive loop has no clean handle on the agent's current work-item id (per AD-918: `work_item_id` reaches an agent only via `intent.params["work_item_id"]` during work-item dispatch; there is no persistent `current_task_id`). v1 omits `task_id`; `create_group_chat` already makes it optional. The seam for a future AD that threads the active work-item id into the proactive context is noted.

**Non-goals.** No UI (AD-917/919 cover the Captain-facing surface); no change to the AD-918 service internals (AD-924 only *calls* `create_group_chat`); no agent-to-agent auto-reply loop (the extractor opens the room + posts the optional first message, nothing more — an agent-created room has no Captain post, so AD-914 fan-out does not auto-run); no consensus gate (opening a room is reversible + low-risk — Safety Budget axiom; the cooldown + cap are the spam control, matching AD-918's `requires_consensus=False`); no bus/`handle_intent` change; no decomposer/NL exposure. **Tests:** `tests/test_ad924_group_chat_trigger.py` (+11, BF-287 — real service + real store + real `CallsignRegistry`, `MagicMock(spec=ProbOSRuntime)` shell only, all room assertions against the real store). Focused gate 27 (11 + 16 AD-918); blast-radius `-k "proactive or group or thread or chat or standing or manual"` 978 passed.

### AD-923: Meeting presence + speaking indicator + transcript writeback — wrapper-treatment speaking highlight, presence header, deterministic `role:'system'` end marker (CLOSES the Ad-hoc Crew Collaboration epic AD-913 → AD-923)

**Final AD of the ad-hoc crew-collaboration epic.** The visual + record completion of the "video call": the active speaker's avatar lights, the others dim, a presence header shows who's in, and ending the meeting writes a transcript marker back to the thread. Purely-additive FRONTEND — NO backend change, NO new pytest (the `POST /messages` endpoint, the store method, and the `system` role enum all already exist).

**Decision A — the who's-speaking highlight is a WRAPPER treatment, `CrewVRM` untouched.** `MeetingView` gains ONE optional prop `speakingAgentId?: string | null` (kept optional so AD-920's `MeetingView.test.tsx`, which renders `<MeetingView threadId=… />`, stays green); `ProfileChatTab` passes the value already destructured from `useMeetingVoice` (AD-921) and already live at the mount (it feeds the AD-922 mic echo gate). Per-slot it threads `speaking={id === speakingAgentId}` + `someoneSpeaking={speakingAgentId != null}`; `AvatarSlot` applies an amber ring (`boxShadow`) + `meetingSpeakingPulse` `@keyframes` + full opacity on the speaker, `opacity:0.5` dim on non-speakers while someone speaks, and a neutral idle state — all on the INNER avatar container `<div>`, never on `CrewVRM`. `data-speaking` on the slot root + `data-dim` on the inner container give jsdom-safe assertions (the animation itself is browser-real; jsdom ignores it). HXI #4 motion = state, amber active, co-located `<style>` idiom (mirrors `CrewCollaborationPanel.tsx:186`), no emoji.

**Decision B — presence is a count header + a Captain-present chip, no new code for join/leave.** A `meeting-presence` header renders `{crewIds.length} in meeting` + a `captain-present` chip (`You (Captain)` — the Captain is the viewer, excluded from the gallery, always present). Join/leave needs no new wiring: the gallery already re-renders on `thread.participants` change (AD-920).

**Decision C — transcript writeback is a DETERMINISTIC, client-side `role:'system'` marker — no LLM, no backend.** A thin `threadApi.appendMessage(threadId, {author_id, role, body, metadata?})` wrapper (Tier-2 honest-degrade → `null`) POSTs the EXISTING `/api/threads/{id}/messages` endpoint. In `GroupChatHeader.handleToggleMeeting`, on END ONLY and BEFORE `setMeetingActive(false)`, it appends `"Meeting ended — N participant(s): <callsigns>."` with `role:'system'`. `role:'system'` is already a valid enum value (`threads.py:71`) and SKIPS the AD-914 `role=="captain"` fan-out gate (`threads.py:291`) — no agent dispatch. Honest-degrade: a `null`/failed append NEVER blocks ending the meeting (the `await` proceeds to clear the flag regardless). The marker persists server-side and appears on next thread load — an immediate in-transcript echo would have to lift `ProfileChatTab`'s local message state, deferred to AD-923-3.

**Decision D — the marker carries crew count + callsigns, not a start time.** `meeting_started_at` is not persisted (AD-920 stores only the boolean flag), so a deterministic v1 marker uses what IS available — participant count + callsigns — rather than fabricating a duration. Start-time persistence is AD-923-2.

**Boundaries.** NO agent raise-hand / turn-request primitive (the lit avatar IS the turn signal). NO LLM-generated summary (AD-923-1). NO live in-transcript echo (AD-923-3). NO `meeting_started_at` / backend change / new store method. NO `CrewVRM` change, NO audio recording, NO full-duplex barge-in (AD-922 forward marker), NO federation, NO new config, NO `Glyphs.tsx` change.

**Consequence.** +14 Vitest across 3 new files (`MeetingView.speaking.test.tsx` 6 — lit speaker via `data-speaking`, dimmed non-speakers via `data-dim`, neutral idle, presence count, Captain-present chip, no-emoji; `GroupChatHeader.transcript.test.tsx` 4 — End appends a `role:'system'` marker AND clears `meeting_active`, append fires before clear, Start does not append, no-emoji on the composed body; `threadApi.appendMessage.test.ts` 4 — POST endpoint/method/serialized `role:'system'` body, dict-on-ok, `null` on `!res.ok`, no-emoji). One-line completion of AD-920's `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` `threadApi` mock (adds `appendMessage: vi.fn()`) since the End path now calls it. Full UI vitest green (1208 passed / 1 skipped, +14); `npm run build` (tsc -b + vite) green.

**Epic complete.** AD-923 closes the **Ad-hoc Crew Collaboration (group chat → meeting)** epic (AD-913 → AD-923). Phase 1 (text): participant management, group fan-out, turn-taking facilitator, file sharing, group-chat UI, agent-initiated chats, visibility + join (AD-913 → AD-919). Phase 2 (meeting voice + avatars): meeting mode + avatar gallery, sequenced meeting voice, Captain voice input, presence + speaking indicator + transcript writeback (AD-920 → AD-923). The Captain can create/join a group chat, promote it to a live meeting, see/hear the crew speak in turn with the speaker lit, talk back by voice, and end the meeting with a transcript marker written back to the thread. Forward markers: AD-923-1 (LLM summary on End), AD-923-2 (persist `meeting_started_at` for start-time + duration), AD-923-3 (immediate in-transcript echo), agent raise-hand / explicit turn-request, full-duplex barge-in.

### AD-922: Captain voice input to the meeting — push-to-talk STT → AD-914 group fan-out, echo-gated on `speakingAgentId`

**Context.** AD-921 made the crew speak their replies; the meeting was one-way (Captain types, crew talk). AD-922 closes the loop: the Captain TALKS, STT transcribes, and the transcript goes through the AD-914 GROUP fan-out — a two-way voice "call."

**Decision (purely-additive frontend; no backend change).** The genuine net-new is a meeting-scoped push-to-talk affordance — NOT a routing change — because `sendText` (`ProfileChatTab.tsx`) ALREADY self-routes to the group via the AD-917 branch (≥2 crew → `POST /api/threads/{id}/messages`). Three pieces: (1) NEW pure-DI hook `ui/src/audio/useMeetingMic.ts` — arms `armTransformersStt` (BF-301; not the deprecated `whisperStt`) for ONE VAD-bounded utterance, a one-shot `onTransformersTranscript` listener torn down before `submit` on every exit path (BF-319), gate inputs via live refs (BF-292), opens no new mic (taps the app-wide `startVoiceActivity` stream), reuses `getMicPermissionState`/`onMicPermissionState`, honest-degrades to typing. (2) NEW presentational `MeetingMicButton.tsx` — local inline mic SVG (HXI #3; `Glyphs.tsx` untouched). (3) EDIT `ProfileChatTab.tsx` — mount the hook with `submit: sendText`, render the button gated on `meetingActive && supported`.

**Echo gate (the load-bearing safety call).** The mic refuses to arm while ANY agent speaks, using `speaking = useMeetingVoice.speakingAgentId != null` — the meeting-wide signal, NOT BF-300's `ttsActiveRef` (host-filtered: `event.agent_id !== agentId` → skip, so it misses non-host speakers in a multi-agent meeting). This stops the Captain's mic transcribing the crew's TTS. Full-duplex barge-in (Captain interrupting agents mid-utterance) is explicitly DEFERRED to AD-923.

**Boundaries.** NO new dispatch branch / parallel POST path (`sendText` self-routes). NO change to agent voice-out (AD-921 `useMeetingVoice`/`meetingVoice.ts` consumed read-only). NO new STT engine / VAD / `getUserMedia` (reuse `transformersStt` + the app-wide mic; `voiceActivity.ts`/`transformersStt.ts`/`whisperStt.ts` untouched). NO change to the conversation/wake-word 1:1 wiring (`conversationController.ts`, `IntentSurface.tsx` STT — no AD-705a regression). NO presence/raise-hand/transcript-writeback (AD-923). NO backend change (the `POST /messages` endpoint already exists).

**Consequence.** +17 Vitest (`ui/src/audio/__tests__/useMeetingMic.test.tsx` 10 — `renderHook` + mocked `transformersStt`/`speechInput`/`wakeWord`, fake `submit`: transcript→submit-with-trimmed-text, arm/disarm one-shot, not-armed when meeting inactive / while an agent speaks / when SR unavailable / when mic denied, second-toggle cancels, empty-transcript no-submit, one-shot listener torn down; `ui/src/components/profile/__tests__/MeetingMicButton.test.tsx` 6 — render/aria/disabled/muted/no-emoji; `ui/src/components/profile/__tests__/MeetingMic.routing.test.ts` 1 — AD-917 `routeSend` mirror proving the transcript POSTs to `/api/threads/{id}/messages`, not `/api/agent/{id}/chat`). Full UI vitest green (1194 / 1 skipped); `npm run build` green. (Implementation authored by the Builder subagent; completed + tested + committed by the orchestrator after the subagent crashed pre-test/pre-commit — diff reviewed, gates re-run.)

### AD-921: Sequenced meeting voice — `onSpeechEvent('end')` await wrap over the fire-and-forget `speakResponse`, per-agent voice resolver, generation-token no-talk-over

**Second Phase-2 AD of the ad-hoc crew-collaboration epic.** When a meeting is active, the AD-914 `per_agent_replies` (in AD-915 facilitator order) are SPOKEN one at a time, each in its per-agent voice (AD-718), with the speaker's avatar lip-syncing (AD-721b). Purely-additive FRONTEND — NO backend change, NO new pytest. Zero change to `voice.ts`/`useLipSyncCapture.ts`/`CrewVRM.tsx`/`MeetingView.tsx`.

**Decision A — sequence by WRAPPING `speakResponse`, do NOT add a resolve-on-end return.** `speakResponse` is fire-and-forget (`void`, AD-738) and fires a matching `onSpeechEvent('end')` on both the browser `onend` and the server `<audio>` `ended`/`error` paths. The new pure `_speakAndWait` subscribes to `onSpeechEvent('end')` (filtered on `agent_id`, the BF-290 subscribe-before-speak one-shot) BEFORE calling `speak`, and resolves on the matching `'end'`. The only path with no `'end'` is `speakResponse`'s `(!speechSynthesis && !Audio)` early return (TTS unavailable) — a ~20s per-utterance safety timeout covers it so the queue DRAINS (avatars + transcript still render) rather than deadlocking. This keeps `speakResponse`'s signature/contract untouched.

**Decision B — the speaking→lip-sync binding already exists; AD-921 builds no lip-sync.** Passing the speaking `agent_id` to `speakResponse` fires `onSpeechEvent({agent_id})`; `CrewVRM` mounts `useLipSyncCapture({agentId})` and short-circuits on `if (e.agent_id !== agentId) return` (`CrewVRM.tsx:459`), building its viseme track from the event. One speaker at a time → exactly one gallery avatar animates. `speakResponse` cancels in-flight audio at its top, so a strictly one-at-a-time queue is both REQUIRED (two utterances would cancel each other) and SUFFICIENT (each `agent_id`-tagged utterance routes to one avatar).

**Decision C — per-agent `VoiceProfile` resolver over the existing endpoint, cached, Tier-2.** `ProfileChatTab` only fetched the HOST agent's `voiceProfile`; a meeting has many speakers. `createVoiceProfileResolver` resolves each speaking `agent_id`'s profile over the SAME `GET /api/agent/{id}/profile` endpoint (caches per `agent_id`; any failure → `undefined` = the global default voice, still emotion-modulated by `agent_id` inside `speakResponse` — distinct-voice degrades to same-voice, NEVER to silence). No new endpoint.

**Decision D — meeting gate is `meetingActive && voiceEnabled`; the per-agent localStorage TTS override is intentionally NOT applied.** The 1:1 conversation path keys TTS on a per-agent localStorage flag, but a meeting has many speakers and a single per-agent key doesn't map cleanly — the meeting-level global `voiceEnabled` governs. The hook reads both gates live via `useStore.getState()` at call time (BF-292 stale-closure discipline), keeping `speakReplies` reference-stable.

**Decision E — generation-token supersession (no talk-over across re-sends).** Each `speakReplies` batch takes a generation number; `shouldContinue` (checked before each utterance) and the `onSpeakingChange` setter both gate on `genRef.current === myGen`, so a newer Captain send supersedes the older batch and a stale `onSpeakingChange` from a superseded batch can't clobber `speakingAgentId`. `speakingAgentId` is exposed as the AD-923 presence-indicator seam but renders NOTHING in AD-921.

Gate: focused vitest 18 (`meetingVoice.test.ts` 12 + `useMeetingVoice.test.tsx` 6); full UI 1177 passed / 1 skipped (+18); `npm run build` green. Non-goals (explicit): NO Captain STT/voice-input (AD-922), NO presence/raise-hand/transcript writeback (AD-923), NO text-fanout change, NO new TTS/lip-sync engine, NO `speakResponse` signature change.

### AD-920: Meeting mode + avatar gallery — scoped `set_meeting_active` writer + `MeetingView` gallery bound to the fleet telemetry stream

**First Phase-2 AD of the ad-hoc crew-collaboration epic.** A *meeting* is a live MODE of a Phase-1 group chat — "Start Meeting" flips a persisted flag and renders every crew participant's VRM avatar at once; the chat thread stays the transcript. NO voice/STT/presence (AD-921/922/923).

**Decision A — persist `metadata.meeting_active` via a scoped, additive writer (NOT a generic metadata PATCH).** New `ChatThreadStore.set_meeting_active(thread_id, active)` does a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` read-modify-write that MERGES the JSON `metadata` column, mirroring `set_title(lock=True)`: `active=True` sets `meeting_active=True`, `active=False` deletes the key (clean "not in a meeting"); sibling keys (`created_by_agent` AD-918, `title_locked` AD-794) are preserved; returns the updated `ChatThread` or `None`. A new `UpdateThreadRequest.meeting_active: bool | None` plus an EARLY branch at the top of the `PATCH /api/threads/{id}` handler routes the flag and returns `to_dict()` (404 on missing). Scoping to one flag is **Defense-in-Depth** — a generic arbitrary-metadata PATCH would let a client clobber `created_by_agent`/`title_locked`. It survives reload and is visible to other surfaces (AD-919 `GroupChatListPanel`, the future AD-921/922/923 voice path).

**Decision B — `MeetingView` gallery iterates `thread.participants`** (crew only, excludes the `"captain"` sentinel), one `AvatarSlot` per participant: `<Canvas><CrewVRM …/></Canvas>` when the agent has a `vrm_url`, else the fallback. Reuses `CrewVRM` per participant (the roadmap's prescription) and the proven `CrewAvatarPopout` `showVRM ? CrewVRM : fallback` shape.

**Decision C — VRM-absent fallback is `AgentAvatarBadge`, NOT `ParametricAvatar`.** `.vrm` binaries are operator-provided/gitignored, so CI and most dev envs have **zero** `.vrm` — nearly every slot degrades. `AgentAvatarBadge` is a pure `<span>` (no WebGL, no R3F), so the gallery renders cleanly with no assets; `ParametricAvatar` is itself a 3D Canvas (N of them = N WebGL contexts) — wrong fallback at gallery scale. Two triggers: no `appearance.vrm_url`, or `CrewVRM.onLoadError` fires.

**Decision D — Start/End Meeting toggle lives in `GroupChatHeader`** (reuses its `thread`/`agents`/`setChatThread` wiring + `crewParticipants`), shown when `crewParticipants.length >= 1`, using a **local inline stroke-SVG video glyph** (HXI #3) — NOT a `Glyphs.tsx` export, avoiding the `Glyphs.test.tsx` export-count bump (the AD-917/919 gotcha). Amber when active, `aria-pressed` reflects the flag.

**Decision E — `MeetingView` mounts inside `ProfileChatTab`** directly below the header, gated on a reactive `meetingActive` selector over `metadata.meeting_active`. The chat is hosted per-crew-agent (`ProfileChatTab agentId=…`); the gallery iterates ALL participants (not just the host), and because the flag is persisted on the SHARED thread, opening the same group thread from any participant's profile shows the same meeting + gallery. A unified host-independent meeting surface is an AD-923 concern — not built here. No new overlay/modal/route.

**Decision F — telemetry binding via `useFleetAvatarTelemetry`** (frames → the shared `setAvatarTelemetryFrame` sink, fan-out by `agent_id`) so the stream is live while the meeting is open, independent of whether `CognitiveCanvas` is mounted (idempotent double-sink is benign). v1 per-avatar `AgentSignals` come from the existing **`deriveAgentSignals`** — NO telemetry-payload→signals converter (that's AD-921/923; the populated `avatarTelemetry` map is the forward binding those consume).

**Build finding — `tsc -b` caught type drift the editor language service missed.** `appearance` is a field of `AgentProfileData`, NOT the store's base `Agent` (which also lacks `department`). `MeetingView` therefore reads appearance via a narrow runtime-field cast (the established `GroupChatHeader` `department` precedent) and casts the `deriveAgentSignals` store argument exactly like `voice.ts:323` (`useStore.getState() as unknown as Parameters<typeof deriveAgentSignals>[1]`). The editor reported no errors on both; only the strict project build surfaced them — a reminder to always run `npm run build`, not just trust the language service.

**Tests:** +8 pytest (`tests/test_ad920_meeting_active.py`, real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path` + real FastAPI router via `TestClient`, BF-287) + 17 Vitest across 3 files (`MeetingView.test.tsx` 8, `GroupChatHeader.meeting.test.tsx` 5 SEPARATE file, `threadApi.meeting.test.ts` 4; R3F/`CrewVRM`/fleet-hook mocked per the `CrewAvatarPopout.test.tsx` precedent — no WebGL, no `.vrm`; no-emoji guard each). Backend §1 gate green (43); full UI suite 1159 pass/1 skip; `npm run build` green; thread/chat blast radius green (468).

### AD-919: Group-chat visibility surface + join — focused `GroupChatListPanel` over the dormant LeftRail

**Context.** AD-913→918 built the full group-chat backend + in-chat UI, including agent-initiated chats tagged `metadata.created_by_agent`. But the Captain had no surface to *discover* group chats — especially the ones agents started on their own — and no one-click way to join them. The roadmap framed AD-919 as "wire the dormant LeftRail (AD-719b) into a live group-chat list."

**Decision A — a focused `GroupChatListPanel`, NOT the LeftRail wire.** `LeftRail.tsx` is built but not imported by `App.tsx`; its `LeftRailThread = {thread_id, title, is_dm?}` has no `participants`/`metadata`/`created_by_agent`/Join concept, and wiring it into the root flex is a persistent-left-column layout reflow — high blast radius for the last Phase-1 AD. Delivering through it would force extending its props/types/render (breaking its "self-contained presentational shell" contract + its vitest tests). So the full LeftRail parent-wire stays forward marker **AD-719b-parent-wire** (default-flip **AD-719b-2**), untouched; AD-919 ships a new self-contained panel surfaced by a `TopNav` toggle (NotebooksPanel precedent — open-flag self-gate + NavButton + unconditional mount), the smallest additive `App.tsx`/store edit.

**Decision B — frontend-only, no backend change.** `GET /api/threads` already returns `metadata` (incl. AD-918 `created_by_agent`), `participants`, `title`, and `task_id` via `ChatThread.to_dict()`; the store's `AD791aChatThreadView` already carries `metadata?`. The group-vs-1:1 split is a pure client predicate, so no `routers/threads.py` change, no new endpoint, no pytest.

**Decision C — group predicate + the Captain sentinel.** A thread is a group chat when `metadata.created_by_agent` is truthy OR it has ≥2 crew participants (id ≠ literal `"captain"` and `agents.get(id)?.isCrew`). Join calls `addParticipant(threadId, "captain")` via the single `CAPTAIN_PARTICIPANT_ID` constant — the v1 sentinel, verified consistent across AD-914 (the `is_crew_agent` fan-out gate excludes it), AD-917 (`GroupChatHeader` strips it), and era-4/5 (Captain posts use `author_id="captain"`). Adding `"captain"` does not change the crew count (it is excluded), so it never spuriously trips the AD-914 ≥2-crew gate. (era-5 note: a future canonical captain DID / `is_captain()` helper makes this a one-line swap.)

**Decision D — open-on-click routes per-host via `threadIdByAgent`, not `activeThreadId`.** `ProfileChatTab` resolves its thread from `threadId ?? s.threadIdByAgent.get(agentId)`, and the chat tab is mounted inside one crew agent's profile panel — so an AD-917 group chat is always hosted in a crew "host" agent's tab. Open-on-click therefore picks host = first crew participant, then `setThreadForAgent(host, thread.id)` + `openAgentProfile(host)`. Wiring the row to the store's top-level `setActiveThread`/`setChatThread` would be a **silent no-op** (`ProfileChatTab` ignores them for thread selection). If no crew host resolves (agents not yet hydrated) the row still renders but the open is a Tier-2 no-op.

**Decision E — keep `Glyphs.tsx` untouched.** Reuse the shared `UserPlus` glyph for Join + a local inline stroke-SVG header glyph (the LeftRail `GlyphAgents` precedent), so `Glyphs.tsx`/`Glyphs.test.tsx` (the export-count assertion) need no change.

**Boundaries.** AD-919 is the LAST Phase-1 AD — no meeting/voice/VRM avatars (Phase 2, AD-920+), no `LeftRail.tsx` change, no `App.tsx` layout reflow, no backend change, no `Glyphs.tsx` change, no consensus gate (Join is a reversible Captain-authority participant add — Safety-Budget / Minimal-Authority). Un-joined agent-created chats sort to the top (HXI #9). **+10 Vitest** (`GroupChatListPanel.test.tsx`, real store + `vi.mock` of `threadApi` per BF-287, no-emoji guard); full UI suite 1142 pass / 1 skip + `npm run build` green.

### AD-918: Agent-initiated group chats — `create_group_chat` intent + bare-callable handler + rate-limited service

**Context.** AD-913→917 gave the Captain a full group-chat surface, but every chat was still Captain-seeded: `ChatThreadStore.create_thread` was only called by the 1:1 default-thread path and the REST handler, and AD-914 fan-out fires only on a Captain post (`role=="captain"`). A crew agent mid-task had no way to say "Bones and I need to coordinate — open a room." The AD-719a Ward Room contract froze this ("agent-to-agent without a Captain seed deferred to AD-719a-2"). AD-918 lifts that deferral on the **ChatThreadStore** substrate (the Captain ruling — NOT Ward Room).

**Decision.** A governed `create_group_chat` **intent** (roadmap-prescribed) handled by a **bare-callable bus subscriber** — `IntentHandler` is a `Callable[[IntentMessage], Awaitable[IntentResult | None]]`, and non-agent handlers already subscribe directly (`yeoman.py:242` `proactive_scan` precedent). The coordinator is a synthetic subscriber under a stable id (`group_chat_coordinator`): NO new agent, NO `_create_pools` wiring, NO registry entry. All logic lives in a new stateful `AgentGroupChatService` (`src/probos/threads/agent_group_chat.py`), constructor-injected and real-fixture testable (BF-287), mirroring the AD-915 pure/impure split. This honors the **uniform transport invariant** (Design Principle #10 — agent actions route through the bus, not a side-channel; the BF-265/267 lesson) over a bare `runtime.<svc>.create()` call from agent code. Rejected: a full `GroupChatCoordinatorAgent` utility agent (heavier `_create_pools` + registry + onboarding, no v1 benefit since decomposer/Captain-NL discovery is deferred).

**Consensus — `requires_consensus=False`, justified, not gated.** Creating a chat is reversible (`ChatThreadStore.delete_thread`) and low-risk. Per the **Safety Budget** axiom (consensus is risk-proportional) and **Minimal Authority**, a reversible non-destructive create does not warrant a quorum gate — that is reserved for destructive/irreversible intents. The genuine risk is a create-storm, addressed by a per-agent **cooldown** + sliding-window **cap** (BF-163 + BF-257 shape) on a long-lived `_create_times` dict — three new `GroupChatConfig` fields (`agent_create_cooldown_seconds=60.0`, `agent_create_max_per_window=5`, `agent_create_window_seconds=3600.0`). Budget is consumed only after the crew check, so non-crew rejections cost nothing; a rogue agent gets at most 5 rooms/hour ≥60 s apart.

**Persistence + v1/deferred seams.** An additive optional `metadata: dict | None = None` param on `ChatThreadStore.create_thread` extends the INSERT to write the existing (AD-791a) `metadata` column — NULL and `{}` both decode to `{}` via `_row_to_thread`, so every existing caller is unaffected — tagging `metadata.created_by_agent=<id>` (intended discoverability for AD-919's surface + Captain-join; no hidden channel). `task_id` is an **optional caller param** passed through to the existing column; live auto-wiring of an agent's current work item (which reaches the agent only via `intent.params["work_item_id"]` during `work_item_dispatch`) is a documented deferred seam. Decomposer/Captain-NL discovery is deferred — `CREATE_GROUP_CHAT_DESCRIPTOR` is a forward marker, not attached to a registered agent.

**Loop-safety.** Structurally no auto-reply storm in v1: (1) no agent-to-agent reply is wired; (2) the created thread has no Captain post, and AD-914 `group_chat_fanout` fires only on `role=="captain"`, so creation never triggers a fan-out; (3) the optional first message is a single persisted `role=="agent"` row that is NOT dispatched. The created thread is a normal `ChatThread` — AD-913 add/remove and a later Captain post (AD-919) fan out normally.

**Consequence.** +16 pytest (`tests/test_ad918_agent_initiated_group_chat.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore` + real `IntentBus(SignalManager(reap_interval=1.0))` + real-but-fake registry/callsign stubs + injectable fake clock; real `CallsignRegistry` for the callsign-resolution case): crew-only create + tag + creator auto-add, agent_id + callsign participant resolution, non-crew drop, task_id linkage, single first-message post, cooldown + window-cap + window-reset, empty-title + non-crew rejection (budget not consumed), the bus-handler round-trip, and the created thread driving AD-913 + AD-914 ops with no auto-fan. Focused gate green (66); `-k "thread or chat or fanout or group or intent"` blast-radius green (1005 passed, 4 skipped). No UI, no Ward Room, no new agent/pool, no consensus gate, no fan-out change.

### AD-916: File sharing in group chat — attachment refs + vision threading

**Context.** AD-913/914/915 built the text group chat (participants, fan-out, facilitator), but a chat message could not carry a file, and a vision-capable agent in a group chat could not see a shared image. The Captain's epic calls for file sharing for ad-hoc collaboration.

**Decision.** Two additive seams on the `ChatThreadStore` substrate, no schema/protocol/config change. (1) `AppendMessageRequest` (`routers/threads.py`) gains `attachment_ids: list[str]` — SHA-256 refs of files already uploaded via the existing `POST /api/chat/attachments` endpoint (bytes stored ONCE there; AD-916 references, never re-validates, mirroring `agents.py req.attachment_ids`). A new `resolve_attachment_refs(store, attachment_ids)` (`thread_fanout.py`) resolves each SHA → `{content_hash, mime}` via `FilesystemAttachmentStore.mime_for`; the append handler folds the result into `metadata.attachments` (existing JSON column) before `append_message`. (2) `group_chat_fanout` builds the AD-730/731 `vision_messages` array once from the Captain message's `metadata.attachments` via `build_chat_vision_messages` (filters `image/*` mimes, reuses `build_multimodal_messages` → exact AD-731 `attachment_ref` blocks); `_send_one` sets `params["vision_messages"]` ONLY for `vision_capable=True` participants (`callsign_registry.get_profile(agent_type).vision_capable`, mirroring the `agents.py` DM gate). The agent side already consumes `params["vision_messages"]`; the LLM client resolves the ref from `runtime.attachment_store`.

**Tier-2 honest-degrade throughout.** Unknown SHA → skipped with a warning (never fabricates a mime). Attachments-disabled or any resolution failure → plain message persisted (bytes already stored). No image refs → `vision_messages=None` → byte-identical AD-914 text-only fan-out. Vision-capable gate failure → text-only for that agent. Reuses `chat._get_attachment_store(runtime)` for byte-identical parity with the proven DM path (same on-disk root as `runtime.attachment_store`, so refs resolve); lazy imports avoid `chat.py`↔`threads.py`/`thread_fanout.py` load cycles.

**Boundaries.** v1 persists refs + threads image refs to vision agents; non-image attachments are stored+referenced+link-only — NO PDF/doc text extraction, NO new blob store, NO UI drag-drop (AD-917), NO agent-initiated attachments. `body` stays `min_length=1` (image-only messages need a caption/space until AD-917 defaults it). The AD-730-2 hard-cap/downscale/budget (DM-side) is a forward marker, not in the group fan-out. AD-914/915 dispatch+persist+facilitator paths unchanged; non-attachment messages byte-identical.

**Consequence.** +16 pytest (`tests/test_ad916_chat_file_sharing.py`, BF-287 real `FilesystemAttachmentStore` tmp dir + real `ChatThreadStore` + real `IntentBus`; e2e fan-out cases seed `chat._ATTACHMENT_STORE_CACHE[id(runtime)]`): store+ref roundtrip, ref persisted + survives `to_dict()`, vision participant receives the image ref in fan-out params, non-vision unaffected, non-image stored+referenced, unknown-SHA skip. Focused gate green (70); `-k "thread or chat or fanout or attachment or vision"` blast-radius green (666).

### AD-915: Turn-taking facilitator — relevance-ranked speaking order + convergence-gated termination

**Context.** AD-914's `group_chat_fanout` fans the Captain's turn to ALL crew-agent participants in parallel, once, and stops. With many participants this floods: every agent replies to every Captain turn regardless of relevance, and there is no termination signal when the exchange has converged. AD-915 turns the blind all-at-once into "the most relevant participants reply, in a sensible order, and the exchange stops when it converges" — the shared sequencer AD-921 (meeting voice) will reuse so avatars do not talk over each other.

**Decision.** A new **pure, deterministic, LLM-free** `ChatFacilitator` value-class (`src/probos/cognitive/chat_facilitator.py`: `SpeakerSignals`/`SpeakerScore`/`FacilitationResult`/`ChatFacilitator` with `rank`/`is_converged`/`facilitate`/`from_config`) mirrors the AD-641c `ThreadPriorityScorer` pure/impure split. `rank()` scores speakers by weighted factors (mention 0.40, recency 0.25 = anti-domination fairness, department 0.25 = Jaccard over the captain turn vs the agent's dept+type descriptor, trust 0.10 = optional injected neutral-0.5). `facilitate()` hard-includes any @-addressed agent at the FRONT (overriding both the cap and convergence), truncates NON-mentioned speakers to `max_speakers_per_turn`, and suppresses non-mentioned speakers when `is_converged()` returns True. The impure `_assemble_speaker_signals` (in `thread_fanout.py`, Tier-2 log-and-degrade on every runtime lookup) builds the snapshots; the facilitator is wired INSIDE `group_chat_fanout` between participant resolution and the `asyncio.gather`, which now iterates `result.speaking_order` — AD-914's `_send_one` dispatch+persist primitive is unchanged. A new `GroupChatConfig` (mounted on `SystemConfig` after `ward_room`) carries the cap + convergence knobs; `ChatFacilitator.from_config` reads it (None → all defaults, zero-config boot).

**Honest reuse-vs-new.** (1) AD-641c `ThreadPriorityScorer` scores **threads** (`ThreadPriorityInput` = thread snapshot), not which agent should speak — forcing it to rank speakers would be wrong-shape, so AD-915 adds a NEW pure scorer that *mirrors its pattern*. (2) The AD-583 convergence DETECTORS are substrate-coupled — `check_cross_agent_convergence` reads `RecordsStore` notebook entries and `ThreadEchoAnalyzer` reads Ward Room posts via the async `ThreadManagerProtocol` and detects *pathological echo*, not healthy agreement-termination — neither can be pointed at `chat_thread_messages` rows. Their atomic PURE primitive `probos.cognitive.similarity.jaccard_similarity(set, set)` + `text_to_words(str)` IS directly reusable (the same call `ThreadEchoAnalyzer` makes); threshold `0.6` follows the AD-614 `dm_similarity_threshold` precedent. (3) `WardRoomRouter.check_and_increment_reply_cap` is a **phantom** (does not exist) and the real Ward Room cap (`max_thread_posts`, BF-201) is the wrong substrate — the chat-substrate cap is a NEW `GroupChatConfig.max_speakers_per_turn`, default **0 = off** to preserve AD-914.

**Boundaries.** Text-only ordering — no meeting/voice/avatars/VRM (AD-920/921/922/923), no UI (AD-917), no agent-to-agent auto-reply or multi-round loop (still fans the Captain's single turn, just ordered/truncated/gated; convergence is single-turn suppression, not a self-feeding loop — AD-918). AD-914's dispatch/persist primitive (`_send_one`, the `direct_message` shape, `role="agent"` persistence, `metadata.fanout="ad914"`) is byte-identical; the facilitator only reorders/filters the `agent_ids` list. The `routers/threads.py` endpoint gate (`role=="captain"` AND ≥2 crew) is untouched. `_build_session_history` gains only an additive optional `prior=None` param (the 4-arg AD-914 call is byte-identical). Do NOT touch `WardRoomRouter`, `ThreadPriorityScorer`/`ThreadPriorityService`, `check_cross_agent_convergence`, `ThreadEchoAnalyzer`, or the `chat.py` AD-719 branch. No LLM calls anywhere; no new EventType/store/API route/consensus gate (Captain-authority, fully reversible ordering — Minimal Authority). All defaults make AD-914 inert (cap 0; convergence below `min_messages=4`/`min_agents=2`).

**Consequence.** +21 pytest (`tests/test_ad915_turn_taking_facilitator.py`, BF-287 real `ChatThreadStore` + real `IntentBus(SignalManager(reap_interval=1.0))` + real-but-fake registry/callsign/ontology — no MagicMock): pure ranking/truncation/convergence/mention-override cases, the impure assembly helper (mention detection, recency from prior, department relevance + ontology-absent fallback + neutral trust), and the `group_chat_fanout` integration invariant (AD-914 two-agent path unchanged; converged thread suppresses with the Captain message still persisted and no new agent rows; @-mention in a converged thread dispatches only the mentioned agent; 4-arg `_build_session_history` back-compat). Focused gate green (68); `-k "thread or chat or fanout or facilitat or convergence or priority"` blast-radius green (677).

### AD-914: Group-chat fan-out + cross-agent visibility on ChatThreadStore

**Context.** AD-913 made a thread's participant set mutable, but a multi-participant `ChatThreadStore` (AD-791) thread was still N blind 1:1s: the only reply path (`POST /api/agent/{id}/chat`) targets one agent and injects only client-supplied history, so two agents in the same thread never saw each other. The transient @-mention fan-out (AD-719, `routers/chat.py`) resolves callsigns, passes blind `session_history: []`, and does not persist — the roadmap's `AD-719a-wire` marker deferred wiring it into a persistence layer. AD-914 delivers that on the `ChatThreadStore` substrate, implementing the AD-719a contract (Captain messages are the seed; agents observe each other once both are in the thread; agent-to-agent without a Captain seed stays deferred to AD-918).

**Decision.** Extend the existing `POST /api/threads/{thread_id}/messages` handler (the least-invasive seam — the Captain turn is already persisted there). After the append + AD-793 project-touch, if `body.role == "captain"` AND the thread has ≥2 crew-agent participants (`is_crew_agent(runtime.registry.get(pid), runtime.ontology)` — naturally excludes the literal `"captain"` sentinel and any non-crew/unresolvable id), call a new focused module `routers/thread_fanout.py` (`group_chat_fanout` / `crew_agent_participants` / `_build_session_history`). Fan-out dispatches the `direct_message` intent to each crew participant in parallel via `runtime.intent_bus.send` (targeted request/reply, **not** `broadcast`; mirrors the 1:1 `agent_chat` path), reads `IntentResult.result`, and persists each reply as a `role="agent"` `chat_thread_messages` row (`metadata.fanout="ad914"`). Cross-agent visibility is a server-side `session_history` built from `list_messages(before=captain_msg.created_at, limit=1000)` tail-sliced `[-20:]` (the store is `ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT ?`, so a bare limit returns the OLDEST N — the tail-slice is load-bearing), mapped to `{"role": <callsign|Captain|system>, "text": body}` (the `cognitive_agent.py` consumer reads the `text` key; agent rows labelled by callsign). The Captain's current turn rides `params["text"]`, excluded from history. The response gains `per_agent_replies` only when fan-out fires; every other case returns `msg.to_dict()` byte-identical to before.

**Boundaries.** Fan the Captain seed out ONCE in parallel and STOP — no agent-to-agent auto-reply (AD-918), no turn-taking facilitator / convergence gating (AD-915), no file handling (AD-916), no `create_group_chat` intent (AD-918). All agents in a turn receive the SAME history snapshot (sequential turn-taking where B sees A's same-turn reply is AD-915). The chat.py AD-719 branch is untouched (a future AD-914a may unify the shared parallel-dispatch shape — forward marker only). No change to `IntentMessage`/`IntentResult`/`BaseAgent`/`IntentBus` or the `ChatThreadStore` public API (reuses `list_messages(before=...)` + `append_message`). No config field — the history window is the module constant `_FANOUT_HISTORY_LIMIT=20`. The 1:1 `agent_chat` endpoint and the Ward Room `multi_agent.py` contract are untouched (AD-914 implements the WardRoom rules on the `ChatThreadStore` substrate, not in WardRoom).

**Consequence.** +15 pytest (`tests/test_ad914_group_chat_fanout.py`, real `ChatThreadStore` + real `IntentBus(SignalManager(reap_interval=1.0))` + a real-but-fake subscribed handler that records the injected `session_history`, BF-287; no MagicMock at the store/bus boundary). Per-agent dispatch and the whole gate are Tier-2 log-and-degrade — one agent's failure (no subscriber → `(no response)`, raising handler → `(delivery failed)`) never blocks the others, and the gate-check runs inside the guard so even a minimal runtime without a `registry` degrades to a plain append (caught by `test_project_touch.py`, whose `_FakeRuntime` has no registry). Focused gate `test_ad914 + test_ad913 + test_ad791` green (47); thread/chat/fanout/intent blast-radius green.

### AD-913: Chat-thread participant management

**Context.** The ad-hoc crew-collaboration epic (group chat → meeting; Captain's ruling 2026-06-07) is built on the AD-791 `ChatThreadStore` — a SQLite-backed, Teams-style group-DM where `participants` is a first-class JSON `list[str]` column — **not** the Ward Room forum. The store could `create_thread`, `get_thread`, `update_thread`, `set_title`, and `append_message`, but there was **no way to mutate the participant set of an existing thread**, so "start a 1:1, then add crew" and "the Captain joins an agent-created chat" had no substrate. AD-913 is the foundation AD the rest of the epic (AD-914 fan-out, AD-919 join) calls.

**Decision.** Two synchronous, idempotent store methods placed next to the `set_title(lock=True)` `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` precedent: `add_participant(thread_id, agent_id)` appends the agent if absent; `remove_participant(thread_id, agent_id)` drops every copy if present (defensive against a pre-existing duplicate). Each runs a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` read-modify-write of the JSON `participants` column for race safety, returns the updated `ChatThread` (or `None` when the row is missing — the `update_thread` return-shape precedent), and bumps `last_active_at` via the injected `self._clock()` **only on the mutating path**. Idempotency is a **true no-op**: re-adding a present member or removing an absent one performs no write and no activity bump, but still returns the (unchanged) thread. Two REST routes on the existing `threads` router: `POST /{thread_id}/participants` (body `ParticipantRequest.agent_id: str = ""` + an explicit `if not agent_id.strip(): 400` — deliberately NOT `Field(..., min_length=1)`, which would yield `422`; this makes both *missing* and *empty* → `400`) and `DELETE /{thread_id}/participants/{agent_id}` (an empty path segment simply fails route matching; removing an absent-but-nonempty agent is the 200 no-op). Both return `thread.to_dict()`, `404` on a missing thread, `503` via `_get_store` when the store is absent.

**Boundaries.** No fan-out / cross-agent visibility / message broadcast (that is AD-914) — AD-913 only mutates the participant list. No `AgentRegistry` validation (pure list ops; a future AD may gate `agent_id`). No change to the `ChatThread` dataclass, the `chat_threads` schema, or `to_dict()` (the `participants` column already existed). `api.py` is unchanged (the `threads` router is already imported and registered, so the new routes ride that registration); the legacy `/api/agent/{id}/chat` path and the Ward Room are untouched; no UI (AD-917/919).

**Consequence.** +14 pytest (`tests/test_ad913_participant_management.py`, real `ChatThreadStore` on `tmp_path` per BF-287, no MagicMock at the substrate boundary; a deterministic monotonic clock drives the two `last_active_at` assertions). 8 store-level (append, idempotent no-duplicate, bumps/does-not-bump `last_active_at`, missing-thread `None`; remove, absent-is-noop, missing-thread `None`) + 6 REST-level (add happy/404/400-empty/400-missing, remove happy/404). Focused gate `test_ad913_participant_management + test_ad791_chat_threads` green (32); thread/chat blast-radius green (416, no regressions).

### BF-612: Empty-content 200 → recycle the LLM connection pool and retry once

**Context.** After ProbOS had been up for ~11-18 hours under continuous proactive load, DMs to crew agents began returning `(no reply — agent's LLM endpoint returned empty content; check upstream proxy/endpoint at the configured tier)` (the BF-289 surface). Restarting the **proxy** fixed it; restarting **ProbOS** fixed it; the failure also self-recovered after an idle gap. Live triage isolated the fault to the runtime, not the proxy: a fresh `Invoke-RestMethod` to the Copilot proxy at `127.0.0.1:8080` returned real content even at Ezri's full ~14k-char prompt size, while the same agent through the runtime's pooled `httpx.AsyncClient` got empty content. The Captain confirmed the longer history — ProbOS previously ran for days without LLM connectivity issues, and something introduced the instability. Mechanism: the LLM client holds one long-lived `httpx.AsyncClient` per `base_url|format` with keep-alive sockets. When the proxy rotates its upstream Copilot session in the background (token refresh) it keeps the TCP socket open; the runtime reuses a pooled connection now bound to a dead upstream session, so the proxy answers **HTTP 200 with empty content** — no transport error, so `raise_for_status()` passes and the empty reply surfaces as BF-289. Under continuous load the socket never idles past the keep-alive expiry, so it is reused indefinitely; a proxy restart "fixes" it only by force-closing every socket. (AD-835, 2026-05-31, was the most recent prior touch of `llm_client.py` and matched one reported timeline, but it only added the system-prompt suffix and did not alter connection handling — correlation, not cause.)

**Decision.** Reproduce the proxy-restart fix in-process. (1) Centralise client construction in `OpenAICompatibleClient._build_client(tier)` (single source of truth, shared by `__init__` and the new refresh path). (2) Add `async _refresh_client(tier)` — closes the tier's stale `httpx.AsyncClient` (Tier-2 log-and-degrade: a close failure is logged and a fresh client is installed regardless) and rebuilds it via `_build_client`, so tiers sharing a `base_url|format` pool recover together. (3) In the `call()` fallback loop, after `_call_api` returns, detect an empty-content reply (`not response.content and not response.content_blocks and not response.error and api_format != "ollama"`) and, **at most once per tier per call** (guarded by a `_refreshed_tiers` set), call `_refresh_client` and retry the same tier on a fresh socket. A genuinely empty upstream therefore costs one extra call and then surfaces empty as before (no spin); a stale socket recovers transparently.

**Boundaries.** OpenAI/proxy path only — the Ollama-native path is excluded (local server, no upstream-session rotation). Tool-call replies carry `content_blocks` and are never treated as empty, so the SWE-harness path is untouched. Multimodal/vision replies that legitimately have empty `prompt` text are unaffected because the guard keys on `response.content`/`content_blocks`, not on the request shape. No behavioural change when the endpoint is healthy: a non-empty first reply takes exactly one `_call_api` call as before, and the empty-content reply that survives the single retry still reaches BF-289 unchanged. No new config field; zero-config boot is byte-identical. BF-289's detection/reporting is intentionally left in place as the last-resort surface when even the fresh socket returns empty (genuine upstream outage).

**Consequence.** +12 pytest (`tests/test_bf612_empty_content_retry.py`, real `OpenAICompatibleClient` per BF-287, patching only `_call_api`/`_build_client`): `_build_client` URL-normalisation + auth header; `_refresh_client` installs-new/closes-old/survives-close-failure; empty→content recovery, one-refresh-per-tier guard, no-refresh on healthy reply, tool-call not treated as empty, Ollama path not recycled. `tests/test_llm_client.py` (35) and `tests/test_ad835_tier_adaptation.py` (6) green. The restart-the-proxy ritual is no longer needed for the stale-socket failure mode.

### AD-912: Generalize 1:1 notebook persistence from Yeoman-only to all crew agents

**Context.** AD-911 let the Yeoman durably save a Captain-requested note from a 1:1 chat (`[NOTEBOOK slug]…[/NOTEBOOK]`), but scoped both the teaching hook and the `DmReplyPipeline` persistence to `agent_type == "yeoman"`. The Captain pointed out that creating a notebook entry from a 1:1 conversation is a general crew capability — notebooks are already a universal agent capability on the proactive / Ward-Room path (`extract_and_execute_actions` is not crew-gated and `extract_and_execute_notebooks` already resolves callsign + department generically). Scoping the 1:1 path to one agent was an artificial restriction.

**Decision.** Bring the 1:1 path to parity with the proactive path by removing the two Yeoman-only gates. (1) `CognitiveAgent._conversational_notebook_protocol` (the base hook) now teaches the `[NOTEBOOK topic-slug]…[/NOTEBOOK]` reply tag to **any** agent that has a records store wired (honest-degrade to `""` without one, via `getattr(self, "_runtime", None)` so a runtime-less or store-less agent is never told it can save notes the substrate cannot back — the AD-592 confabulation lesson), instead of returning `""` by default. (2) `YeomanAgent` drops its now-redundant override and inherits the base hook (DRY). (3) `DmReplyPipeline.step_4i_notebook_parse` removes the `agent_type != "yeoman"` gate: it persists for **any** agent via `extract_and_execute_notebooks` (which keys the note by the agent's callsign and runs the AD-550 dedup gate), and a final **safety-net unwrap** strips any markers that survive (no store wired, a write failure, or the proactive loop unavailable) so the Captain never sees a raw block regardless of agent or substrate state.

**Boundaries.** No new store, no new consensus gate, and no change to `extract_and_execute_notebooks` itself (it was already generic — the Yeoman scoping lived only in the hook override and the pipeline gate). The base hook is still overridable, so an agent can tailor the framing (Open/Closed). The honest-degrade gate is unchanged — an agent without a records store is taught nothing and persists nothing.

**Consequence.** +11 pytest (`tests/test_ad912_crew_notebook_generalization.py`, real `RecordsStore` + real `ProactiveCognitiveLoop` + real `DmReplyContext` per BF-287: the base hook teaches any agent with a store / honest-degrades without a store or runtime / is gap-regex-safe, the Yeoman now inherits the base hook, the pipeline step persists for a non-Yeoman crew agent under its own callsign, and the safety-net unwrap keeps the inner text when the proactive loop is unwired). The AD-911 suite was updated to match (the former "non-Yeoman unwraps without persisting" test now asserts the non-Yeoman crew agent persists). `tests/test_ad726_dm_reply_pipeline.py`, `test_ad845`, `test_ad869`, `test_ad870`, `test_bf599`, `test_ad550_notebook_dedup.py`, `test_yeoman_agent.py`, `test_proactive*.py` all green. Any crew agent the Captain DMs can now durably save a note to its own notebook when asked.

### AD-911: Yeoman notebook persistence from 1:1 Captain DMs

**Context.** The Captain asked Yeo (the Yeoman, AD-766) in a 1:1 chat to "save this to your notebook"; Yeo emitted a `[NOTEBOOK spacex-ipo-trade-setup]…[/NOTEBOOK]` block and replied "Done — that's saved." Nothing was persisted. Trace: a 1:1 Captain chat hits `agent_chat` → `direct_message` intent → the **`DmReplyPipeline`** post-LLM cleanup chain, which has **no notebook extractor** (only `[DM]`, `[MESH]`, `[CREATE_TASK]`, etc.). Notebook persistence (`records_store.write_notebook` with the AD-550 dedup gate) lived **only** on the proactive / Ward-Room path (`ProactiveLoop.extract_and_execute_actions`, reached from `ward_room_pipeline`). Worse, the 1:1 system prompt explicitly tells agents "Do NOT use any structured output formats," so Yeo emitting the tag at all was off-script and nothing was listening for it. The Yeoman — whose entire role is record-keeping — could not save a note when the Captain asked. The note survived only as an episodic memory, not a durable record.

**Decision.** Scope the fix to the Yeoman (the Captain's record-keeper) so other agents' 1:1 replies are byte-unaffected. Three additive pieces: (1) An overridable base hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_notebook_protocol(observation) -> str` (default `""`), appended in `_decide_via_llm`'s `is_conversation` branch next to the BF-599 capability block and the AD-845 task protocol. `YeomanAgent` overrides it to teach the `[NOTEBOOK topic-slug]…[/NOTEBOOK]` reply tag — **honest-degrade**: returns `""` when `runtime._records_store` is absent, so Yeo is never told he can save notes the substrate cannot back (the AD-592 confabulation lesson). All tag text is `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`-clean. (2) `ProactiveLoop.extract_and_execute_notebooks(agent, text) -> (cleaned, actions)`, a lean writer that mirrors `extract_and_execute_dms`: parses `[NOTEBOOK slug]…[/NOTEBOOK]`, runs the AD-550 read-before-write dedup gate, calls `write_notebook`, and strips the markers. It deliberately omits the proactive path's AD-552/553/554/555 anti-flooding telemetry (which targets autonomous repetitive writes, not explicit low-frequency Captain requests). (3) `DmReplyPipeline.step_4i_notebook_parse`, registered after `step_4b_dm_outbound_parse` and before `step_5_episodic_store` (so the stored episode shows cleaned text): for the Yeoman it calls the new extractor; for any other agent (or when the proactive loop is unwired) it unwraps stray markers (keeps inner text, removes tags) so the Captain never sees a raw block, and persists nothing.

**Boundaries.** No new store, no new consensus gate, no change to the proactive notebook path (its full telemetry stack is untouched — zero regression risk there). The base hook returns `""` so every non-Yeo agent is byte-unaffected (Open/Closed). The 1:1 "no structured formats" instruction is unchanged for everyone except Yeo, who now receives the explicit notebook affordance only when a records store is wired.

**Consequence.** +14 pytest (`tests/test_ad911_yeoman_notebook.py`, real `RecordsStore` + real `ProactiveCognitiveLoop` + real `DmReplyContext` per BF-287: base hook returns `""`, Yeo hook teaches/degrades on the store, gap-regex-safe, the lean writer persists + strips + dedups + skips empty blocks + no-ops without a store, and the pipeline step persists for the Yeoman / unwraps-without-persisting for a non-Yeoman / no-ops without a marker). `tests/test_ad726_dm_reply_pipeline.py`, `tests/test_ad845_yeo_chat_task_creation.py`, `tests/test_ad869_mesh_read_inline.py`, `tests/test_ad870_yeo_delegation_threshold.py`, `tests/test_ad550_notebook_dedup.py` all green. When the Captain asks Yeo to save a note in 1:1 chat, it is now durably written to Ship's Records and Yeo's "saved it" is true.

### AD-910: Yeoman personal standing orders + Bridge department assignment

**Context.** Yeo (the Captain's Yeoman, AD-766) had **no** personal standing orders. `config/standing_orders/` keys the Tier-5 agent file as `{agent_type}.md`, and no `yeoman.md` existed, so `compose_instructions` loaded only the federation + ship tiers for him. Separately, the legacy department fallback `_AGENT_DEPARTMENTS` in `standing_orders.py` had no `yeoman` entry — `get_department("yeoman")` returned `None`, and since the conversational compose call passes no explicit `department`, Yeo also missed the Bridge department tier (`bridge.md`) that the Counselor (`"counselor": "bridge"`) inherits. Yeo was running on federation + ship orders alone, with none of his AD-766 role expressed as standing orders.

**Decision.** Two additive config/data changes. (1) `config/standing_orders/yeoman.md` — Yeo's Personal Standing Orders, modeled on `counselor.md`'s section structure (Role / Standards / Boundaries / Cadence / Personality) and aligned with the AD-766 `_ROLE_RULES`: act in the Captain's name for admin; triage proactive scans into one digest; delegate specialist work via @-mention; maintain the Captain's standing orders and surface conflicts; never make tactical/financial/destructive decisions without approval. It adds an explicit **Honesty About Your Capabilities** section ("Never claim to have done something you did not do… only report a note as saved when it is genuinely written to durable storage") — the standing-order seam against the confabulation the Captain observed (AD-911 is the code seam). (2) `_AGENT_DEPARTMENTS["yeoman"] = "bridge"` so Yeo inherits the Bridge department protocols like the Counselor. The `YeomanAgent.department = "Bridge"` class attribute (and the `test_yeoman_agent` assertion on it) is unchanged.

**Boundaries.** Content/config only — no code path beyond the one-line department map entry. The Tier-5 agent file loads unconditionally (independent of department), and the existing Bridge mapping (`counselor`) is untouched (Open/Closed).

**Consequence.** +6 pytest (`tests/test_ad910_yeoman_standing_orders.py`: the file exists with the right header, `compose_instructions(agent_type="yeoman", …)` includes the personal orders + a role phrase + the honesty clause, `get_department("yeoman") == "bridge"`, the Counselor mapping is unchanged, and an unmapped agent still returns `None`). Yeo now composes with all the standing-order tiers his Bridge-officer role warrants.

### BF-611: Web search must parse DuckDuckGo result blocks before truncating — raw HTML spent the budget on page chrome

**Context.** `WebSearchAgent` (AD-248, `agents/utility/web_agents.py`) fetches `https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=<query>` through the mesh, then hands the body to its LLM to extract the top results. `perceive()` set `obs["fetched_content"] = body[:8000]` — the **raw, unparsed** DuckDuckGo HTML truncated at 8000 chars. The DDG page emits a large `<head>`/inline-CSS block, a header banner, and the search `<form>` *before* the first `<div class="result results_links results_links_deep web-result">`, so the 8000-char budget was consumed by page chrome and the result `<div>`s were cut off. The LLM never saw any result entries. This is exactly what Yeoman reported on a live SpaceX-IPO search: *"The HTML was cut off before the actual result entries rendered… I won't invent search results."* — an honest-degrade landing where the agent should have had data. The sibling `PageReaderAgent` already does the right thing (strips tags via `re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body)` **before** truncating); `WebSearchAgent` lacked the equivalent parse-before-truncate step. `http_fetch`'s 1 MiB `MAX_BODY_BYTES` cap was *not* involved — the DDG page is well under 1 MiB; the 8000-char slice in `perceive` was the truncation.

**Decision.** Parse the DuckDuckGo result blocks into structured `{title, url, snippet}` entries *before* applying any char budget, mirroring `PageReaderAgent`'s clean-before-truncate pattern. Three module-level helpers in `web_agents.py`: `_strip_tags(fragment)` (tag strip + `html.unescape`), `_decode_ddg_url(href)` (extracts the real target from DDG's `//duckduckgo.com/l/?uddg=<url-encoded>&rut=…` redirect, falls back to scheme-completing a `//` href or passing through), and `_parse_ddg_results(body, max_results=10)` (regex over `result__a` title anchors and `result__snippet` blocks, paired by index — DDG emits one snippet per result in parallel order; a result missing a snippet gets `""` rather than being dropped). `_format_ddg_results` renders the parsed entries as a compact `Result N: / Title / URL / Snippet` block. `WebSearchAgent.perceive` now sets `fetched_content` to the formatted parsed results (capped at 8000 chars of *result text*, not page chrome); when nothing parses it honest-degrades to the tag-stripped body (readable context, never raw markup) so the LLM can explain what came back without fabricating (enforced by the existing instructions).

**Boundaries.** Touches only `agents/utility/web_agents.py` (three helpers + the one `perceive` body). No change to `_mesh_fetch`, `http_fetch.py`, `PageReaderAgent`, or the mesh/consensus path. The instructions string is unchanged (it already says parse the provided results and never fabricate). No new store, no config, no events.

**Consequence.** +7 pytest (`TestBF611DdgParsing` in `tests/test_utility_agents.py`, real HTML fixture with 9000 chars of `<head>` chrome ahead of two result `<div>`s — asserts the parser extracts title/url/snippet, decodes the `uddg` redirect, respects `max_results`, returns `[]` on no results, and that `perceive` hands the LLM the parsed entries with the page chrome stripped). `tests/test_utility_agents.py` (70) and `tests/test_bf599_yeo_web_research_delegation.py` green. Yeo's web searches now receive actual result entries (title + URL + snippet) instead of truncated boilerplate, so a genuine search returns results rather than an honest-but-empty degrade.

### AD-902: Per-agent developmental skill management surface

**Context.** BF-610 fixed the Service Record's `Skills 0` contradiction by relabelling the two skill systems, and in doing so surfaced a real gap: there is no per-agent skill *management* surface. **Cognitive** (T2, `SKILL.md` instruction-knowledge) skills are rank/department-gated and not individually editable — they follow the agent's billet — but **developmental** (T3, proficiency-tracked) skills are acquired through `AgentSkillService` (AD-428) per agent, and the Captain had no way to acquire, re-level, or retire one from the personnel console. The service already had `acquire_skill`, `assess_skill`, and `exercise_skill`, plus a `suspended` record field and an `assessment_history` field, but no soft-suspend verb, no Captain-driven proficiency override, and no HTTP/UI surface.

**Decision.** Two thin additive layers over the existing AD-428 service — no new store, no parallel state, no consensus gate. **Backend (`skill_framework.py`):** `AgentSkillService.suspend_skill(agent_id, skill_id, suspended=True)` flips the existing `suspended` flag on a held record (returns `None` when not held; preserves proficiency and `assessment_history` across the SQLite round-trip, so a reinstate restores the full record rather than re-acquiring at FOLLOW), and `update_proficiency(agent_id, skill_id, new_level, source="assessment", notes="")` sets a new `ProficiencyLevel`, refreshes `last_exercised`, appends an audit entry to `assessment_history`, and emits `SKILL_REGRESSION` on a downward move else `SKILL_EXERCISED`. **HTTP (`routers/crew.py`, prefix `/api/crew`):** `GET /{id}/skills` (lists all records incl. suspended, joined with their definition `name`/`category`, honest-degrading to empty), `POST /{id}/skills` (acquire, surfacing the unmet-prerequisite `ValueError` as a 400), `PATCH /{id}/skills/{skill_id}` (re-level via `update_proficiency` and/or suspend/reinstate via `suspend_skill`), `DELETE /{id}/skills/{skill_id}` (soft-suspend). **UI (`SkillManagement.tsx`, mounted in the AD-897 Service Record skills section):** a `DEVELOPMENTAL SKILLS` panel with acquire, single-click level-up, two-step confirm level-down, two-step confirm suspend, and one-click reinstate.

**Governance.** No new consensus gate (Minimal Authority). Every verb is a Captain-authority proficiency edit, and every one is reversible: a level change appends to `assessment_history` rather than overwriting history, and the destructive verb is a **soft-suspend** (`DELETE` flips the `suspended` flag, it does not drop the record) so a suspended skill can be reinstated with its full proficiency and history intact (Reversibility Preference). The two destructive affordances in the UI (level-down, suspend) are gated behind a two-step confirm, and the server's rejection `detail` (a 503/400/404 or the unmet-prerequisite message) is surfaced to the Captain rather than swallowed.

**Boundaries.** Touches only `AgentSkillService` (two new verbs over the existing record shape — `suspended` and `assessment_history` already existed), the already-registered `crew` router (four new routes, no `api.py` change), and the AD-897 Service Record (one mounted child). No new store, no `EventType`/events migration, no consensus/trust core change. Cognitive (T2) skills are explicitly NOT made editable here (they are billet-gated, not per-agent), the skill-definition catalog CRUD is AD-898's surface (not duplicated), and the BF-610 count display is unchanged. `acquire_skill`/`assess_skill`/`exercise_skill` and the AD-887 unified-profile path are untouched.

**Consequence.** +8 pytest (`tests/test_ad902_skill_management.py`, BF-287 real `AgentSkillService` + `SkillRegistry` on `tmp_path` through an in-process FastAPI `AsyncClient`) + 7 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/SkillManagement.test.tsx`). Full backend gate green (15669 passed, 22 skipped); the AD-897 (5) and full personnel Vitest suite (36) still green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The Captain can now manage a crew member's developmental skills — acquire, re-level, suspend, reinstate — from the personnel console, closing the gap BF-610 named.

### BF-610: Service Record "Skills 0" contradicted the cognitive-skill list — count and list measured different skill systems

**Context.** The AD-897 Service Record's **Skills & Proficiency** section showed a single unlabeled `Skills` count taken from `rec.skill_count`, then rendered the agent's cognitive-skill list directly beneath it.
