Looking at Yeoman's record, the Captain saw `Skills 0` sitting above four populated cognitive skills (`communication-discipline`, `leadership-feedback`, `notebook-quality`, `self-image-awareness`) — a self-contradiction that read as a bug.

**Root cause.** The two numbers measure two different skill systems. `rec.skill_count` is the **developmental** (T3, proficiency-tracked) skill count from `AgentSkillService.get_profile().total_skills` (acm.py block 5) — agents acquire these through commissioning/training, and Yeo has none. The listed items are **cognitive** (T2, `SKILL.md` instruction-knowledge) skills from `cognitive_skill_catalog.get_descriptions(department, rank)` (acm.py block 7), gated by the agent's crew identity, with their own `cognitive_skill_count` field. The UI labelled the developmental count simply `Skills` and gave the cognitive list no count header, so the two were visually conflated.

**Decision.** Relabel the developmental count `Developmental skills` and add a `COGNITIVE SKILLS (N)` subheader (`sr-cognitive-skills-header`) above the cognitive list, where `N = rec.cognitive_skill_count ?? cognitiveSkills.length`. Both counts are now honest and each matches what it labels; no contradiction. Pure presentation change — no backend touched; the ACM already supplied both `skill_count` and `cognitive_skill_count`.

**Consequence.** `ui/src/components/personnel/ServiceRecord.tsx` skills section updated; the AD-897 Vitest suite seeds `cognitive_skill_count` and asserts both the `Developmental skills` label and the `COGNITIVE SKILLS (1)` header (5 tests, still green). Surfaces the real gap the Captain also flagged — there is no per-agent skill *management* surface yet (cognitive skills are rank/department-gated, not per-agent; developmental skills are acquired via `AgentSkillService`); that is scoped as the AD-902 proposal, not part of this fix.

### AD-899: Tool certification management view (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 11 — #863)

**Context.** AD-894 gave each crew agent a tool-certification facet backed by the `ToolPermissionStore` — active grants (and restrictions) joined with the tool registry catalog — and a governed HTTP surface (`GET /api/crew/{id}/tools`, `POST` to grant, `DELETE /{grant_id}` to revoke), with the ship-wide tool catalog at `GET /api/tools`. AD-899 is the Captain-facing admin console over that surface, framed as PQS-style qualification: the asset-management counterpart to the personnel record. The authority model (a grant is a Captain-authority `ToolAccessGrant`, recorded for audit; revoke is a soft, reversible, audit-retained revocation) already lives behind the endpoints; AD-899 surfaces it, it does not re-implement it. This is the final AD of the epic.

**Decision.** A new `ui/src/components/personnel/ToolCertifications.tsx` that browses the tool catalog (`GET /api/tools`, honest-degrading to empty), carries a self-contained crew selector (`GET /api/crew/roster`) so the view is decoupled from the roster master pane, and on selection lists the agent's active certifications (`GET /api/crew/{id}/tools`). It exposes two verbs: **grant** (a `tool-grant-form` — a catalog tool select, an `observe`/`read`/`write`/`full` permission select, an optional reason — client-validating that a crew member and a tool are chosen before `POST /api/crew/{id}/tools`, surfacing the server `detail` inline) and **revoke** (a two-step `Revoke` → `Confirm revoke` red affordance, `DELETE /api/crew/{id}/tools/{grant_id}`). Restrictions (`is_restriction`) render with a red `RESTRICTION` flag alongside elevations. The view mounts in the console behind a third header view-switcher tab (`personnel-tab-tools`, the `view` type extended to `roster`|`skills`|`tools`, defaulting to `roster`) in its own `personnel-tools-pane`.

**Governance.** No new consensus gate (Minimal Authority). AD-899 is a thin UI over the AD-894 endpoints; granting and revoking a tool are audited Captain-authorized `ToolAccessGrant` edits whose authority model and audit trail live entirely in the backend `ToolPermissionStore` and are not bypassed. A grant is reversible and a revoke is a soft, audit-retained operation, so neither warrants a consensus gate; the destructive revoke is nonetheless gated behind a two-step confirm, and the server's rejection `detail` is shown to the Captain rather than swallowed.

**Boundaries.** No backend code is touched — AD-899 consumes the AD-894 crew-tool endpoints and the `GET /api/tools` catalog only. The AD-896 console shell gains a third view-switcher tab and a `personnel-tools-pane`, but the master-detail body and the AD-898 skills pane are preserved and `roster` remains the default view, so every AD-896/AD-897 testid and behavior renders unchanged. The crew selector is self-contained (it does not couple to the console's `selectedId`), and no skill action is added; the per-agent skill library is AD-898.

**Consequence.** +6 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/ToolCertifications.test.tsx`). The AD-896 (8) suite remains green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The Captain can now certify and revoke a crew member's tool qualifications from the personnel console, with restrictions flagged and the server's protection errors surfaced inline. **This completes the Crew Personnel Management epic (AD-891 → AD-901, eleven ADs).**

### AD-898: Skill Library management view (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 10 — #862)

**Context.** AD-895 gave the skill-definition library (`runtime.skill_registry`) a delete verb and a governed HTTP surface (`GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/skills/definitions`) with two Minimal-Authority guards (built-in PCC never deletable, in-active-use never deletable) and validation (duplicate `skill_id`, dangling prerequisite). Client-side validation blocks a submit with a missing name (or missing `skill_id` on create) before any request; the AD-895 server-side rejections are surfaced inline (`skill-form-error` for create/edit, `skill-row-error` for retire). The view mounts in the console behind a new header view-switcher (`personnel-view-tabs`, Roster ↔ Skill Library, defaulting to `roster`).

**Governance.** No new consensus gate (Minimal Authority). AD-898 is a thin UI over the AD-895 endpoints; the built-in-PCC and in-active-use delete guards, the duplicate/dangling-prerequisite validation, and the whole protection model live entirely in the backend registry verbs and are not bypassed. The destructive retire action is gated behind a two-step confirm, and the server's protection errors are shown to the Captain rather than swallowed.

**Boundaries.** No backend code is touched — AD-898 consumes the AD-895 skill-definition endpoints only. The AD-896 console shell gains a view-switcher and a `personnel-skills-pane`, but the master-detail body (roster pane + record pane) is preserved and remains the default view, so every AD-896/AD-897 testid and behavior renders unchanged. No skill-assignment (grant/revoke per agent) or tool action is added; the tool certification view is AD-899.

**Consequence.** +5 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/SkillLibrary.test.tsx`). The AD-897 (5) and AD-896 (8) suites remain green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The Captain can now author and retire skill definitions from the personnel console, with the AD-895 protections surfaced inline.

### AD-901: Standing Orders & Directives management view (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 9 — #865)

**Context.** AD-900 added the governed HTTP surface over the `DirectiveStore` (issue/approve/revoke/amend a runtime directive), and AD-897 rendered the read-only four standing-order tiers inside the Service Record. AD-901 joins them: the Captain needs to *act on* an agent's standing orders from the personnel console, not just read them. The directive endpoints already enforce the chain-of-command authorization and the approval state machine (Captain `CAPTAIN_ORDER`s land ACTIVE; lower-authority directives stay PENDING_APPROVAL) — AD-901 makes that gate visible and operable, it does not re-implement it.

**Decision.** A new `ui/src/components/personnel/StandingOrders.tsx` that extends the Service Record's Standing Orders section into a two-part view: (1) the read-only four-tier composed orders (AD-893) — the same `sr-order-tier-{tier}` rows, lifted out of `ServiceRecord` and passed down as a `tiers` prop so the AD-897 testids and behavior are preserved — and (2) a Directives panel bound to AD-900. The panel fetches `GET /api/crew/{id}/directives` (honest-degrading to an empty list), lists active + pending-approval directives, and exposes three governed actions: **issue** a Captain's order (`content` + `priority`, `POST /api/crew/{id}/directives`, surfacing the authorization `detail` inline on a 400), **approve** a pending directive (`POST /api/crew/directives/{id}/approve`), and **revoke** with a two-step confirm (first click reveals "Confirm revoke", second issues `DELETE /api/crew/directives/{id}`). Pending directives are amber/awaiting with an Approve affordance; active directives are teal. `ServiceRecord` renders `<StandingOrders agentId tiers={tiers} />` inside its `sr-section-orders`.

**Governance.** No new consensus gate (Minimal Authority). AD-901 is a thin UI over the AD-900 endpoints; the authorization model (`authorize_directive`) and the PENDING_APPROVAL → ACTIVE approval state machine live entirely in the backend and are not bypassed. The view surfaces the existing approval gate (a Captain explicitly approving a pending lower-authority directive) rather than introducing a new authority. Revoke is a governing/destructive action and is gated behind a two-step confirm.

**Boundaries.** No backend code is touched — AD-901 consumes the AD-900 directive endpoints and the AD-893 tiers (passed as props) only. The AD-897 Service Record's other five sections, the AD-896 console shell, and the store slice are untouched except for the one tier-rendering block in `sr-section-orders` being replaced by `<StandingOrders>`. The AD-897 `sr-order-tier-{tier}` testids and the 600-char tier truncation are preserved. The `PATCH` (amend/FRAGO) endpoint is left unconsumed in this view (issue/approve/revoke cover the epic's stated surface); no skill or tool actions are added.

**Consequence.** +5 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/StandingOrders.test.tsx`). The AD-897 (5) and AD-896 (8) suites remain green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. The Captain can now issue, approve, and revoke an agent's directives directly from the service record; the immutable four-tier `.md` orders remain read-only as designed.

### AD-897: Service Record detail view — the ESR (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 8 — #861)

**Context.** AD-896 shipped the Crew Personnel Console window with a master roster and a deliberately empty detail pane. AD-897 fills that pane with the per-agent personnel profile — the Workday-style Electronic Service Record. The three backend reads it needs already exist: the ACM consolidated profile (`GET /api/crew/{id}/record`, AD-892, which the endpoint augments with a `billet` block and `active_assignments`), the four standing-order tiers (`GET /api/crew/{id}/standing-orders`, AD-893), and the certified tool grants (`GET /api/crew/{id}/tools`, AD-894). The design constraint is that the personnel record must surface **both** qualification homes — the AD-894 tool certifications and the AD-595d billet qualification standing — which are distinct subsystems that the console renders side by side.

**Decision.** A new read-only `ui/src/components/personnel/ServiceRecord.tsx`, mounted into the AD-896 detail pane (replacing the placeholder) and keyed on the selected `agent_id`. A single `useEffect` fetches all three endpoints in parallel via a `safeJson` helper that returns `null` on a non-ok or thrown response, so each facet degrades independently. The record body is accepted only when it carries an `agent_id` facet — a roster-shaped or null body is rejected and the view falls back to the roster `summary` props passed down from the console, so the Identity header always renders even when the record fetch fails. Six progressive-disclosure sections: **Identity & Role** (callsign, post/billet, department, rank, lifecycle, Big-Five personality bars), **Skills & Proficiency** (count, avg-proficiency bar, cognitive-skill list), **Qualifications** (certified tools with restrictions flagged red, AND billet qualification standing — qualified vs. missing tests), **Duties & Active Assignments** (configured watch-bill duties + in-flight work), **Standing Orders** (the four tiers, present/absent distinct), **Experience** (trust, earned agency, episode count). Every empty facet renders a calm empty state.

**Governance.** No consensus gate (Minimal Authority). AD-897 is a read-only display surface — it consumes the three existing read endpoints and renders them; it issues no mutations. The grant/revoke and skill-edit write actions are explicitly deferred to AD-898/899.

**Boundaries.** No backend code is touched — AD-897 consumes the existing `/record`, `/standing-orders`, and `/tools` read endpoints only. The AD-896 console shell, store slice, and roster master pane are untouched except for the one-line detail-pane mount of `<ServiceRecord>`. The AD-896 test's obsolete placeholder-text assertion (`"Service record detail loads here."`) was updated to assert the `service-record` view mounts — a faithful consequence of AD-897 replacing the scaffold the AD-896 test asserted. The grant/revoke (AD-899) and skill-edit (AD-898) actions are out of scope.

**Consequence.** +5 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/ServiceRecord.test.tsx`). UI typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) clean. The console now renders a complete per-agent service record; AD-898/899 layer the management (write) actions on top.

### AD-896: Crew Personnel Console shell — the Ship's Office (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 7 — #860)

**Context.** The Crew Personnel Management epic needs a *home* in the HXI — a dedicated window through which a Captain reviews and manages the crew's service records, skills, qualifications, standing orders, and assignments. The design constraint (from the epic spec) is that this is a *separate experience* — the Ship's Office — **not** another tab on the existing agent profile panel. The AD-837 Ward Room (`ui/src/components/wardroom/WardRoomPanel.tsx`) already established the three-mode window pattern (`docked` ↔ `floating` ↔ `maximized`) with drag, resize, and `localStorage`-persisted geometry; AD-896 mirrors that pattern for a second independent window. The backend roster surface (`GET /api/crew/roster`, AD-892) already exists.

**Decision.** A new `CrewPersonnelConsole` window component plus an independent store slice, wired into the App shell.

1. **Store slice (`useStore.ts`).** Reuses the WardRoom `WardRoomDisplayMode`/`WardRoomWindowRect` types (no new geometry vocabulary). Four fields — `personnelConsoleOpen`, `personnelDisplayMode`, `personnelWindowRect` — seeded from a new exported `loadPersonnelLayout()` (defaults `mode='floating'`, rect `{x:120,y:80,w:880,h:660}`; log-and-degrade `try/catch` that falls back to the default rect on malformed JSON). `persistPersonnelMode`/`persistPersonnelRect` writers persist under the `probos.personnel.mode`/`probos.personnel.rect` keys (independent of the WardRoom keys, so the two windows remember their own geometry). Four actions — `openPersonnelConsole`, `closePersonnelConsole`, `setPersonnelDisplayMode`, `setPersonnelWindowRect` — are shaped exactly like the WardRoom precedent (persist-then-`set`).
2. **Component (`components/personnel/CrewPersonnelConsole.tsx`).** Master-detail layout. The master (left) pane is the crew roster bound to `GET /api/crew/roster`, fetched in an `open`-gated `useEffect` into component-local state, department-grouped with rank badges reusing the CrewRosterPanel `DEPT_COLORS`/`RANK_LABELS` conventions. Selecting a row sets a component-local `selectedAgentId`; the detail (right) pane is a deliberate **placeholder** (`data-testid="personnel-record-pane"`) that AD-897 (Service Record) fills in. Header chrome carries Dock/Undock, Maximize/Restore (hidden when docked), and Close stroke-SVG glyphs (`Glyphs.tsx`, amber active `#f0b060`). Floating mode adds a header drag handle and a bottom-right resize handle, both with the WardRoom add-on-mousedown/remove-on-mouseup window-listener discipline and min-size clamps (480×360). A failed fetch honest-degrades to an empty roster ("No crew aboard.") rather than crashing the shell.
3. **App wiring (`App.tsx`).** A `PERSONNEL` `NavButton` (testId `personnel-toggle`) in the TopNav People group, and `<CrewPersonnelConsole />` mounted in the App return alongside `<WardRoomPanel />`/`<CrewRosterPanel />`.

**Governance.** No consensus gate (Minimal Authority). AD-896 is a read-only window shell — it fetches the roster and renders it; it issues no mutations. The detail pane is a stub. The console is purely a viewing surface at this stage, so there is no governed action to gate.

**Boundaries.** No backend code is touched — AD-896 consumes the existing `GET /api/crew/roster` only. The roster list and `selectedAgentId` are component-local state (not promoted to the global store): only the window's open/mode/rect — which the launch NavButton and persistence need — live in the store, keeping the store change minimal. The WardRoom store slice, component, and `probos.wardroom.*` keys are untouched. The right detail pane is a placeholder by design; the AD-897 Service Record fills it.

**Consequence.** +8 Vitest (`ui/src/components/personnel/CrewPersonnelConsole.test.tsx`). UI typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) clean. The Ship's Office is launchable from the TopNav and renders the live roster; AD-897 builds the service-record detail into the placeholder pane.

### AD-900: Governed directive authoring surface (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 6 — #864)

**Context.** The personnel console needs to issue, approve, revoke, and amend standing-order directives. The `DirectiveStore` (AD-386, `runtime.directive_store`) is the evolvable runtime overlay that `compose_instructions` merges as tier 6 on top of the immutable four-tier `.md` standing-order files. It was already writable, but only through the `/order` and `/directives` shell CLI — there was no HTTP surface, so a Captain could not author or manage a directive from the manning view. The chain-of-command authorization model (`authorize_directive`) and the approval state machine (`create_directive`: Captain `CAPTAIN_ORDER`→ACTIVE, lower-authority→PENDING_APPROVAL until `approve`) already exist and are the governance gate.

**Decision.** A thin HTTP surface over the **existing** governed write path — six endpoints on `routers/crew.py` (prefix `/api/crew`), plus a `_serialize_directive` helper that projects `RuntimeDirective` to the personnel-record shape `{id, directive_type, content, status, priority, issued_by, target_department}`.

1. **`GET /{agent_id}/directives`** — resolves `agent_type` via the registry (404 unknown), returns every non-inactive directive (`store.all_directives(include_inactive=False)`) targeting that type or the `"*"` broadcast, including PENDING_APPROVAL items so the approval queue is visible; honest-degrades to `{directives: [], count: 0}` when the store is absent.
2. **`POST /{agent_id}/directives`** (`{content, priority?}`) — issues a `CAPTAIN_ORDER` at `Rank.SENIOR`, resolving the target department via `runtime.ontology.get_agent_department` with a `standing_orders.get_department` fallback. 503 no store, 404 unknown agent, 400 missing content, 400 with the authorization `reason` (e.g. a duplicate) when `create_directive` returns `None`.
3. **`POST /directives/{id}/approve`** — promotes a PENDING_APPROVAL directive to ACTIVE (`store.approve`); 404 unknown/not-pending.
4. **`DELETE /directives/{id}`** — soft-revoke (`store.revoke(revoked_by="captain")`); 404 unknown.
5. **`PATCH /directives/{id}`** (`{content}`) — FRAGO amend-in-place (`store.amend`); 400 missing content, 404 unknown/not-amendable.

Mirroring the `/order` CLI, every mutation calls `standing_orders.clear_cache()` to invalidate the composed-instruction cache.

**Governance.** No new consensus gate is introduced, by deliberate Minimal-Authority design. The directive write path is *already* governed: `authorize_directive` (unchanged) is the chain-of-command gate, and `create_directive` enforces the approval state machine — a Captain `CAPTAIN_ORDER` lands ACTIVE immediately (the existing AD-386 policy: the Captain has top authority), while every lower-authority directive stays PENDING_APPROVAL until explicit `approve`. Re-gating an already-governed, single-actor (Captain) authoring action behind agent consensus would invert the chain of command. Every mutation is **reversible** (revoke/amend) and **audited** (the store records `issued_by`/`revoked_by`/`revoked_at`), satisfying the Reversibility-Preference and Minimal-Authority axioms without a quorum vote.

**Boundaries.** `directive_store.py` (including `authorize_directive`, `create_directive`, `approve`, `revoke`, `amend`, `all_directives`), `standing_orders.py`, and the order `.md` files are untouched — the endpoints only call the existing public API. The endpoints are async but the store is synchronous `sqlite3`; tests drive the app via `httpx.ASGITransport`/`AsyncClient` so the store and endpoints share one thread (BF-287: real tmp-file store, no MagicMock at the substrate boundary).

**Consequence.** +18 pytest (`tests/test_ad900_directive_api.py`). The Captain can now author and manage the runtime directive overlay from the personnel console (AD-901 builds the UI), with the chain-of-command governance preserved and unmodified.

### AD-895: Skill library CRUD — delete verb, validated authoring, HTTP surface (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 5 — #859)

**Context.** The personnel console needs to browse, author, and retire skill *definitions*. The skill-definition library is `runtime.skill_registry` (`SkillRegistry`, SQLite-backed, cloud-ready via an injected `connection_factory`). It was already writable through `register_skill`, but it had two gaps: there was **no delete verb** (a skill, once registered, could never be retired) and **no HTTP read/write surface** (the library was invisible and unauthorable from the UI). The ontology role-template path (`config/ontology/skills.yaml` via `ontology/loader.py::_load_skills_schema`, AD-429b) is a *different* subsystem and is deliberately left untouched — AD-895 does not seed from it or build a parallel persisted store.

**Decision.** Two registry verbs, one service helper, and four HTTP endpoints.

1. **`SkillRegistry.update_skill_definition(defn, *, create=False)`** — a validated wrapper over `register_skill`. `create=True` rejects a duplicate `skill_id`; every prerequisite must reference an already-registered skill (a dangling prerequisite, or a self-referential one, raises `ValueError`) so the prerequisite DAG never points at a missing node; then it persists and returns the definition. The full `SkillDefinition` is passed (consistent with `register_skill(defn)`) rather than a loose `**fields` kwargs bag — the router owns HTTP-shape→`SkillDefinition` construction, the registry validates and persists (clean DI boundary).
2. **`SkillRegistry.delete_skill_definition(skill_id, *, skill_service=None)`** — two guards: a **built-in PCC** (seeded from `BUILTIN_PCCS`) is never deletable, and a skill **in active use** (`skill_service.count_agents_with_skill(skill_id) > 0`) is refused so a delete cannot orphan acquired records. On success it pops the cache and `DELETE`s from the store.
3. **`AgentSkillService.count_agents_with_skill(skill_id)`** — `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM agent_skills WHERE skill_id = ?`, returns 0 when there is no backing store. Supplies the in-use signal for the delete guard.
4. **HTTP (`routers/skills.py`, prefix `/api/skills`):** `GET /api/skills/definitions` (optional `category`/`domain`; honest-degrades to `{"definitions": [], "count": 0}` when the registry is absent; 400 invalid category), `POST` (build `SkillDefinition` from body; 503 no registry, 400 missing `skill_id`/`name`/`category` or invalid category, 400 duplicate/dangling `from None`; `create=True`), `PUT /{skill_id}` (404 when `get_skill` is None; `create=False`), `DELETE /{skill_id}` (404 unknown, 400 `from None` on the built-in/in-use guards). Reuses the `/registry` dict serialization shape.

**Governance — no consensus gate (Minimal-Authority).** Skill-library authoring is a **Captain-authority** edit, gated by the **Minimal-Authority** axiom, not a consensus quorum. Rationale: (a) the actor is the Captain, the ship's sole human authority — there is no peer quorum above the Captain to vote on a library edit; (b) every write is **reversible** — a created skill can be deleted, an updated one re-updated, satisfying the Reversibility-Preference axiom; (c) the action's blast radius is bounded by validation, not ceremony — the **delete guards** (built-in PCC protected, in-use skill refused) and the **create/update guards** (no duplicate, no dangling prerequisite) are the safety mechanism that keeps the prerequisite DAG sound and prevents orphaned agent records. A consensus gate here would add ceremony without adding safety: the authority is already the top of the trust hierarchy, the writes are validated, and the destructive verb (delete) is itself guarded against the two ways it could harm the ship.

**Boundaries.** The per-agent skill-record endpoints (assess/exercise/commission), the AD-887 unified-profile path, the `SkillDefinition` field shape, and `register_skill`/`start`/`register_builtins` are all untouched. No seeding from the ontology skills YAML. No paging/search on the list endpoint (the library is small; a later AD if it grows).

**Consequence.** The Skill Library UI (AD-898) has a stable browse surface (`GET /api/skills/definitions`) and a governed create/edit/retire path (`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE`) with inline validation errors surfaced as 400s. +18 pytest (`tests/test_ad895_skill_library_crud.py`, BF-287 real fixtures: real `SkillRegistry`/`AgentSkillService` on `tmp_path`, TestClient driven through a FastAPI lifespan so the aiosqlite connections share the request event loop per the AD-894 cross-loop lesson). Fifth AD of the Crew Personnel Management epic (#855-865).

### AD-894: Tool asset catalog + per-agent certification HTTP surface (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 4 — #858)

**Context.** The personnel console needs to show the ship's tool inventory and let the Captain certify a crew member on a tool from the manning view. The infrastructure already existed: `ToolRegistry` (AD-422) holds the tool catalog with `to_dict()` projections, and `ToolPermissionStore` (AD-423b) holds the additive CRUD+O grants (`ToolAccessGrant`), both wired onto the runtime (`runtime.tool_registry`, `runtime.tool_permission_store`). Neither had an HTTP read/write surface, so the catalog and per-agent certifications were invisible to the UI and there was no certify/decertify path outside the CLI.

**Decision.** A ship-wide catalog endpoint plus three per-agent certification endpoints, split across two routers.

1. **Catalog — `GET /api/tools`.** Lives in a **new** `src/probos/routers/tools.py` (prefix `/api/tools`, registered in `api.py` alongside `crew_router`). Honest-degrades to `{"tools": [], "count": 0}` when `runtime.tool_registry` is absent; else returns `{tools: [reg.to_dict() for reg in registry.list_tools()], count}`.
2. **Certifications — `GET/POST/DELETE /api/crew/{agent_id}/tools[/{grant_id}]`.** Live in `routers/crew.py` as personnel-record facets. `GET` lists the agent's active grants (`get_active_grants_sync`) joined with catalog metadata (`registry.get(grant.tool_id).to_dict()`, `tool: null` when no longer registered). `POST` certifies (503 no store, 400 missing `tool_id`/`permission`, 404 unknown tool, 400 invalid `ToolPermission` via `raise … from None`, else `await issue_grant(agent_id, tool_id, perm, reason=…, issued_by="captain")`). `DELETE` revokes (`await revoke_grant`, 404 when unknown).

**Router split (why two routers).** A FastAPI prefix applies to every route in a router. The catalog is ship-scoped, not crew-scoped, so it cannot live under `/api/crew`. Rather than relativize the catalog under a crew agent (semantically wrong — the catalog is not a property of any one agent), the catalog gets its own `/api/tools` router; the certify/decertify endpoints stay under `/api/crew/{agent_id}` because a certification *is* a facet of that agent's personnel record. The split is documented in the `tools.py` module docstring.

**Governance — no consensus gate.** The grant/revoke pair is a **Captain-authority privilege edit**, gated by the **Minimal-Authority** axiom, not a consensus quorum. Rationale: (a) the actor is the Captain (`issued_by="captain"`), the ship's sole human authority — there is no peer quorum above the Captain to vote; (b) every grant is recorded as a `ToolAccessGrant` (audited) and is **reversible** via `revoke_grant`, satisfying the Reversibility-Preference axiom; (c) the grant only *widens or narrows* an agent's tool access within the existing permission lattice — it cannot create a tool or escalate beyond `FULL`, so the Safety-Budget risk is bounded by the catalog the runtime already trusts. A consensus gate here would add ceremony without adding safety, since the authority being exercised is already the top of the trust hierarchy and the action is logged and undoable.

**Boundaries.** Neither `ToolRegistry` nor `ToolPermissionStore` is modified — the endpoints only read (`list_tools`, `get`, `get_active_grants_sync`) and wrap the existing async mutators (`issue_grant`, `revoke_grant`). No change to `crew_tasks`, the ACM, or the AD-892/893 crew endpoints. The catalog does not page or filter (the full catalog is small); filtering is a later AD if the catalog grows.

**Consequence.** The Tool Certifications UI (AD-899) has a stable read surface (`GET /api/tools`, `GET /api/crew/{id}/tools`) and a governed grant/revoke path (`POST`/`DELETE`). +11 pytest (`tests/test_ad894_tool_cert_api.py`, BF-287 real fixtures: real `ToolRegistry` with `_StubTool` Tool-protocol stubs + real tmp-file `ToolPermissionStore` whose lifecycle runs in the `TestClient` loop via a lifespan handler). Fourth AD of the Crew Personnel Management epic (#855-865).

### AD-893: Standing-orders read surface — public four-tier reader + HTTP (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 3 — #857)

**Context.** The service record should show the orders an agent operates under, but standing orders were internal system-prompt composition only. `compose_instructions(agent_type, hardcoded_instructions, ...)` returns a single merged string (`## `-prefixed sections + identity/personality injection), not four discrete tiers. The Service Record (AD-897) renders the tiers as distinct sections, so the merged prompt string is the wrong shape — and re-running the full LLM-prompt composition (with personality blocks) for a read view would surface the assembled *prompt*, not the *orders*.

**Decision.** Two additive pieces, no change to composition.

1. **Public tier reader.** `standing_orders.get_order_tiers(agent_type, *, orders_dir=None) -> list[dict]` reads the four tier files (`federation.md`, `ship.md`, `{dept}.md`, `{agent_type}.md`) directly via the existing private `_load_file` reader and `get_department`, returning each as `{tier, source_file, present, text}`. The department tier's `source_file` is `None` when the agent has no department. An absent file yields `present: False` + empty `text` rather than an omitted entry, so the manning view always sees the full four-tier shape. It runs no LLM composition and injects no personality block. The private `_load_file`/`_DEFAULT_ORDERS_DIR` are not widened — one public function consumes them. The `orders_dir` keyword exists for testability (point at a `tmp_path`).
2. **HTTP endpoint.** `GET /api/crew/{agent_id}/standing-orders` (`routers/crew.py`) resolves `agent_type` via `runtime.registry.get(agent_id)` (404 when unknown), calls `get_order_tiers`, and returns `{agent_id, agent_type, tiers}`.

**Boundaries.** No change to `compose_instructions`, the order `.md` files, or any private helper signature. This is a read surface only — there is no editing path here; the governed write path for standing orders is the directive surface (AD-900). No consensus gate (read-only projection of files the runtime already loads — Minimal-Authority).

**Consequence.** The Service Record (AD-897) can render the four standing-orders tiers as distinct, source-attributed sections. +6 pytest (`tests/test_ad893_standing_orders_api.py`, tier reader against `tmp_path` + endpoint against real `AgentRegistry` per BF-287). Third AD of the Crew Personnel Management epic (#855-865).

### AD-892: Crew roster + service record HTTP read surface (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 2 — #856)

**Context.** AD-891 closed the duty-schedule seam in the ACM lens, but the consolidated personnel data (AD-885 capability lens + AD-891 duties) had no HTTP surface — the Crew Personnel Console (AD-896) and Service Record (AD-897) UIs need a roster list and a per-agent record endpoint to render. The ontology already exposed the org-chart manifest (`get_crew_manifest`) and the ACM exposed the consolidated profile (`get_consolidated_profile`), but no router joined them into a who-is-aboard roster or a single record document.

**Decision.** A new router `src/probos/routers/crew.py` (prefix `/api/crew`, `tags=["crew"]`) — kept distinct from the existing `crew_tasks` router (`/api/crew-tasks`) — wired into `api.py` via the import tuple (`crew as crew_router`) and the include loop. Two async read-only endpoints.

1. **`GET /api/crew/roster`.** Walks `runtime.registry.all()`, filters to crew via `crew_utils.is_crew_agent(agent, ontology)`, and joins each against `ontology.get_crew_manifest(trust_network=..., callsign_registry=...)` keyed by `agent_type`. Manifest-present → `callsign/post/department/rank` + `assigned: true`, `billet_state: "billeted"`. Crew-recognized but manifest-absent → `post/department/rank: null`, `assigned: false`, `billet_state: "unbilleted"` (callsign falls back to `agent.callsign`) — a visible manning gap rather than a silent omission. Each entry augmented with `lifecycle_state` (`(await acm.get_lifecycle_state(id)).value`), `skill_count` (`len((await skill_service.get_profile(id)).all_skills)`), `tool_count` (non-restriction active grants via `tool_permission_store.get_active_grants_sync`), each in its own Tier-2 debug-degrade guard. Sorted by `(department, agent_type)`. None registry → `{"crew": [], "count": 0}`.
2. **`GET /api/crew/{agent_id}/record`.** 503 when `acm` absent; 404 when `registry.get(agent_id)` is None; else `await acm.get_consolidated_profile(agent_id, runtime)` augmented with `active_assignments` (from `await work_item_store.list_work_items(assigned_to=id, limit=100)` filtered to `open`/`in_progress`) and a `billet` block (resolve `assignment.post_id` → `billet_registry.resolve` for title/department → `await billet_registry.check_qualifications` for `qualified` + `missing_qualifications`), the billet block omitted via honest-degrade when the agent has no assignment.

**Governance — no consensus gate.** Both endpoints are **read-only projections** of state the runtime already holds (registry, ontology manifest, ACM profile, work-item store, billet registry). They grant no authority, mutate no state, and issue no directive. Minimal-Authority: a read lens needs no consensus gate. The mutating crew endpoints (tool certification AD-894, directives AD-900) carry their own governance decisions in their ADs.

**Boundaries.** No change to `crew_tasks` router, `AgentRegistry`, `VesselOntologyService`, ACM, or any store. The roster does **not** reconcile the registry/manifest divergence — the unbilleted state is reported, not resolved (reconciliation, if ever, is a separate AD). The module docstring records the authority model: roster is registry-authoritative for who-is-aboard + ontology-authoritative for the org chart; record is ACM-authoritative for the HR view; the two drift and are not merged.

**Consequence.** The crew roster and service record now have a stable HTTP read surface for the Personnel Console (AD-896) and Service Record (AD-897) UIs. +9 pytest (`tests/test_ad892_crew_record_api.py`, real `AgentRegistry` substrate + explicit hand-written ontology/ACM fakes per BF-287). Second AD of the Crew Personnel Management epic (#855-865).

### AD-891: Duty-schedule lens — public, non-mutating per-agent duty accessor (Crew Personnel Management epic, part 1 — #855)

**Context.** The ACM consolidated profile (AD-885) is the single capability lens, but a crew agent's **configured duty schedule** was absent from its personnel record. AD-885 and AD-889 both explicitly recorded "NO duties step" as a verify-first NO-SEAM: no *public, non-mutating* per-agent duty accessor existed. The proactive cognition loop owned the schedule as a private `_duty_tracker`, and the only read path — `DutyScheduleTracker.get_due_duties` — returns the volatile "due now" subset **and records executions** (it mutates per-duty status). A personnel record needs the stable *configured* view, not the volatile due-now view, and must not have a read side-effect.

**Decision.** Three additive pieces, no protocol or schema change.

1. **Non-mutating list method.** `DutyScheduleTracker.list_duties_for_agent(self, agent_type: str) -> list[DutyDefinition]` (`src/probos/duty_schedule.py`) returns `list(self._schedules.get(agent_type, []))` sorted by `priority` descending. It **never reads or writes** the execution-status map (`self._status`) — explicitly contrasted in its docstring with `get_due_duties` (the "due now" mutating-status view). This is the stable personnel-record projection of the schedule.
2. **Law-of-Demeter accessor.** A public `ProactiveCognitionLoop.duty_tracker` property (`src/probos/proactive.py`) returns `self._duty_tracker`, so callers read the tracker through a public surface instead of reaching the private attr. It returns `None` when proactive cognition is disabled.
3. **Runtime wiring.** In `startup/finalize.py`, after the `if config.proactive_cognitive.duty_schedule.enabled: proactive_loop.set_duty_schedule(...)` block, `runtime.duty_schedule_tracker = proactive_loop.duty_tracker` runs at the `if`'s indentation level (unconditionally), so the runtime always carries the handle — `None` when the feature is disabled.

The ACM lens gains **block 9** (`src/probos/acm.py`, after block 8 tool grants, before `return profile`): guarded by `getattr(runtime, 'duty_schedule_tracker', None)`, it resolves `agent_type` via `runtime.registry.get(agent_id)` and, when an `agent_type` is found, sets `profile["duties"]` (list of `{duty_id, description, cron, interval_seconds, priority}`) and `profile["duty_count"]`. The whole block is Tier-2 log-and-degrade (`logger.debug("Duty schedule fetch failed", exc_info=True)`), matching blocks 5-8.

**Governance — no consensus gate.** Block 9 is a **read-only lens projection** — it reads the configured schedule and returns it; it grants no authority, mutates no state, and records no execution. It therefore introduces no destructive intent and requires no consensus gate (Minimal-Authority: the lens reads only what the runtime already holds; no new write surface).

**Boundaries.** No change to `get_due_duties` (the proactive loop's due-now path is untouched), no change to `DutyDefinition`/`DutyScheduleConfig`, no new public attr beyond the `duty_tracker` property and the `runtime.duty_schedule_tracker` handle. Honest-degrade: missing tracker → block omitted; unknown agent (no `agent_type`) → block omitted; unconfigured agent type → empty list, count 0.

**Consequence.** The personnel record now shows what an agent is *scheduled to do*, closing the AD-885/AD-889 duties NO-SEAM and laying the read surface the Crew Service Record (AD-897) renders. First AD of the Crew Personnel Management epic (#855-865).

### AD-890: Supersede the stale capability docs (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 6 — #854)

**Context.** `docs/development/unified-tool-layer.md` titles itself "AD-543: Unified Tool Layer — Skill-Tool Binding & Agentic Tool Adapters," but **AD-543 is a number collision**: the real AD-543 shipped as the Native SWE Harness Tool Execution Abstraction (`src/probos/tools/executor.py`). The doc's skill→tool design was therefore orphaned — and it actually landed, four epic parts later, as **AD-888** (the `resolve_tools_for_skill` resolver) wired end-to-end by the **AD-889** commissioning capstone. Left unmarked, the doc misleads every future reader into thinking AD-543 is the skill→tool binding.

**Decision (docs only — no code).**
1. **SUPERSEDED banner** prepended to `docs/development/unified-tool-layer.md`: states the AD-543 number collision (AD-543 = Native SWE Harness / `tools/executor.py`), notes the skill→tool design actually shipped as AD-888 + AD-889, and redirects readers to the canonical `docs/development/skills-and-tools-architecture.md`. The original doc body is retained for historical context.
2. **Canonical pointer** added atop `docs/research/crew-capability-architecture.md`: a one-line note that `skills-and-tools-architecture.md` is the authoritative, shipped capability spine (Role → Skills → Tools, AD-885 → AD-890) and this document is the originating design analysis.
3. **Verify-only (no edit):** confirmed the AD-543 collision fact is already recorded in the canonical doc — the seam table (#6 row) and the §8 convergence sequence (item 6) both state it. No third edit needed.

**Boundaries.** No source, no test, no other doc touched. Docs-only — the epic's final step ran the full serial gate to confirm AD-885 → AD-889 left the suite green.

**Consequence.** The Skills & Tools Unification epic (#849-854) is closed: AD-885 (ACM single lens) → AD-886 (designed skill reclassified as Tool) → AD-887 (skill-library merge) → AD-888 (skill→tool resolver) → AD-889 (Role→Skills→Tools commissioning capstone) → AD-890 (docs). No future reader is misled by the AD-543 collision; the capability spine has one canonical home.

### AD-889: Commissioning capstone — walk Role → Skills → Tools at agent birth (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 5 — #853)

**Context.** The epic's first four parts unified the *query* surfaces: the ACM capability lens (AD-885), the designed-skill→tool reclassification (AD-886), the dual skill-library merge (AD-887), and the orphaned skill→tool resolver (AD-888). But nothing walked the chain end-to-end when a crew agent was *born*. The ingredients existed in isolation — `OntologyService.get_role_template_for_agent` (role → required skills), `AgentSkillService.acquire_skill` (developmental acquisition with prereq math), `resolve_tools_for_skill` (AD-888 skill → tools), and `ToolPermissionStore.issue_grant` (AD-885's grant surface) — but no single call turned "this agent is a science_officer" into "it holds the tactical-debug skill and a READ grant on the scanner tool."

**Decision.** Add `AgentCapitalService.commission(self, agent_id: str, agent_type: str, runtime: Any) -> dict[str, Any]` (`src/probos/acm.py`) as the single commissioning front door. It is **self-stateless** — it reads only `runtime` and the module logger, never `self._db`, so it requires no `acm.start()` and can be unit-tested against a bare `AgentCapitalService(tmp_dir)`. The walk:

1. **Legacy back-compat.** If `runtime.skill_service` is present, `await skill_service.commission_agent(agent_id, agent_type)` first (wrapped, debug-on-fail) so the pre-existing AD-428 commission path still runs.
2. **Role → Skills.** Read `runtime.ontology.get_role_template_for_agent(agent_type)`; for each `SkillRequirement` map `min_proficiency` → `ProficiencyLevel` (an out-of-range value falls back to `ProficiencyLevel.FOLLOW`, never raises), then `await skill_service.acquire_skill(agent_id, req.skill_id, source="commission", proficiency=level)`. A `ValueError` (unmet prerequisite) is **debug-logged, not raised** — partial commissioning is acceptable; a missing prereq is a soft skip.
3. **Fetch the profile once.** `profile = await skill_service.get_profile(agent_id)` — a single read, reused for the tool walk; `summary["skills_acquired"]` is `[r.skill_id for r in profile.all_skills]`.
4. **Skills → Tools (idempotent).** Only when `profile is not None` **and** all three of `runtime.tool_permission_store` / `runtime.tool_registry` / `runtime.skill_registry` are present: for each acquired skill, look up its `SkillDefinition` (`skill_registry.get_skill`, skip if absent), `resolve_tools_for_skill(skill_def, agent_id=, tool_registry=)`, and for each resolved tool check `tool_permission_store.get_active_grants_sync(agent_id, tool_id)` — if any **non-restriction** active grant already exists, skip (no double-grant); otherwise `await tool_permission_store.issue_grant(agent_id, tool_id, ToolPermission.READ, is_restriction=False, reason="commission", issued_by="captain")` and append to `summary["tools_granted"]`.

Returns `{agent_id, agent_type, skills_acquired: [...], tools_granted: [...]}`.

**Wiring — Option A (birth path at `create_pool`), chosen over Option B (`agent_onboarding.wire_agent`).** The commission hook lives in `ProbOSRuntime.create_pool` (`src/probos/runtime.py`) inside the existing post-creation `for agent in self.registry.get_by_pool(name)` loop, immediately after `await self.onboarding.wire_agent(agent)`, guarded `if self.acm and is_crew_agent(agent, self.ontology)` and wrapped in a Tier-2 `try/except` → `logger.debug(..., exc_info=True)` so a commission failure never aborts pool creation. **Why Option A and not Option B:** the AD-515 `AgentOnboardingService.wire_agent` deliberately carries a dependency-light surface — it has no handle to `runtime`, `skill_registry`, or `tool_permission_store`. Threading those four services into the onboarding service to host the commission walk would invert AD-515's design. The ACM front door instead pulls every dependency off the live `runtime` it already receives, so onboarding stays lean and the commission logic lives with the ACM (the unification owner). `is_crew_agent(agent, self.ontology)` scopes commissioning to crew agents (infrastructure/utility agents are not commissioned).

**Endpoint re-point — deliberate contract change.** `/skills/agents/{agent_id}/commission` (`src/probos/routers/skills.py`) now calls `runtime.acm.commission(agent_id, req.agent_type, runtime)` and **returns the commission summary dict** (`{agent_id, agent_type, skills_acquired, tools_granted}`) instead of the previous `profile.to_dict()`. This is an intentional, documented consequence of collapsing the two commission paths behind one lens — the endpoint now reports exactly what was commissioned (which skills acquired, which tools granted) rather than a full profile dump. A `503` is raised when `runtime.acm` is absent.

**NO duties step.** Same verify-first NO-SEAM as AD-885: there is no public per-agent duty accessor (`DutyScheduleTracker.get_due_duties` is private on `runtime.proactive_loop._duty_tracker`, a Law-of-Demeter violation to reach). Duties join the commissioning walk in a future AD that first ships a public duty-tracker surface.

**Honest-degrade matrix.** Missing `skill_service` → empty summary, no crash. Missing `ontology` or no template for the type → legacy-only (step 1 ran, no template skills). Missing any of the three tool services → skills acquired but `tools_granted == []`. Every branch is a soft path; `commission` never raises for an absent collaborator.

**Tests.** +6 in `tests/test_ad889_commission_chain.py` (BF-287 real fixtures — real `AgentCapitalService`, real `SkillRegistry` + `AgentSkillService` on a tmp `skills.db`, real `ToolRegistry`, real `ToolPermissionStore`; a `_StubOntology`/`_StubRuntime` attribute holder only for the runtime-attribute boundary, no MagicMock at the substrate boundary; the `(service, registry)` tuple helper avoids any private-attr reach into the service): template skills acquired + tools granted; legacy-only fallback when no template; idempotent re-commission (second pass grants nothing new); a skill with no preferred tool grants nothing cleanly; degrade without a permission store; empty summary without a skill_service. Full gate green (15589 passed, 22 skipped; the only 2 reds — `test_auto_commit_after_debounce`, `test_bf304_single_flight_drops_concurrent_describe` — are xdist-parallel timing flakes that pass serially, unrelated to commissioning). One commit.

**Consequence.** The Skills & Tools Unification epic's capstone: a crew agent born into a pool is now commissioned automatically — its role template's required skills are acquired and the tools those skills resolve to are granted — through one ACM front door, and the same front door backs the `/commission` endpoint. AD-890 (docs) closes the epic.

### AD-888: Skill→Tool binding — finish the orphaned resolver (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 4 — #852)

**Context.** `SkillDefinition.preferred_tools: list[ToolPreference]` has existed since AD-423 (with a SQLite migration), but **nothing resolved it** — there was no code path from "this agent exercises skill X" to "invoke the tool(s) that fulfil X." This was Part 4 of the orphaned `docs/development/unified-tool-layer.md` plan: the schema was in place, the binding was never built.

**Decision.** Add a pure, side-effect-free resolver as a standalone substrate module `src/probos/tools/skill_tool_resolver.py` (chosen over a `ToolRegistry` method for Dependency Inversion — the resolver depends on the registry abstraction, not vice-versa): `resolve_tools_for_skill(skill: SkillDefinition, *, agent_id: str, tool_registry: ToolRegistry, hebbian: "HebbianRouter | None" = None) -> list[ToolRegistration]`. Resolution order:

1. **Preferred tools, in priority order.** Iterate `sorted(skill.preferred_tools, key=lambda p: p.priority)` (lower `priority` = higher precedence). For each, look up `tool_registry.get(pref.tool_id)`; skip if missing, disabled, or already seen; keep only if `tool_registry.check_permission(agent_id, tool_id, ToolPermission.READ)` (READ = the minimum an agent needs to use a tool, matching `check_and_invoke`'s default floor). If any preferred tool resolves, return that list.
2. **Capability-tag fallback.** Only when no preferred tool resolved and the skill declares a concrete `domain` (not the universal `"*"`): iterate `tool_registry.list_tools(tag=skill.domain)`, dedup, permission-filter (READ), debug-log on fallback success.
3. **Hebbian no-op.** The optional `hebbian` parameter is a **documented no-op** today. The real ranking primitive `HebbianRouter.get_preferred_targets` ranks agent→agent (`REL_AGENT`) compatibility; there are no agent→tool edges in the routing graph yet, so there is nothing to rank tools by. The param is kept with a `# TODO(AD-888)` so this is the activation point once agent→tool edges exist. The resolver works with `hebbian=None`.

**Boundaries.** The resolver only **resolves** — it never invokes a tool, grants a permission, or touches consensus (auto-invocation/granting is AD-889 + the AD-543-549 agentic executor, both unchanged). The `ToolPreference`/`preferred_tools` schema is untouched. An empty result is a clean `[]`, never a raise. Layer discipline: the substrate module imports `SkillDefinition` (foundation) and the tool types (same layer) at runtime, but keeps the `hebbian` annotation behind a `TYPE_CHECKING` guard so the substrate never imports the mesh layer at runtime (`from __future__ import annotations` makes the forward-ref string annotation cost-free).

**Tests.** +6 in `tests/test_ad888_skill_tool_resolver.py` (BF-287 real fixtures — real `ToolRegistry` + real `SkillDefinition`/`ToolPreference` + a minimal `Tool`-protocol stub, no MagicMock at the substrate boundary): preferred tool returned first by priority; permission-denied preferred tool skipped (`restricted_to`); tag-fallback when no preferred tool; tag-fallback respects permission; a provided `hebbian` does not change ordering; empty result is a clean `[]`. AD-423 tool-foundation/permission/context + skill-framework blast-radius suites green (98) serially.

**Consequence.** The skill→tool binding the unified-tool-layer plan promised now exists. AD-889 (the commissioning capstone) hard-depends on this resolver to turn a newly-acquired skill into concrete tool grants.

### AD-887: Skill Library unification — one query surface for both skill kinds (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 3 — #851)

**Context.** ProbOS carries two parallel skill stores: the AD-428 `AgentSkillService` holds **developmental** (T3) proficiency-tracked `AgentSkillRecord`s (PCC / role / acquired), and the AD-596 `CognitiveSkillCatalog` holds **cognitive** (T2) instruction-defined `SKILL.md` entries. AD-596c bridged catalog→registry (`SkillBridge`, `src/probos/cognitive/skill_bridge.py`, holding `_catalog` = T2 and `_service` = T3, wired as `runtime.skill_bridge`), but the two stores were still queried separately — so "what skills does this agent have?" had two answers. The developmental `SkillProfile` (`skill_framework.py`) had no cognitive field and `AgentSkillService.get_profile` (T3-only) never consulted the catalog.

**Decision.** Make a single call report both skill kinds, **merging at the bridge** (not the service, not the catalog).

1. **Additive field, foundation-layer-safe.** Add `cognitive_skills: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)` to the `SkillProfile` dataclass (`src/probos/skill_framework.py`). It is typed as plain kind-tagged dicts — **not** `list[CognitiveSkillEntry]` — so this foundation-layer module (no LLM calls, no I/O in data classes) stays decoupled from the cognitive-layer `CognitiveSkillEntry` type. `Any`/`field` are already imported.
2. **Bridge merge method.** Add `async def get_unified_profile(self, agent_id, *, department=None, agent_rank=None) -> SkillProfile` to `SkillBridge`. It calls `await self._service.get_profile(agent_id)` for the developmental profile, then `self._catalog.list_entries(department=department, min_rank=agent_rank)` for the cognitive entries, appending each as `{name, description, skill_id, department, min_proficiency, min_rank, origin, kind: "cognitive"}` to `profile.cognitive_skills`. Developmental records stay in their existing `pccs`/`role_skills`/`acquired_skills` buckets (implicitly developmental).
3. **T3 stays pure.** `AgentSkillService.get_profile` is unchanged — it never consults `_catalog`, so a directly-fetched profile has `cognitive_skills == []`. The merge is bridge-only.
4. **No schema change.** The cognitive kind is derived at read time, not stored — no `skills.db` migration.
5. **Optional dept/rank filters.** The keyword-only `department`/`agent_rank` mirror the AD-885 lens pattern and pass straight through to `list_entries`; defaulting both to `None` returns all visible cognitive entries (wildcard `department == "*"` always visible). The `SkillProfile`/`get_profile` API carries no dept/rank today, so the caller supplies them — chosen over inferring crew identity inside the bridge to keep the merge a pure read with no extra dependency.
6. **Honest-degrade.** A catalog query failure is caught and logged Tier-2 (`logger.warning(..., exc_info=True)`) and the method returns the developmental-only profile rather than raising — a cognitive-store outage must not break the unified query.

**Verify-first facts.** The bridge ctor is `SkillBridge(catalog, skill_registry, skill_service)` (the prompt's L22 `SkillBridge(catalog, skill_service)` reference predates the registry arg); `get_profile` is async; `list_entries(department=None, min_rank=None)` returns all entries when both are `None` and filters department by wildcard-or-exact and rank by `_RANK_ORDER`. `from __future__ import annotations` is present in both edited files, so the `-> SkillProfile` return annotation in the bridge (where `SkillProfile` is only `TYPE_CHECKING`-imported) is a lazy string needing no runtime import.

**Untouched.** The `SKILL.md` on-disk format, progressive-disclosure loading (`get_instructions`/`find_by_intent` stay the runtime context-injection path), and the developmental proficiency math.

**Tests.** `tests/test_ad887_skill_library_unification.py` (+7, BF-287 real fixtures — real `SkillRegistry`+`AgentSkillService` on a tmp DB + real `CognitiveSkillCatalog` + real `SkillBridge`): an agent with both kinds reports both; cognitive entries carry `kind="cognitive"` and the required keys; cognitive-only and developmental-only agents resolve; a department filter excludes department-specific entries while keeping wildcards; `get_profile` stays T3-only; a forced `list_entries` exception degrades to developmental-only. AD-428 + AD-596 blast-radius suites green (94) serially. One commit.

### AD-886: Reclassify the legacy self-mod Skill as a Tool (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 2 — #850)

**Context.** The self-modification pipeline (`SelfModificationPipeline.handle_add_skill`, `src/probos/cognitive/self_mod.py`) designs new `Skill` objects (async handler + `IntentDescriptor`) and attaches them to the `SkillBasedAgent` dispatch path via the `add_skill_fn` callback. But a designed skill was **invisible to the AD-423 `ToolRegistry`**: the unified capability lens (AD-885 block 8), per-agent tool-grant permission checks, and any tool-aware routing enumerate `tool_registry.list_tools()` — and designed skills never appeared there. The two capability surfaces (skill-dispatch and tool-registry) had diverged.

**Decision.** Register every designed skill into the `ToolRegistry` as a first-class tool, **without coupling the cognitive layer to the substrate `ToolRegistry`** (layer discipline: `cognitive/` must not import `tools/registry`). Use **callback injection** (Dependency Inversion): `SelfModificationPipeline.__init__` gains an optional `register_tool_fn: Callable | None = None` stored as `self._register_tool_fn`; `handle_add_skill` adds a "step 5b" immediately after the existing `await self._add_skill_fn(...)` (step 5) and before the step-6 record:

```python
if self._register_tool_fn is not None:
    try:
        self._register_tool_fn(skill)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning(
            "AD-886: ToolRegistry registration failed for designed skill %s; "
            "skill remains dispatchable via SkillBasedAgent",
            intent_name, exc_info=True,
        )
```

The callback is **synchronous** (Tier-2 log-and-degrade — a ToolRegistry write failure must never abort skill design, since the skill is already dispatchable). The concrete implementation is the new `ProbOSRuntime._register_designed_tool(self, skill)` (`src/probos/runtime.py`), wired through `startup/cognitive_services.py` `init_cognitive_services` (new keyword-only `register_tool_fn` passed to the pipeline ctor) from `runtime.py` Phase 4.

**Adapter choice — InfraServiceAdapter, not DeterministicFunctionAdapter.** A `Skill.handler` is an **async, bus-dispatched** coroutine, not a pure local function. `_register_designed_tool` builds `InfraServiceAdapter(tool_id=skill.name, name=skill.name, description=<descriptor.description or skill.name>, intent_name=skill.name, intent_bus=self.intent_bus)` and registers it with `provider="designed"`. Invoking the resulting tool re-broadcasts `skill.name` on the intent bus and returns the first successful responder's result as a `ToolResult` — so a designed skill is invocable both as a tool (`reg.tool.invoke(...)`) and via `SkillBasedAgent.handle_intent`. The two paths coexist; neither replaces the other.

**Startup-ordering — closure resolves the seam.** Phase 4 (`init_cognitive_services`) runs **before** Phase 7 (`init_communication`), and `self.tool_registry` is only populated in Phase 7 (`self.tool_registry = comm.tool_registry`). But `_register_designed_tool` is a closure passed into the pipeline; it is only *called* at skill-design time, which is strictly post-startup. So `self.tool_registry` is always populated by the time the callback fires. The method still honest-degrades — `if registry is None: logger.debug(...); return` — for any pre-startup or registry-disabled deployment.

**Tests.** +8 pytest (`tests/test_ad886_selfmod_tool_registration.py`, BF-287 — real `ToolRegistry()`, a `SimpleNamespace` runtime stub holding the real registry and a fake recording intent bus, calling the REAL `ProbOSRuntime._register_designed_tool`; no MagicMock at the substrate boundary): a designed deterministic skill appears in `list_tools()` with `provider="designed"` + `tool_type == ToolType.INFRA_SERVICE`; it is invocable (awaitable) through the adapter (`result.success`, `result.output == "hello"`, the bus saw the `greet_user` intent); a `None` `register_tool_fn` / `None` registry is a clean no-op; the pipeline defaults `_register_tool_fn` to `None` and stores/invokes a provided callback; and `SkillBasedAgent` dispatch still handles its intent after tool registration (class-level `_handled_intents`/`intent_descriptors` snapshotted and restored in a `finally` to avoid test pollution — `add_skill` mutates class state in place). Blast radius `tests/test_self_mod.py` (66) green serially. One commit.

### AD-885: ACM becomes the true single capability lens — additive cognitive-skill + tool-grant blocks (Skills & Tools Unification epic, part 1 — #849)

**Context.** `AgentCapitalService.get_consolidated_profile` (`src/probos/acm.py:277`) is meant to answer "what can this agent do, and why?" across the whole capability spine. At HEAD it aggregated six blocks — lifecycle, crew profile (AD-376), trust, earned agency (AD-357), AD-428 developmental skills, and episode count — but was **blind** to two shipped subsystems: cognitive skills (AD-596 `CognitiveSkillCatalog`) and tool grants (AD-423 `ToolRegistry`). The lens was incomplete.

**Decision.** Append two **additive, read-only** blocks to `get_consolidated_profile`, each guarded with the same `hasattr(runtime, ...) and runtime....` + per-block `try`/`logger.debug` pattern as blocks 5-6, so a missing subsystem omits its keys without crashing and no existing block changes. **(7) Cognitive skills:** when `runtime.cognitive_skill_catalog` is present, `profile["cognitive_skills"] = [{"name": n, "description": d, "skill_id": s} for (n, d, s) in catalog.get_descriptions(department=profile.get("department"), agent_rank=profile.get("rank"))]` plus `profile["cognitive_skill_count"]`. `get_descriptions` (`src/probos/cognitive/skill_catalog.py:353`) returns `list[tuple[name, description, skill_id]]` already filtered by department + rank, so the lens shows exactly what THIS agent is permitted to see (progressive disclosure). **(8) Tool grants:** when `runtime.tool_registry` is present, iterate `tool_registry.list_tools()` and keep each `reg.tool_id` for which `tool_registry.check_permission(agent_id, reg.tool_id, ToolPermission.READ, agent_department=<dept>, agent_rank=<rank or "ensign">)` is true → `profile["tools"]` + `profile["tool_count"]`. The agent's **real** `rank`/`department` come from block 2's crew identity (`profile.get("rank")`/`profile.get("department")`); falling back to the `"ensign"` default would understate a senior agent's grants. `ToolPermission` is imported lazily inside the block (matching block 4's inline `from probos.earned_agency import ...` pattern) to avoid any `tools`-package import-cycle risk at module load.

**Verify-first NO-SEAM: duties omitted.** The epic originally called for three blocks (the third = duties). Verify-first established there is **no public per-agent duty accessor** at HEAD: `runtime.duty_schedule` is a `DutySchedule` scan-policy gate (`should_scan`/`next_scan_window`), not a per-agent lookup; the real `DutyScheduleTracker.get_due_duties(agent_type)` is **private** on `runtime.proactive_loop._duty_tracker` (`src/probos/proactive.py:384`) and reaching it would be a Law-of-Demeter violation; `runtime.duty_schedule_tracker` is aspirational/unshipped. **No duty block was added and `_duty_tracker` is not reached.** Duties join the lens in a future AD that first ships a public `runtime.duty_schedule_tracker` property.

**Why additive-only.** Smallest blast radius first (the epic ships the read-only lens before any subsystem-mutating AD). The method signature, the six existing blocks, and the `acm.db` schema are untouched — AD-885 only reads. Block 3's existing `hasattr`-only (no truthiness) guard means a stub runtime must OMIT `trust_network`/`registry`/`skill_service`/`episodic_memory` attributes rather than set them `None`; the test runtime stub does exactly that.

**Tests.** +8 pytest (`tests/test_ad885_acm_unified_lens.py`, BF-287 real fixtures — real `AgentCapitalService(data_dir=tmp_path)`, real `ToolRegistry()`, real started `CognitiveSkillCatalog(skills_dir=tmp_path)` with an on-disk `SKILL.md`, and a plain `_LensRuntime` stub that holds only the real subsystems under test so the other blocks stay dormant via `hasattr`): cognitive skills present / absent-no-catalog / empty-catalog; tool grants ship-wide / **rank-gated** (a `commander`-only tool is excluded for an ensign and included for the agent's real higher rank — proving the real rank is passed, not the default) / absent-no-registry / empty-registry; and the existing blocks (e.g. `lifecycle_state`) remain present alongside the new keys. Blast radius `tests/test_acm.py` (37) green. One commit.

### BF-609: Per-intent TTL for Yeo's inline mesh reads — network reads need a larger ceiling than local-IO reads (#848)

**Context.** Yeo's AD-869 Tier-2 "do-and-report" path resolves a single read-only intent synchronously in the chat turn via `DmReplyPipeline.step_4h_mesh_read_parse` and renders the result inline. A Captain web lookup returned `"Good catch on the name — let me look that up now. (The web_search lookup came back empty (Agent did not respond in time.))"` — the dispatch fired but the agent never replied inside the TTL.

**Root cause.** AD-869 applied one flat `_MESH_READ_TTL_SECONDS = 5.0` ceiling to every allowlisted intent (`_MESH_READ_INTENT_POOLS`). That is correct for the local-IO reads (`list_directory`, `read_file`, `stat_file`, `search_files` — milliseconds) but wrong for `web_search` / `read_page`: `WebSearchAgent`/`PageReaderAgent` mesh-fetch through the AD-270 rate-limited `http_fetch` path (≥2s per-domain wait + internet round-trip) and then, because both `IntentDescriptor`s carry `requires_reflect=True`, run a synthesis LLM call — realistically 8-20s. The 5s `asyncio.wait_for` in `IntentBus.send` timed out every time, producing the literal `"Agent did not respond in time."` This was a latent defect in AD-869 from day one: the inline-web path could never have succeeded under a 5s ceiling.

**Decision.** Keep the tight default for local reads and add a per-intent override map for the network + LLM-bound reads, rather than raising the global ceiling (which would let a slow local read block the reply for 25s) or making the dispatch async (which breaks the "answer this turn" Tier-2 contract). New constants in `src/probos/cognitive/dm/reply_pipeline.py`: `_MESH_READ_NETWORK_TTL_SECONDS = 25.0` and `_MESH_READ_TTL_BY_INTENT = {"web_search": ..., "read_page": ...}`; the dispatch uses `ttl_seconds=_MESH_READ_TTL_BY_INTENT.get(intent_name, _MESH_READ_TTL_SECONDS)`. The longer wait does **not** weaken the Tier-2 safety boundary — read-only safety is enforced by the allowlist plus the structural fact that consensus (and therefore any mutation) cannot resolve in one turn, not by the latency ceiling. `http_fetch` and writes stay excluded. +4 pytest in `tests/test_ad869_mesh_read_inline.py` (real `IntentBus`/`AgentRegistry` per BF-287): network intents dispatch at 25s, local reads keep 5s, the map covers exactly `{web_search, read_page}`.

### AD-882: Federation node-scope guard — default-safe no-op with a forward seam (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 8/final — #847)

**Context.** Liveness is checked against the **local** `AgentRegistry` (`WorkItemReconciler.resolve_live_agent`). In a multi-node federated mesh, a work item whose assignee is a live agent on **another node** resolves to `None` locally and would be wrongly reclaimed by this node's periodic sweep — a node stealing another node's in-flight work.

**Verify-first finding.** There is **no per-agent or per-work-item node marker at HEAD.** Node identity exists only at config/peer granularity (`FederationConfig.node_id`, `FederationConfig.enabled` in `src/probos/config.py`; both default to single-node: `node_id="node-1"`, `enabled=False`). `WorkItem.assigned_to` is a bare agent id with no node qualifier, and the registry tracks no owning node. So AD-882 **cannot determine** remote ownership from existing data — a true federation-aware reclaim needs a node marker that does not yet exist. Building that marker (peer gossip of work ownership, a `WorkItem.owner_node` field, registry node tagging) is a federation-layer change well beyond this hardening epic's scope.

**Decision.** Ship the **guard seam** now, default-safe, so the moment a node marker exists the protection is already in place. The convention: an optional `metadata['owner_node']` key future federation code can populate. In the shared `_process_item` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`), **before** acting on a `clear_and_reroute` decision and **before** the AD-877 attempt counter increments, when `self._federation_enabled` and `metadata.get("owner_node")` is set and `!= self._local_node_id`, the sweep skips with `reason="remote_owner"`, increments `counts["remote_owner_skipped"]`, and returns without unassigning, re-dispatching, or accruing a local attempt. Federation disabled (default), marker absent, or marker == local node → unchanged behavior. **On a single-node deployment the branch is never taken — a pure no-op.** Local node id + federation flag are injected in `startup/finalize.py` `_wire_board_reconciler` from `config.federation.{node_id,enabled}`; constructor kwargs `local_node_id="node-1"` / `federation_enabled=False` mirror them for direct construction. The always-present counts dict gains `remote_owner_skipped` (AD-875 empty-board exact-dict updated).

**Why a seam, not full federation reclaim.** Reversibility + Minimal Authority: the safe default is to **not** touch an item this node cannot prove it owns. Skipping a possibly-remote item is reversible (a later sweep, or the owning node, handles it); reclaiming a remote item is a cross-node mutation with no rollback. The guard chooses the reversible default and leaves real ownership resolution to the federation layer.

**Tests.** +5 pytest (`tests/test_ad882_federation_node_guard.py`, real `WorkItemStore` + real `AgentRegistry` per BF-287): federation-off ignores the marker (item reclaimed), enabled+remote-owner skipped and left untouched (not unassigned, not dispatched), enabled+local-owner reclaimed normally, enabled+no-marker treated as local, remote_owner skip does not bump `reconcile_attempts`. One commit. **Epic #847 complete (AD-877 → AD-884).**

### AD-881: Detect live-but-stalled assignees — coarse, config-gated, default-off (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 7 — #847)

**Decision:** Add a config-gated, default-off (`0`) staleness signal so an `in_progress` item whose assignee is **live** but has made **no board progress** within `stall_timeout_seconds` is rerouted (`reason="stalled"`) instead of skipped. The sweep owns the clock and threshold and passes a precomputed `is_stalled` boolean into `WorkItemReconciler.classify(wi, *, is_dispatchable, is_stalled=False)` (`src/probos/cognitive/work_reconciler.py`) — keeping the reconciler pure (no clock, no config); when `is_stalled` and the assignee resolves live and `status == "in_progress"`, classify returns `clear_and_reroute reason="stalled"` instead of the usual `in_progress_live_owner` skip. The stall computation lives in the shared `_process_item` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`): `is_stalled = _stall_timeout_seconds > 0 and status == "in_progress" and float(updated_at) < time.time() - _stall_timeout_seconds` (**strict `<`** older-than), and `counts["stalled"]` (init `0` in `_new_counts`) increments when a `clear_and_reroute` carries `reason="stalled"`. Because the logic is in `_process_item`, it applies to both periodic `reconcile()` and reactive `reconcile_for_agent()`. A stall-reroute flows through the **AD-877 attempt guard** like any other clear_and_reroute (increments `reconcile_attempts`, honours backoff, quarantines at the threshold). New bounded config `stall_timeout_seconds: int = Field(default=0, ge=0, le=86400)` on `WorkBoardReconcilerConfig` (`src/probos/config.py`, transitional default-off — conv #14), injected as `agent._stall_timeout_seconds` in `startup/finalize.py` `_wire_board_reconciler` with a matching `stall_timeout_seconds=0` constructor kwarg.

**Rationale (documented limitation drives the scope):** Verify-first established that `updated_at` is **last board-mutation, not a heartbeat** — `WorkItemStore.update_work_item` (`src/probos/workforce.py:1130`) sets `updated_at = time.time()` on every update, so it advances on claim / status transition / assignment changes routed through the board, but **does not** advance from agent-internal "I'm still working" progress that never touches the board. Therefore `now - updated_at` is a *coarse* "claimed long ago, never progressed" signal, **not** a true liveness heartbeat. That is exactly why this ships **default-off (0)** and why no heartbeat/progress plumbing or new timestamp was added (explicitly out of scope, pending a real progress signal in a later AD). Stall applies only to `in_progress` claimed work — `open`/non-`in_progress` items are never reclaimed as stalled. Passing `is_stalled` into a pure `classify` (rather than giving the reconciler a clock) preserves AD-874's side-effect-free decision service. Tests: `tests/test_ad881_stall_detection.py` (+6, real `WorkItemStore` + real `AgentRegistry` per BF-287 so `resolve_live_agent` resolves a registered live agent; `updated_at` seeded via `create_work_item`): disabled (0) never reclaims a live-old item, enabled reroutes an old live in_progress item with `counts['stalled']++` and a persisted `reconcile_attempts`, a fresh item is not reclaimed, an absent assignee takes the normal `assignee_not_live` path (never counted as stalled), a stall-reroute quarantines at the AD-877 threshold, and the strict-`<` boundary (`updated_at == now - stall_timeout_seconds`) is not stalled. The AD-875 empty-board exact-dict gained the always-present `stalled` key (obsolete-contract guard). One commit.

### AD-880: Reactive reclaim on `AGENT_REMOVED` — additive, default-off, shared per-item path (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 6 — #847)

**Decision:** Add an event-driven reclaim path that complements (does not replace) the periodic sweep. `AgentRegistry.unregister` (`src/probos/substrate/registry.py`) — the single agent-removal chokepoint reached by `pool.remove_agent → registry.unregister` — emits a new `EventType.AGENT_REMOVED` (`src/probos/events.py`, agent-lifecycle cluster) carrying `{agent_id, agent_type}`. The emit happens **outside** the registry lock (BF-598 re-entrancy safety), only when a present agent was actually popped, and only when a `_emit_event_fn` is bound (late-bound by finalize; an unbound fn is a silent no-op). The Quartermaster gains `reconcile_for_agent(agent_id)` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`): an honest-degrade scoped sweep that filters the `open` + `in_progress` board to the dead agent's items and reuses a new shared `_process_item` per-item routine. `_process_item` is the inline per-item body of `reconcile()` extracted verbatim, and the 11-key counts dict was extracted into `_new_counts` (single source of truth) — so the AD-877 thrash/quarantine/backoff guards, AD-878 boot-grace skip, and AD-879 oldest-first ordering apply identically to both reclaim paths and `reconcile()` behavior is byte-for-byte preserved. The reactive sweep emits `WORK_ITEM_RECONCILED` with `{**counts, "trigger": "reactive", "agent_id": ...}`, stores an episode, and records the AD-883 `_last_sweep` surface with `trigger="reactive"`. New default-off config `reactive_reclaim: bool = False` on `WorkBoardReconcilerConfig` (`src/probos/config.py`, transitional flag — conv #14); when enabled and the reconciler is otherwise wired, `startup/finalize.py` `_wire_board_reconciler` subscribes a Tier-2-guarded async handler to `AGENT_REMOVED` via `runtime.add_event_listener`, holding the reference on `runtime.board_reactive_reclaim_handler`. When disabled (default) no subscription is created.

**Rationale:** Periodic-only reclaim leaves a crashed agent's in-flight work stranded for up to `interval_seconds` (default 300s); a reactive trigger closes that latency without changing the safety-net cadence. The registry `unregister` is the correct emission point because it is the single chokepoint for agent removal — instrumenting `pool.remove_agent_by_id` (pool-only bookkeeping that never hits the registry) was explicitly avoided. Emitting outside the lock follows the BF-598 idempotency/re-entrancy lesson: event listeners can run arbitrary code, and holding the registry lock across a fan-out invites deadlock/re-entrancy. Extracting `_process_item` + `_new_counts` is DRY (standing order) and the coordination point for the rest of the epic — AD-881's stall detection and AD-882's federation node guard both land inside `_process_item`, so they apply to reactive and periodic reclaim uniformly without duplication. Default-off keeps the reactive path opt-in (conv #14); the periodic sweep remains the always-on guarantee. Tests: `tests/test_ad880_reactive_reclaim.py` (+8, real `AgentRegistry` + real `WorkItemStore` per BF-287, `_Fake` only at the router/runtime-bus boundary): present-agent unregister emits once, absent-id emits nothing, unbound emit-fn doesn't crash, payload carries id+type, `reconcile_for_agent` reclaims only the named agent's items and honours the AD-877 attempt guard, records a `trigger="reactive"` last-sweep, `reactive_reclaim=False` creates no subscription, and `reactive_reclaim=True` wires a handler that reclaims a dead agent's orphan item. One commit.

### AD-883: Reconciliation observability via `QuartermasterAgent.info()` — no new command or endpoint (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 5 — #847)

**Decision:** Surface the Quartermaster's last reconcile sweep through the **existing introspection path** rather than adding any new operator surface. `QuartermasterAgent.reconcile()` now records `self._last_sweep = {"counts": dict(counts), "at": time.time(), "trigger": "periodic"}` at the end of every pass (initialized to `None` in `__init__` for the never-run state), and a new `QuartermasterAgent.info()` override (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`) calls `super().info()` and adds a `reconciliation` block: `{"last_sweep": None}` when never run, otherwise `{"last_sweep": {...counts...}, "age_seconds": round(time.time() - at, 1), "trigger": ...}`. The block copies the whole counts dict and hard-indexes no individual key, so later-AD counters (`quarantined`, `too_fresh`, `truncated`, `stalled`, `remote_owner_skipped`) never KeyError an older renderer. The summary reaches the Captain automatically via the `agent_info quartermaster` intent (AD-320 introspection delegation → `IntrospectionAgent._agent_info` (agents/introspect.py:271) → `agent.info()`). **No `/board` slash command, no HTTP endpoint, and no `panels.py`/`shell.py` change** were added.
