**Rationale:** A verify-first pass found no `/board` command and no quartermaster reference in `experience/`, and the epic's "Do not add a new HTTP endpoint unless required; prefer the existing introspection path" guard pointed directly at `BaseAgent.info()` (substrate/agent.py:159) being overridable and already merged into the introspection render. Overriding `info()` is the minimum-surface change: it reuses the AD-320 self-knowledge path the Captain already uses to inspect agents, keeps the reconciliation state where the agent owns it, and avoids a new command/endpoint that would have to be documented, tested, and maintained. Copying the whole counts dict (instead of formatting a fixed human-readable line) is deliberate forward-compat: every subsequent AD in this epic adds a counter key, and a `.get`-free dict copy renders all of them without a per-AD renderer edit. Tests: `tests/test_ad883_reconcile_observability.py` (+5, real `WorkItemStore` + real `QuartermasterAgent` per BF-287): `reconcile()` records the summary, `info()` includes the `reconciliation.last_sweep` block, never-run reports `last_sweep: None` without crashing, `age_seconds` reflects elapsed time, and `info()` renders cleanly when counts carry later-AD keys. One commit.

### AD-884: Authority scoped to reconcile-only — consensus-free by Reversibility + Minimal Authority (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 4 — #847)

**Decision:** Recorded and regression-locked the `QuartermasterAgent`'s authority scope. The Quartermaster's authority is **scoped to reconcile-only operations** — `unassign_work_item`, re-`dispatch_work_item`, and the AD-877 metadata `quarantined` flag — all reversible board housekeeping. Per the Reversibility Preference and Minimal Authority axioms, **no consensus gate is required**: the agent performs no destructive, irreversible, or externally-visible side-effecting intents. It declares a single intent (`reconcile_board`) and must never declare a `requires_consensus=True` destructive intent; if a future change needs one, that is a new AD with a consensus design, not a Quartermaster capability. This AD adds **no** consensus gate, quorum vote, or red-team hook — the decision is that none is needed — and records the reasoning plus a regression guard instead. The only code change is one class constant on `QuartermasterAgent` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`): `RECONCILE_ONLY_INTENTS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"reconcile_board"})`, the allow-list the guard test asserts the declared descriptor names are a subset of.

**Rationale:** The scoping was previously **implicit** — the agent simply happened not to declare a consensus-gated intent. The Minimal Authority axiom wants scoped capabilities to be explicit and earned, and the Reversibility Preference axiom is the actual justification for the consensus-free design: every Quartermaster mutation is undoable board housekeeping (an item can be re-assigned, re-dispatched, or un-quarantined), so gating it behind a quorum vote would add governance cost with no safety benefit while slowing the very reconciliation sweep that exists to keep the board healthy. Making the scope explicit (the constant + the guard test) converts an accidental property into a deliberate, enforced contract: a future contributor who adds a destructive intent to the agent now trips the guard test rather than silently widening the Quartermaster's authority. Keeping the record in DECISIONS.md rather than a standalone governance doc keeps the architectural-decision trail in one append-only place. Tests: `tests/test_ad884_authority_scope.py` (+3, real `QuartermasterAgent` per BF-287, no LLM): declared `intent_descriptors` names are reconcile-only (`⊆ RECONCILE_ONLY_INTENTS` and `== {"reconcile_board"}`), no declared descriptor sets `requires_consensus=True`, and the agent stays `tier="utility"` / `agent_type="quartermaster"`. One commit.

### AD-878: Boot-race grace period — skip items younger than `min_item_age_seconds` (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 3 — #847)

**Decision:** Added a per-item boot-race grace period to `QuartermasterAgent.reconcile()` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`) so a work item created moments before a warm-boot sweep is not reclaimed mid-first-dispatch. A new bounded config field `min_item_age_seconds: int = Field(default=30, ge=0, le=600)` on `WorkBoardReconcilerConfig` (`src/probos/config.py`) is injected onto the live agent in `startup/finalize.py` `_wire_board_reconciler` (`agent._min_item_age_seconds = cfg.min_item_age_seconds`) alongside the AD-876/877 injections, with a matching constructor kwarg (`min_item_age_seconds=30`). The check runs **inside** the per-item Tier-2 `try`, after `md_current = wi.get("metadata") or {}` and **before** the AD-877 already-quarantined / backoff guards and any classification: if `self._min_item_age_seconds > 0` and `wi["created_at"] > time.time() - self._min_item_age_seconds`, the item is counted `too_fresh` and skipped (`continue`). The summary dict always carries the new `too_fresh` counter (default `0`, stable shape for the HXI and the AD-876 ticker logging). Setting the grace to `0` disables the skip entirely. No `WorkItemStatus` change; no change to `list_work_items`.

**Rationale:** Without the grace period there is a race: the dispatch path creates an `open` work item and is about to dispatch it, but a concurrent warm-boot reconcile sweep sees the item as "unassigned + dispatchable", classifies it `clear_and_reroute`, bumps `reconcile_attempts` (AD-877), and competes with the legitimate dispatch — wasting an attempt (moving the item closer to AD-877 quarantine) for an item that was never actually stranded. The grace period is an **always-on safety bound, not a transitional flag** (hence default `30` rather than the convention-#14 default-`False`): a sub-grace item is, by definition, too young to be confidently classified as stranded, so the conservative action is to leave it for the next sweep. The check is placed before the AD-877 attempt/backoff guards specifically so a fresh item neither accrues an attempt nor consumes a backoff window — it is treated as if the sweep never saw it. The bound is `[0, 600]`: `0` disables (for tests and operators who want eager reclaim), `600` (10 min) caps how long a genuinely-stranded item can hide behind the grace. Because the default is always-on, every pre-AD-878 quartermaster test (AD-875/876/877) that drives the sweep with fresh items now sees them skipped; those tests are pre-AD-878-contract and opt out of the grace (`min_item_age_seconds=0` in their `_qm` helper / `cfg.work_board_reconciler.min_item_age_seconds = 0` in the AD-876 warm-boot integration test), and the AD-875 empty-board exact-dict gained the always-present `too_fresh` key — an obsolete-contract fixture update, not a behavior regression. Tests: `tests/test_ad878_boot_grace_period.py` (+6, real `WorkItemStore` per BF-287, `_FakeRouter` only for the dispatch boundary, every item seeds an explicit `created_at`): a fresh item is skipped and never dispatched; an old item (`created_at = now - 120`) is processed normally; the boundary at exactly `now - min_item_age_seconds` is processed (strict `>` comparison); `min_item_age_seconds=0` disables the grace; the `too_fresh` key is present (`0`) when the grace is zero; and a `clear_and_reroute` of an old item does not let a fresh sibling accrue an attempt. One commit.

### AD-879: Deterministic oldest-first scan ordering + starvation guard (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 2 — #847)

**Decision:** Fixed item starvation in `QuartermasterAgent.reconcile()` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`). The sweep lists `open` + `in_progress` items via `WorkItemStore.list_work_items(status=…, limit=self._scan_limit)`, whose SQL is `ORDER BY priority ASC, created_at DESC` — newest-first within a priority band. Merged into the id-keyed dict and iterated in insertion order, the **oldest** stranded items sorted last and could fall outside the `scan_limit` window forever. The verify-first pass confirmed the epic's "ordering is already oldest-first; confirm only" branch is FALSE, so AD-879 adds an explicit re-sort of the merged set right after the merge: `ordered = sorted(merged.values(), key=lambda i: (i.priority, i.created_at))` (priority ascending = critical first, then `created_at` ascending = oldest first within a band), and the per-item loop iterates `ordered`. Added a starvation-visibility flag to the summary: `counts["truncated"]` defaults `False` and, when `len(merged) >= self._scan_limit`, is set `True` with one Tier-2 warning (`"Board reconcile truncated: merged=%d >= scan_limit=%d; oldest items prioritized but backlog growing"`). The key is always present in the counts dict. No SQL change to `list_work_items` and no change to the `scan_limit` default (200).

**Rationale:** Re-routing the *oldest* stranded item first is the correct policy — an item that has been stuck longest is the one most in need of reconciliation, and starving it indefinitely behind a stream of newer items defeats the purpose of the sweep. The re-sort lives **in the sweep only**, not in `list_work_items`' SQL, because the create-dispatch path and the REST board view depend on the existing newest-first ordering; changing the shared query to satisfy the reconciler would silently reorder unrelated callers (Open/Closed — extend the consumer, don't mutate the shared primitive). Full backlog drainage beyond `scan_limit` is deliberately out of scope: raising the cap or paginating the whole board is a separate capacity decision, and the honest signal for "the backlog is outgrowing the per-sweep window" is the `truncated` flag plus a warning, not an unbounded scan that could make a single sweep arbitrarily expensive. The per-status DB `limit` still caps the fetch; the re-sort only guarantees that *within whatever was fetched*, the oldest are processed first — so even a truncated sweep makes maximal progress on the items most at risk. `truncated` is always present (not conditionally added) so the counts dict has a stable shape for the HXI and the AD-876 ticker's logging. Tests: `tests/test_ad879_scan_ordering.py` (+5, real `WorkItemStore` per BF-287; a `_FakeRouter` records `dispatch_work_item` call order via the `unassigned_dispatchable → live_redispatch` path, which dispatches in processing order without mutating metadata): processing order is `(priority asc, created_at asc)`, same-priority older-first, lower-priority-number before higher regardless of age, `truncated` True when merged ≥ `scan_limit` (seeded small via the injected `_scan_limit`), and `truncated` False (key present) for a small backlog. The AD-875 empty-board exact-dict test gained the always-present `truncated` key (obsolete-contract guard, not a behavior regression). One commit.

### AD-877: Reconcile-attempt tracking + dead-letter quarantine thrash guard (Quartermaster-hardening epic, part 1 — #847)

**Decision:** Hardened `QuartermasterAgent.reconcile()` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`) so a permanently-stranded work item can no longer be unassigned and re-dispatched on every sweep indefinitely. Each `clear_and_reroute` action now performs read-modify-write on the item's `metadata` (`update_work_item` REPLACES the metadata column, so the agent reads the current item, mutates its dict, and writes it back): it increments `reconcile_attempts` and stamps `last_reconcile_at = time.time()` after the unassign + before the re-dispatch. When `reconcile_attempts + 1 >= self._max_reconcile_attempts` (config default 3) the item is **dead-lettered** instead: its metadata is stamped `quarantined=True`, `quarantine_reason="max_reconcile_attempts"`, `quarantined_at`, and the attempt counter is persisted; a single `EventType.WORK_ITEM_QUARANTINED` event is emitted (`{"work_item_id", "reason", "attempts"}`); and the item is **left assigned** (NOT unassigned) so it stops thrashing the board. Two early-skip guards run inside the per-item Tier-2 try before classification: an already-`quarantined` item (metadata flag truthy) is skipped and counted as `quarantined_skipped`; an item whose `last_reconcile_at` is within `self._reconcile_backoff_seconds` (config default 600s; `0` disables the cooldown) is skipped and counted as `backoff_skipped`. The summary dict always carries the three new counters (`quarantined`, `quarantined_skipped`, `backoff_skipped`, all `0` on an empty board); `degraded` keeps its AD-875 bool semantics. New bounded config on `WorkBoardReconcilerConfig` (`src/probos/config.py`): `max_reconcile_attempts: int = Field(default=3, ge=1, le=20)` and `reconcile_backoff_seconds: int = Field(default=600, ge=0, le=86400)`, injected onto the live agent in `startup/finalize.py` `_wire_board_reconciler` (`agent._max_reconcile_attempts`, `agent._reconcile_backoff_seconds`) alongside the AD-876 `_scan_limit` injection. New constructor kwargs with the same defaults. `import time` added at module top.

**Rationale:** AD-875's sweep re-dispatches any stranded `clear_and_reroute` item every cadence tick; for an item that is genuinely un-routable (no matching capability, a permanently dead department) that is an unbounded re-dispatch loop — the same work churning the bus and the dispatcher forever. A dead-letter quarantine is the standard bound: after N attempts, stop trying and surface the item for human/Captain attention via a distinct `WORK_ITEM_QUARANTINED` event, rather than silently dropping it or thrashing. Quarantine is recorded as a **metadata flag**, not a new `WorkItemStatus` enum value, deliberately: the work-type transition graph (AD-498) and the store's `_IMMUTABLE_FIELDS` stay untouched, no migration is needed, and the item keeps its real lifecycle status (an `open` quarantined item is still `open` — just flagged "don't reconcile me"). The item is left **assigned** on quarantine (not unassigned) because unassigning it would re-open it to the AD-581a create-dispatch path and defeat the guard; leaving it parked is what actually stops the thrash. Read-modify-write is mandatory because `update_work_item` replaces the metadata column wholesale (the BF-607/BF-608 lesson) — a blind write would erase every other metadata key. The `reconcile_backoff_seconds` cooldown is a second, softer guard: even below the attempt ceiling, an item shouldn't be hammered on back-to-back ticks, so a per-item cooldown gives a transient capability gap time to resolve before the next attempt. Both knobs are bounded Pydantic fields validated at parse time, and both default to safe production values (3 attempts, 10-minute cooldown) so the guard is active the moment the reconciler is enabled — this is a safety bound, not a transitional capability, so it does NOT default off. Tests: `tests/test_ad877_reconcile_thrash_guard.py` (+10, real `WorkItemStore`/`AgentRegistry`/`WorkItemReconciler` per BF-287; `_FakeRouter` only at the dispatch boundary): attempt-counter increment + `last_reconcile_at` stamp on `clear_and_reroute`, reaching the ceiling quarantines-not-redispatches and leaves the assignee untouched, the `WORK_ITEM_QUARANTINED` payload, `max_reconcile_attempts=1` quarantines on first attempt, already-quarantined → `quarantined_skipped` (untouched), recent `last_reconcile_at` → `backoff_skipped`, `backoff=0` disables the cooldown, the empty-board summary always carries the three new keys, and a per-item exception still marks `degraded` while the sibling item is cleared. The AD-875 empty-board exact-dict test was updated to include the three new always-present counters (obsolete-contract guard, not a behavior regression). One commit.

### AD-876: Wire the Quartermaster into the runtime with a cadence ticker (Quartermaster epic, part 3 — closes #846)

**Decision:** Wired the AD-875 `QuartermasterAgent` into boot, shutdown, and a periodic cadence, closing the work-board reconciliation epic. New transitional config `WorkBoardReconcilerConfig` (`src/probos/config.py`): `enabled: bool = False` (conv #14 — transitional flag defaults off), `interval_seconds: int = Field(default=300, ge=30, le=3600)`, `warm_boot: bool = True`, `scan_limit: int = Field(default=200, ge=1, le=2000)`; docstring notes it requires `hybrid_dispatch`. Added to `SystemConfig` as `work_board_reconciler: WorkBoardReconcilerConfig = Field(default_factory=…)` beside `hybrid_dispatch`. The `quartermaster` template is registered in `runtime.py` (`spawner.register_template("quartermaster", QuartermasterAgent)`, mirrors `introspect`), and a single-agent `quartermaster` pool is created in `startup/agent_fleet.py` **only when** `config.work_board_reconciler.enabled`. New `src/probos/mesh/board_reconciler_ticker.py` — `BoardReconcilerTicker(*, agent, interval_seconds, warm_boot, startup_delay=10.0)` owns the cadence (the agent itself has no loop): an idempotent `start()` parks the `asyncio.create_task(self._loop(), name="ad876-board-reconciler")` reference on `self._task`; `_loop()` runs an optional warm-boot reconcile after `startup_delay` then `await self._agent.reconcile()` every `interval_seconds`, each sweep wrapped in `_safe_reconcile()` (Tier-2 log-and-degrade, `CancelledError` re-raised); an idempotent `async stop()` cancels + awaits the task, swallows `CancelledError`, log-warns any other teardown exception, and nulls `self._task`. `startup/finalize.py` gains `_wire_board_reconciler(*, runtime, config) -> bool` (placed between `_wire_hybrid_dispatch` and `_wire_capability_gap_driver`, called inside the finalize try-block right after `_wire_hybrid_dispatch`): returns `False` (INFO no-op) when disabled or when `runtime.work_item_router` (only present with hybrid_dispatch), `work_item_store`, or `registry` is absent; otherwise it builds a `WorkItemReconciler`, resolves the live quartermaster via `registry.get_by_pool("quartermaster")`, injects the collaborators by their exact private attrs (`agent._reconciler/_store/_router/_emit/_episodic/_scan_limit`), constructs and `start()`s the ticker, and parks it on `runtime.board_reconciler_ticker`. `startup/shutdown.py` `await`s `runtime.board_reconciler_ticker.stop()` (after the AD-733-1 attachment_reaper stop, honest-degrade, nulls the attr).

**Rationale:** AD-874 (reusable dispatch + classifier) and AD-875 (the deterministic sweep agent) were deliberately built wiring-free so the cadence and lifecycle could land as a separate, independently-reviewable unit. The ticker owns the cadence rather than the agent so the agent stays a pure `perceive → decide → act → report` sweep with no scheduling concern (Single Responsibility) — the same split as every other ProbOS background loop. `enabled` defaults `False` because a board-reconciliation sweep is a transitional capability that should ship dark and be flipped on deliberately (convention #14 — default-True on a transitional flag is breaking-change-on-first-commit); and because it is gated on `work_item_router`, it is inert unless `hybrid_dispatch` is also enabled, so the default config creates no pool, wires no ticker, and changes no behavior. `_wire_board_reconciler` injects by the exact private attrs the AD-875 constructor reads (not the public kwargs) because the agent is spawned by the pool factory before finalization, so collaborators are injected post-construction — the same late-bind pattern as the other finalize wirers. Every dependency check is INFO-level honest-degrade (a missing router/store/registry/agent is an expected configuration, not an error), and `stop()` is idempotent + non-raising so a duplicate shutdown (sleep/wake SIGTERM, BF-598) tears the ticker down cleanly without becoming an unretrieved task exception. The ticker holds its task reference (asserted by a source scan in the tests, per the fire-and-forget review flag), uses `asyncio.create_task` (never `ensure_future`), and re-raises `CancelledError` so cancellation propagates. Tests: `tests/test_ad876_reconciler_wiring.py` (+12, real `WorkItemStore`/`AgentRegistry`/`SystemConfig` per BF-287; `_FakeRouter`/`_FakeAgent` only at the dispatch/sweep boundary): config defaults + bounds rejection (`interval_seconds`/`scan_limit`), `_wire_board_reconciler` disabled/missing-router/missing-agent no-ops, the enabled injection path (asserts each injected attr incl. `_scan_limit==77` and `runtime.board_reconciler_ticker` set), the ticker task-reference source assertion, warm-boot reconcile-once (`startup_delay=0.0`), idempotent `stop()`, a real-store warm-boot redispatch integration (stranded dispatchable item → `router.dispatched` non-empty), and the default-config gate predicate (no pool, `_wire` returns `False`). Blast-radius gate (runtime/workforce/dispatch/finalize/config/shutdown) 181 green. One commit.

### AD-875: QuartermasterAgent — deterministic work-board reconciliation sweep (Quartermaster epic, part 2)

**Decision:** Added `QuartermasterAgent` (`src/probos/agents/quartermaster.py`), a plain deterministic `BaseAgent` (`tier="utility"`, `agent_type="quartermaster"`, no LLM — mirrors `IntrospectionAgent`) that consumes the AD-874 `WorkItemReconciler` decisions and performs the board mutations. `reconcile()` lists only the live `open` + `in_progress` work items from the `WorkItemStore` (`list_work_items(status=…, limit=scan_limit)`, merged by id; terminal statuses are never scanned), and for each item classifies via `WorkItemRouter.is_dispatchable(wi)` + `WorkItemReconciler.classify(wi, is_dispatchable=…)`, then executes the action: `live_redispatch → router.dispatch_work_item(wi)`; `clear_and_reroute → store.unassign_work_item(id, reason=…)` then re-dispatch the freshly-read cleared item; `skip → count only`. Returns a `{scanned, redispatched, cleared, skipped, degraded}` counts dict. Per-item failures are tier-2 log-and-degrade (`degraded=True`, sweep continues to the next item); a missing collaborator (`store`/`router`/`reconciler` is `None`) returns a degraded zero-summary without raising. On completion it emits a single `EventType.WORK_ITEM_RECONCILED` (new enum value, added after `WORK_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGED`) carrying the counts, and stores an optional episodic `Episode` summary (lazy import, tier-2). The agent follows the `perceive → decide → act → report` lifecycle; `handle_intent` services only `reconcile_board` (any other intent → `None`).

**Rationale:** AD-874 split the pure classifier (`WorkItemReconciler.classify`) from any sweep loop precisely so AD-875 could add the *mechanical* half — listing the board, calling the classifier, and mutating — as a separate, independently-testable unit. The Quartermaster is the agent that owns those board mutations, kept deliberately LLM-free: re-dispatching a stranded item or clearing a dead assignee is deterministic policy, not cognition, so it is a utility-tier `BaseAgent` rather than a `CognitiveAgent` (no instructions, no reasoning, no consensus). Scanning only `open` + `in_progress` keeps the sweep cheap and naturally excludes `done`/`failed`/`cancelled` (the classifier's `terminal` branch is a defensive belt that the status filter already exercises). The single `WORK_ITEM_RECONCILED` summary event (not per-item events) keeps the bus quiet — one event per sweep, with aggregate counts for the HXI — and the counts dict is the agent's machine-readable report for the future ticker (AD-876) to log/trend. Honest-degrade everywhere (per-item and missing-collaborator) means a misbehaving store/router can never crash the sweep or the eventual background ticker; a degraded sweep reports `degraded=True` rather than silently completing. No ticker, startup wiring, pool creation, or config yet — AD-876 wires it. Tests: `tests/test_ad875_quartermaster.py` (+12, real `WorkItemStore` + real `AgentRegistry` + real `WorkItemReconciler` per BF-287; a `_FakeRouter` records dispatch calls and reads `metadata["dispatchable"]` at the dispatch boundary): live-assignee/dead-assignee/in-progress-owner/non-dispatchable/empty-board/per-item-error/missing-collaborator sweeps, the `reconcile_board` lifecycle round-trip, non-matching intent → `None`, utility tier, and a decomposer gap-regex hygiene check on the descriptor strings. One commit.

### AD-874: Reusable work-item dispatch path + deterministic stranded-item classifier (Quartermaster epic, part 1)

**Decision:** Two changes, no behavior change to live paths. (1) Refactored the AD-581a `WorkItemRouter` (`src/probos/mesh/work_item_router.py`) for Open/Closed reuse: extracted `async dispatch_work_item(wi: dict) -> None` containing everything from the `is_dispatchable` early-return through `DepartmentDispatcher.route` (direct/broadcast `RoutingDecision`), `TaskEvent` construction (`task_event_for_agent` / `task_event_broadcast`), the `HYBRID_DISPATCH_DIRECT` / `HYBRID_DISPATCH_BROADCAST` emits, and `dispatcher.dispatch`. `on_work_item_created(event)` now only unwraps the `{"data": {"work_item": …}}` envelope and delegates to `dispatch_work_item`, keeping its tier-2 log-and-degrade wrapper. (2) Added `WorkItemReconciler` (`src/probos/cognitive/work_reconciler.py`), a pure deterministic classifier: `resolve_live_agent(assigned_to)` returns the live agent slot for an assignee by checking `AgentRegistry.get` first, then walking the AD-441 sovereign-DID seam (assignee slot → `AgentIdentityRegistry.get_by_slot` birth-cert `agent_uuid` → the live registry agent whose own cert carries the same `agent_uuid`); `classify(wi, *, is_dispatchable)` returns a frozen `ReconcileDecision(work_item_id, action, assignee, resolved_agent_id, reason)` with `action ∈ {skip, live_redispatch, clear_and_reroute}` and reasons `terminal`, `not_dispatchable`, `unassigned_dispatchable`, `in_progress_live_owner`, `assignee_live`, `assignee_not_live`. All collaborator access is tier-2 log-and-degrade.

**Rationale:** The Quartermaster reconciler (AD-875) must re-dispatch work items stranded by agent re-spawns (slot churn from warm boot / AD-441 sovereign identity), but the only dispatch logic lived inside the `WORK_ITEM_CREATED` event listener, which a sweep cannot reuse without faking an event envelope. Extracting `dispatch_work_item` gives both the create-listener and the future reconciler one governed dispatch path (same `DepartmentDispatcher`, same `TaskEvent` shape, same emits) — Open for the new caller, Closed against duplicating routing. The classifier is deliberately split from any sweep loop or wiring: it is a side-effect-free function of `(work_item_dict, is_dispatchable)` so it can be unit-tested against a real registry with no runtime, and so the policy (which states get re-dispatched vs cleared vs left alone) is auditable in isolation before AD-875 adds the loop and AD-876 wires the ticker. `resolve_live_agent` reuses the existing AD-441 birth-certificate seam rather than introducing a new agent-identity map: an assignee recorded against a now-dead slot is still the *same sovereign agent* if a live slot shares its `agent_uuid`, so the work should follow the agent, not be orphaned. No sweep, no scheduling, no LLM (this is mechanical reconciliation, not cognition). Tests: `tests/test_ad874_work_reconciler.py` (+13, real `AgentRegistry` + real `AgentIdentityRegistry` per BF-287) and `tests/test_ad839_work_item_dispatch.py` (+4 — direct and broadcast routing identical through `dispatch_work_item`, non-dispatchable early-return, `on_work_item_created` still routes via the shared path). One commit.

### BF-608: Enforce AD-498 `requires_assignment` at the store boundary (a task cannot enter `in_progress` while `Unassigned`)

**Decision:** Made `WorkItemStore.transition_work_item` (`src/probos/workforce.py`) honor the `requires_assignment` flag that AD-498 attached to state-machine transitions but never read. New `WorkTypeRegistry.transition_requires_assignment(type_id, from_status, to_status) -> bool` exposes the per-edge flag (unknown type / unknown edge → `False`, matching `validate_transition`'s backward-compat stance). Immediately after the AD-498 `validate_transition` check — where `item.assigned_to` is available — `transition_work_item` now refuses the move when `item.assigned_to is None` and the edge is flagged `requires_assignment` (e.g. `task` `open → in_progress`, `work_order`/`incident` `scheduled/open → in_progress`): it logs a `BF-608` warning and returns `None`, leaving the item in its prior (dispatchable) status. Two legitimate consumers that promote an unassigned item to `in_progress` were updated to claim an owner first: the AD-867 crew **parent** promotion (`crew_orchestrator._promote_parent`) now assigns the coordination-container parent to `"crew_orchestrator"` before transitioning (its children already carry the real per-agent assignments via `_assign_child`); the BF-607 dispatch handler and `crew_executor` (children) already assign before transitioning, so they were unaffected.

**Rationale:** BF-606 and BF-607 each addressed one facet of Captain-reported work item `1e0ffcdb7b57` ("Bayesian trust calibration best practices", `yeo-delegated`) showing `in_progress` / `Unassigned`, but the item *stayed* unassigned after BF-607 shipped. Ground-truth inspection of the live runtime API (`/api/work-items`) confirmed the item was created at 11:03 and reached `in_progress` at 11:08 — **before** the BF-607 server restart at 15:01 — so it is a stale orphan from pre-fix code that the `WorkItemRouter` (which dispatches only on `WORK_ITEM_CREATED`) never re-dispatches. More importantly, BF-607 only claims on the *direct*-dispatch path (`intent.target_agent_id == self.id`); this item reached `in_progress` via a broadcast dispatch / the AD-855 capability-gap `blocked → in_progress` resume, neither of which runs the claim. The true root cause is upstream of all of these: AD-498 defined `WorkTypeTransition("open", "in_progress", requires_assignment=True)` to encode "you cannot start work without an owner", but `validate_transition` only checked that the edge *exists*, never the flag — so **any** path could drive an unassigned item into `in_progress` and the board faithfully rendered the contradictory state. Enforcing the flag at the single store-boundary chokepoint (where `assigned_to` is known) makes the contradictory state unreachable from every path — direct dispatch, broadcast, AD-855 resume, the REST transition endpoint — without the store needing to know about the agent registry (layer discipline preserved: the store rejects rather than auto-assigning a synthetic owner). A refused transition leaves the item `open` and dispatchable, which is the honest state (nobody has claimed it) rather than a lie (in-progress with no owner). The crew parent is the one genuine "no single worker" case — it is a coordination container, so it is claimed for the orchestrating subsystem (`"crew_orchestrator"`), which is both correct (the orchestrator owns the parent) and more honest on the board than `Unassigned`. The stale orphan itself predates the fix and is cleaned up out-of-band via the live API; BF-608 prevents recurrence. Tests: `tests/test_workforce.py` (+5 — refusal of an unassigned `open → in_progress` with no DB write / no `STATUS_CHANGED` emit, the `BF-608` warning, an assigned item transitions, the AD-855 `blocked → in_progress` resume keeps an existing owner, and the `transition_requires_assignment` registry helper across task/work_order/unknown edges) plus 9 existing transition tests updated to assign an owner before promoting; `tests/test_ad867_crew_orchestrator.py` (parent-promotion now asserts `assigned_to == "crew_orchestrator"`). **Reconciliation:** this commit also lands the **BF-606** same-status no-op guard (`if new_status == item.status: return item`, before `validate_transition`) and its two tests — BF-606 was *documented* in `a33f67bd` but its `workforce.py`/`test_workforce.py` code was never committed (only the banners landed), so HEAD's runtime never actually had the BF-606 fix. The BF-606 and BF-608 changes are entangled in the same hunks (the BF-606 same-status tests' setup transition into `in_progress` now requires BF-608 assignment), so a clean per-BF split is not safely separable; they ship together and HEAD's code now matches its BF-606 docs. One commit.

### BF-607: Dispatched work item is claimed by the handling agent (stop the `in_progress` / `Unassigned` board state)

**Decision:** When a `CognitiveAgent` handles a directly-dispatched work item, `_handle_work_item_dispatch` (`src/probos/cognitive/cognitive_agent.py`) now claims the item for itself — it reads the current item and, only if `assigned_to` is empty, calls `store.update_work_item(work_item_id, assigned_to=self.id)` immediately before the existing `transition_work_item(id, "in_progress")`. An item that the Captain or crew orchestrator already assigned is left untouched (no reassignment). The claim is tier-2 log-and-degrade: a failure logs a warning and the item still transitions to `in_progress`.

**Rationale:** A Captain-reported board screenshot showed a `yeo-delegated` task as `in_progress` + `dispatched` with `Assigned to: Unassigned`. The AD-581a `WorkItemRouter` resolves a direct agent (`decision.agent_id`) and emits a `work_item_dispatched` task event to it, but it never persists the assignment to the store — and the AD-839 dispatch handler only transitioned status, so the board faithfully reported work running with nobody assigned. The handling agent is the correct place to record the assignment: it is the one actually doing the work, so claiming `assigned_to = self.id` makes the displayed assignee reflect reality. The `if not current.assigned_to` guard preserves the Captain/crew-orchestrator push-assignment path (those set `assigned_to` at create/delegate time, e.g. `crew_orchestrator._assign_child`), so this only fills in the gap left by router dispatch. `assigned_to` is a mutable field (`update_work_item` writes it; it is not in `_IMMUTABLE_FIELDS = {"id", "created_at", "created_by"}`). Single-point fix co-located with the in_progress transition; the dispatch re-run / acknowledgment behavior is untouched. The concurrently-reported `tier=standard` empty-content LLM warnings were diagnosed as a transient (the config pins `llm_model_standard: claude-sonnet-4.6` and the live proxy log confirmed Sonnet 4.6 serving healthy responses; AD-632c caught the one-off empty completion and AD-643a fell back and recovered) — no code change for that. Tests: `tests/test_ad839_work_item_dispatch.py` (+3 — claims unassigned, does not reassign already-assigned, log-and-degrades a failed claim while still transitioning); the existing 5 AD-839 tests stay green. One commit.

### BF-606: Same-status work-item transition is an idempotent no-op (stop the `in_progress → in_progress` warning loop)

**Decision:** Made `WorkItemStore.transition_work_item` (`src/probos/workforce.py`) treat a transition to the status the item is already in as an idempotent no-op success. A new early guard — `if new_status == item.status: return item` — runs immediately after the item is fetched and *before* the AD-498 `validate_transition` state-machine check. For a same-status request it returns the item unchanged: no DB write, no `WORK_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGED` event, and no `logger.warning("Invalid transition …")`. The pre-existing `test_transition_from_terminal_status_rejected` was relying on the old behavior by accident (it created a `task`, called `transition_work_item(id, "done")` which is **not** a legal `open → done` transition for `task`, so the item never left `open`, then asserted `open → open` returned `None`); its setup was corrected to reach `done` via the valid `open → in_progress → done` path so it genuinely exercises terminal-status rejection.

**Rationale:** A crash forensic of the live runtime (process hard-killed 2026-06-05 11:28:08) surfaced a death-spiral pathology: work item `1e0ffcdb7b57` logged `Invalid transition for 1e0ffcdb7b57: Work type 'task' does not allow transition 'in_progress' → 'in_progress'` dozens of times. Root cause: `work_item_dispatched` is delivered **at-least-once** — it broadcasts to every crew agent (each recipient's `_handle_work_item_dispatch` calls `transition_work_item(id, "in_progress")` at the end), the AD-855 capability-gap `_resume` path sets an item to `in_progress` and then re-dispatches it, and the bus can redeliver — so an already-`in_progress` item is repeatedly re-driven. The AD-498 state machine has no `in_progress → in_progress` edge, so each redundant delivery logged a warning and returned `None` (which `_resume` and other callers read as a *failure*). The idempotent-consumer pattern is the correct fix for at-least-once delivery: transitioning to the current state is success-by-definition, not a state-machine violation. The guard sits before `validate_transition` so it cannot interact with terminal-status logic (a terminal item asked to move to a *different* status still hits the existing rejection; asked to "move" to its own terminal status is a harmless no-op). This is a single-point fix at the store boundary — it does not touch the dispatch handler's re-run behavior, so the AD-855 resume re-dispatch keeps working (it now gets the item back instead of a spurious `None`). The broadcast/redelivery amplification of the *agentic re-run* is a separate, broader concern (IntentBus fan-out) left for a follow-up. Tests: `tests/test_workforce.py` (+2 — same-status returns the item with zero emits; same-status emits no `Invalid transition` warning) plus the corrected terminal-status test. One commit.



**Decision:** Updated the count assertion in `ui/src/components/icons/Glyphs.test.tsx` from `expect(count).toBe(25)` to `29` to match the 29 glyph components currently exported from `ui/src/components/icons/Glyphs.tsx`. Comment updated to note the +4 drift since BF-041.

**Rationale:** Four glyphs were added to `Glyphs.tsx` (last touched 2026-05-31) without updating the hardcoded export-count guard in its test (last touched 2026-04-26), leaving the test red on `main` — unrelated to and discovered during BF-604. The count is derived (`Object.keys(Glyphs).filter(typeof === 'function').length`), so the assertion is purely a tripwire that a glyph was added/removed deliberately; bumping it to the real count restores the tripwire. Trivial, low-risk stale-constant fix; one commit.
 Board layout — clear the tab bar, resizable WORK columns, auto-hide the empty KANBAN tab

**Decision:** Fixed three HXI board complaints from the Captain in one cohesive UI change (no backend touched). (1) **Overlap:** the crew WORK board (`ui/src/components/work/WorkBoard.tsx`) and the Mission-Control KANBAN board (`ui/src/components/bridge/FullKanban.tsx`) rendered their headers under the fixed `ViewSwitcher` tab bar (`position: fixed; top: 12; left: 12`). Both root containers now reserve `paddingTop` clearance (`TAB_BAR_CLEARANCE = 40` on WORK, matching `40` on KANBAN) with `boxSizing: 'border-box'`, so the toolbar sits below the floating tabs. (2) **Resizable columns:** WORK columns were fixed equal-flex (`flex: 1; minWidth: 160`). Added `colWidths` state (`Record<ColKey, number | null>`, all `null` = auto) and a `startResize` pointer handler; each non-terminal column renders a `role="separator"` drag handle on its right edge (`cursor: col-resize`). A resized column switches to explicit `width: Xpx; flex: '0 0 auto'`; un-resized columns keep `flex: 1; minWidth: MIN_COL_WIDTH (140)`. (3) **Two-board confusion:** the KANBAN tab is now hidden when there are no active builds — `ViewSwitcher` (`ui/src/components/ViewSwitcher.tsx`) reads `missionControlTasks` and only includes the KANBAN tab when it is non-empty, with a `useEffect` that redirects `mainViewer` from `'kanban'` → `'work'` if the tab is hidden out from under the viewer. Tests: `ui/src/__tests__/WorkBoard.bf604.test.tsx` (+3 — top clearance, one resize handle per non-terminal column, col-resize cursor), `ui/src/__tests__/ViewSwitcher.bf604.test.tsx` (+4 — KANBAN hidden when no builds, shown when builds active, redirect-when-hidden, no-redirect-while-active); the existing `ComponentRendering.test.tsx` ViewSwitcher case was updated to seed a build so the full tab set renders. One commit.

**Rationale:** The Captain reported the board overlapping the menu, asked why WORK and KANBAN both exist, and noted KANBAN was always empty. WORK (WorkItemStore, AD-496/497) and KANBAN ("Mission Control" build/design pipeline, BuildQueueManager, AD-322/325) are **different systems that share a kanban-style UI** — different actors (crew agents vs. Architect/Builder), different stores, different semantics — so merging them would conflate crew task tracking with the self-modification build queue. The right fix is progressive disclosure (HXI Design Principle #5): KANBAN only surfaces when it has content, so a Captain with no active builds sees one board, not two, and the empty-board confusion disappears without removing the pipeline view. The overlap fix is a pure layout offset (the tab bar is `position: fixed`, so it does not participate in the board's flow and the board must reserve space for it). Resizable columns honor the Captain's direct request and use a pointer-drag handle rather than a library, keeping the dependency surface flat. The `useEffect` redirect is load-bearing: without it, a Captain sitting on the KANBAN view when the last build completes would be stranded on a now-tabless viewer.

### BF-603: Intent self-tag must tolerate quoted values and strip from any position (no leak to the Captain)

**Decision:** Hardened the AD-722a intent self-tag parse/strip regexes in `src/probos/avatars/divergence_detector.py` so the `<intent emotion=NAME>` tag can never reach the Captain. Three regex-only changes (no wiring touched): (1) `_TAG_RE` (parse, searches anywhere) now accepts an optional quote around the value — `<intent\s+emotion\s*=\s*["']?([a-zA-Z_]+)["']?\s*/?\s*>`. (2) `_TAG_STRIP_RE` gains the same optional-quote tolerance AND drops the trailing `\s*$` end-of-line anchor plus the `re.MULTILINE` flag, so it matches the tag at any position (leading / inline / trailing) and consumes adjacent whitespace. (3) `strip_intent_self_tag` now does `_TAG_STRIP_RE.sub(" ", text).strip()` (was `.sub("", text).rstrip()`) — collapsing each match to a single space so inline removal of a mid-prose tag never glues the surrounding words together, then trimming the result.

**Rationale:** Yeo (YeomanAgent) leaked a literal `<intent emotion="warm">` at the head of a 1:1 DM reply. The AD-722a self-tag is operator opt-in (`avatar_telemetry.divergence_detection`, default OFF); when ON, the LLM is instructed to append `<intent emotion=NAME>` and `apply_divergence_check` (single call site, `routers/agents.py:agent_chat`) parses + **unconditionally strips** it before `mark_reply_emitted` — "the tag MUST NEVER reach the Captain." The instruction teaches the unquoted form, but the model emitted a **quoted** value, which the value class `[a-zA-Z_]+` could not match: the tag therefore failed BOTH to parse (divergence signal silently lost) and to strip (raw tag leaked). The strip regex was additionally anchored to end-of-line, so even an unquoted tag placed at the start (as Yeo did) would not have been removed. The fix attacks both gaps at the single source of truth — the two module-level regexes — rather than touching the call site, preserving the AD-722a single-call-site invariant. `sub(" ")` + `strip()` replaces `sub("")` + `rstrip()` so that an inline tag (`"Acknowledged <intent emotion='warm'> Captain."`) collapses to `"Acknowledged Captain."` instead of `"Acknowledged Captain."` losing the space; trailing/leading cases trim cleanly. Idempotency and the prose-safety guarantee (`"I am intent on warmth."` untouched) are preserved and pinned by tests. Tests: `tests/test_ad722a_divergence_detector.py` (+7 — double/single-quoted parse, quoted self-closing, the exact leading-quoted leak shape, leading-unquoted strip, inline-no-word-merge, quoted idempotency). The full 91-case AD-722a/AD-737 divergence + taxonomy suite stays green. One commit.

### BF-602: Ward Room routing must quiesce on shutdown (no fire-and-forget post into a closed DB)

**Decision:** Gave `WardRoomRouter` (`src/probos/ward_room_router.py`) an explicit shutdown teardown and made its coalesced-routing path crash-safe during shutdown. Four changes: (1) two new instance attributes — `_stopping: bool = False` and `_coalesce_fire_tasks: set[asyncio.Task[None]]` — plus a new sync, idempotent `stop()` method that sets `_stopping = True`, cancels every pending `_coalesce_timers` `TimerHandle` (and clears the dict), and cancels every in-flight `_fire` task (and clears the set). (2) An early-return guard `if self._stopping: return` at the top of `route_event_coalesced`. (3) The same guard at the top of `route_event` (after the existing `if not self._ward_room` check) so the direct routing path is also suppressed once shutdown begins. (4) `route_event_coalesced` no longer schedules `_fire` as a bare `asyncio.create_task`; a new `_spawn_fire` closure holds the task in `_coalesce_fire_tasks` (drained via `task.add_done_callback(self._coalesce_fire_tasks.discard)`), guards on `_stopping`, and `_fire` itself re-checks `_stopping`, then wraps `route_event` in a try/except that re-raises `asyncio.CancelledError` and log-and-degrades any other `Exception`. Wiring: `startup/shutdown.py` calls `runtime.ward_room_router.stop()` immediately after the BF-296 Phase A intent-dispatch close — before the explicit consolidation `dream_cycle` — inside a Tier-2 honest-degrade try/except (absent router/attr on transitional procs logs a warning and proceeds).

**Rationale:** On shutdown the explicit dream_cycle drives agents to post to the Ward Room (a real shutdown log showed `yeoman` running `proactive_think` during consolidation). Each `ward_room_post_created` event schedules a ~200ms AD-616 coalesce timer whose `_fire()` callback calls `route_event → get_thread`. The timer was a fire-and-forget `asyncio.create_task` with no reference held, so when it fired *after* the ward_room aiosqlite connection was torn down it raised `ValueError('no active connection')` that nobody awaited — surfacing as the noisy `asyncio: Task exception was never retrieved` traceback at the very end of shutdown. The fix attacks all three latent faults the bug exposed: the **ordering** fault (routing kept running after the DB closed) is closed by quiescing the router at BF-296 Phase A, before any shutdown post is created; the **fire-and-forget** fault (exceptions silently lost / unretrieved) is closed by holding the task reference and draining it on done; and the **defense-in-depth** fault (a late or in-flight fire could still race) is closed by the `_stopping` guards on both routing entry points plus the log-and-degrade wrapper in `_fire`. `stop()` is synchronous because it only cancels handles/tasks (no awaitable teardown) and idempotent because shutdown can re-enter (BF-598). The guard reads a plain `bool` attribute always set in `__init__`; no defensive `getattr` was added to production code (the one partial-construction unit test in `test_ad616_router_hot_path.py` got `_stopping = False` added to its `__new__` fixture, mirroring the BF-598 precedent where MagicMock/partial doubles were given the new guard attribute). Tests: `tests/test_bf602_ward_room_shutdown_quiesce.py` (11 — `stop()` exists/sync/idempotent, sets the flag, cancels a pending coalesce timer + clears it, cancels an in-flight `_fire` task; `route_event`/`route_event_coalesced` no-op when stopping while the normal path still schedules; the closed-DB regression where `_fire`'s `route_event` raises `ValueError('no active connection')` is caught and degraded with a BF-602 warning rather than left unretrieved; the in-flight `_fire` task reference is held while routing and drained on completion; and a `startup/shutdown.py` source assertion that it calls `ward_room_router.stop()`). Real-object fixtures (`WardRoomRouter.__new__` + minimal attributes, `AsyncMock` only for the `route_event` collaborator being simulated) per the no-MagicMock-at-substrate-boundary rule.

### AD-873: Ebbinghaus episode decay + composite retrieval reranking

**Decision:** Closed the Memory Epistemics wave (the third and final unit after AD-871 provenance + AD-872 forge observability) with a forgetting curve over episodic memory and a config-gated composite recall reranker. Five changes: (1) Two new last-position fields on the frozen `Episode` dataclass (`src/probos/types.py`): `strength: float = 1.0` and `stability: float = EBBINGHAUS_DEFAULT_STABILITY_SECONDS`, plus the module constant `EBBINGHAUS_DEFAULT_STABILITY_SECONDS: float = 1_728_000.0` (20 days). (2) Two pure, fully-typed decay helpers in `src/probos/cognitive/episodic.py`: `decayed_strength(strength, stability, delta_seconds) -> float` (`strength * math.exp(-delta_seconds / stability)`, guarding `stability <= 0` and `delta_seconds <= 0` by returning `strength` unchanged) and `reinforced_stability(stability, activation) -> float` (`stability * (1.0 + _STABILITY_REINFORCEMENT_GAIN * activation)` with `_STABILITY_REINFORCEMENT_GAIN = 0.25`, guarding a non-positive activation). (3) `EpisodicMemory.sweep_episode_decay(activation_tracker=None, *, limit=500) -> dict[str, int]` — reads one page of episode metadata via `asyncio.to_thread(self._collection.get, ...)`, batch-reads activations (honest-degrade → `{}`), and per episode recomputes `stability` **idempotently from the default baseline** (`reinforced_stability(EBBINGHAUS_DEFAULT_STABILITY_SECONDS, activation)`), decays `strength`, and persists via the AD-608 `update_episode_metadata` read/merge/update primitive; returns `{"swept": N, "reinforced": M}`. (4) A `DreamingEngine` Step 7f2 decay sweep (`src/probos/cognitive/dreaming.py`, between Step 7f and 7g) that calls `sweep_episode_decay(self._activation_tracker)` during the offline dream cycle. (5) Config-gated composite recall reranking: `EpisodicMemory.recall` over-fetches (`k * 10` instead of `k * 3`) and reranks via a static geometric `_composite_recall_score` (similarity baseline multiplied by `_clamp01(field) ** weight` for strength / recency=`exp(-age_hours/168.0)` / importance / confidence, each `if w:` skipped when its weight is 0) when `self._recall_rerank_enabled`, preserving the AD-607a anomaly gate and the relevance threshold; gated by two new `__init__` kwargs (`recall_rerank_enabled: bool = False`, `recall_rerank_weights: dict[str, float] | None = None`) backed by two new `MemoryConfig` fields (`config.py`) and wired at the primary `__main__.py` boot site (the migration CLI site left at defaults → rerank disabled). The new fields round-trip through ChromaDB via `_episode_to_metadata` (`float(ep.strength)` / `float(ep.stability)`) and `_metadata_to_episode` (float reads with defaults `1.0` / `EBBINGHAUS_DEFAULT_STABILITY_SECONDS`).

**Rationale:** Provenance (AD-871) gave a memory graded belief and forge observability (AD-872) made the designer measurable; the missing third piece was that memory had no notion of *forgetting* — every episode was equally retrievable forever, so stale low-importance traces competed with fresh load-bearing ones at recall time. The Ebbinghaus forgetting curve (`strength = e^(-Δt / stability)`) is the canonical model: a reinforced (recently-activated) memory grows its `stability` (the time constant), so it decays slower; an un-reinforced one fades. Recomputing `stability` **idempotently from the default baseline** rather than compounding the stored value is load-bearing — a decay sweep that ran twice (two dream cycles before a new activation) must not double-reinforce, so the sweep is safe to re-run. Decay runs only in `DreamingEngine` (the offline consolidation path), never on the recall hot path, so retrieval latency is untouched. The composite reranker is **disabled by default** (`recall_rerank_enabled=False`) so zero-config boot behavior is byte-identical to pre-AD-873 semantic-only recall; the geometric form (multiply, not add) means any single near-zero factor suppresses a result (an AND of soft constraints), and an all-zero weight map collapses `_composite_recall_score` back to the raw similarity so a misconfigured weight set degrades to semantic-only rather than to noise. The over-fetch (`k * 10`) gives the reranker a candidate pool to reorder while the relevance threshold and AD-607a anomaly gate still bound what is eligible. Every new seam honest-degrades: a missing/throwing activation tracker yields an empty batch (decay still proceeds with `activation=0`), a per-episode persist failure logs and continues the sweep, the dream-cycle Step 7f2 wraps the whole call in Tier-2 log-and-degrade so a decay failure never aborts consolidation, and the ChromaDB read seam defaults malformed `strength`/`stability` values so pre-AD-873 rows recall cleanly with neutral defaults — zero migration. Tests: `tests/test_ad873_episode_decay.py` (25 — decay-helper guard matrix, geometric composite-score incl. all-zero-weights→similarity, strength/stability ChromaDB round-trip on a real `EpisodicMemory`/`tmp_path` fixture, idempotent decay sweep against a real memory + fake/broken activation trackers, rerank ordering, and a real `DreamingEngine`/`MockEpisodicMemory` Step-7f2 integration that seeds an episode before constructing the engine — the dream cycle early-returns on empty memory), real fixtures per BF-287; `tests/test_episodic.py` + `tests/test_dreaming.py` + `tests/test_ad871_provenance_envelope.py` (70) green. Closes [#845](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/845). Final unit of the Memory Epistemics wave (AD-871 → AD-872 → AD-873). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-872: Forge observability for the self-modification pipeline

**Decision:** Added a new pure, fully-typed, side-effect-free module `src/probos/cognitive/forge_observability.py` with three units and read-only honest-degrade wiring into `SelfModificationPipeline`. (1) `validate_forge_shape(intent_name: str, intent_description: str, parameters: dict[str, str] | None) -> list[str]` — a cheap pre-design gate returning error strings (empty list = proceed, mirroring `CodeValidator.validate`'s contract shape) for an empty/whitespace name, a degenerate (<2 char) name, a non-alphanumeric name, an empty description, `None` parameters, or an empty parameter key; an empty `{}` param map is explicitly **valid** (a no-parameter intent). (2) `classify_forge_rejection(record, validator_errors: list[str] | None = None) -> str` — deterministic bucketing into `syntax_error | forbidden_import | schema_nonconformance | judge_correctness | dependency_declined | dependency_failed | user_rejected | max_limit | design_failed | failed_sandbox | failed_registration | shape_rejected | other`, duck-typed on `.status`/`.error`; `failed_validation` combines `validator_errors` + `record.error` and substring-matches (`syntax error`, `forbidden import`, `judge`/`correctness`, schema signals) defaulting to `schema_nonconformance`; a direct status→bucket map covers the rest; an explicit `else → "other"` fallback means a future/unseen status (`failed_pool`, unknown) never crashes the aggregator. (3) `ForgeStatsAggregator(records: list)` — materializes a local copy of the records and reports `total_attempts`, `total_unique_intents`, `attempt_approval_rate`, `unique_intent_approval_rate`, `rejection_histogram: dict[str, int]`, and a flat `summary()` dict; `active`/`removed` count as approvals. Wiring in `src/probos/cognitive/self_mod.py`: a top-level import of `ForgeStatsAggregator`/`validate_forge_shape`; `forge_stats(self) -> ForgeStatsAggregator` returning `ForgeStatsAggregator(list(self._records))`; and a Tier-2 honest-degrade shape gate at the very top of `handle_unhandled_intent` that, on a non-empty error list, appends a `DesignedAgentRecord(status="shape_rejected", error="; ".join(shape_errors))` to `_records` and returns `None` before the design call. The optional `EventType.FORGE_SHAPE_REJECTED` was **not** added.

**Rationale:** The forge was a black box — only a `status` string and scattered logs, so designer-quality drift (rising rejection rate, retry storms on a single intent) was invisible. The three units make throughput measurable without touching the design/validate/sandbox path: `validate_forge_shape` short-circuits obviously-malformed requests *before* the expensive LLM design call (a pure gate, no side effects), `classify_forge_rejection` turns the flat status string into actionable rejection buckets, and `ForgeStatsAggregator` separates `unique_intent_approval_rate` from `attempt_approval_rate` — the load-bearing distinction, because a 3-retry recovery on one intent is one success, not three. The aggregator materializes its own copy of the records so post-construction source mutation can't silently drift the stats. Every wiring seam honest-degrades: a shape-gate exception logs a warning and falls through to normal design (a gate failure must never block a legitimate request); `classify_forge_rejection`'s `other` fallback keeps an unforeseen status from crashing the histogram. The circular-import risk (forge_observability references `DesignedAgentRecord`, which lives in self_mod) is resolved by importing it only under `TYPE_CHECKING` and duck-typing at runtime, so self_mod can import forge_observability at module top-level with no cycle. The `EventType.FORGE_SHAPE_REJECTED` emission was skipped because self_mod's `EventLog` uses string event names (`log(category, event, detail)`), not the `EventType` enum — it did not slot cleanly, and the prompt marked it optional ("only if it slots cleanly"). No new LLM calls, no persistence (in-memory aggregation over `_records` only), no memory-layer change. Tests: `tests/test_ad872_forge_observability.py` (28 — shape-gate accept/reject matrix incl. empty-`{}`-is-valid, every status→bucket mapping + validator-error substrings + `other` fallback, attempt-vs-unique-rate separation on a retried+distinct fixture, histogram correctness, local-copy materialization, `summary()` shape, `shape_rejected` short-circuits `handle_unhandled_intent` with the designer's `design_agent` asserted not-called, honest-degrade when the gate raises via monkeypatched `validate_forge_shape`, and `forge_stats()` returning a populated aggregator after a real design), real `DesignedAgentRecord` + real `SelfModificationPipeline` fixtures per BF-287 (no MagicMock at the substrate boundary). `tests/test_self_mod.py` + `tests/test_self_mod_deps.py` green; full gate 15411 passed, 22 skipped. Closes [#844](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/844). Second unit of the Memory Epistemics wave; AD-873 (Ebbinghaus decay + composite rerank) deferred to a later commit.

### AD-871: Provenance-aware memory envelope (source_type/confidence/verification_count/contradicted_by)

**Decision:** Added four last-position fields to the frozen `Episode` dataclass (`src/probos/types.py`): `source_type: str = ""`, `confidence: float = 1.0`, `verification_count: int = 0`, `contradicted_by: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)`. Added a provenance kernel to `types.py`: `SOURCE_TYPE_CONFIDENCE` (per-source default belief — `user_statement`/`tool_result`=1.0, `observation`/`external`=0.8, `agent_inference`/`reflection`=0.5), `SOURCE_TO_SOURCE_TYPE` (maps the legacy `MemorySource` string to a `source_type`: `direct`→`observation`, `secondhand`→`agent_inference`, `ship_records`/`briefing`→`external`, `reflection`→`reflection`), `resolve_provenance(source, source_type, confidence) -> tuple[str, float]`, and `mark_contradicted(episode, contradicting_id) -> Episode`. Wired three seams in `src/probos/cognitive/episodic.py`: (1) `store()`'s AD-598 importance rescore reconstructs the frozen Episode via `dataclasses.replace(episode, importance=...)` so the new fields survive; (2) `_episode_to_metadata` stamps the envelope onto the ChromaDB row (`contradicted_by` JSON-encoded to `contradicted_by_json` per the metadata str/int/float/bool-only rule, source/type resolved through `resolve_provenance` at the write boundary); (3) `_metadata_to_episode` decodes it back with Tier-2 honest-degrade. `compute_episode_hash` and `_hash_v` untouched.

**Rationale:** Memory previously recorded *what* happened but not *how it was learned* or *how trustworthy it is*. The provenance envelope lets a memory carry graded belief (`confidence`), its acquisition source (`source_type`), corroboration (`verification_count`), and contradiction links (`contradicted_by`) — the substrate for future belief-revision and contradiction handling (AD-872/873). `resolve_provenance` derives confidence from the source map **only** when the field is set AND confidence is still the 1.0 default, so an explicit caller-supplied graded belief is never overwritten; an empty `source_type` is back-filled from the legacy `source` string so pre-existing call sites get a sensible type for free. The `store()` reconstruction fix was load-bearing: a failure outcome at default importance=5 rescores to 7, and the prior field-by-field copy silently dropped the new fields — `dataclasses.replace` preserves every carried field by construction. The read seam honest-degrades every malformed value (bad `confidence`→1.0, bad `verification_count`→0, bad/non-list `contradicted_by_json`→`[]`) so pre-AD-871 rows recall cleanly with neutral defaults — zero migration. Tests: `tests/test_ad871_provenance_envelope.py` (14 — defaults, store/recall round-trip of all four fields, legacy-source back-fill, `resolve_provenance` derive-vs-preserve matrix, map self-consistency, graded round-trip, `mark_contradicted` idempotency, read-seam honest-degrade on malformed/non-list metadata, pre-AD-871 default recall, and the AD-598 reconstruction regression), real `EpisodicMemory`/`tmp_path` fixtures per BF-287. `tests/test_episodic.py` (16) green; full gate 15382 passed. Closes [#843](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/843). First unit of the Memory Epistemics wave; AD-872 (forge observability) and AD-873 (decay + rerank) deferred to later commits.

### AD-847: Desktop notification on Yeo task completion (renderer → preload → main → native notify)

**Decision:** Closed the wave's final surface: a native OS notification when a Yeo-delegated task finishes. Added a `notifyTaskDone({title, body, route})` method to the `window.probos` context-bridge API (`desktop/src/preload/index.ts`) that `ipcRenderer.invoke("probos:notifyTaskDone", payload)`s the main process. The main process (`desktop/src/main/index.ts`) registers `ipcMain.handle("probos:notifyTaskDone", ...)` which coerces the untrusted renderer payload via a new pure helper `coerceTaskDonePayload(payload): NotifyArgs | null` (`desktop/src/main/notifications.ts`) and, on success, calls the existing AD-759 `notify(args, { showAndRoute })` primitive. When `route` is present (e.g. Yeo's 1:1 chat deep-link), clicking the notification activates the window and routes there via the existing `showAndRoute`. Reuses the existing `probos:*` channel naming and the AD-759 notification wrapper — no new WebSocket, no new window plumbing.

**Rationale:** AD-846 posts the completion DM into Yeo's chat channel, but a desktop user with the window minimized would still miss it. AD-847 adds the OS-level surface so a finished task can pull the Captain back to the exact place to read the result. The renderer payload is untrusted across the context-isolation boundary, so `coerceTaskDonePayload` validates `title` (non-empty string) / `body` (string) and drops a blank `route` to `undefined` (so a click never routes to an empty path) — making validation the testable unit independent of Electron. The notification dispatch degrades silently when the OS reports no notification support (AD-759 behavior, unchanged). Tests: `desktop/src/main/notifications.test.ts` (9 — 5 coercion: route/blank-route/empty-title/non-string-body/non-object; 4 dispatch: shows/click-routes/no-route-no-handler/unsupported-suppressed; electron mocked via `vi.mock`). Full desktop gate 65 green; `electron-vite build` clean. Closes [#842](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/842). Completes the AD-869→870→846→847 lightweight-delegation wave.

### AD-846: Yeo task-completion → proactive Captain DM (async half of the Tier-3 delegation loop)

**Decision:** Added `src/probos/task_completion_notifier.py` (`notify_captain_of_task_completion(runtime, event)`) and wired it in `startup/finalize.py` (`_wire_task_completion_notifier`) as a listener on `EventType.WORK_ITEM_STATUS_CHANGED`. When a work item reaches a terminal status (`done`/`failed`) AND it is a Yeo-originated dispatchable task (`metadata.dispatchable` truthy AND `tags` contains `"yeo-delegated"`), Yeo proactively DMs the Captain with the outcome — a one-line "Task complete: <title>." (done) or "Task did not finish: <title>… let me know if you'd like me to open it again." (failed). The DM reuses the AD-485 Captain-DM primitive: find-or-create the `dm-captain-{yeo_id[:8]}` channel via `ward_room.list_channels()`/`create_channel(channel_type="dm")`, then `ward_room.create_thread(...)` authored by the live Yeo agent (resolved from the `yeoman` registry pool). Listener wired via `runtime.add_event_listener(_on_status_changed, event_types=["work_item_status_changed"])`.

**Rationale:** AD-845 gave Yeo Tier-3 (`[CREATE_TASK]` → kanban) but the loop was open: once Yeo wrote a task down, the Captain had to discover the result on the board. AD-846 closes the async half so a task Yeo opened on the Captain's behalf reports back to the same 1:1 channel it came from. The `yeo-delegated` tag gate is load-bearing — only tasks Yeo opened notify, so system/crew work items never spam the Captain's DM. Every failure mode is Tier-2 honest-degrade (no ward room, no live Yeo, registry raises, non-matching event → log if relevant and return, never raise); a missing chat substrate never blocks a status transition. The kanban board remains the result surface regardless. Desktop notification (AD-847) is the gated follow-up, NOT built here. Tests: `tests/test_ad846_completion_dm.py` (9, real fake ward room + real registry pool fixtures per the no-MagicMock-at-substrate-boundary rule).

### AD-870: Yeo's four-tier delegation threshold instructions (when to [MESH] vs [CREATE_TASK])

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Decision:** Extended `YeomanAgent._conversational_task_protocol` (the AD-845 hook) to teach the full four-tier delegation threshold in plain language instead of only the Tier-3 `[CREATE_TASK]` guidance: Tier 1 Answer (reply directly, no tag) / Tier 2 Do-and-report (a quick read-only lookup Yeo can finish *this turn* → emit the AD-869 `[MESH <intent> key=value ...]` tag) / Tier 3 Write-it-down (substantial work or anything that changes state → `[CREATE_TASK ...]`) / Tier 4 Get-help (`specialist=@Callsign`). A new helper `_available_mesh_read_intents()` reads the live registry and returns `{intent: param-hint}` only for read pools that currently have an agent (`directory`→`list_directory path=<dir>`, `filesystem`→`read_file path=<file>`, `search`→`search_files path=<dir> pattern=<glob>`, `web_search`→`web_search query=<terms>`, `page_reader`→`read_page url=<url>`) — so the `[MESH]` guidance lists only forms the ship can actually serve. The closing "rule of thumb" encodes the two-axis threshold: "if you can get the answer in the time it takes to reply and it changes nothing, just do it; otherwise write it down as a task."
**Rationale:** AD-869 built the Tier-2 *seam* but Yeo had no instruction telling it *when* to prefer an inline `[MESH]` read over opening a `[CREATE_TASK]` — without the threshold rule Yeo would either over-escalate (open a task for a one-line directory listing) or under-deliver. The threshold is grounded in graduated-autonomy doctrine (command-by-negation / Mission Command: act within intent, escalate by exception) and a decision-cost model (Vroom–Yetton: match decision mode to the stakes): the two axes Yeo weighs are *latency* (can I finish this turn?) and *reversibility/cost* (does it change anything?). Teaching this in the conversational prompt (not `decide()`/`act()`) keeps Yeo instructions-first (Design Principle #6). Honest-degrade is preserved and tightened: `[MESH]` guidance is gated per-pool on a live agent and `[CREATE_TASK]` guidance on a wired work-item store, so Yeo is never told to use a seam the substrate cannot back; a registry that raises during the read-intent build degrades to the `[CREATE_TASK]`-only block and never crashes the reply. All text remains free of the `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` tokens (asserted).
**Status:** Implemented. +8 pytest (`tests/test_ad870_yeo_delegation_threshold.py`, real `AgentRegistry` fixtures per the no-MagicMock-at-substrate-boundary rule — all-tiers-when-fully-wired, MESH-lists-only-live-pools, no-seams→empty, MESH-only-when-store-absent, CREATE_TASK-only-when-no-read-pools, gap-regex-safe full block, registry-raises→degrade-to-CREATE_TASK, base-hook no-op); `tests/test_ad845_yeo_chat_task_creation.py` + `tests/test_yeoman_agent.py` (34) green. Closes [#840](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/840). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-869: Yeo's Tier-2 "do-and-report" — synchronous inline mesh reads from a 1:1 chat reply

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Decision:** Added Yeo's lightweight delegation *default* — the missing Tier-2 of the four-tier delegation model (Tier 1 Answer / **Tier 2 Do-and-report** / Tier 3 Write-it-down = AD-845 `[CREATE_TASK]` / Tier 4 Get-help = AD-845 `specialist=@`). When the Captain asks for a quick read-only lookup Yeo can answer *this turn*, Yeo emits a reply tag `[MESH <intent> key=value key=value]`. Two new `DmSanityGate` methods parse it (`extract_mesh_read(text) -> tuple[str, dict[str,str]] | None` / `strip_mesh_read(text) -> str`, with `_MESH_READ_RE` / `_MESH_READ_STRIP_RE` / `_MESH_PARAM_KEY_RE`; the key regex anchors on a token boundary so a `=` inside a value such as a URL query string is preserved, and multi-word values like `query=Nvidia SPARK RTX` parse intact). A new `DmReplyPipeline.step_4h_mesh_read_parse` (registered before `step_4f_extract_artifacts`, so a large read result is still eligible for artifact extraction + episodic storage) maps the intent to its registry pool via the module-level allowlist `_MESH_READ_INTENT_POOLS` (`list_directory`→`directory`, `read_file`/`stat_file`→`filesystem`, `search_files`→`search`, `web_search`→`web_search`, `read_page`→`page_reader`), resolves the first live agent in that pool via `runtime.registry.get_by_pool(pool)` (reusing the BF-599 resolution pattern), runs ONE targeted `IntentBus.send(IntentMessage(intent, params, target_agent_id, ttl_seconds=5))` (single dispatch — NOT a broadcast, which would fan out to every pool subscriber), renders the result inline (truncated to 1500 chars), and strips the tag. A non-allowlisted intent (e.g. `http_fetch`) is stripped and shipped, never executed.
**Rationale:** AD-845 built the *escalation* path (async tracked `[CREATE_TASK]` work) but live testing showed the right *default* is a lightweight synchronous read the Captain gets back this turn — "if I can get the answer in the time it takes to reply, and it doesn't change anything, I just do it; otherwise I write it down." The allowlist is the Tier-2 safety boundary and it is structural, not merely a policy list: a single-turn ~5s synchronous read is *incapable* of mutation because destructive ops require consensus and consensus cannot resolve in one turn, so the latency ceiling enforces the safety ceiling. `http_fetch` is consensus-gated and therefore excluded; writes are excluded; anything heavier belongs on the Tier-3 async path. The seam follows the established in-reply-tag precedent (`[MOVE]`, `[SELF_CHECK]`, `[GEN_IMAGE]`, `[ACTION]`, `[CREATE_TASK]`) rather than a decomposer intent (never fires on the conversational path). Web/file access stays mesh-delegated (Design Principle #10): no `httpx`/`requests` import is added (asserted by source scan). Every failure mode is Tier-2 honest-degrade (missing gate/bus/agent, send failure, timeout, unsuccessful result → strip tag, append a brief note whose wording avoids the `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` tokens, never raise). The Yeo-facing threshold instructions that teach *when* to emit `[MESH]` vs `[CREATE_TASK]` vs `specialist=@` ship next in AD-870; completion → Captain DM (AD-846) and desktop notification (AD-847) are gated follow-ups, NOT built here.
**Status:** Implemented. +16 pytest (`tests/test_ad869_mesh_read_inline.py`, real `IntentBus` + `SignalManager` + `AgentRegistry` + subscribed handler + real `DmSanityGate` per the no-MagicMock-at-substrate-boundary rule — extract/strip unit tests incl. multi-word value + embedded-`=` URL + parameterless-malformed, allowlisted read executes/renders/strips with single targeted dispatch, non-allowlisted `http_fetch` not executed, no-tag no-op, intent-bus-None degrade, no-capable-agent honest note, send-failure honest note, unsuccessful-result empty note, large-payload truncation, allowlist excludes writes/consensus-gated intents, no-direct-http-import source scan; all degrade notes asserted gap-regex-clean); DM pipeline + sanity-gate regression suites (53) green. Closes [#839](https://github.com/seangalliher/ProbOS/issues/839). Design grounded in graduated-autonomy doctrine (command-by-negation / Mission Command; workflows-vs-agents; Vroom–Yetton decision model). Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### AD-845: Yeo creates a dispatchable task from a 1:1 chat reply (D2 auto-delegation, Phase 1)

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Decision:** Added a second overridable base hook `CognitiveAgent._conversational_task_protocol(self, observation: dict) -> str` (default `""`), appended next to the BF-599 `_conversational_capability_block` inside `_decide_via_llm`'s `is_conversation` branch. `YeomanAgent` overrides it to teach a reply tag `[CREATE_TASK title=... | instructions=... | specialist=@callsign]` (honest-degrade: returns `""` when `runtime.work_item_store` is absent, so Yeo is never told it can open tasks it cannot back; tag text is `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE`-clean). A new `DmReplyPipeline.step_4g_create_task_parse` (sibling of the AD-572 `[MOVE]` / AD-728d `[SELF_CHECK]` steps, registered after `step_4f_extract_artifacts`, before `step_5_episodic_store`) parses the tag via two new `DmSanityGate` methods (`extract_create_task` / `strip_create_task` + `_CREATE_TASK_RE` / `_CREATE_TASK_STRIP_RE`), resolves the specialist callsign → live agent UUID through `callsign_registry.resolve` (fallback: Yeo's `resolve_delegate` department keyword map over the instructions text), creates a `dispatchable=True` work item tagged `yeo-delegated` via `WorkItemStore.create_work_item(work_type="task", created_by="captain", ...)`, strips the tag, and appends the new task id to the Captain-visible reply. The dispatchable item then runs automatically through the AD-834/AD-839 `WorkItemRouter` — no new execution code.
**Rationale:** BF-599/BF-601 closed D1 (grounding — telling Yeo *what* it can delegate) but live testing showed the deeper D2 gap: Yeo's conversational path is pure text generation and has no seam to actually *fire* a mesh intent, so even when correctly grounded it emitted fake `[MESH http_fetch ...]` text and then honestly refused to pretend it had executed (the confabulation guard working as designed). AD-845 gives the conversational reply a real action seam following the established in-reply-tag precedent (`[MOVE]`, `[CHALLENGE]`, `[SELF_CHECK]`, `[GEN_IMAGE]`, `[ACTION]`) rather than adding a decomposer intent (which never fires on the conversational path) or overriding Yeo's `decide()`/`act()`. The hook stays Open/Closed (base `""`, only Yeo opts in); the work item is the existing dispatch primitive (no new router/execution code); every failure mode is Tier-2 honest-degrade (missing gate/store/create-failure → strip tag, ship reply, never raise). Supersedes the deferred "BF-599b / AD-840" marker (AD-840–844 are reserved for the Desktop Console epic). AD-846 (completion → proactive Captain DM) and AD-847 (desktop notification) are gated follow-ups, NOT built here.
**Status:** Implemented. +9 pytest (`tests/test_ad845_yeo_chat_task_creation.py`, real `WorkItemStore` in-memory + real `AgentRegistry`/`CallsignRegistry` + real `DmSanityGate` per the no-MagicMock-at-substrate-boundary rule — dispatchable-item creation, tag strip + task-id surface, no-tag no-op, store-None honest-degrade, keyword-map specialist fallback, unresolved→unassigned-but-dispatchable, gap-regex-safe protocol text, store-absent hook degrade, base-hook no-op); `tests/test_bf599_yeo_web_research_delegation.py` + `tests/test_yeoman_agent.py` (43 total) and `tests/test_ad726_dm_reply_pipeline.py` + `tests/test_ad724_dm_sanity_gate.py` + `tests/test_ad724_dm_hardening.py` (38) green. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### BF-601: Yeo conversational capability grounding — filesystem trio (sibling of BF-599)

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Decision:** Extended `YeomanAgent._conversational_capability_block` (the BF-599 base-hook override) to also surface the always-registered core filesystem pools: `directory` → `list_directory`, `filesystem` → `read_file`, `search` → `search_files`, appended to the existing web trio (`web_search` / `read_page` / `http_fetch`). The closing instruction is generalized so Yeo delegates "research or read a web page, list a directory, read a file, or find files" through the mesh rather than declining. Same honest-degrade contract (returns `""` on no runtime / no registry / registry read raises / no relevant pools) and the rendered block remains free of every `_CAPABILITY_GAP_RE` token (asserted by test).
**Rationale:** Live testing reproduced the BF-599 confabulation for a different capability family — asked "what files are in `D:\ProbOS\src\probos\cognitive`," Yeo replied "I don't have a direct filesystem browsing capability built in. I can't list directory contents on my own," despite the `directory` / `filesystem` / `search` pools being core, always-present agents. The root cause is identical (the DM prompt composes with `hardcoded_instructions=""`, so Yeo's static role rules never reach the conversational turn and the LLM fills the void with a plausible-but-false limitation). BF-599 fixed only the web trio; the filesystem trio was structurally uncovered. Because these are core pools, listing them is always truthful and self-updating from the live registry — no static drift. The fix reuses the existing seam (no new hook, Open/Closed preserved) and adds no direct filesystem-walking code to Yeo: access stays mesh-delegated (Design Principle #10).
**Status:** Implemented. +3 pytest (`tests/test_bf599_yeo_web_research_delegation.py` — filesystem-pool listing, gap-regex-clean, combined web+filesystem block; 9 total in file), `tests/test_yeoman_agent.py` (25) green — 34 passed. Verify all changes comply with the Engineering Principles in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

### BF-599: Yeo conversational capability grounding (overridable base hook)

**Date:** 2026-06-03
